OL:OL20867W.title: Middlemarch
OL:OL20867W.author: George Eliot
OL:OL20867W.description: In the provincial English town of Middlemarch, the idealistic Dorothea Brooke marries the dry scholar Edward Casaubon while the ambitious young doctor Tertius Lydgate sinks into debt and a difficult marriage, their lives crossing amid the politics and gossip of the community. A long Victorian novel known for its psychological realism and interlocking provincial portraits.

OL:OL267096W.title: Anna Karenina
OL:OL267096W.author: Leo Tolstoy
OL:OL267096W.description: In imperial Russia, the married Anna Karenina abandons her husband and son for an affair with the officer Count Vronsky, while the landowner Konstantin Levin courts Kitty and searches for meaning on his estate. Known for its realism and its parallel treatment of love, marriage, and Russian society.

OL:OL86318W.title: Ulysses
OL:OL86318W.author: James Joyce
OL:OL86318W.description: Leopold Bloom wanders through Dublin over the course of a single day, June 16, 1904, crossing paths with the young Stephen Dedalus as his wife Molly waits at home. Known for its stream-of-consciousness technique and its parallels to Homer's Odyssey.

OL:OL19350876W.title: Madame Bovary
OL:OL19350876W.author: Gustave Flaubert
OL:OL19350876W.description: In provincial Normandy, the doctor's wife Emma Bovary, bored by her marriage to the dull Charles, pursues affairs and luxuries on credit until her debts overwhelm her. Known for its realism and the obscenity trial that followed its serialization.

OL:OL50548W.title: Beloved
OL:OL50548W.author: Toni Morrison
OL:OL50548W.description: In Ohio after the Civil War, the former slave Sethe lives in a house haunted by the daughter she killed to keep her from being returned to slavery, until a young woman calling herself Beloved arrives. A novel known for its treatment of slavery and memory, and winner of the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL34381078W.title: The Great Gatsby
OL:OL34381078W.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
OL:OL34381078W.description: On Long Island in the 1920s, the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby throws lavish parties in pursuit of his lost love Daisy Buchanan, watched by his neighbor and narrator Nick Carraway. Known for its portrait of the Jazz Age and the American Dream.

OL:OL1190289W.title: In Search of Lost Time
OL:OL1190289W.author: Marcel Proust
OL:OL1190289W.description: The narrator recalls his life in French high society, from childhood in Combray to love affairs and salons in Paris, his memories triggered by sensations like the taste of a madeleine. A seven-volume novel known for its length and its exploration of involuntary memory.

OL:OL39396W.title: To the Lighthouse
OL:OL39396W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL39396W.description: The Ramsay family and their guests gather at a summer house on the Isle of Skye, where a planned trip to a nearby lighthouse is delayed for years across the span of the novel. Known for its stream-of-consciousness narration and shifting points of view.

OL:OL267171W.title: War and Peace
OL:OL267171W.author: Leo Tolstoy
OL:OL267171W.description: Aristocratic families including the Bezukhovs, Bolkonskys, and Rostovs live through Russia's wars against Napoleon, as Pierre, Andrei, and Natasha search for meaning amid invasion and society. A long novel known for blending domestic drama with the history of the 1812 French invasion.

OL:OL102749W.title: Moby-Dick
OL:OL102749W.author: Herman Melville
OL:OL102749W.description: Aboard the whaling ship Pequod, the sailor Ishmael joins Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for the white whale that bit off his leg, as the voyage drives toward disaster. Known for its digressions on whaling and its symbolic ambition.

OL:OL274505W.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
OL:OL274505W.author: Gabriel García Márquez
OL:OL274505W.description: In the founded town of Macondo, seven generations of the Buendía family live through love, war, and repetition, marked by prophecies and strange occurrences. A novel known for its magical realism and its allegory of Latin American history.

OL:OL1095427W.title: Jane Eyre
OL:OL1095427W.author: Charlotte Brontë
OL:OL1095427W.description: Orphaned and mistreated, Jane Eyre grows up to become governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with her employer Mr. Rochester and discovers the secret he keeps locked upstairs. Known for its first-person narration and its blend of romance and Gothic elements.

OL:OL627084W.title: Lolita
OL:OL627084W.author: Vladimir Nabokov
OL:OL627084W.description: The middle-aged European Humbert Humbert becomes obsessed with twelve-year-old Dolores Haze, marries her mother to be near her, and takes the girl on a long road trip across America after the mother's death. A novel known for its controversial subject and its elaborate prose.

OL:OL15165350W.title: Pride and Prejudice
OL:OL15165350W.author: Jane Austen
OL:OL15165350W.description: In rural England, Elizabeth Bennet, second of five daughters, clashes with the proud, wealthy Mr. Darcy while her family pursues advantageous marriages. Known for its wit and its treatment of class, marriage, and reputation.

OL:OL53908W.title: Huckleberry Finn
OL:OL53908W.author: Mark Twain
OL:OL53908W.description: Huckleberry Finn fakes his own death and floats down the Mississippi River on a raft with the runaway slave Jim, drifting through encounters with con men and feuding families. Known for its vernacular narration and its treatment of slavery and race.

OL:OL26733889W.title: Mrs Dalloway
OL:OL26733889W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL26733889W.description: In London on a single day, Clarissa Dalloway prepares for an evening party while the shell-shocked veteran Septimus Smith spirals toward suicide across the city. Known for its stream-of-consciousness narration and its compression of time into one day.

OL:OL190034W.title: Emma
OL:OL190034W.author: Jane Austen
OL:OL190034W.description: In the village of Highbury, the wealthy and clever Emma Woodhouse meddles in the romances of those around her, mismatching couples while remaining blind to her own feelings for Mr. Knightley. A comic novel known for its handling of self-deception and social misjudgment.

OL:OL32013322W.title: The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman
OL:OL32013322W.author: Laurence Sterne
OL:OL32013322W.description: Tristram Shandy sets out to tell the story of his own life but is constantly sidetracked by digressions, leaving his birth and family, including his father Walter and Uncle Toby, the real subject. A comic novel known for its digressive structure and typographic experiments.

OL:OL40756300W.title: Persuasion
OL:OL40756300W.author: Jane Austen
OL:OL40756300W.description: Years after being persuaded to reject the naval officer Frederick Wentworth, Anne Elliot encounters him again, now wealthy, as her vain father's debts force the family to economize. A novel known for its mature romance and its restrained, ironic tone.

OL:OL14868508W.title: Bleak House
OL:OL14868508W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL14868508W.description: The interminable lawsuit Jarndyce and Jarndyce drags through the Court of Chancery as Esther Summerson, Lady Dedlock, and a wide cast become entangled in its mysteries and the secrets of Esther's birth. A novel known for its satire of the English legal system and its dual narration.

OL:OL276365W.title: The Portrait of a Lady
OL:OL276365W.author: Henry James
OL:OL276365W.description: The independent young American Isabel Archer inherits a fortune and travels through Europe, rejecting suitors before marrying the cold dilettante Gilbert Osmond and learning the truth about his motives. Known for its psychological portraiture and its study of a woman's choices.

OL:OL44222301W.title: Don Quixote
OL:OL44222301W.author: Miguel de Cervantes
OL:OL44222301W.description: The aging Alonso Quijano of La Mancha reads so many chivalric romances that he names himself Don Quixote, recruits the peasant Sancho Panza as his squire, and rides out tilting at windmills he takes for giants. Often called the first modern novel and known for its satire of chivalric romance.

OL:OL8721462W.title: Great Expectations
OL:OL8721462W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL8721462W.description: The orphan Pip, raised by his sister in the Kent marshes, receives a fortune from an unknown benefactor and moves to London to become a gentleman, pining for the cold Estella. A novel known for its first-person narration and its theme of social ambition.

OL:OL21170W.title: Wuthering Heights
OL:OL21170W.author: Emily Brontë
OL:OL21170W.description: On the Yorkshire moors, the foundling Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw form a destructive bond that, after her marriage to another, drives Heathcliff to revenge across two generations of two families. Known for its frame narration and its bleak, passionate intensity.

OL:OL10432709W.title: The Brothers Karamazov
OL:OL10432709W.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL:OL10432709W.description: In a Russian town, the brothers Dmitri, Ivan, and Alexei Karamazov clash with their dissolute father Fyodor, whose murder brings suspicion onto Dmitri and a trial. A novel known for its debates on faith, doubt, and morality, including the parable of the Grand Inquisitor.

OL:OL166894W.title: Crime and Punishment
OL:OL166894W.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL:OL166894W.description: In St. Petersburg, the impoverished former student Raskolnikov murders a pawnbroker to test his theory that some men are above moral law, then is consumed by guilt as the detective Porfiry circles him. Known for its psychological study of crime and conscience.

K:3b04f3eef439.title: Stories of Flannery O'Connor
K:3b04f3eef439.author: Flannery O’Connor
K:3b04f3eef439.description: A collection of thirty-one short stories set largely in the rural American South, including "A Good Man Is Hard to Find" and "Everything That Rises Must Converge," many ending in sudden violence or revelation. Awarded the National Book Award for Fiction and known for its dark comedy and Catholic themes.

OL:OL495470W.title: Invisible Man
OL:OL495470W.author: Ralph Ellison
OL:OL495470W.description: An unnamed Black narrator recounts his journey from a Southern college through Harlem and a political organization called the Brotherhood, concluding that society refuses to see him. A novel known for its treatment of race and identity, and winner of the National Book Award.

OL:OL1168083W.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
OL:OL1168083W.author: George Orwell
OL:OL1168083W.description: In the totalitarian superstate of Oceania, the party functionary Winston Smith secretly rebels against the surveillance of Big Brother and begins an affair with Julia before the Thought Police catch them. A dystopian novel known for concepts like doublethink, Newspeak, and Room 101.

K:6b584d1b9428.title: Stories of Anton Chekhov
K:6b584d1b9428.author: Anton Chekhov
K:6b584d1b9428.description: A collection of short stories set across Russia, depicting peasants, doctors, clerks, and gentry in works such as "The Lady with the Dog" and "Ward No. 6." Known for their understated realism and lack of conventional moralizing.

OL:OL498463W.title: The Trial
OL:OL498463W.author: Franz Kafka
OL:OL498463W.description: The bank official Josef K. is arrested one morning by unidentified agents for a crime that is never named, and is drawn into a baffling, faceless legal bureaucracy as he tries to defend himself. A novel known for its nightmarish portrayal of an opaque justice system.

OL:OL59048W.title: The Remains of the Day
OL:OL59048W.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
OL:OL59048W.description: The English butler Stevens takes a motoring trip across the countryside in 1956, recalling his decades of service at Darlington Hall and his repressed feelings for the housekeeper Miss Kenton. A novel known for its restrained narration and winner of the Booker Prize.

OL:OL82870W.title: The Sound and the Fury
OL:OL82870W.author: William Faulkner
OL:OL82870W.description: The decline of the Compson family in Mississippi is told in four sections, including ones narrated by the disabled Benjy and the suicidal Quentin, circling the lost sister Caddy. A novel known for its stream-of-consciousness narration and fractured chronology.

K:fbe28ea907ef.title: Hamlet
K:fbe28ea907ef.author: William Shakespeare
K:fbe28ea907ef.description: Prince Hamlet of Denmark is visited by the ghost of his murdered father, who names his uncle Claudius as the killer, and Hamlet feigns madness while plotting revenge as the court spirals toward death. A tragedy famous for its soliloquies and its hero's hesitation.

OL:OL627081W.title: Pale Fire
OL:OL627081W.author: Vladimir Nabokov
OL:OL627081W.description: The exiled scholar Charles Kinbote edits a 999-line poem by the recently murdered American poet John Shade, filling his foreword, commentary, and index with a delusional tale of his own escape as the deposed king of distant Zembla. A novel built entirely as a poem with annotations, leaving its true authorship in doubt.

OL:OL457179W.title: Midnight's Children
OL:OL457179W.author: Salman Rushdie
OL:OL457179W.description: Saleem Sinai, born at the stroke of midnight as India gains independence on August 15, 1947, finds himself telepathically linked to the other children born that hour and narrates his family's history against the nation's turbulent decades. It won the Booker Prize and was later named the best of the prize's first twenty-five years.

OL:OL23205W.title: The Grapes of Wrath
OL:OL23205W.author: John Steinbeck
OL:OL23205W.description: The Joad family, driven off their Oklahoma farm by drought and the Dust Bowl, load a truck and migrate to California seeking work, only to meet exploitation and hardship in the migrant camps. It won the Pulitzer Prize and became a defining account of the Great Depression.

K:d2d9f9b0f145.title: Absalom, Absalom!
K:d2d9f9b0f145.author: William Faulkner
K:d2d9f9b0f145.description: Quentin Compson and others piece together the rise and fall of Thomas Sutpen, a poor man who builds a Mississippi plantation dynasty before the Civil War and is destroyed by his own designs and the secrets of his children. A novel told through layered, conflicting narrators reconstructing the same Southern past.

OL:OL891786W.title: Things Fall Apart
OL:OL891786W.author: Chinua Achebe
OL:OL891786W.description: Okonkwo, a respected wrestler and yam farmer in the Igbo village of Umuofia, governs his household by strength and pride until the arrival of British missionaries and colonial administrators unravels his world. One of the most widely read works of African literature, written in English.

OL:OL26437W.title: The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie
OL:OL26437W.author: Muriel Spark
OL:OL26437W.description: At a girls' school in 1930s Edinburgh, the charismatic teacher Jean Brodie grooms a chosen set of pupils with her ideas on art, love, and fascism, until one of them betrays her. A short novel that moves back and forth in time to reveal which girl turns against her.

OL:OL8662242W.title: David Copperfield
OL:OL8662242W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL8662242W.description: David Copperfield recounts his life from a harsh childhood under his cruel stepfather Murdstone, through schooling, work, and marriage, encountering figures such as Mr. Micawber, Uriah Heep, and his aunt Betsey Trotwood. A largely autobiographical novel issued in monthly serial parts.

K:04ef5684be62.title: Dubliners
K:04ef5684be62.author: James Joyce
K:04ef5684be62.description: Fifteen short stories trace the lives of Dublin residents, moving from childhood through adolescence and maturity to public life, and closing with "The Dead," in which Gabriel Conroy confronts his wife's buried memory. A collection known for its precise realism and moments of sudden self-recognition.

OL:OL42718662W.title: Rabbit, Run
OL:OL42718662W.author: John Updike
OL:OL42718662W.description: Harry "Rabbit" Angstrom, a twenty-six-year-old former high school basketball star stuck in a dull job and marriage in small-town Pennsylvania, abruptly abandons his pregnant wife and drifts between her and a part-time prostitute. The first of four novels following Rabbit across the decades.

OL:OL463820W.title: Rabbit Is Rich
OL:OL463820W.author: John Updike
OL:OL463820W.description: Now in his forties and running his late father-in-law's Toyota dealership during the 1979 energy crisis, Harry "Rabbit" Angstrom enjoys new prosperity while contending with his troubled adult son Nelson. The third Rabbit novel, which won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL463809W.title: Rabbit at Rest
OL:OL463809W.author: John Updike
OL:OL463809W.description: An aging, heart-troubled Harry "Rabbit" Angstrom, semi-retired in Florida and still tangled with his son Nelson's addictions and the family business, moves toward a final reckoning with his own mortality. The fourth and last Rabbit novel, which won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL40879W.title: Blood Meridian
OL:OL40879W.author: Cormac McCarthy
OL:OL40879W.description: A runaway teenager known as the kid falls in with the Glanton gang of scalp hunters along the Texas-Mexico borderlands around 1850, riding through relentless massacres dominated by the enormous, philosophizing Judge Holden. A novel known for its extreme violence and dense prose.

OL:OL38663W.title: Heart of Darkness
OL:OL38663W.author: Joseph Conrad
OL:OL38663W.description: The seaman Marlow recounts his journey up the Congo River for a Belgian trading company to find Kurtz, an ivory agent who has set himself up as a godlike ruler among the people of the interior. A novella widely read as a study of imperialism and moral corruption.

K:5fcc86b529ea.title: Rabbit Redux
K:5fcc86b529ea.author: John Updike
K:5fcc86b529ea.description: Harry "Rabbit" Angstrom, now a aging-feeling typesetter whose wife has left him, takes a young runaway and a Black radical named Skeeter into his Pennsylvania home as the country churns through 1969. The second Rabbit novel, set against the moon landing and racial unrest.

OL:OL98491W.title: The Age of Innocence
OL:OL98491W.author: Edith Wharton
OL:OL98491W.description: In 1870s upper-class New York, the lawyer Newland Archer is engaged to the conventional May Welland when he falls for her unconventional cousin, the Countess Ellen Olenska, who has fled a bad European marriage. It won the Pulitzer Prize and dissects the rigid codes of Gilded Age society.

OL:OL14866824W.title: The Magic Mountain
OL:OL14866824W.author: Thomas Mann
OL:OL14866824W.description: Hans Castorp, a young engineer, visits his cousin at a tuberculosis sanatorium high in the Swiss Alps for three weeks and ends up staying seven years, drawn into illness, ideas, and debates among the patients. A long novel of ideas set just before the First World War.

OL:OL50564W.title: Song of Solomon
OL:OL50564W.author: Toni Morrison
OL:OL50564W.description: Macon "Milkman" Dead, born into a well-off Black family in Michigan, travels south to trace his ancestry and a rumored cache of gold, uncovering his family's history of flight and a legend of an ancestor who flew back to Africa. It won the National Book Critics Circle Award.

OL:OL675783W.title: The Handmaid's Tale
OL:OL675783W.author: Margaret Atwood
OL:OL675783W.description: In the near-future theocracy of Gilead, which has overthrown the United States, the handmaid Offred is assigned to a Commander's household to bear children for the ruling class amid widespread infertility. A dystopian novel narrated by a woman reduced to her reproductive role.

K:bc4aa7549271.title: King Lear
K:bc4aa7549271.author: William Shakespeare
K:bc4aa7549271.description: The aging King Lear divides his kingdom among his daughters by how much they flatter him, banishing the honest Cordelia and falling into madness after the scheming Goneril and Regan turn on him. A tragedy paired with a subplot of the betrayed Earl of Gloucester and his sons.

OL:OL3140822W.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
OL:OL3140822W.author: Harper Lee
OL:OL3140822W.description: In Depression-era Maycomb, Alabama, young Scout Finch watches her lawyer father Atticus defend Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of raping a white woman, while she and her brother puzzle over their reclusive neighbor Boo Radley. It won the Pulitzer Prize and became a standard of American school reading.

OL:OL26860869W.title: Frankenstein
OL:OL26860869W.author: Mary Shelley
OL:OL26860869W.description: The scientist Victor Frankenstein assembles a living creature from dead matter, then flees in horror as the rejected being, denied companionship, turns to vengeance against his maker's family. An early work of science fiction told through nested narratives.

OL:OL509889W.title: The Good Soldier
OL:OL509889W.author: Ford Madox Ford
OL:OL509889W.description: John Dowell slowly pieces together how his wife Florence and his friend Edward Ashburnham carried on a long affair at a German spa, exposing the wreckage beneath two outwardly proper marriages. A novel told out of sequence by an unreliable narrator.

OL:OL1230613W.title: The Outsider
OL:OL1230613W.author: Albert Camus
OL:OL1230613W.description: Meursault, a detached French Algerian clerk, shows no grief at his mother's funeral and later shoots an Arab man on a sunlit Algiers beach, then faces trial more for his indifference than for the killing. A novel associated with absurdist philosophy and its emotionally flat narration.

OL:OL151411W.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
OL:OL151411W.author: Lewis Carroll
OL:OL151411W.description: A bored girl named Alice follows a waistcoated white rabbit down a hole and wanders an underground world of riddles and changing sizes, meeting the Cheshire Cat, the Mad Hatter, and the Queen of Hearts. A children's book famous for its nonsense logic and wordplay.

OL:OL41225848W.title: A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man
OL:OL41225848W.author: James Joyce
OL:OL41225848W.description: Stephen Dedalus grows up in late nineteenth-century Ireland, moving from a strict Catholic boyhood and Jesuit schooling toward a decision to reject religion and country and devote himself to art. A semi-autobiographical novel whose style matures alongside its protagonist.

K:de8ae851971a.title: The Odyssey
K:de8ae851971a.author: Homer
K:de8ae851971a.description: The Greek hero Odysseus spends ten years struggling home from the Trojan War, surviving the Cyclops, Circe, the Sirens, and the wrath of Poseidon, while his wife Penelope holds off suitors in Ithaca. An ancient Greek epic poem and a foundation of Western literature.

OL:OL16313W.title: Vanity Fair
OL:OL16313W.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
OL:OL16313W.description: Across early nineteenth-century England, the scheming, penniless Becky Sharp climbs through society by any means while her gentle schoolmate Amelia Sedley suffers in love and fortune. A satirical novel subtitled "A Novel without a Hero."

OL:OL2386322W.title: The Leopard
OL:OL2386322W.author: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa
OL:OL2386322W.description: As Garibaldi's troops land in Sicily in 1860, the aristocrat Don Fabrizio, Prince of Salina, watches his class lose power to a rising middle order while his nephew Tancredi marries into new money. A historical novel published after its author's death.

OL:OL27778127W.title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
OL:OL27778127W.author: Zora Neale Hurston
OL:OL27778127W.description: Janie Crawford returns to her Florida town and recounts her life through three marriages, finding independence and love with the younger Tea Cake before tragedy strikes during a hurricane. A novel notable for its use of Black Southern vernacular speech.

OL:OL464512W.title: Wolf Hall
OL:OL464512W.author: Hilary Mantel
OL:OL464512W.description: In Tudor England, the blacksmith's son Thomas Cromwell rises to become Henry VIII's chief minister, engineering the king's break with Rome and divorce from Catherine of Aragon so he can marry Anne Boleyn. It won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL1052133W.title: The God of Small Things
OL:OL1052133W.author: Arundhati Roy
OL:OL1052133W.description: In Kerala, India, the twins Rahel and Estha reunite as adults and recall the childhood day in 1969 when a visiting cousin drowned and their family was torn apart by a forbidden love across caste lines. It won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL62979W.title: The Sun Also Rises
OL:OL62979W.author: Ernest Hemingway
OL:OL62979W.description: A group of American and British expatriates, including the wounded veteran Jake Barnes and Lady Brett Ashley, drift from Paris cafés to the bullfights at the Pamplona fiesta, drinking and chasing one another. A novel associated with the disillusioned postwar "Lost Generation."

OL:OL98459W.title: Slaughterhouse-Five
OL:OL98459W.author: Kurt Vonnegut
OL:OL98459W.description: Billy Pilgrim, an American optometrist and World War II veteran who survived the firebombing of Dresden as a prisoner of war, becomes "unstuck in time" and is abducted by aliens from the planet Tralfamadore. An anti-war novel that mixes autobiography, science fiction, and a fractured chronology to depict the Dresden bombing.

OL:OL12791W.title: My Ántonia
OL:OL12791W.author: Willa Cather
OL:OL12791W.description: Jim Burden recalls his Nebraska boyhood and his friendship with Ántonia Shimerda, the daughter of Bohemian immigrant homesteaders, as the two grow up on the prairie and follow separate paths into adulthood. Known for its portrait of immigrant pioneers and frontier life on the Great Plains.

OL:OL3335245W.title: The Catcher in the Rye
OL:OL3335245W.author: J. D. Salinger
OL:OL3335245W.description: Holden Caulfield, a teenager recently expelled from his prep school, wanders New York City over a few days, avoiding home and meeting old friends, teachers, and strangers while narrating his disgust with "phonies." Told in colloquial first-person voice, it became a defining novel of adolescent alienation.

OL:OL93082W.title: The Divine Comedy
OL:OL93082W.author: Dante Alighieri
OL:OL93082W.description: The poet, guided first by the Roman poet Virgil and later by Beatrice, journeys through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise, meeting damned, penitent, and blessed souls across the three realms of the afterlife. An epic poem in Italian terza rima that became a foundational work of Western literature.

OL:OL103066W.title: The Transit of Venus
OL:OL103066W.author: Shirley Hazzard
OL:OL103066W.description: Two orphaned Australian sisters, Caro and Grace Bell, settle in England in the 1950s, where the astronomer Ted Tice loves Caro while she pursues the unscrupulous playwright Paul Ivory across three decades. Known for its compressed prose, ironic foreshadowing, and its tracing of love and fate.

OL:OL1875010W.title: Housekeeping
OL:OL1875010W.author: Marilynne Robinson
OL:OL1875010W.description: After their mother's suicide, sisters Ruth and Lucille are raised in the Idaho town of Fingerbone by a succession of relatives and finally by their drifting aunt Sylvie, whose unconventional ways pull the girls in opposite directions. Known for its prose and its themes of transience and loss.

OL:OL500451W.title: Disgrace
OL:OL500451W.author: JM Coetzee
OL:OL500451W.description: David Lurie, a Cape Town professor disgraced after an affair with a student, retreats to his daughter Lucy's smallholding, where a brutal attack by three men forces both of them to confront violence and powerlessness in post-apartheid South Africa. Won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL31259W.title: The Golden Notebook
OL:OL31259W.author: Doris Lessing
OL:OL31259W.description: The writer Anna Wulf keeps four colored notebooks recording different parts of her life—politics, her African past, a novel, and her emotional breakdown—which she tries to unify in a fifth, golden notebook. Known for its fragmented structure and its treatment of women's inner lives and 1950s communism.

OL:OL468485W.title: Tender Is the Night
OL:OL468485W.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
OL:OL468485W.description: Dick Diver, a promising American psychiatrist, marries his wealthy patient Nicole, and the couple's glamorous life among expatriates on the French Riviera slowly unravels as his career and marriage decline. Known for its account of expatriate decadence and a deteriorating marriage in the 1920s.

OL:OL676009W.title: The Master and Margarita
OL:OL676009W.author: Mikhail Bulgakov
OL:OL676009W.description: The Devil, calling himself Professor Woland, arrives in atheist Soviet Moscow with a retinue including a talking black cat and wreaks havoc, while a parallel narrative retells Pontius Pilate's judgment of Yeshua and the imprisoned Master writes a novel about it. A satire of Soviet society combining comedy and the supernatural.

OL:OL82929W.title: As I Lay Dying
OL:OL82929W.author: William Faulkner
OL:OL82929W.description: The Bundren family of rural Mississippi hauls the coffin of their mother, Addie, across flooded country to bury her in Jefferson, each member narrating chapters that reveal private motives behind the funeral journey. Told through fifteen narrators in stream-of-consciousness chapters.

OL:OL39316W.title: The Waves
OL:OL39316W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL39316W.description: Six friends—Bernard, Susan, Rhoda, Neville, Jinny, and Louis—speak in alternating interior monologues that follow them from childhood to old age, punctuated by descriptions of the sun crossing the sea over a single day. An experimental novel built almost entirely from soliloquies.

OL:OL41368739W.title: Our Mutual Friend
OL:OL41368739W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL41368739W.description: The presumed-drowned John Harmon returns to London under an assumed name to observe Bella Wilfer, the woman he must marry to claim his father's fortune, while the dust-heap inheritance entangles the Boffins, the Wilfers, and a cast of schemers along the Thames. The author's last completed novel, a satire of money and class.

OL:OL88881W.title: Howards End
OL:OL88881W.author: EM Forster
OL:OL88881W.description: The cultured, half-German Schlegel sisters, Margaret and Helen, become entangled with the wealthy, business-minded Wilcox family and the struggling clerk Leonard Bast, with the country house Howards End at the center of their conflicting claims. Known for its examination of class and connection in Edwardian England.

OL:OL26099415W.title: The Golden Bowl
OL:OL26099415W.author: Henry James
OL:OL26099415W.description: The American widower Adam Verver and his daughter Maggie each marry—she to the impoverished Italian prince Amerigo, he to Maggie's friend Charlotte—not knowing that the prince and Charlotte were once lovers and resume their affair. A late novel known for its dense style and study of marriage and adultery.

OL:OL1858668W.title: Wide Sargasso Sea
OL:OL1858668W.author: Jean Rhys
OL:OL1858668W.description: On a Jamaican estate after emancipation, the Creole heiress Antoinette Cosway endures a troubled marriage to an unnamed Englishman who renames her Bertha and takes her to England. A reimagining of the madwoman in Jane Eyre that explores colonialism, race, and identity in the Caribbean.

OL:OL274518W.title: Love in the Time of Cholera
OL:OL274518W.author: Gabriel García Márquez
OL:OL274518W.description: In a Caribbean port city, Florentino Ariza waits more than fifty years for Fermina Daza, who married the doctor Juvenal Urbino, and renews his courtship after Urbino dies in old age. Known for its treatment of love, aging, and patience over half a century.

K:a63cc765d5fe.title: Stories of John Cheever
K:a63cc765d5fe.author: John Cheever
K:a63cc765d5fe.description: Sixty-one stories follow suburban commuters, fading aristocrats, and adulterers through New York apartments and the Westchester suburbs, including "The Enormous Radio," "The Country Husband," and "The Swimmer." A collected volume that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

K:ef3be8623dfc.title: Stories of Isaac Babel
K:ef3be8623dfc.author: Isaac Babel
K:ef3be8623dfc.description: Stories drawn chiefly from Red Cavalry, which follows a Jewish intellectual riding with Cossack troops during the 1920 Polish-Soviet war, and the Odessa Tales, which depict Jewish gangsters in the Moldavanka district. Known for compressed, vivid prose and scenes of war and Jewish life.

OL:OL67334W.title: The Tin Drum
OL:OL67334W.author: Günter Grass
OL:OL67334W.description: In postwar Danzig, Oskar Matzerath, who willed himself to stop growing at age three and carries a tin drum, narrates his life from a mental institution, recounting his family and the city through the Nazi era. The first novel of the Danzig Trilogy, known for its grotesque comedy and treatment of German guilt.

OL:OL98587W.title: The House of Mirth
OL:OL98587W.author: Edith Wharton
OL:OL98587W.description: Lily Bart, a beautiful but unmarried woman of New York high society, gambles her dwindling resources on finding a rich husband, but missteps and gossip steadily push her down the social ladder. Known for its critique of the marriage market in Gilded Age New York.

OL:OL455305W.title: The Scarlet Letter
OL:OL455305W.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
OL:OL455305W.description: In Puritan Boston, Hester Prynne bears a child out of wedlock and is forced to wear a scarlet "A," refusing to name the father, the minister Arthur Dimmesdale, while her vengeful husband Roger Chillingworth hunts him. Known for its treatment of sin, guilt, and Puritan hypocrisy.

OL:OL273644W.title: The Color Purple
OL:OL273644W.author: Alice Walker
OL:OL273644W.description: In rural early-twentieth-century Georgia, Celie, a poor Black woman abused by her father and husband, writes letters to God and to her sister Nettie, gradually finding strength through the blues singer Shug Avery and other women. An epistolary novel that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL276798W.title: Catch-22
OL:OL276798W.author: Joseph Heller
OL:OL276798W.description: Captain John Yossarian, a World War II bombardier stationed on a Mediterranean island, tries to escape combat duty, but the catch-22 rule means anyone sane enough to want out must keep flying. A satire of war and bureaucracy built from circular logic and dark comedy.

OL:OL103113W.title: A House for Mr Biswas
OL:OL103113W.author: VS Naipaul
OL:OL103113W.description: Mohun Biswas, born into a poor Indo-Trinidadian family, marries into the domineering Tulsi clan and spends his life striving for independence and a house of his own in colonial Trinidad. Known for its tragicomic portrait of a man seeking dignity and a home.

OL:OL74666W.title: American Pastoral
OL:OL74666W.author: Philip Roth
OL:OL74666W.description: Seymour "Swede" Levov, a successful New Jersey businessman and former high-school athlete, sees his comfortable life destroyed when his teenage daughter Merry bombs a post office in protest of the Vietnam War. Won the Pulitzer Prize and traces an American family's collapse across postwar decades.

OL:OL498556W.title: The Metamorphosis
OL:OL498556W.author: Franz Kafka
OL:OL498556W.description: The traveling salesman Gregor Samsa wakes one morning transformed into a giant insect, and as he hides in his room his family shifts from concern to revulsion while he becomes a burden they wish to be rid of. A novella known for its treatment of alienation and dehumanization.

OL:OL2980902W.title: A Fine Balance
OL:OL2980902W.author: Rohinton Mistry
OL:OL2980902W.description: In 1970s India during the Emergency, the widow Dina Dalal takes in two tailors and a student boarder, and the four strangers form a fragile household amid poverty and state repression. Known for its panoramic depiction of caste, poverty, and political turmoil.

OL:OL16520879W.title: My Brilliant Friend
OL:OL16520879W.author: Elena Ferrante
OL:OL16520879W.description: In a poor Naples neighborhood in the 1950s, the narrator Elena Greco recounts her intense, competitive childhood friendship with the brilliant, volatile Lila Cerullo as the two girls grow up and pursue different futures. The first of the four Neapolitan Novels.

OL:OL228702W.title: Giovanni's Room
OL:OL228702W.author: James Baldwin
OL:OL228702W.description: David, a young American living in Paris, leaves his fiancée Hella while she travels and begins an affair with the Italian bartender Giovanni, struggling against his shame over his desire. A novel that treats homosexuality, denial, and self-deception.

OL:OL4112928W.title: The Known World
OL:OL4112928W.author: Edward P. Jones
OL:OL4112928W.description: In antebellum Manchester County, Virginia, Henry Townsend, a freed Black man, becomes himself a slaveholder, and after his death his plantation and its enslaved people fall into disorder. A novel about Black slaveowners in the American South that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL733640W.title: The Red and the Black
OL:OL733640W.author: Stendhal
OL:OL733640W.description: Julien Sorel, an ambitious carpenter's son in Restoration France, rises through the church and aristocratic society as a tutor and secretary while pursuing affairs with Madame de Rênal and Mathilde de la Mole. Known for its psychological portrait of ambition and hypocrisy.

OL:OL501911W.title: Revolutionary Road
OL:OL501911W.author: Richard Yates
OL:OL501911W.description: In 1950s suburban Connecticut, Frank and April Wheeler, who think themselves superior to their conformist neighbors, plan to move to Paris to escape their stifling lives, but the scheme collapses amid disappointment and recrimination. Known for its critique of suburban conformity.

K:d3e96a7e3439.title: The Canterbury Tales
K:d3e96a7e3439.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
K:d3e96a7e3439.description: A group of pilgrims traveling from London to the shrine of Thomas Becket at Canterbury pass the time in a storytelling contest, spinning tales that range from courtly romance to bawdy farce, framed by a General Prologue introducing the Knight, the Miller, the Wife of Bath, the Pardoner, and others. Written in Middle English and left unfinished, it is one of the foundational works of English literature.

OL:OL20600W.title: Gulliver's Travels
OL:OL20600W.author: Jonathan Swift
OL:OL20600W.description: Lemuel Gulliver, a ship's surgeon, is shipwrecked or stranded on four voyages, landing among the tiny Lilliputians, the giant Brobdingnagians, the floating island of Laputa, and the rational horse-like Houyhnhnms who rule over brutish humanlike Yahoos. A prose satire of human nature, politics, and the travel-narrative genre.

OL:OL82931W.title: Light in August
OL:OL82931W.author: William Faulkner
OL:OL82931W.description: In Mississippi, the pregnant Lena Grove walks from Alabama searching for the father of her child, while Joe Christmas, a drifter unsure whether he has Black ancestry, drifts toward violence and the murder of Joanna Burden, and the disgraced ex-minister Gail Hightower lives alone with his memories. A novel exploring race, religion, and isolation in the American South.

OL:OL668682W.title: The Makioka Sisters
OL:OL668682W.author: Junichiro Tanizaki
OL:OL668682W.description: The four Makioka sisters of a declining wealthy Osaka merchant family try repeatedly to arrange a marriage for the shy third sister, Yukiko, while the youngest, Taeko, pursues her own affairs, against the backdrop of the late 1930s and the approach of war. A novel chronicling the slow decline of an upper-middle-class family and its traditions.

OL:OL46611W.title: The Rings of Saturn
OL:OL46611W.author: WG Sebald
OL:OL46611W.description: A narrator on a walking tour through Suffolk in eastern England reflects on the places he passes and digresses into history, biography, and memory, ranging across silkworms, herring fishing, the Taiping Rebellion, Joseph Conrad, and the decay of country estates. A blend of fiction, travel writing, and essay illustrated with grainy photographs.

K:1953ba5c8e84.title: Dead Souls
K:1953ba5c8e84.author: Nikolai Gogol
K:1953ba5c8e84.description: Pavel Ivanovich Chichikov arrives in a provincial Russian town and travels its estates buying up "dead souls," serfs who have died but still appear on the tax rolls, intending to mortgage them for profit while charming the local landowners and officials. A satirical novel about Russian provincial life and corruption, left unfinished.

OL:OL46615W.title: Austerlitz
OL:OL46615W.author: WG Sebald
OL:OL46615W.description: The narrator meets Jacques Austerlitz in a Belgian railway station and, over decades of chance encounters, learns how Austerlitz, raised in Wales under another name, gradually uncovers that he was sent to Britain as a child on the Kindertransport and that his mother died in the Theresienstadt ghetto. A novel about memory, loss, and the Holocaust, illustrated with photographs.

OL:OL44986W.title: Jude the Obscure
OL:OL44986W.author: Thomas Hardy
OL:OL44986W.description: Jude Fawley, a poor stonemason in rural Wessex who dreams of studying at the university town of Christminster, abandons his ambitions after marrying Arabella, then falls into a doomed relationship with his free-thinking cousin Sue Bridehead. A novel that drew controversy for its frank treatment of marriage, religion, and class.

OL:OL14867081W.title: Buddenbrooks
OL:OL14867081W.author: Thomas Mann
OL:OL14867081W.description: Across four generations, the prosperous Buddenbrook family of merchants in a northern German port city slowly declines in wealth, vitality, and confidence, as the sensitive Thomas, the unhappy Tony, and the frail, musical Hanno fail to sustain the family firm. A novel tracing the decay of a bourgeois merchant dynasty over the nineteenth century.

OL:OL66530W.title: Mansfield Park
OL:OL66530W.author: Jane Austen
OL:OL66530W.description: Fanny Price, a poor girl sent as a child to live with her wealthy relatives at Mansfield Park, grows up overlooked and timid but quietly principled, watching as the charming, worldly Henry and Mary Crawford disrupt the household and as she loves her cousin Edmund from a distance. A novel about morality, social position, and family.

OL:OL757983W.title: Independent People
OL:OL757983W.author: Halldór Laxness
OL:OL757983W.description: Bjartur of Summerhouses, a stubborn Icelandic sheep farmer, finally buys his own croft after eighteen years of servitude and insists on total independence, refusing all help even as poverty, harsh weather, and family tragedy grind down his wife and children. A novel about the hardship of rural Icelandic life and the cost of self-reliance.

K:4d4b9f43727e.title: All the King's Men
K:4d4b9f43727e.author: Robert Penn Warren
K:4d4b9f43727e.description: Jack Burden, a journalist turned political aide, narrates the rise and fall of Willie Stark, a populist Southern governor who begins as an idealistic reformer but grows ruthless and corrupt, until a personal scandal leads to his assassination. A novel about political power and moral responsibility, loosely inspired by Louisiana governor Huey Long.

K:655dc7057956.title: Stories of Franz Kafka
K:655dc7057956.author: Franz Kafka
K:655dc7057956.description: A collection gathering all of the author's short fiction outside his novels, including "The Metamorphosis," in which Gregor Samsa wakes transformed into an insect, "In the Penal Colony," "A Hunger Artist," "The Judgment," and many shorter pieces and fragments. The stories are known for their nightmarish logic, bureaucratic menace, and themes of guilt and alienation.

OL:OL81293W.title: The Rainbow
OL:OL81293W.author: DH Lawrence
OL:OL81293W.description: Across three generations of the Brangwen family on a Nottinghamshire farm, Tom marries a Polish widow, their daughter Anna marries his nephew Will, and their daughter Ursula grows into a young woman searching for independence and meaning through education, work, and a relationship with the soldier Anton Skrebensky. A novel about marriage, sexuality, and changing English life.

K:86720a12eae7.title: Stories of Eudora Welty
K:86720a12eae7.author: Eudora Welty
K:86720a12eae7.description: A collection bringing together the author's short stories set largely in the American South, including "Why I Live at the P.O.," in which a postmistress narrates her feud with her returning sister, "A Worn Path," "Petrified Man," and "A Curtain of Green." The stories are known for their comic dialogue, eccentric characters, and Mississippi settings.

OL:OL43041145W.title: A Passage to India
OL:OL43041145W.author: E. M. Forster
OL:OL43041145W.description: Adela Quested and Mrs. Moore travel to colonial India, where the Muslim doctor Aziz befriends them and arranges an excursion to the Marabar Caves, after which Adela accuses him of assault, igniting a trial that inflames tensions between the British rulers and the Indians. A novel about colonialism, friendship, and the divide between cultures.

K:addeb3f5ad0c.title: Macbeth
K:addeb3f5ad0c.author: William Shakespeare
K:addeb3f5ad0c.description: Returning from battle in Scotland, the general Macbeth meets three witches who prophesy he will become king, and, spurred on by his wife, he murders King Duncan and seizes the throne, then descends into tyranny and paranoia as he kills to keep his crown. A tragedy about ambition, guilt, and the corrupting pull of power.

K:7d6f4598f836.title: Paradise Lost
K:7d6f4598f836.author: John Milton
K:7d6f4598f836.description: After rebelling against God and being cast out of Heaven, Satan rouses his fallen angels in Hell and journeys to the newly created Earth, where he tempts Adam and Eve into eating the forbidden fruit, bringing about humanity's fall and expulsion from the Garden of Eden. An epic poem in blank verse retelling the biblical fall of man.

OL:OL2074162W.title: A Dance to the Music of Time
OL:OL2074162W.author: Anthony Powell
OL:OL2074162W.description: Narrated by Nicholas Jenkins, a twelve-novel sequence follows a wide circle of English friends and acquaintances, including the ambitious Kenneth Widmerpool, from their schooldays before the First World War through the social and political upheavals of the mid-twentieth century. A roman-fleuve surveying English upper-class and artistic life over fifty years.

OL:OL466942W.title: The Radetzky March
OL:OL466942W.author: Joseph Roth
OL:OL466942W.description: Across three generations, the Trotta family rises from peasant origins after a soldier saves the emperor's life at the Battle of Solferino, and his descendants serve as officials and officers while the multiethnic Austro-Hungarian Empire drifts toward collapse in the First World War. A novel about duty, decline, and the end of the Habsburg monarchy.

OL:OL27217159W.title: Robinson Crusoe
OL:OL27217159W.author: Daniel Defoe
OL:OL27217159W.description: Shipwrecked and stranded alone on a deserted Caribbean island, the English sailor Robinson Crusoe survives for twenty-eight years by salvaging supplies, building shelter, farming, and keeping a journal, eventually rescuing a captive he names Friday. An early English novel framed as a castaway's first-person account of survival and self-reliance.

K:450eb07e587b.title: The Bible
K:450eb07e587b.description: A compilation of sacred texts, the Hebrew Bible recounts the creation of the world, the covenant with the patriarchs, the Exodus from Egypt, and the laws, history, and prophecy of Israel, while the Christian New Testament narrates the life, teaching, death, and resurrection of Jesus and the early church. The central scripture of Judaism and Christianity, written by many authors over centuries.

OL:OL1993508W.title: The Line of Beauty
OL:OL1993508W.author: Alan Hollinghurst
OL:OL1993508W.description: In 1980s London, Nick Guest, a young gay graduate from a modest background, lodges with the wealthy family of Conservative MP Gerald Fedden, immersing himself in their world of money and politics during the Thatcher years and pursuing relationships as the AIDS epidemic spreads. A novel about class, sexuality, and 1980s Britain.

OL:OL509919W.title: Parade's End
OL:OL509919W.author: Ford Madox Ford
OL:OL509919W.description: Christopher Tietjens, a brilliant and old-fashioned English government statistician, endures a tormenting marriage to the unfaithful Sylvia while falling in love with the young suffragette Valentine Wannop, then serves in the trenches of the First World War as the old social order collapses around him. A tetralogy about England before and during the Great War.

OL:OL15400582W.title: The Big Sleep
OL:OL15400582W.author: Raymond Chandler
OL:OL15400582W.description: Private detective Philip Marlowe is hired by the wealthy, dying General Sternwood to deal with a blackmailer, and his investigation in Los Angeles draws him into a tangle of pornography, gambling, missing persons, and murder involving the general's two wild daughters. A hardboiled detective novel known for its convoluted plot and wisecracking narrator.

OL:OL27448W.title: The Lord of the Rings
OL:OL27448W.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
OL:OL27448W.description: The hobbit Frodo Baggins inherits a magic ring that turns out to be the source of the Dark Lord Sauron's power, and he sets out from the Shire with a fellowship of companions on a quest to destroy it in the fires of Mount Doom, where it was forged. An epic fantasy novel of the war for Middle-earth, published in three volumes.

OL:OL59434W.title: The Talented Mr Ripley
OL:OL59434W.author: Patricia Highsmith
OL:OL59434W.description: Tom Ripley, a young con man, is sent to Italy by a wealthy shipbuilder to persuade his idle son Dickie Greenleaf to return home, but Ripley grows obsessed with Dickie's life, murders him, and assumes his identity, evading suspicion through manipulation and further killing. A crime novel narrated from the murderer's point of view.

OL:OL20933W.title: Daniel Deronda
OL:OL20933W.author: George Eliot
OL:OL20933W.description: In Victorian England, the beautiful, willful Gwendolen Harleth makes a loveless marriage to the cruel Henleigh Grandcourt and turns for moral guidance to Daniel Deronda, a thoughtful young man who, uncertain of his own origins, discovers his Jewish heritage and embraces a proto-Zionist mission. A novel interweaving English society with Jewish identity and ideals.

OL:OL118986W.title: Germinal
OL:OL118986W.author: Émile Zola
OL:OL118986W.description: Étienne Lantel, a young migrant worker, takes a job in a coal mine in northern France and, appalled by the miners' brutal poverty, helps organize a strike that ends in violence, starvation, and disaster for the workers and their families. A novel depicting the harsh lives of coal miners and the conflict between labor and capital.

OL:OL106084W.title: The Power and the Glory
OL:OL106084W.author: Graham Greene
OL:OL106084W.description: During an anticlerical purge in a Mexican state where Catholicism has been outlawed, an unnamed "whisky priest," weak, alcoholic, and the father of a child, flees from a relentless police lieutenant while continuing to perform his priestly duties for the peasants who shelter him. A novel about faith, sin, and martyrdom under persecution.

OL:OL228705W.title: Go Tell It on the Mountain
OL:OL228705W.author: James Baldwin
OL:OL228705W.description: On his fourteenth birthday in 1930s Harlem, John Grimes wrestles with his faith, his hatred of his stern, hypocritical stepfather Gabriel, and his own emerging identity, as a single day at the storefront Pentecostal church unfolds alongside the histories of his family. A semi-autobiographical novel about religion, family, and growing up Black in America.

OL:OL44927W.title: Tess of the D'urbervilles
OL:OL44927W.author: Thomas Hardy
OL:OL44927W.description: Tess Durbeyfield, a poor country girl sent to claim kinship with the wealthy d'Urbervilles, is seduced and made pregnant by Alec d'Urberville, then later marries the idealistic Angel Clare, who abandons her when she confesses her past, setting her on a path toward tragedy. A novel about sexual double standards, class, and injustice in rural England.

OL:OL15297W.title: Invisible Cities
OL:OL15297W.author: Italo Calvino
OL:OL15297W.description: In a frame narrative, the aging emperor Kublai Khan listens as the traveler Marco Polo describes the many fantastical cities he has visited throughout the empire, each city, named for a woman, embodying an idea about memory, desire, signs, or death. A novel made of short prose poems about imaginary cities and the nature of cities themselves.

OL:OL500388W.title: Waiting for the Barbarians
OL:OL500388W.author: J. M. Coetzee
OL:OL500388W.description: A magistrate running a frontier settlement for an unnamed Empire begins to question its policies after a Colonel arrives to torture nomadic prisoners labeled barbarians, and he is himself imprisoned when he tries to return a tortured native woman to her people. An allegorical novel about colonialism, imperial brutality, and complicity.

OL:OL50565W.title: The Bluest Eye
OL:OL50565W.author: Toni Morrison
OL:OL50565W.description: In 1940s Lorain, Ohio, Pecola Breedlove, a young Black girl treated as ugly by those around her, prays for blue eyes and is raped and impregnated by her father, while the MacTeer sisters narrate her unraveling. A first novel that examines racism, beauty standards, and the destruction of a child.

OL:OL276386W.title: The Turn of the Screw
OL:OL276386W.author: Henry James
OL:OL276386W.description: A governess takes charge of two orphaned children, Miles and Flora, at the remote country estate of Bly and becomes convinced that the ghosts of a former valet and governess, Peter Quint and Miss Jessel, are corrupting them. A ghost story whose ambiguity leaves the apparitions open to psychological interpretation.

OL:OL63072W.title: A Farewell to Arms
OL:OL63072W.author: Ernest Hemingway
OL:OL63072W.description: Frederic Henry, an American ambulance driver serving with the Italian army during World War I, falls in love with the British nurse Catherine Barkley, is wounded, and deserts after the chaotic retreat from Caporetto to flee with her to Switzerland. A war novel drawn partly from its author's own experience as an ambulance driver.

OL:OL59038W.title: Never Let Me Go
OL:OL59038W.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
OL:OL59038W.description: Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy grow up at Hailsham, an English boarding school, and gradually learn that they are clones raised to donate their vital organs, with Kathy narrating their lives as she works as a carer. A dystopian novel about love, mortality, and a society built on engineered humans.

OL:OL39360W.title: Orlando
OL:OL39360W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL39360W.description: Orlando, a young Elizabethan nobleman, lives for centuries without aging and, midway through, wakes one morning transformed into a woman, moving through English history and shifting social roles across the eras. A novel partly inspired by the family history of Vita Sackville-West that plays with gender and biography.

OL:OL5731542W.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
OL:OL5731542W.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
OL:OL5731542W.description: In Nigeria before and during the Biafran war of the late 1960s, the twin sisters Olanna and Kainene, the houseboy Ugwu, and the Englishman Richard live through the country's collapse into civil war, starvation, and violence. A novel that depicts the Nigerian-Biafran conflict through intertwined personal lives.

OL:OL481143W.title: White Teeth
OL:OL481143W.author: Zadie Smith
OL:OL481143W.description: In multicultural London, the friendship between the Englishman Archie Jones and the Bangladeshi Samad Iqbal spans decades as their families, including Samad's twin sons and Archie's daughter Irie, navigate immigration, religion, and identity. A debut novel about race, generations, and life in contemporary England.

OL:OL24156W.title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
OL:OL24156W.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
OL:OL24156W.description: The London lawyer Gabriel Utterson investigates the connection between his respectable friend Dr. Henry Jekyll and the violent, repugnant Edward Hyde, eventually learning that a potion lets Jekyll transform into Hyde to indulge his darker impulses. A novella that gave a lasting metaphor for the divided self.

OL:OL2005223W.title: The Third Policeman
OL:OL2005223W.author: Flann O'Brien
OL:OL2005223W.description: An unnamed narrator who has murdered an old man for his money arrives at a strange police barracks pursuing a hidden cash box, where he meets policemen obsessed with bicycles and absurd theories, and slowly grasps that he is dead and trapped in a cyclical hell. A comic novel of surreal logic published posthumously.

OL:OL2466637W.title: Lanark
OL:OL2466637W.author: Alasdair Gray
OL:OL2466637W.description: The story alternates between Duncan Thaw, an artist struggling in mid-twentieth-century Glasgow, and Lanark, a man who arrives without memory in the sunless dystopian city of Unthank, where people contract literal diseases like dragonhide. A genre-blending novel that mixes realism and fantasy across four nonlinear books.

OL:OL23166W.title: East of Eden
OL:OL23166W.author: John Steinbeck
OL:OL23166W.description: In California's Salinas Valley, the intertwined Trask and Hamilton families live out conflicts echoing the story of Cain and Abel across generations, as Adam Trask raises his sons Caleb and Aron after his wife Cathy abandons them. A long family saga about good, evil, and free will.

K:da7daa0a88e4.title: Ask the Dust
K:da7daa0a88e4.author: John Fante
K:da7daa0a88e4.description: Arturo Bandini, a struggling young writer of Italian descent living in a Depression-era Los Angeles boarding house, pursues literary success and a turbulent romance with the Mexican waitress Camilla Lopez. A novel about poverty, ambition, and desire in 1930s California.

K:fa6d27467a77.title: The Long Goodbye
K:fa6d27467a77.author: Raymond Chandler
K:fa6d27467a77.description: The Los Angeles private detective Philip Marlowe befriends the troubled drunk Terry Lennox, helps him flee to Mexico after Lennox's wealthy wife is found murdered, and is drawn into a tangle of suicide, blackmail, and corruption when he refuses to drop the case. A detective novel often regarded as the most personal in its series.

K:ee34a6c50dbf.title: The Iliad
K:ee34a6c50dbf.author: Homer
K:ee34a6c50dbf.description: In the final year of the Trojan War, the Greek warrior Achilles withdraws from battle after a quarrel with Agamemnon over a captive woman, and the Greeks suffer until the death of his friend Patroclus drives him back to kill the Trojan prince Hector. An ancient Greek epic poem about rage, honor, and war.

OL:OL7180368W.title: The Decameron of Boccaccio
OL:OL7180368W.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
OL:OL7180368W.description: Ten young Florentines, seven women and three men, flee plague-stricken Florence to a country villa and pass ten days telling one hundred tales of love, wit, fortune, and trickery. A frame-story collection that became a landmark of Italian prose.

K:906ffc5082cd.title: Stories of Alice Munro
K:906ffc5082cd.author: Alice Munro
K:906ffc5082cd.description: Selected short stories drawn from a Canadian writer's earlier collections follow the lives of girls and women in small-town Ontario as they navigate marriage, family, ambition, and shame across decades. Short fiction known for psychological detail and ordinary domestic settings.

K:2ecba695b7ae.title: Stories of Ernest Hemingway
K:2ecba695b7ae.author: Ernest Hemingway
K:2ecba695b7ae.description: Short stories set across war-torn Europe, the American Midwest, Africa, and Spain follow soldiers, hunters, expatriates, and ordinary people facing violence, loss, and disillusionment, including pieces about the recurring figure Nick Adams. Short fiction marked by spare, understated prose.

K:a7d082925dfc.title: Stories of Raymond Carver
K:a7d082925dfc.author: Raymond Carver
K:a7d082925dfc.description: Short stories set among working-class people in the American Pacific Northwest follow waitresses, salesmen, and alcoholics through marriages, layoffs, and small crises rendered in plain language. Minimalist short fiction associated with the "dirty realism" of late-twentieth-century America.

K:751bbe356d28.title: Nine Stories
K:751bbe356d28.author: J. D. Salinger
K:751bbe356d28.description: Nine short stories follow troubled and perceptive characters, several connected to the Glass family, including a soldier who shoots himself after meeting a child on a Florida beach in "A Perfect Day for Bananafish." A collection that gathers some of its author's best-known short fiction.

OL:OL15859552W.title: Herzog
OL:OL15859552W.author: Saul Bellow
OL:OL15859552W.description: Moses Herzog, a middle-aged Jewish intellectual reeling from a second divorce, writes unsent letters to friends, family, philosophers, and the dead as he tries to make sense of his collapsing life. A novel built around its protagonist's restless, comic interior monologue.

K:ef6aa2e15e06.title: The Tempest
K:ef6aa2e15e06.author: William Shakespeare
K:ef6aa2e15e06.description: The exiled sorcerer Prospero, former Duke of Milan, conjures a storm to wreck his usurping brother's ship on the island where he lives with his daughter Miranda and the spirit Ariel and the creature Caliban, then engineers reconciliation and his daughter's marriage. A late play built around magic, forgiveness, and renunciation.

K:6d7a4faa0e0d.title: Winesburg, Ohio
K:6d7a4faa0e0d.author: Sherwood Anderson
K:6d7a4faa0e0d.description: In the small town of Winesburg, Ohio, the young reporter George Willard moves among lonely, frustrated townspeople whose private lives are revealed in linked stories before he leaves for the city. A collection of interrelated tales depicting small-town isolation.

OL:OL479009W.title: Love Medicine
OL:OL479009W.author: Louise Erdrich
OL:OL479009W.description: Across several decades on and around a North Dakota Ojibwe reservation, the interconnected Kashpaw and Lamartine families live through love affairs, marriages, and deaths narrated by many voices, beginning with the drowning of June Kashpaw. A linked-story novel about Native American families.

K:969b47058d9c.title: Ficciones
K:969b47058d9c.author: Jorge Luis Borges
K:969b47058d9c.description: Seventeen short stories present invented books and labyrinths, including a library containing every possible book, a man who rewrites Don Quixote word for word, and a fictional encyclopedia entry that begins reshaping reality. A collection that established its author's reputation for philosophical, fantastical fiction.

K:2484db8decc1.title: Jesus' Son
K:2484db8decc1.author: Denis Johnson
K:2484db8decc1.description: Linked short stories follow a drifting, drug-addicted narrator nicknamed Fuckhead through the American Midwest as he passes through car wrecks, hospitals, bars, and odd jobs in the 1970s. A spare collection of interconnected stories about addiction and grace.

OL:OL505583W.title: Nightwood
OL:OL505583W.author: Djuna Barnes
OL:OL505583W.description: In 1920s Paris and Vienna, the lives of several expatriates tangle around the elusive Robin Vote, whose relationships with Felix Volkbein, Nora Flood, and Jenny Petherbridge are dissected in the monologues of the talkative Doctor Matthew O'Connor. A modernist novel notable for its dense prose and its lesbian themes.

OL:OL8193416W.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
OL:OL8193416W.author: Oscar Wilde
OL:OL8193416W.description: In London, the beautiful young Dorian Gray wishes that a portrait of himself would age in his place, then plunges into a life of corruption and cruelty while his face stays youthful and the hidden picture grows monstrous. A novel about vanity, hedonism, and moral decay.

OL:OL842158W.title: The Deptford Trilogy
OL:OL842158W.author: Robertson Davies
OL:OL842158W.description: Across three linked novels, a single childhood snowball thrown in a Canadian town ripples through the lives of the schoolteacher Dunstan Ramsay, the tycoon Boy Staunton, and the magician Magnus Eisengrim. A trilogy that weaves myth, magic, and Jungian ideas through intertwined Canadian lives.

K:c70aa81a21ba.title: The Aeneid
K:c70aa81a21ba.author: Virgil
K:c70aa81a21ba.description: After Troy falls, the Trojan hero Aeneas leads survivors across the Mediterranean, pauses for a doomed love affair with Queen Dido of Carthage, descends to the underworld, and wages war in Italy to found the people who will become the Romans. A Latin epic poem written to celebrate Rome's mythic origins.

K:312f2e675a9c.title: Tom Jones
K:312f2e675a9c.author: Henry Fielding
K:312f2e675a9c.description: The good-natured foundling Tom Jones, raised by the wealthy Squire Allworthy, is cast out after misadventures and a forbidden love for Sophia Western, then journeys across England toward London amid mistaken identities before his true parentage is revealed. A long, comic novel ranging across eighteenth-century English society.

OL:OL1503886W.title: So Long, See You Tomorrow
OL:OL1503886W.author: William Maxwell
OL:OL1503886W.description: An aging Midwestern man recalls his boyhood friendship with Cletus Smith and the murder on a nearby tenant farm, when Cletus's father killed a neighbor over an affair and then himself, reconstructing the events he failed to understand at the time. A short novel about memory, guilt, and a remembered crime.

K:bbf3fa01dd65.title: Leaves of Grass
K:bbf3fa01dd65.author: Walt Whitman
K:bbf3fa01dd65.description: A collection of free-verse poems, opening with the long "Song of Myself," celebrates the body, the self, democracy, nature, and the American people in a sprawling, cataloging voice. A poetry collection its author revised and expanded across many editions throughout his life.

K:77a9e9d519f7.title: The Oresteia
K:77a9e9d519f7.author: Aeschylus
K:77a9e9d519f7.description: Across three linked tragedies, Agamemnon returns victorious from Troy and is murdered by his wife Clytemnestra, his son Orestes avenges him by killing her, and Orestes is then pursued by the Furies and tried before Athena in Athens. The only complete surviving trilogy of ancient Greek drama, ending with blood vengeance replaced by trial and the rule of law.

OL:OL119436W.title: The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier and Clay
OL:OL119436W.author: Michael Chabon
OL:OL119436W.description: Sammy Clay and his refugee cousin Josef Kavalier, an artist who has fled Nazi-occupied Prague, create a hit costumed superhero called the Escapist in the comic-book boom of late-1930s and 1940s New York. A novel that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and ranges over the golden age of comics, World War II, and Jewish American life.

OL:OL20769W.title: The Beginning of Spring
OL:OL20769W.author: Penelope Fitzgerald
OL:OL20769W.description: In Moscow in 1913, the English printer Frank Reid is left to manage his business and three children after his wife Nellie abruptly returns to England, and he hires a young Russian woman, Lisa, to look after them. A short novel set among the British expatriate community on the eve of the Russian Revolution, shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL893802W.title: Sentimental Education
OL:OL893802W.author: Gustave Flaubert
OL:OL893802W.description: Frédéric Moreau, a young provincial in 1840s France, comes to Paris to study law and falls into a lifelong infatuation with the married Madame Arnoux while drifting through love affairs, friendships, and the political upheavals of the 1848 Revolution. A novel tracing one man's wasted ambitions against the failures of his generation.

OL:OL16847W.title: Money
OL:OL16847W.author: Martin Amis
OL:OL16847W.description: John Self, a hard-drinking, hedonistic London advertising director, shuttles between London and New York to make his first film while a producer named Fielding Goodney bankrolls his spending and manipulates him toward ruin. A satirical novel narrated by Self about greed and excess in the 1980s.

OL:OL66562W.title: Sense and Sensibility
OL:OL66562W.author: Jane Austen
OL:OL66562W.description: After their father's death leaves them with little money, the Dashwood sisters Elinor and Marianne move to a cottage in Devonshire and navigate courtships with Edward Ferrars, Colonel Brandon, and the charming Willoughby. Known for contrasting Elinor's restraint with Marianne's emotional impulsiveness in matters of love and marriage.

K:d4f54d0b665c.title: Labyrinths
K:d4f54d0b665c.author: Jorge Luis Borges
K:d4f54d0b665c.description: Twenty-three short stories alongside ten essays and eight short parables, including "Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius," "The Garden of Forking Paths," and "The Library of Babel," drawn from earlier Spanish-language collections. The English-language anthology that introduced many readers to the author's work, recurring through images of mirrors, infinity, mazes, and imaginary books.

OL:OL276470W.title: The Ambassadors
OL:OL276470W.author: Henry James
OL:OL276470W.description: Lambert Strether, a middle-aged American, is sent from Massachusetts to Paris by his wealthy fiancée to retrieve her son Chad Newsome, but he finds the young man improved by European life and begins to question his own mission. A late novel centered on Strether's awakening to experience he feels he has missed.

K:936c038de83f.title: The Things They Carried
K:936c038de83f.author: Tim O'Brien
K:936c038de83f.description: Linked stories follow the soldiers of an American infantry platoon, including Lieutenant Jimmy Cross and a narrator named Tim O'Brien, as they carry physical loads and private burdens through the Vietnam War and afterward. A work of fiction that blurs memory and invention while examining how war stories are told.

OL:OL1150725W.title: Clarissa Harlowe
OL:OL1150725W.author: Samuel Richardson
OL:OL1150725W.description: Clarissa Harlowe, a virtuous young Englishwoman pressured by her family into an odious marriage, flees with the rake Robert Lovelace, who imprisons, manipulates, and ultimately rapes her. An epistolary novel told through letters and one of the longest in the English language.

OL:OL724067W.title: The Death of the Heart
OL:OL724067W.author: Elizabeth Bowen
OL:OL724067W.description: Sixteen-year-old orphan Portia Quayne comes to live with her half-brother Thomas and his cool wife Anna in London, keeps a diary, and falls for Anna's careless friend Eddie before discovering that Anna has been reading her private writing. A novel about a naive girl's collision with adult deception between the world wars.

OL:OL1921185W.title: Underworld
OL:OL1921185W.author: Don DeLillo
OL:OL1921185W.description: Beginning with a 1951 baseball game at the Polo Grounds, the narrative traces the journey of the home-run ball and the entangled lives of figures like waste manager Nick Shay across the second half of the American twentieth century. A long novel that uses the Cold War, nuclear anxiety, and consumer culture as its backdrop.

OL:OL2636675W.title: Gravity's Rainbow
OL:OL2636675W.author: Thomas Pynchon
OL:OL2636675W.description: In the final months of World War II, American lieutenant Tyrone Slothrop is pursued across a ruined Europe because his sexual encounters seem to predict where German V-2 rockets will strike. A long, sprawling novel filled with hundreds of characters, technical digressions, paranoia, and dark comedy.

OL:OL1865528W.title: The Bell Jar
OL:OL1865528W.author: Sylvia Plath
OL:OL1865528W.description: Esther Greenwood, a talented college student, wins a magazine internship in New York City, then returns home to Massachusetts and sinks into mental illness, a suicide attempt, and psychiatric treatment. A semi-autobiographical novel about a young woman's breakdown and the pressures placed on women in 1950s America.

OL:OL2564006W.title: The Tale of Genji
OL:OL2564006W.author: Murasaki Shikibu
OL:OL2564006W.description: At the Heian court, the emperor's son Genji, known as the Shining Prince, moves through a long series of love affairs, marriages, and political shifts before the story continues into the next generation after his death. An early Japanese work often called the world's first novel.

OL:OL5721394W.title: Brideshead Revisited
OL:OL5721394W.author: Evelyn Waugh
OL:OL5721394W.description: Stationed at a country house during the war, army officer Charles Ryder recalls his Oxford friendship with the charming, doomed Sebastian Flyte and his entanglement with the aristocratic, Catholic Marchmain family at their estate Brideshead. A novel about memory, faith, and the decline of the English aristocracy.

OL:OL39329W.title: Jacob's Room
OL:OL39329W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL39329W.description: The life of Jacob Flanders is glimpsed indirectly through the impressions of others, from his Cambridge years and travels in Greece to his death in the First World War, his presence largely conveyed by absence. An early experimental novel built from fragmentary perceptions rather than continuous narration.

OL:OL17661158W.title: Nervous Conditions
OL:OL17661158W.author: Tsitsi Dangarembga
OL:OL17661158W.description: In 1960s Rhodesia, Shona girl Tambu takes her dead brother's place at her uncle Babamukuru's mission school, where she grows close to her Westernized cousin Nyasha while confronting poverty, colonialism, and the limits placed on women. A coming-of-age novel and the first published in English by a Black Zimbabwean woman.

OL:OL59800W.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
OL:OL59800W.author: Ursula K Le Guin
OL:OL59800W.description: The envoy Genly Ai arrives on the icy planet Gethen, whose inhabitants are ambisexual and assume gender only periodically, and forms a fraught alliance with the exiled politician Estraven amid the rival nations of Karhide and Orgoreyn. A science fiction novel exploring gender, politics, and trust.

OL:OL106073W.title: The End of the Affair
OL:OL106073W.author: Graham Greene
OL:OL106073W.description: In postwar London, novelist Maurice Bendrix hires a detective to investigate Sarah Miles, the married woman whose passionate wartime affair with him ended abruptly, and learns she left him because of a vow she made to God. A novel about love, jealousy, and religious faith told through Bendrix's bitter narration.

OL:OL35616W.title: Kindred
OL:OL35616W.author: Octavia E Butler
OL:OL35616W.description: On her twenty-sixth birthday in 1976 Los Angeles, the Black writer Dana is repeatedly pulled back in time to an antebellum Maryland plantation, where she must keep a white slaveholding boy named Rufus alive because he is her ancestor. A novel combining time travel with the slave narrative.

OL:OL19690272W.title: Rebecca
OL:OL19690272W.author: Daphne du Maurier
OL:OL19690272W.description: A shy young woman marries the wealthy widower Maxim de Winter and arrives at his Cornish estate Manderley, where the housekeeper Mrs. Danvers keeps alive the memory of his glamorous first wife, Rebecca. A Gothic novel narrated by the unnamed second wife as she uncovers the truth about Rebecca's death.

OL:OL85892W.title: Dracula
OL:OL85892W.author: Bram Stoker
OL:OL85892W.description: Solicitor Jonathan Harker travels to Transylvania to assist Count Dracula's move to England, and a group including Professor Van Helsing, Mina, and Lucy come to realize the count is a vampire spreading his curse in London. An epistolary horror novel told through journals, letters, and newspaper clippings.

OL:OL1330246W.title: The Man Without Qualities
OL:OL1330246W.author: Robert Musil
OL:OL1330246W.description: In Vienna on the eve of the First World War, the detached mathematician Ulrich is drawn into the "Parallel Campaign," a committee planning a patriotic celebration of the Austro-Hungarian emperor's jubilee, while he reflects on love, science, and morality. An unfinished modernist novel of ideas left incomplete at its author's death.

OL:OL55239W.title: Ragtime
OL:OL55239W.author: EL Doctorow
OL:OL55239W.description: In early-twentieth-century New York, the intertwined stories of an upper-class family, an immigrant Jewish father and daughter, and the Black musician Coalhouse Walker unfold alongside real figures such as Houdini, J. P. Morgan, and Emma Goldman. A novel mixing historical personages with invented characters in the ragtime era.

OL:OL17334243W.title: The Vegetarian
OL:OL17334243W.author: Han Kang
OL:OL17334243W.description: After a violent nightmare, the Seoul homemaker Yeong-hye suddenly refuses to eat meat, a decision that escalates through her husband's anger, her brother-in-law's obsession, and her sister's despair across three connected sections. A Korean novel, winner of the International Booker Prize, narrated by those around its silent central figure.

OL:OL11081469W.title: The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter
OL:OL11081469W.author: Carson McCullers
OL:OL11081469W.description: In a Georgia mill town during the Depression, the deaf-mute John Singer becomes a confidant for a restless girl named Mick Kelly, a Black doctor, a café owner, and a radical drifter, who each pour their longings out to him. A novel about loneliness and the failure of people to truly connect.

K:6c48d4f8f588.title: Romeo and Juliet
K:6c48d4f8f588.author: William Shakespeare
K:6c48d4f8f588.description: In Verona, the teenage children of the feuding Montague and Capulet families, Romeo and Juliet, fall in love and secretly marry, but a chain of misunderstandings and deaths leads the pair to take their own lives. A tragedy whose final loss reconciles the two warring families.

K:1369db891f94.title: Mrs. Bridge
K:1369db891f94.author: Evan S. Connell
K:1369db891f94.description: In 117 brief episodes, India Bridge raises three children and keeps house in an affluent Kansas City family between the world wars while her lawyer husband Walter works long hours and she struggles with her own emptiness. A novel portraying the conformity and limits of an upper-middle-class woman's life.

K:ca7944d7d49e.title: Mr. Bridge
K:ca7944d7d49e.author: Evan S. Connell
K:ca7944d7d49e.description: Told in short vignettes, the Kansas City lawyer Walter Bridge devotes himself to work, money, and propriety while remaining emotionally remote from his wife India and their three children between the world wars. A companion novel that retells the same household from the husband's perspective.

K:81ff245a8bfa.title: Death Comes for the Archbishop
K:81ff245a8bfa.author: Willa Cather
K:81ff245a8bfa.description: Sent to the newly American territory of New Mexico in 1851, the French Catholic bishop Jean Marie Latour and his vicar Joseph Vaillant travel the desert for decades to rebuild the church, contending with rebellious priests, the landscape, and local custom. A novel based on the life of Archbishop Jean-Baptiste Lamy.

OL:OL697429W.title: Nights at the Circus
OL:OL697429W.author: Angela Carter
OL:OL697429W.description: Aerialiste Sophie Fevvers, a London circus performer who claims to have hatched from an egg and grown real wings, is interviewed by skeptical American journalist Jack Walser, who then joins the circus as it tours from St. Petersburg into Siberia. A picaresque novel mixing the fantastical with turn-of-the-century settings.

OL:OL43161739W.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
OL:OL43161739W.author: Alexandre Dumas
OL:OL43161739W.description: Falsely accused and imprisoned in the Château d'If, the young sailor Edmond Dantès escapes after years in captivity, discovers a hidden fortune, and returns disguised as the Count of Monte Cristo to reward his friends and destroy the men who betrayed him. An adventure novel of imprisonment, escape, and elaborate revenge.

K:338581d02713.title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
K:338581d02713.author: Haruki Murakami
K:338581d02713.description: In a Tokyo suburb, the unemployed househusband Toru Okada searches for his wife Kumiko's missing cat and then for Kumiko herself, descending into a dry well and a surreal underworld beneath ordinary life. A long novel mixing the mundane and the supernatural, with strands reaching back to Japan's wartime history in Manchuria.

OL:OL5721561W.title: Vile Bodies
OL:OL5721561W.author: Evelyn Waugh
