OL:OL5721561W.description: Adam Fenwick-Symes loses his only manuscript to customs officers, repeatedly cannot afford to marry Nina Blount, and drifts through the parties, gossip columns, and stunts of London's Bright Young Things. A satire of fashionable interwar society that ends with its characters facing another world war.

K:daa94665cde4.title: Metamorphoses
K:daa94665cde4.author: Ovid
K:daa94665cde4.description: In fifteen books of Latin verse, the poem recounts the history of the world from creation to the deification of Julius Caesar through more than 250 myths in which gods and mortals are transformed into animals, plants, stars, and stones. A foundational source of classical mythology that shaped later Western literature and art.

K:93dc6897f134.title: Ship of Fools
K:93dc6897f134.author: Katherine Anne Porter
K:93dc6897f134.description: Aboard the German passenger ship Vera sailing from Veracruz, Mexico, to Bremerhaven in 1931, a large international cast of passengers reveals its prejudices and cruelties over the long voyage. An allegorical novel that traces the social tensions and rising bigotry of the period between the world wars.

OL:OL103095W.title: The Enigma of Arrival
OL:OL103095W.author: V. S. Naipaul
OL:OL103095W.description: An Indian-Trinidadian writer rents a cottage on a decaying country estate near Salisbury in Wiltshire and, over five sections, watches the people and landscape around him change while reflecting on his own life and arrival in England. A largely autobiographical novel about displacement, memory, and gradual belonging.

OL:OL134601W.title: Lonesome Dove
OL:OL134601W.author: Larry McMurtry
OL:OL134601W.description: Former Texas Rangers Augustus McCrae and Woodrow Call run a cattle outfit in the dusty border town of Lonesome Dove until they drive a stolen herd north to settle the unspoiled grasslands of Montana, losing men along the way. A Western that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL1715276W.title: Life, a User's Manual
OL:OL1715276W.author: Georges Perec
OL:OL1715276W.description: Removing the facade of a Paris apartment block at 11 rue Simon-Crubellier, the novel moves room by room through its residents' lives, centered on the wealthy Bartlebooth, who paints watercolors worldwide and has them cut into jigsaw puzzles. An intricate work built on elaborate mathematical and structural constraints.

OL:OL166973W.title: The Idiot
OL:OL166973W.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL:OL166973W.description: The epileptic, guileless Prince Myshkin returns to Russia and is drawn between the proud Nastasya Filippovna and the gentler Aglaya, his innocence colliding with a grasping, scheming St. Petersburg society. A novel that tests whether a truly good man can survive in the world.

OL:OL38282W.title: The Moviegoer
OL:OL38282W.author: Walker Percy
OL:OL38282W.description: Binx Bolling, a young New Orleans stockbroker who escapes into movies, drifts through the week of Mardi Gras alongside his troubled cousin Kate while pursuing what he calls a search for meaning. A novel of existential malaise that won the National Book Award.

OL:OL7972956W.title: Ceremony
OL:OL7972956W.author: Leslie Marmon Silko
OL:OL7972956W.description: Tayo, a half-white Laguna Pueblo veteran of World War II, returns home traumatized after a Japanese prison camp and the death of his cousin, and undergoes a healing ceremony guided by the medicine man Betonie. A novel that weaves Pueblo storytelling and verse through its account of recovery.

OL:OL50567W.title: Sula
OL:OL50567W.author: Toni Morrison
OL:OL50567W.description: In the Black neighborhood of the Bottom in Medallion, Ohio, the conventional Nel and the defiant Sula grow up as close friends until adulthood, marriage, and a betrayal drive them apart. A novel about female friendship, community judgment, and the lives of Black women across several decades.

OL:OL5860211W.title: Small Island
OL:OL5860211W.author: Andrea Levy
OL:OL5860211W.description: In 1948, the Jamaican couple Hortense and Gilbert come to London seeking a better life and lodge with Queenie, an Englishwoman whose husband Bernard returns from the war, and the four narrate clashing experiences of race and migration. A novel about postwar Caribbean immigration to Britain.

OL:OL26424W.title: A Far Cry From Kensington
OL:OL26424W.author: Muriel Spark
OL:OL26424W.description: Looking back from Italy, the war-widowed editor Mrs. Hawkins recalls 1950s South Kensington, where her loathing for a pretentious hack named Hector Bartlett costs her a job and entangles her in blackmail, anonymous letters, and a suicide. A comic novel narrated as memory of her younger self.

K:aa9d8baf7d95.title: The Heart of the Matter
K:aa9d8baf7d95.author: Graham Greene
K:aa9d8baf7d95.description: Scobie, a scrupulous British police officer in a West African colony during the war, is pushed by pity for his unhappy wife and a young widow into adultery, deception, and a crisis of his Catholic faith. A novel about conscience, sin, and despair.

OL:OL480955W.title: Quartet in Autumn
OL:OL480955W.author: Barbara Pym
OL:OL480955W.description: Four unmarried or widowed London office workers nearing retirement—Letty, Marcia, Edwin, and Norman—lead isolated lives that begin to unravel as the women leave their jobs and the eccentric Marcia withdraws. A spare, late novel about loneliness and aging that was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL1063588W.title: Les Misérables
OL:OL1063588W.author: Victor Hugo
OL:OL1063588W.description: The ex-convict Jean Valjean rebuilds his life under a new name while the relentless inspector Javert pursues him, and their fates cross with the orphan Cosette and the 1832 Paris uprising. A vast novel of poverty, justice, and redemption in nineteenth-century France.

OL:OL1992198W.title: In Cold Blood
OL:OL1992198W.author: Truman Capote
OL:OL1992198W.description: In November 1959, two ex-convicts murder the four members of the Clutter family in their Kansas farmhouse, and the book reconstructs the crime, the manhunt, the trial, and the killers' executions. A nonfiction novel that helped define the true-crime genre.

K:bd646529eae4.title: The Possessed
K:bd646529eae4.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
K:bd646529eae4.description: In a provincial Russian town, the arrival of the charismatic, nihilistic Nikolai Stavrogin and the agitator Pyotr Verkhovensky draws a revolutionary cell into manipulation, scandal, and political murder. A novel inspired by a real radical conspiracy and aimed at the destructive ideologies of its time.

OL:OL1230715W.title: The Plague
OL:OL1230715W.author: Albert Camus
OL:OL1230715W.description: When rats begin dying in the Algerian city of Oran, bubonic plague takes hold and the town is sealed off, while Dr. Bernard Rieux and others labor to treat the sick and endure the quarantine. A novel often read as an allegory of occupation and of human resistance to suffering.

OL:OL81618W.title: The Stand
OL:OL81618W.author: Stephen King
OL:OL81618W.description: A government-engineered superflu called Captain Trips wipes out most of humanity, and the scattered survivors are drawn into two camps—the good gathered in Boulder around Mother Abagail and the evil ruled by Randall Flagg in Las Vegas. A long post-apocalyptic novel of a final confrontation between good and evil.

K:9b6c22f83dd1.author: George Orwell
K:9b6c22f83dd1.description: In the superstate Oceania, the low-ranking Party worker Winston Smith secretly rebels against the all-seeing Big Brother, falls in love with Julia, and is caught and broken by the Thought Police. A dystopian novel that introduced terms like Newspeak, doublethink, and Big Brother.

K:f547ea8e2ecf.title: The Fountain Overflows
K:f547ea8e2ecf.author: Rebecca West
K:f547ea8e2ecf.description: Through the eyes of young Rose Aubrey, the gifted but unstable Aubrey family struggles in a London suburb before the First World War, held together by their pianist mother as their charming father gambles away their security. The first novel of an unfinished trilogy drawing on the author's childhood.

K:98c8438f910d.title: The Arabian Nights: Tales from a Thousand and One Nights
K:98c8438f910d.description: Spared each dawn by telling her king an unfinished tale, Scheherazade spins a thousand and one nights of stories, framing folk tales of merchants, genies, sailors, and lovers such as Aladdin, Ali Baba, and Sinbad. A collection of Middle Eastern and South Asian stories gathered over many centuries.

OL:OL17644895W.title: Cousin Bette
OL:OL17644895W.author: Honoré de Balzac
OL:OL17644895W.description: The embittered, unmarried Lisbeth Fischer hides her envy behind a mask of devotion as she schemes, with the help of the seductress Valérie Marneffe, to ruin her prosperous Parisian relatives the Hulots. A novel of jealousy, debt, and revenge set in mid-nineteenth-century Paris.

K:017afa232b50.title: The Hamlet
K:017afa232b50.author: William Faulkner
K:017afa232b50.description: The cold, ambitious Flem Snopes arrives with his sharecropper family in the rural Mississippi community of Frenchman's Bend and steadily takes over its store, land, and economy before moving on to Jefferson. The first volume of a trilogy chronicling the rise of the Snopes clan in Yoknapatawpha County.

OL:OL21025633W.title: Notes From the Underground
OL:OL21025633W.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL:OL21025633W.description: A bitter, unnamed retired civil servant in St. Petersburg pours out his spiteful philosophy in a rambling confession, then recounts how he humiliated old schoolmates and cruelly rejected the prostitute Liza who offered him affection. A short novel often regarded as an early work of existentialist fiction.

K:969799e0bdc1.title: The Charterhouse of Parma
K:969799e0bdc1.author: Stendhal
K:969799e0bdc1.description: The impetuous young Italian nobleman Fabrice del Dongo runs off to fight for Napoleon at Waterloo, then returns to the intrigues of the court of Parma, aided by his devoted aunt Gina and her lover Count Mosca and entangled in love and imprisonment. An early novel of literary realism.

K:9582f8788134.title: Waiting for Godot
K:9582f8788134.author: Samuel Beckett
K:9582f8788134.description: On a bare country road by a tree, the tramps Vladimir and Estragon wait for a man named Godot who never comes, passing the time with talk and routines as the brutal Pozzo and his servant Lucky pass by. A two-act tragicomedy central to the Theatre of the Absurd.

OL:OL65906W.title: On the Road
OL:OL65906W.author: Jack Kerouac
OL:OL65906W.description: Sal Paradise crisscrosses the United States and Mexico with the restless, fast-talking Dean Moriarty, chasing jazz, women, and experience in a series of frenzied road trips. A loosely autobiographical novel that became a defining work of the Beat Generation.

OL:OL44820011W.title: Pnin
OL:OL44820011W.author: Vladimir Nabokov
OL:OL44820011W.description: The genial, accident-prone Russian émigré Timofey Pnin teaches his native language at a small American college, struggling with English, faculty politics, and memories of his lost homeland and his ex-wife. A comic, episodic novel about an exile's dignity and isolation.

OL:OL103108W.title: A Bend in the River
OL:OL103108W.author: V. S. Naipaul
OL:OL103108W.description: Salim, an Indian Muslim shopkeeper, sets up a small business in a town at the bend of a great river in a newly independent African country, watching it lurch through upheaval under a ruler called the Big Man. A novel about exile, corruption, and the precariousness of postcolonial Africa.

K:c34e51144bbc.title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
K:c34e51144bbc.author: Ernest Hemingway
K:c34e51144bbc.description: During the Spanish Civil War, the American dynamiter Robert Jordan joins a band of Republican guerrillas in the mountains to blow up a bridge, falling in love with the young Maria over the few days before the attack. A war novel about duty, comradeship, and mortality.

OL:OL1858631W.title: Good Morning, Midnight
OL:OL1858631W.author: Jean Rhys
OL:OL1858631W.description: Sasha Jansen, a lonely, drinking middle-aged Englishwoman, returns to Paris on borrowed money and wanders its cafés and streets, haunted by an unhappy marriage and a dead child until a young gigolo's attentions turn unsettling. A modernist novel of depression and vulnerability between the wars.

K:1d1ae492ede5.title: Don Juan
K:1d1ae492ede5.author: Lord Byron
K:1d1ae492ede5.description: Don Juan, drawn from the Spanish legend, is sent abroad after a youthful affair and drifts through shipwreck, a Greek island romance, slavery in Constantinople, the siege of Ismail, and the court of Catherine the Great, all narrated by a digressive, satirical voice. An unfinished epic poem in ottava rima that mocks the literary, political, and religious figures of its day.

OL:OL228715W.title: Another Country
OL:OL228715W.author: James Baldwin
OL:OL228715W.description: In 1950s Greenwich Village, jazz drummer Rufus Scott spirals into despair after a destructive affair with a white Southern woman and kills himself, leaving his friends and sister Ida to navigate love and grief across racial and sexual lines. The novel deals openly with bisexuality, interracial relationships, and infidelity.

OL:OL106837W.title: Memoirs of Hadrian
OL:OL106837W.author: Marguerite Yourcenar
OL:OL106837W.description: Dying and around sixty, the Roman emperor Hadrian writes a long letter to his young successor Marcus Aurelius, recalling his rise to power, his military campaigns, his love of art and philosophy, and his grief over his lover Antinous. A first-person historical novel told as the emperor's reflective memoir.

K:c7f77816dbd2.title: The Man Who Loved Children
K:c7f77816dbd2.author: Christina Stead
K:c7f77816dbd2.description: Sam Pollit, a self-absorbed government scientist, dominates his large family with relentless optimism while his embittered wife Henny sinks into despair and their eldest daughter Louie struggles to break free, in a household poisoned by money troubles and mutual hatred. A novel known for its portrait of a destructive family and its origins in the author's own childhood.

OL:OL5721565W.title: A Handful of Dust
OL:OL5721565W.author: Evelyn Waugh
OL:OL5721565W.description: Tony Last, a complacent English squire devoted to his country house Hetton, loses his son and his marriage when his wife Brenda begins an affair, then escapes on a Brazilian expedition that ends with him held captive by a deranged settler who forces him to read Dickens aloud. A satirical novel about the collapse of English upper-class values.

OL:OL159382W.title: The Lover
OL:OL159382W.author: Marguerite Duras
OL:OL159382W.description: A French girl reflects on her impoverished colonial childhood in 1920s Saigon and her affair, begun at fifteen, with a wealthy older Chinese man, alongside memories of her unstable mother and brothers. An autobiographical novel that won the Prix Goncourt.

OL:OL15026613W.title: A Visit From the Goon Squad
OL:OL15026613W.author: Jennifer Egan
OL:OL15026613W.description: Record executive Bennie Salazar and his assistant Sasha anchor thirteen interlinked stories that leap across decades and characters in the music industry, from the late 1970s punk scene into a near-future New York. A novel told in shifting forms, including one chapter written as a PowerPoint presentation, that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL15202030W.title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame
OL:OL15202030W.author: Victor Hugo
OL:OL15202030W.description: In fifteenth-century Paris, the deformed bell-ringer Quasimodo, the Romani dancer Esmeralda, and the archdeacon Claude Frollo become entangled around Notre-Dame Cathedral, with Frollo's obsession driving Esmeralda toward the gallows. A Gothic novel that also argues for the preservation of medieval architecture.

OL:OL1217995W.title: U.s.a.
OL:OL1217995W.author: John Dos Passos
OL:OL1217995W.description: Twelve Americans pursue their fortunes from 1900 through the Great Depression, their stories interrupted by "Newsreel" montages of headlines and songs, capsule biographies of public figures, and autobiographical "Camera Eye" passages. An experimental modernist trilogy surveying American society across three decades.

OL:OL16246083W.title: Death in Venice
OL:OL16246083W.author: Thomas Mann
OL:OL16246083W.description: Gustav von Aschenbach, a disciplined and aging German writer, travels to Venice and becomes consumed by his attraction to Tadzio, a beautiful Polish boy, lingering in the city even as a cholera epidemic spreads until he dies on the beach watching the child. A novella about beauty, desire, and artistic decline.

K:3d8256fe2668.title: Appointment in Samarra
K:3d8256fe2668.author: John O'Hara
K:3d8256fe2668.description: Over three days around Christmas in the small Pennsylvania city of Gibbsville, wealthy car dealer Julian English throws a drink in a man's face and sets off a chain of impulsive acts that destroy his social standing and end in his suicide. A debut novel about self-destruction and class in 1930s America.

OL:OL2009202W.title: Light Years
OL:OL2009202W.author: James Salter
OL:OL2009202W.description: Viri, an architect, and his wife Nedra raise two daughters in a seemingly perfect home in the Hudson Valley starting in the late 1950s, but both conduct affairs and their marriage gradually comes apart, leaving them to age separately. A novel tracing the slow dissolution of a marriage over many years.

OL:OL40885W.title: Suttree
OL:OL40885W.author: Cormac McCarthy
OL:OL40885W.description: Cornelius Suttree abandons his wealthy family to live on a houseboat and fish the Tennessee River in 1950s Knoxville, drifting among drunks, prostitutes, and outcasts in the city's underworld. A semi-autobiographical novel noted for its dense prose and dark humor.

OL:OL953028W.title: Heart so White
OL:OL953028W.author: Javier Marías
OL:OL953028W.description: Juan, a Madrid translator newly married to Luisa, grows uneasy about the secrets in his father's past and the suicide of his father's first wife, and slowly uncovers what happened. A novel about secrets, marriage, and the consequences of knowing, which won the International Dublin Literary Award.

OL:OL4082696W.title: The Corrections
OL:OL4082696W.author: Jonathan Franzen
OL:OL4082696W.description: Elderly Enid Lambert presses her three adult children, Gary, Chip, and Denise, to come home to the Midwest for one last Christmas as her husband Alfred declines into Parkinson's and dementia, while each child wrestles with career failures and tangled relationships. A novel about a Midwestern family and its private crises.

OL:OL1434640W.title: Berlin Alexanderplatz
OL:OL1434640W.author: Alfred Döblin
OL:OL1434640W.description: Franz Biberkopf leaves Berlin's Tegel prison resolved to live honestly but is pulled back into the city's criminal underworld, betrayed by the gangster Reinhold and dragged toward ruin amid the chaos of 1920s Berlin. A modernist novel using collage, slang, and shifting viewpoints to render the city.

OL:OL1209288W.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
OL:OL1209288W.author: Erich Maria Remarque
OL:OL1209288W.description: Paul Bäumer and his schoolmates enlist in the German army during the First World War and endure the trenches, where the slaughter, fear, and numbness strip away their illusions and kill them one by one. A novel about the physical and mental devastation of war, drawn from the author's own service.

K:132c540db579.title: Sister Carrie
K:132c540db579.author: Theodore Dreiser
K:132c540db579.description: Carrie Meeber leaves rural Wisconsin for Chicago in 1889, becomes the mistress of a salesman and then of the married manager Hurstwood, who abandons everything to run off with her, and rises to fame as an actress while he sinks into poverty and suicide. An early American naturalist novel about ambition and the city.

OL:OL20665410W.title: The Mirror and the Light
OL:OL20665410W.author: Hilary Mantel
OL:OL20665410W.description: In the last four years of his life, from 1536 to his execution in 1540, Thomas Cromwell serves Henry VIII at the height of his power, managing the king's marriages and enemies as his own fall approaches. The final novel in a trilogy about Cromwell's rise and fall in the Tudor court.

OL:OL112983W.title: A Month in the Country
OL:OL112983W.author: JL Carr
OL:OL112983W.description: Tom Birkin, a shell-shocked First World War veteran, spends a summer in the Yorkshire village of Oxgodby uncovering a medieval mural hidden under whitewash in the church, finding a measure of peace among the villagers. A short novel about recovery, memory, and a vanished rural England.

OL:OL20771W.title: The Blue Flower
OL:OL20771W.author: Penelope Fitzgerald
OL:OL20771W.description: In late-eighteenth-century Germany, the young Friedrich von Hardenberg, later the poet Novalis, falls in love with twelve-year-old Sophie von Kühn and pursues a courtship cut short by her early death from tuberculosis. A historical novel based on the philosopher-poet's youth, named after his image of the blue flower.

OL:OL40873W.title: The Road
OL:OL40873W.author: Cormac McCarthy
OL:OL40873W.description: A father and his young son walk south through a gray, ash-covered America destroyed by an unnamed catastrophe, scavenging for food and hiding from roving bands of cannibals as they try to reach the coast. A post-apocalyptic novel about survival and the bond between parent and child that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL2196010W.title: The Summer Book
OL:OL2196010W.author: Tove Jansson
OL:OL2196010W.description: A young girl named Sophia and her elderly grandmother spend summers together on a small island in the Gulf of Finland, talking, quarreling, and exploring while quietly carrying the absence of Sophia's dead mother. A novel told in short episodes about childhood, old age, and nature.

OL:OL2943602W.title: Infinite Jest
OL:OL2943602W.author: David Foster Wallace
OL:OL2943602W.description: Hal Incandenza trains at his late father's Enfield Tennis Academy while nearby residents of the Ennet House recovery home struggle with addiction, all set against the search for a film so entertaining it kills anyone who watches it. An encyclopedic novel known for its length and its hundreds of endnotes.

OL:OL27871634W.title: Septology
OL:OL27871634W.author: Jon Fosse
OL:OL27871634W.description: Asle, an aging painter and recent Catholic convert living on the Norwegian coast, reflects on his life, his late wife, and God during the days before Christmas while looking after a namesake double, a fellow painter dying of drink. A seven-part novel written as a single unbroken sentence.

OL:OL44994W.title: The Return of the Native
OL:OL44994W.author: Thomas Hardy
OL:OL44994W.description: On the bleak Egdon Heath, the restless Eustacia Vye marries Clym Yeobright, who has returned from Paris hoping to become a schoolmaster, but her longing for a wider life and a rekindled affair with Damon Wildeve lead to drownings and ruin. A tragic novel set across a single year in the author's fictional Wessex.

OL:OL1731119W.title: Pedro Páramo
OL:OL1731119W.author: Juan Rulfo
OL:OL1731119W.description: Juan Preciado travels to the town of Comala to find the father he was promised on his mother's deathbed, only to discover the place deserted and peopled by the ghosts of the dead, who recount the cruelty of the landowner Pedro Páramo. A short novel that became a foundational work of magic realism.

OL:OL17063057W.title: How to Be Both
OL:OL17063057W.author: Ali Smith
OL:OL17063057W.description: A sixteen-year-old girl named George in present-day Cambridge mourns her mother, while in another section the Renaissance painter Francesco del Cossa recalls life and work in fifteenth-century Ferrara; the two halves were printed in different orders in different copies. A novel built so its two stories can be read in either sequence.

OL:OL17351965W.title: Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead
OL:OL17351965W.author: Olga Tokarczuk
OL:OL17351965W.description: Janina Duszejko, an eccentric older woman living in a remote Polish village near the Czech border, blames the local hunters for a string of deaths and pushes her own astrological theory of the murders on the police. A mystery with an unreliable narrator by a Nobel laureate.

OL:OL1095403W.title: Villette
OL:OL1095403W.author: Charlotte Brontë
OL:OL1095403W.description: Lucy Snowe leaves England with little money and takes a teaching post at a girls' boarding school in the fictional French-speaking city of Villette, where she observes those around her and falls into a guarded attachment to the irascible teacher Monsieur Paul. A novel drawn from the author's time in Brussels.

OL:OL157104W.title: Life and Fate
OL:OL157104W.author: Vasily Grossman
OL:OL157104W.description: During the Battle of Stalingrad, the physicist Viktor Shtrum and the scattered Shaposhnikov family endure war, antisemitism, and Stalinist repression, as the narrative draws parallels between the Nazi and Soviet states. A novel suppressed by the KGB and published abroad decades after it was written.

OL:OL102389W.title: The Years
OL:OL102389W.author: Annie Ernaux
OL:OL102389W.description: Moving from the end of the Second World War to the early 2000s, the narrator traces French society through shared memories, photographs, songs, news, and consumer life, writing of herself only as "she," "we," and "they." A collective autobiography that blends personal and national history.

OL:OL8996439W.title: The Name of the Rose
OL:OL8996439W.author: Umberto Eco
OL:OL8996439W.description: In 1327, the Franciscan friar William of Baskerville and his young assistant Adso arrive at a northern Italian abbey for a theological dispute and instead investigate a series of deaths centered on the monastery's labyrinthine library. A historical murder mystery steeped in medieval philosophy and semiotics.

OL:OL109724W.title: Barchester Towers
OL:OL109724W.author: Anthony Trollope
OL:OL109724W.description: The Reverend Septimus Harding and his daughter Eleanor are caught up in the church politics of the cathedral town of Barchester, where the new bishop's wife and the oily chaplain Mr. Slope vie for control of clergy appointments against the worldly archdeacon Grantly. A Victorian comic novel about ecclesiastical rivalry and provincial society.

OL:OL2047674W.title: The Go-Between
OL:OL2047674W.author: LP Hartley
OL:OL2047674W.description: During a hot summer at a Norfolk country house in 1900, twelve-year-old Leo Colston carries secret messages between Marian Maudsley and the tenant farmer Ted Burgess, not grasping the affair he is enabling until it ends in catastrophe. The story is framed by the elderly Leo looking back on the events.

OL:OL9362446W.title: The Easter Parade
OL:OL9362446W.author: Richard Yates
OL:OL9362446W.description: Sisters Emily and Sarah Grimes grow up after their parents' divorce and follow diverging paths across the decades, with the conventional Sarah marrying into an abusive household and the intellectual Emily drifting through unsatisfying jobs and affairs. A novel tracing two women's disappointments from the 1930s to the 1970s.

K:3e4c8a960300.title: Candide
K:3e4c8a960300.author: Voltaire
K:3e4c8a960300.description: Candide, raised in a baron's castle on the optimistic philosophy that this is the best of all possible worlds, is expelled and thrown into war, earthquake, slavery, and betrayal as he wanders Europe and the Americas searching for his beloved Cunégonde. A satire ridiculing philosophical optimism, ending with the resolve to cultivate one's garden.

K:6baf284ba2c5.title: Poems of Emily Dickinson
K:6baf284ba2c5.author: Emily Dickinson
K:6baf284ba2c5.description: Several hundred short, compressed lyrics treat death, immortality, nature, love, and the inner life, most written in slant-rhymed quatrains and left unpublished during the poet's lifetime. The first collection appeared posthumously and established a reputation as a major American poet.

OL:OL81294W.title: Women in Love
OL:OL81294W.author: D. H. Lawrence
OL:OL81294W.description: Sisters Ursula and Gudrun Brangwen pursue relationships with the school inspector Rupert Birkin and the industrialist Gerald Crich in the English Midlands, their two couplings developing along sharply different lines toward love and destruction. A novel examining sexuality, marriage, and personal connection in early twentieth-century England.

K:8a974c3db91a.title: Troilus and Criseyde
K:8a974c3db91a.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
K:8a974c3db91a.description: In besieged Troy during the Trojan War, the young knight Troilus falls in love with the widow Criseyde with the help of her uncle Pandarus, only for Criseyde to be traded to the Greeks and transfer her affection to Diomede. A Middle English poem in rhyme royal retelling the lovers' tragedy.

OL:OL40690787W.title: Washington Square
OL:OL40690787W.author: Henry James
OL:OL40690787W.description: In 1840s New York, the plain, dutiful Catherine Sloper is courted by the charming but penniless Morris Townsend, while her sharp father Dr. Sloper insists the young man is only after her inheritance and threatens to disinherit her. A short novel about a daughter caught between a suitor and a controlling father.

OL:OL20422365W.title: Woodcutters
OL:OL20422365W.author: Thomas Bernhard
OL:OL20422365W.description: The narrator sits in a wing chair at a late-night "artistic dinner" in a Viennese apartment, silently dissecting the pretentious hosts and guests while awaiting a Burgtheater actor and recalling Joana, an old friend buried that same day. A monologue novel built from obsessive, repetitive interior invective.

K:009fc9ee2b85.title: Molloy, Malone Dies, and The Unnamable
K:009fc9ee2b85.author: Samuel Beckett
K:009fc9ee2b85.description: Three linked first-person narratives follow increasingly broken-down men, beginning with the wandering Molloy, moving to the dying Malone telling himself stories in bed, and ending with a bodiless voice unable to stop or locate itself. A prose trilogy reducing narrative and identity toward an unnamable speaking presence.

K:95fdf062893b.title: Hard Times
K:95fdf062893b.author: Charles Dickens
K:95fdf062893b.description: In the grim industrial town of Coketown, the fact-obsessed schoolmaster Thomas Gradgrind raises his children on hard utilitarian principle while the mill owner Josiah Bounderby exploits workers like Stephen Blackpool. A novel attacking utilitarianism and the dehumanizing effects of industrial society.

K:a6094632e300.title: The Bear
K:a6094632e300.author: William Faulkner
K:a6094632e300.description: In the Mississippi wilderness, the boy Isaac McCaslin learns hunting and woodcraft over successive years as the men pursue Old Ben, a huge and elusive bear, while Ike comes to reckon with the legacy of slavery in his family's plantation ledgers. A novella about wilderness, initiation, and inherited guilt.

OL:OL1921196W.title: White Noise
OL:OL1921196W.author: Don DeLillo
OL:OL1921196W.description: Jack Gladney, a professor of Hitler studies at a Midwestern college, navigates his blended family and consumer-saturated life until an "Airborne Toxic Event" forces an evacuation and deepens his terror of death. A novel satirizing media, consumerism, and the fear of mortality in modern America.

OL:OL26201952W.title: Chronicle of a Death Foretold
OL:OL26201952W.author: Gabriel García Márquez
OL:OL26201952W.description: In a Colombian town, the Vicario brothers announce all over town that they intend to kill Santiago Nasar to avenge their sister Angela's lost honor, and almost everyone knows yet no one prevents the murder. A short novel reconstructing the foretold killing through a narrator's later inquiry.

OL:OL8972751W.title: The Unbearable Lightness of Being
OL:OL8972751W.author: Milan Kundera
OL:OL8972751W.description: In Prague around the 1968 Soviet invasion, the surgeon and womanizer Tomas, his wife Tereza, his lover the painter Sabina, and her lover Franz move through love affairs, political pressure, and exile. A novel interweaving their relationships with reflections on weight, lightness, and recurrence.

K:5610cd9f092e.title: The Killer Inside Me
K:5610cd9f092e.author: Jim Thompson
K:5610cd9f092e.description: Lou Ford, a mild-mannered, seemingly genial deputy sheriff in a small Texas town, narrates how he conceals a violent compulsion he calls "the sickness" and commits a series of murders behind his polite facade. A crime novel told from inside the mind of a psychopathic lawman.

OL:OL483391W.title: Charlotte's Web
OL:OL483391W.author: E. B. White
OL:OL483391W.description: On a farm, a pig named Wilbur is saved from slaughter by the barn spider Charlotte, who spins words like "SOME PIG" into her web to make him famous, aided by the girl Fern and the rat Templeton. A children's novel about friendship, mortality, and the cycle of life.

K:76ef59a89b06.title: Death of a Salesman
K:76ef59a89b06.author: Arthur Miller
K:76ef59a89b06.description: Aging Brooklyn salesman Willy Loman returns home exhausted and slips between present failure and memory as he clashes with his disappointed son Biff and clings to dreams of being well-liked and successful. A play about the costs of the American dream and self-delusion.

OL:OL2384132W.title: Cry, the Beloved Country
OL:OL2384132W.author: Alan Paton
OL:OL2384132W.description: The Zulu pastor Stephen Kumalo travels from his rural village to Johannesburg to find his sister and son, only to learn his son has killed a white man, the son of a neighboring farmer. A novel about racial injustice and reconciliation in South Africa before apartheid.

K:910a38647a5c.title: Stories of Grace Paley
K:910a38647a5c.author: Grace Paley
K:910a38647a5c.description: Across three decades of stories, working-class New Yorkers, especially the recurring Faith Darwin, raise children, argue politics, and manage love and friendship in Greenwich Village and the Bronx. This collected volume gathers the author's short fiction known for its compressed, talky, vernacular voice.

OL:OL103123W.title: Farenheit 451
OL:OL103123W.author: Ray Bradbury
OL:OL103123W.description: Guy Montag, a fireman in a future America whose job is burning books, begins hiding and reading them after meeting his curious neighbor Clarisse and watching a woman die with her library, turning against his book-burning society. A novel about censorship, conformity, and mass media.

K:a452f45af6bc.title: Grimm's Fairy Tales
K:a452f45af6bc.description: Hundreds of German folk and fairy tales, including "Cinderella," "Hansel and Gretel," "Rapunzel," "Snow White," and "Little Red Riding Hood," were gathered and reshaped across successive editions. The collection became one of the most influential sources of European fairy tales.

K:23e11cce9bf8.title: Speak, Memory
K:23e11cce9bf8.author: Vladimir Nabokov
K:23e11cce9bf8.description: The author recounts his aristocratic childhood in pre-revolutionary Russia, his family's flight from the Bolsheviks, and his émigré years in Cambridge, Berlin, and Paris, organized around vivid recovered memories rather than strict chronology. A memoir reflecting on time, exile, and the workings of recollection.

K:7a4667d98f9f.title: A Death in the Family
K:7a4667d98f9f.author: James Agee
K:7a4667d98f9f.description: In 1915 Knoxville, Tennessee, six-year-old Rufus Follet and his family absorb the sudden death of his father Jay in a car accident, the household moving through grief, faith, and the children's incomplete understanding of loss. An autobiographical novel published posthumously.

K:d269f3b1008d.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
K:d269f3b1008d.author: Oscar Wilde
K:d269f3b1008d.description: Two friends, Jack Worthing and Algernon Moncrieff, both invent fictitious personas named "Ernest" to escape obligations and court Gwendolen and Cecily, leading to mistaken identities and the discovery of Jack's true parentage. A comedy satirizing the manners and hypocrisies of Victorian high society.

OL:OL1326348W.title: A Severed Head
OL:OL1326348W.author: Iris Murdoch
OL:OL1326348W.description: The wine merchant Martin Lynch-Gibbon, comfortable in his affair while married to Antonia, finds his arrangements collapsing when his wife leaves him for her psychoanalyst and he becomes entangled with the unsettling anthropologist Honor Klein. A comic novel of shifting couplings among the English upper middle class.

K:3370e18f51ca.title: His Dark Materials
K:3370e18f51ca.author: Philip Pullman
K:3370e18f51ca.description: Across parallel worlds, the girl Lyra Belacqua and the boy Will Parry, accompanied by soul-companions called dæmons, are drawn into a cosmic conflict involving the mysterious substance Dust and a rebellion against the Authority. A fantasy trilogy blending adventure with theology, physics, and philosophy.

K:af9b5d2a92ca.title: The Hours
K:af9b5d2a92ca.author: Michael Cunningham
K:af9b5d2a92ca.description: Three women in different eras are linked by the novel Mrs Dalloway: the author writing it in 1920s England, a 1949 Los Angeles housewife reading it, and a present-day New Yorker planning a party for a dying friend. A novel structured around a single day in each woman's life.

K:2ba7f9e2d3da.title: The Untouchable
K:2ba7f9e2d3da.author: John Banville
K:2ba7f9e2d3da.description: The elderly art historian Victor Maskell, exposed as a Soviet double agent after decades as a respected curator, narrates his life among Cambridge spies, his hidden homosexuality, and his betrayals. A novel based loosely on the real spy Anthony Blunt.

K:19f63e640608.title: The Master
K:19f63e640608.author: Colm Tóibín
K:19f63e640608.description: Between 1895 and 1899, the American-born novelist Henry James endures the failure of his play in London and retreats to a house in Rye, working and brooding over family, friendships, and his unspoken desires. A novel reimagining several pivotal years in the writer's interior life.

K:f5a6ea3da198.title: Miss Lonelyhearts
K:f5a6ea3da198.author: Nathanael West
K:f5a6ea3da198.description: Miss Lonelyhearts, a male newspaper columnist who answers letters from desperate readers, is overwhelmed by their suffering and his cynical editor Shrike, sinking into a religious and emotional crisis. A short novel about despair and the futility of consolation in Depression-era New York.

K:0cedd0859856.title: Stories of William Trevor
K:0cedd0859856.author: William Trevor
K:0cedd0859856.description: Across many stories set mostly in provincial Ireland, ordinary people confront loneliness, thwarted love, religion, and small acts of cruelty and kindness in towns and farms. This gathered volume collects the author's short fiction known for its restraint and attention to ordinary lives.

K:a66bfb050c76.title: The Oedipus trilogy
K:a66bfb050c76.author: Sophocles
K:a66bfb050c76.description: Three Theban plays follow the doomed royal house: Oedipus unknowingly kills his father and marries his mother and is ruined, the blind exile dies at Colonus, and his daughter Antigone defies the king to bury her brother. The plays, written separately, are read together as a sequence on fate and law.

OL:OL7982392W.title: The Story of the Stone, or the Dream of the Red Chamber
OL:OL7982392W.author: Cao Xueqin
OL:OL7982392W.description: Cousins Jia Baoyu, Lin Daiyu, and Xue Baochai grow up inside the sprawling, wealthy Jia household, their entangled loves and rivalries playing out as the family slides toward ruin. A long Chinese novel of manners, widely regarded as a high point of classical Chinese fiction.

OL:OL1337129W.title: Right Ho, Jeeves
OL:OL1337129W.author: P. G. Wodehouse
OL:OL1337129W.description: At his Aunt Dahlia's Brinkley Court, Bertie Wooster meddles in the romances of the newt-loving Gussie Fink-Nottle and Madeline Bassett and his cousin Angela, drunkenly botches a school prize-giving, and finally turns to his valet Jeeves to untangle the mess. A comic novel in the Jeeves series.

K:c157e7e9d2a1.title: The Regeneration trilogy
K:c157e7e9d2a1.author: Pat Barker
K:c157e7e9d2a1.description: At Craiglockhart military hospital and beyond, army psychiatrist William Rivers treats shell-shocked First World War officers, including the poet Siegfried Sassoon and the fictional Billy Prior, across the war's final years. Three linked novels blending real and invented figures; the last, The Ghost Road, won the Booker Prize.

K:3dfab6fbfe3b.title: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich
K:3dfab6fbfe3b.author: Alexander Solzhenitsyn
K:3dfab6fbfe3b.description: Ivan Denisovich Shukhov, wrongly imprisoned as a spy, works through a single freezing day in a Soviet forced-labor camp, from reveille to lights-out, scrounging extra food and laying brick with his squad. One of the first published Soviet accounts of the Gulag.

K:5f7b8a8855e8.title: Airships
K:5f7b8a8855e8.author: Barry Hannah
K:5f7b8a8855e8.description: Twenty stories range across the Vietnam War, the American Civil War, and the contemporary South, peopled by soldiers, musicians, and disappointed men chasing love and drink. A short-story collection associated with Mississippi and the postwar American South.

OL:OL20938W.title: Mill on the Floss
OL:OL20938W.author: George Eliot
OL:OL20938W.description: Maggie and Tom Tulliver grow up at Dorlcote Mill on the River Floss, and after their father loses a lawsuit and the mill, Maggie's bonds with the disabled Philip Wakem and with Stephen Guest collide with Tom's rigid sense of family honor. The novel ends with the siblings drowning together in a flood.

OL:OL644386W.title: The Betrothed
OL:OL644386W.author: Alessandro Manzoni
OL:OL644386W.description: In 1628 Lombardy under Spanish rule, the peasants Renzo and Lucia try to marry, but the local tyrant Don Rodrigo blocks them, scattering the couple across a country gripped by famine, riots, and plague. A historical novel considered a landmark of Italian literature.

K:30993508b211.title: Native Son
K:30993508b211.author: Richard Wright
K:30993508b211.description: Bigger Thomas, a young Black man in 1930s Chicago, takes a chauffeur job with the wealthy white Dalton family and accidentally kills their daughter Mary, setting off his flight, capture, and trial. A protest novel about racism and poverty in America.

K:aad10973ad30.title: An American Tragedy
K:aad10973ad30.author: Theodore Dreiser
K:aad10973ad30.description: Clyde Griffiths, an ambitious poor young man, works his way into his rich uncle's collar factory, courts the socialite Sondra while concealing his pregnant girlfriend Roberta, and plots her drowning before facing arrest and trial. A novel based on a real 1906 murder case.

K:72452c900a94.title: Mike Mulligan and His Steam Shovel
K:72452c900a94.author: Virginia Lee Burton
K:72452c900a94.description: Mike Mulligan and his aging steam shovel Mary Anne, outmoded by newer machines, take on a bet to dig the cellar for Popperville's new town hall in a single day, then must figure out how to get Mary Anne out of the hole. A picture book about a man and his machine.

K:b7e02ad45061.title: The Monster at the End of this Book
K:b7e02ad45061.author: Jon Stone and Mike Smollin
K:b7e02ad45061.description: Grover, alarmed by the title, begs the reader not to turn the pages because a monster waits at the end, tying ropes and building walls to stop them, only to discover that the monster is himself. A Sesame Street picture book that talks directly to the reader.

K:1e0203a3004c.title: Sylvester and the Magic Pebble
K:1e0203a3004c.author: William Steig
K:1e0203a3004c.description: Sylvester the donkey finds a magic pebble that grants wishes, but when a lion frightens him he wishes himself into a rock and drops the pebble, leaving his grieving parents to search for him. A picture book that won the Caldecott Medal.

K:ab6325032b46.title: The Story of the Little Mole Who Went in Search of Whodunit
K:ab6325032b46.author: Werner Holzwarth and Wolf Erlbruch
K:ab6325032b46.description: A mole pokes his head out of the ground and is dropped on by something, so he questions a pigeon, horse, hare, goat, cow, and pig before flies help him identify the butcher's dog as the culprit, whom he repays in kind. A children's picture book, originally German, known for its frank treatment of animal droppings.

K:f5b2e8ed7aaf.title: Charlie the Tramp
K:f5b2e8ed7aaf.author: Russell Hoban and Lillian Russell
K:f5b2e8ed7aaf.description: Charlie, a young beaver, decides he would rather be a wandering tramp than learn to chop trees and build dams, but on his first night away the sound of trickling water and his beaver instincts get the better of him. A children's picture book about work and identity.

K:a32b529baa70.title: In the Night Kitchen
K:a32b529baa70.author: Maurice Sendak
K:a32b529baa70.description: Mickey tumbles out of his pajamas and into the Night Kitchen, where three bakers nearly bake him into the morning cake until he builds a dough airplane, fetches their milk, and crows from atop a giant milk bottle. A picture book noted for its dream imagery and recurring challenges over Mickey's nudity.

K:e58ea2747551.title: Bark, George
K:e58ea2747551.author: Jules Feiffer
K:e58ea2747551.description: George the puppy cannot bark, so his mother takes him to the vet, who reaches inside and pulls out a cat, a duck, a pig, and a cow before George finally barks, only to answer "Hello" on the walk home. A picture book built on repetition and a final joke.

K:f5c7d89b5b99.title: Friday Night At Hodges' Café
K:f5c7d89b5b99.author: Tim Egan
K:f5c7d89b5b99.description: Hodges the elephant runs a café with a strict no-tigers rule, until three tigers barge in demanding elephant schnitzel, and a brawl erupts that ends when a tiger tastes the chef's soufflé and the whole café makes peace. A children's picture book.

K:3217b8f0ad67.title: Frog and Toad
K:3217b8f0ad67.author: Arnold Lobel
K:3217b8f0ad67.description: Across linked easy-reader stories, the cheerful Frog and the worried Toad share the small events of friendship, planting a garden, looking for a lost button, waiting for the mail, and trying to be brave. A series of beginning-reader books known for their gentle humor.

OL:OL15322W.title: The Baron in the Trees
OL:OL15322W.author: Italo Calvino
OL:OL15322W.description: After a quarrel over a dish of snails in 1767, the young nobleman Cosimo Piovasco di Rondò climbs into the trees of his family's estate at Ombrosa and vows never to come down, living out a full life among the branches. A philosophical novel, part of the Our Ancestors trilogy.

OL:OL112623W.title: A High Wind in Jamaica
OL:OL112623W.author: Richard Hughes
OL:OL112623W.description: The Bas-Thornton children, sent from Jamaica to England after a hurricane, are seized by pirates when their ship is boarded, and they settle into shipboard life as the relationship between them and the crew turns dangerous. A novel about childhood and the limits of innocence.

OL:OL463834W.title: Couples
OL:OL463834W.author: John Updike
OL:OL463834W.description: In the small Massachusetts town of Tarbox around 1963, ten married couples swap partners in an interlocking round of affairs centered on the contractor Piet Hanema, whose involvement with the pregnant Foxy Whitman upends two marriages. A novel about sex and middle-class life in 1960s America.

OL:OL2005224W.title: At Swim-Two-Birds
OL:OL2005224W.author: Flann O'Brien
OL:OL2005224W.description: An idle Dublin university student writing a novel introduces a writer named Trellis, whose own characters, drawn from cowboy tales, Irish legend, and the mad king Sweeney, rebel against their author and put him on trial. A metafictional comic novel.

OL:OL240077W.title: The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner
OL:OL240077W.author: James Hogg
OL:OL240077W.description: Robert Wringhim, a fanatical Calvinist convinced he is among the saved, falls under the sway of the shape-shifting stranger Gil-Martin and is led into a series of murders, the story told first by an editor and then by Robert himself. A Scottish novel of religious fanaticism and the divided self.

OL:OL2536262W.title: The Slaves of Solitude
OL:OL2536262W.author: Patrick Hamilton
OL:OL2536262W.description: In the winter of 1943, the lonely middle-aged Miss Roach endures life at the Rosamund Tea Rooms boarding house, tormented by the bullying Mr Thwaites and by her German rival Vicki for the attention of an American lieutenant. A novel of wartime English boarding-house life.

OL:OL457175W.title: The Satanic Verses
OL:OL457175W.author: Salman Rushdie
OL:OL457175W.description: Two Indian actors, Gibreel Farishta and Saladin Chamcha, survive the mid-air explosion of a hijacked jet over the English Channel and fall to earth transformed, one taking on angelic traits and the other devilish, while dream sequences retell the founding of a new religion. A novel whose treatment of Islam drew protests and a fatwa.

K:8f7a8603bc7a.title: The Bacchae
K:8f7a8603bc7a.author: Euripides
K:8f7a8603bc7a.description: The god Dionysus comes to Thebes disguised as a mortal to punish King Pentheus and the city for denying his divinity, driving the women into ecstatic frenzy until Pentheus is torn apart by his own mother Agave on the mountainside. An ancient Greek tragedy performed after its author's death.

OL:OL2276498W.title: Confessions of Zeno
OL:OL2276498W.author: Italo Svevo
OL:OL2276498W.description: At his psychoanalyst's suggestion, the neurotic Trieste businessman Zeno Cosini writes a rambling memoir covering his endless failed attempts to quit smoking, his father's death, his marriage, and a half-hearted affair. A novel structured as a patient's confession and an early use of Freudian ideas in fiction.

OL:OL2399772W.title: The Loser
OL:OL2399772W.author: Thomas Bernhard
OL:OL2399772W.description: Recalling his student days studying piano in Salzburg, an unnamed narrator reflects on the suicide of his friend Wertheimer, whom the genius of fellow pupil Glenn Gould drove to abandon music and despair. A novel written as a single unbroken monologue.

OL:OL1707618W.title: Oscar & Lucinda
OL:OL1707618W.author: Peter Carey
OL:OL1707618W.description: Oscar Hopkins, an English clergyman, and Lucinda Leplastrier, an Australian heiress who owns a glass factory, meet aboard ship and discover a shared compulsion for gambling, leading to a wager to haul a glass church across the New South Wales wilderness. A novel that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL928455W.title: The Famished Road
OL:OL928455W.author: Ben Okri
OL:OL928455W.description: Azaro, a spirit-child who has chosen to stay among the living, moves through the poverty, bars, and political violence of an African city while spirits keep trying to draw him back to their world. A novel mixing everyday life with African spiritual belief that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL2096536W.title: Watership Down
OL:OL2096536W.author: Richard Adams
OL:OL2096536W.description: Warned by his brother Fiver's vision that their warren will be destroyed, the rabbit Hazel leads a small band across the English countryside in search of a safe home, surviving predators, a sinister warren, and the tyrannical General Woundwort. A novel using rabbits and their invented lore to tell an adventure story.

K:6782b3c089d0.title: The Screwtape Letters
K:6782b3c089d0.author: C. S. Lewis
K:6782b3c089d0.description: A senior devil named Screwtape writes thirty-one letters of advice to his nephew Wormwood, a junior tempter assigned to corrupt an ordinary British man and steer him from God toward damnation. A satirical Christian work framed as demonic correspondence.

K:111bd5114ad8.title: Nothing
K:111bd5114ad8.author: Henry Green
K:111bd5114ad8.description: Years after an affair nearly wrecked their marriages, the widow Jane Weatherby and the widower John Pomfret are thrown back together in postwar London when their grown children decide to marry, prompting Jane to scheme against the match. A comic novel told almost entirely in dialogue.

K:9a0ea9d7f91e.title: The Professor's House
K:9a0ea9d7f91e.author: Willa Cather
K:9a0ea9d7f91e.description: Godfrey St. Peter, a history professor in a Midwestern lake town, finishes his life's work and moves to a new house but clings to his cramped old study, dwelling on his late student Tom Outland, who discovered cliff dwellings on a New Mexico mesa. A novel about middle age, memory, and disillusionment, structured around Tom Outland's inset narrative.

OL:OL1846845W.title: The Poisonwood Bible
OL:OL1846845W.author: Barbara Kingsolver
OL:OL1846845W.description: Nathan Price, a Baptist missionary, drags his wife and four daughters to the Belgian Congo in 1959, where the family unravels amid disease, famine, and the violent birth of independent Zaire, narrated in turn by the mother and daughters. A novel about colonialism, faith, and an American family's reckoning with Africa.

K:a54fc089b816.title: Stories of Mavis Gallant
K:a54fc089b816.author: Mavis Gallant
K:a54fc089b816.description: Across dozens of stories, expatriates, exiles, and displaced Europeans navigate hotels, rented rooms, and uneasy marriages in postwar Paris, Montreal, and the Riviera. A collection by a Canadian writer long resident in France, known for its precise observation and detached irony.

OL:OL39108W.title: The Secret Agent
OL:OL39108W.author: Joseph Conrad
OL:OL39108W.description: Adolf Verloc, a London shopkeeper and secret agent for a foreign embassy, is pressured to bomb the Greenwich Observatory and enlists his slow-witted brother-in-law Stevie, with disastrous consequences for his family. A novel about anarchists, espionage, and domestic tragedy, based loosely on the 1894 Greenwich bombing.

OL:OL1855944W.title: Atonement
OL:OL1855944W.author: Ian McEwan
OL:OL1855944W.description: In 1935 England, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis misreads a moment between her sister Cecilia and Robbie Turner and accuses him of a crime he did not commit, an error whose consequences follow all three through World War II. A novel about guilt, imagination, and the limits of fiction's atonement.

OL:OL275946W.title: Black Boy
OL:OL275946W.author: Richard Wright
OL:OL275946W.description: Growing up poor and Black in the Jim Crow South, the young narrator endures hunger, family violence, and constant racial humiliation before fleeing to Chicago, where he begins to read, write, and briefly joins the Communist Party. An autobiography tracing the author's childhood and youth.

K:3c196dac60d1.title: The stories of Andre Dubus
K:3c196dac60d1.author: Andre Dubus
K:3c196dac60d1.description: Across twenty-three stories, working-class men and women in mill towns and military bases of New England confront marriage, divorce, faith, and violence in ordinary American lives. A collection by a writer known for his Catholic sensibility and compassion for troubled, unremarkable people.

K:3b31f95c4a6f.title: Mildred Pierce
K:3b31f95c4a6f.author: James M. Cain
K:3b31f95c4a6f.description: In Depression-era Glendale, California, Mildred Pierce leaves her unfaithful husband and builds a chain of restaurants to support her two daughters, lavishing everything on the cold, ambitious Veda, who repays her with contempt. A novel about maternal sacrifice, class striving, and a destructive mother-daughter bond.

OL:OL14858723W.title: A Prayer for Owen Meany
OL:OL14858723W.author: John Irving
OL:OL14858723W.description: In a New Hampshire town, the diminutive, strange-voiced Owen Meany hits a foul ball that kills his best friend John's mother and grows up convinced he is God's instrument, moving toward a fate he believes he has foreseen. A novel about faith, doubt, friendship, and predestination.

K:1deae2d6a81c.title: Tropic of Cancer
K:1deae2d6a81c.author: Henry Miller
K:1deae2d6a81c.description: A struggling American writer scrapes by in 1930s Paris, drifting among friends, prostitutes, and odd jobs while recording his hungers, squalor, and exhilaration in frank, fragmentary episodes. A semi-autobiographical novel whose sexual explicitness led to long obscenity bans in the United States.

K:c539f3784713.title: The Life of Pi
K:c539f3784713.author: Yann Martel
K:c539f3784713.description: After a shipwreck sinks his family's cargo ship, sixteen-year-old Pi Patel survives 227 days adrift in the Pacific in a lifeboat shared with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker. A novel about survival, religion, and storytelling, ending with two competing accounts of his ordeal.

K:fed4131b3954.title: Doctor Faustus
K:fed4131b3954.author: Thomas Mann
K:fed4131b3954.description: Narrated by his devoted friend Serenus Zeitblom in wartime Germany, the brilliant composer Adrian Leverkühn deliberately contracts syphilis and strikes a Faustian bargain for years of creative genius before madness overtakes him. A novel that reworks the Faust legend as an allegory of Germany's descent into Nazism.

K:9b18dd743820.title: The Mayor of Casterbridge
K:9b18dd743820.author: Thomas Hardy
K:9b18dd743820.description: In a fit of drunkenness at a country fair, Michael Henchard sells his wife and daughter, then reforms and rises to become mayor of the Wessex town of Casterbridge, until the past returns to undo him. A novel about pride, fate, and a self-made man's downfall.

OL:OL1326328W.title: The Black Prince
OL:OL1326328W.author: Iris Murdoch
OL:OL1326328W.description: Bradley Pearson, a blocked London writer in his late fifties, falls obsessively in love with the young daughter of his rival Arnold Baffin, and the affair drives him toward a murder charge. A novel framed by competing forewords and postscripts that cast doubt on its narrator.

OL:OL506115W.title: Seize the Day
OL:OL506115W.author: Saul Bellow
OL:OL506115W.description: Over a single day in a New York hotel, the unemployed, divorcing Tommy Wilhelm seeks help from his cold physician father and gambles his last savings on the commodities market through the dubious Dr. Tamkin. A novella about failure, self-deception, and a man at the end of his resources.

OL:OL847902W.title: I Served the King of England
OL:OL847902W.author: Bohumil Hrabal
OL:OL847902W.description: The diminutive Ditě recounts his rise from hotel busboy to waiter to wealthy hotelier in mid-century Czechoslovakia, marrying a German woman as the Nazis invade and losing everything under communism before retreating to solitude. A picaresque novel about ambition, complicity, and Czech history.

K:0ed1a323eb37.title: The Marquise of O— and Other Stories
K:0ed1a323eb37.author: Heinrich von Kleist
K:0ed1a323eb37.description: A widowed Italian noblewoman, finding herself inexplicably pregnant, advertises for the unknown father to come forward and marry her, in the title novella that anchors a collection of eight tales of violence, justice, and the uncanny. A set of novellas including the long story Michael Kohlhaas.

OL:OL98585W.title: The Custom of the Country
OL:OL98585W.author: Edith Wharton
OL:OL98585W.description: Undine Spragg, a beautiful and ruthless midwestern social climber, arrives in New York and marries her way upward through a series of husbands and divorces in pursuit of wealth and status. A satirical novel of manners about American materialism and the marriage market.

K:58e8ae773c4c.title: A Midsummer Night’s Dream
K:58e8ae773c4c.author: William Shakespeare
K:58e8ae773c4c.description: In and around Athens, four young lovers flee into a forest where a mischievous fairy's love potion scrambles their affections, while a troupe of amateur actors rehearses a play and the fairy king and queen quarrel. A comedy interweaving lovers, fairies, and tradesmen on a midsummer night.

K:fbee4c090e26.title: Stones for Ibarra
K:fbee4c090e26.author: Harriet Doerr
K:fbee4c090e26.description: Richard and Sara Everton leave California for the Mexican village of Ibarra to reopen a copper mine once run by Richard's grandfather, only to learn that Richard has a terminal illness as they slowly enter village life. A novel told in linked vignettes about an American couple among Mexican neighbors.

K:028967a6b1e9.title: Alias Grace
K:028967a6b1e9.author: Margaret Atwood
K:028967a6b1e9.description: In nineteenth-century Canada, the imprisoned servant Grace Marks, convicted of two murders, recounts her life to a young doctor investigating whether she is guilty, insane, or wrongly condemned. A novel based on a real 1843 Canadian murder case.

OL:OL1863530W.title: Lucky Jim
OL:OL1863530W.author: Kingsley Amis
OL:OL1863530W.description: Jim Dixon, a bored, resentful junior lecturer at a provincial English university, blunders through faculty politics, a tiresome senior professor, and a clinging colleague while pining for another man's girlfriend. A comic novel satirizing postwar British academic life.

K:096e7d480771.title: The Once and Future King
K:096e7d480771.author: T.H. White
K:096e7d480771.description: The young Arthur, called Wart, is tutored by the wizard Merlyn, draws the sword from the stone, and becomes King Arthur, founding the Round Table before his realm collapses through Lancelot's love for Guenever and Mordred's treachery. A retelling of the Arthurian legend drawn from Malory.

OL:OL5703422W.title: Jonathan Strange & Mr. Norrell
OL:OL5703422W.author: Susanna Clarke
OL:OL5703422W.description: In an alternate Napoleonic-era England where magic has faded into theory, the reclusive Gilbert Norrell revives practical magic and takes the bold Jonathan Strange as a pupil, until their rivalry and a malevolent fairy lead them into ruin. A novel about English magic, presented with extensive mock-scholarly footnotes.

OL:OL43037384W.title: A Suitable Boy
OL:OL43037384W.author: Vikram Seth
OL:OL43037384W.description: In early-1950s newly independent India, Mrs. Rupa Mehra searches for a husband for her student daughter Lata, whose three suitors and four interlinked families play out against politics, land reform, and Hindu-Muslim tension. A long family saga centered on a young woman's marriage choice.

OL:OL498434W.title: The Castle
OL:OL498434W.author: Franz Kafka
OL:OL498434W.description: A land surveyor known only as K. arrives in a village beneath a castle that has supposedly summoned him, then struggles endlessly against an impenetrable bureaucracy that denies him access to the authorities he serves. An unfinished novel about alienation and inscrutable power.

K:0bcd22fa5600.title: Hedda Gabler
K:0bcd22fa5600.author: Henrik Ibsen
K:0bcd22fa5600.description: Newly married and already bored, the general's daughter Hedda Tesman manipulates the lives around her, destroying a former suitor's manuscript and pushing him toward suicide before turning a pistol on herself. A four-act play about a trapped, destructive woman.

OL:OL47266W.title: The Maltese Falcon
OL:OL47266W.author: Dashiell Hammett
OL:OL47266W.description: San Francisco detective Sam Spade takes a case that leaves his partner dead and entangles him with a lying client, a band of crooks, and the hunt for a jewel-encrusted falcon statuette. A hardboiled detective novel that helped define the genre.

K:79eacb04d3c3.title: London Fields
K:79eacb04d3c3.author: Martin Amis
K:79eacb04d3c3.description: In a near-future London awaiting catastrophe, the femme fatale Nicola Six foresees her own murder and maneuvers two men, the brutish Keith Talent and the wealthy Guy Clinch, toward it, observed by a dying narrator. A novel narrated by a writer who chronicles the plot's unfolding.

K:5ea8a38b90a2.title: The Raj Quartet
K:5ea8a38b90a2.author: Paul Scott
K:5ea8a38b90a2.description: Across four novels spanning 1942 to 1947, British officials, soldiers, and Indians live through the final years of the Raj, the story turning on the rape of an Englishwoman and its long aftermath. A tetralogy about the end of British rule in India.

OL:OL798425W.title: The Time of the Doves
OL:OL798425W.author: Mercè Rodoreda
OL:OL798425W.description: In Barcelona before and during the Spanish Civil War, a young woman called Natalia, nicknamed Colometa, marries the domineering Quimet, raises children amid poverty and his obsession with breeding doves, and struggles to survive after he goes to war. A novel narrated in the first person by an ordinary working woman.

OL:OL120601W.title: Two Serious Ladies
OL:OL120601W.author: Jane Bowles
OL:OL120601W.description: Two wealthy women, the eccentric Christina Goering and Mrs. Frieda Copperfield, drift away from respectable life into bars, brothels, and strange entanglements, Copperfield in Panama and Goering among odd men, before meeting again. A modernist novel about two women's pursuit of salvation through dissolution.

OL:OL17081245W.title: Those Who Leave and Those Who Stay
OL:OL17081245W.author: Elena Ferrante
OL:OL17081245W.description: Now grown, Lila works as a laborer in Naples after leaving her husband while Elena earns a degree, publishes a novel, and enters educated society, their friendship straining across the political upheavals of the late 1960s and 1970s. The third of the four Neapolitan Novels.

K:b21d24bb8eed.title: Either/Or: A Fragment of Life
K:b21d24bb8eed.author: Soren Kierkegaard
K:b21d24bb8eed.description: Under the pseudonymous editorship of Victor Eremita, papers by an unnamed aesthete known only as "A" set out a pleasure-seeking way of life, while two long letters from Judge William argue for ethical commitment and marriage. A two-volume philosophical work that contrasts the aesthetic and ethical modes of existence and includes the "Diary of a Seducer."

OL:OL19667678W.title: Wise Blood
OL:OL19667678W.author: Flannery O'Connor
OL:OL19667678W.description: Hazel Motes returns from the war to Tennessee, moves to the city of Taulkinham, and preaches a "Church Without Christ" from the hood of his car, drawing in the museum-obsessed Enoch Emery and the fraudulent blind preacher Asa Hawks. A Southern Gothic novel about faith, doubt, and self-destruction.

OL:OL32195W.title: House of Leaves
OL:OL32195W.author: Mark Z. Danielewski
OL:OL32195W.description: Johnny Truant finds a dead man's manuscript analyzing a documentary film about Will Navidson's house on Ash Tree Lane, which proves larger inside than out and contains a shifting, impossible labyrinth. A novel told through nested narrators, footnotes, and unconventional page layouts and typography.

OL:OL118984W.title: Nana
OL:OL118984W.author: Émile Zola
OL:OL118984W.description: Anna "Nana" Coupeau rises from streetwalker to celebrated courtesan in the Paris of the Second Empire, ruining the rich and powerful men who pursue her before smallpox ends her life. The ninth novel in the Rougon-Macquart series, depicting prostitution and moral decay in 1860s France.

OL:OL505439W.title: Under the Volcano
OL:OL505439W.author: Malcolm Lowry
OL:OL505439W.description: Geoffrey Firmin, an alcoholic former British consul in the Mexican town of Quauhnahuac, drinks through the Day of the Dead in November 1938 as his estranged wife Yvonne and half-brother Hugh try to save him. A novel set across a single day, known for its dense symbolism and stream-of-consciousness style.

OL:OL74676W.title: Portnoy's Complaint
OL:OL74676W.author: Philip Roth
OL:OL74676W.description: Alexander Portnoy, a sexually frustrated young Jewish man, pours out his life to his psychoanalyst Dr. Spielvogel, recounting his domineering mother, his guilt, and his compulsive erotic escapades. A monologue novel that drew controversy for its explicit and comic treatment of sexuality.

OL:OL16547664W.title: Bring up the Bodies
OL:OL16547664W.author: Hilary Mantel
OL:OL16547664W.description: In 1535, Thomas Cromwell serves Henry VIII as the king tires of Anne Boleyn and turns toward Jane Seymour, and Cromwell engineers the queen's arrest, trial, and execution for adultery and treason. The second book in the Wolf Hall trilogy, which won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL18020255W.title: Nora Webster
OL:OL18020255W.author: Colm Tóibín
OL:OL18020255W.description: In County Wexford in the late 1960s, Nora Webster is left a widow with four children after her husband's death and must return to work, manage her grief, and slowly rebuild an independent life. A novel about a widow's recovery in a small Irish town.

OL:OL26496349W.title: Tamarisk Row
OL:OL26496349W.author: Gerald Murnane
OL:OL26496349W.description: In a country town in 1940s Victoria, Clement Killeaton grows up amid his father's gambling debts and his mother's piety, channeling his world into an imagined horse-racing game played in the backyard dust. A debut novel built from long single-paragraph sections, drawn from a Catholic childhood.

OL:OL23020966W.title: Small Things Like These
OL:OL23020966W.author: Claire Keegan
OL:OL23020966W.description: Bill Furlong, a coal and timber merchant in the Irish town of New Ross in December 1985, discovers a mistreated young woman while delivering to the local convent and confronts the town's silence about the Magdalene laundry. A novella based on the history of Ireland's Magdalene laundries.

OL:OL1308096W.title: Suite Française
OL:OL1308096W.author: Irène Némirovsky
OL:OL1308096W.description: In "Storm in June," Parisians flee the city ahead of the advancing German army in 1940, and in "Dolce," a French village lives under German occupation as a local woman is drawn to a billeted officer. Two completed parts of a planned five-part sequence, written during the war and published decades after the author's death at Auschwitz.

OL:OL24598751W.title: One Thousand and One Nights
OL:OL24598751W.author: Anonymous
OL:OL24598751W.description: To delay her own execution, Scheherazade tells King Shahryar a chain of unfinished stories night after night, weaving together tales of merchants, genies, sailors, and caliphs across a thousand and one nights. A collection of Middle Eastern and South Asian folk tales compiled in Arabic during the Islamic Golden Age.

OL:OL8640095W.title: Pather Panchali
OL:OL8640095W.author: Bibhutibhushan Bandopadhyay
OL:OL8640095W.description: In a poor Bengali village, the Roy family struggles to survive as the priest Harihar dreams of better work and his children Apu and Durga roam the countryside, until loss drives the family to leave for Benaras. A coming-of-age novel of rural Bengal, first serialized in 1928.

OL:OL59798W.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
OL:OL59798W.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
OL:OL59798W.description: On the island of Gont, a gifted boy named Ged trains as a wizard, but his pride looses a deadly shadow that pursues him across the archipelago of Earthsea until he turns to face it. A fantasy novel of magic and self-knowledge, first in the Earthsea series.

OL:OL35730490W.title: The Dark Is Rising
OL:OL35730490W.author: Susan Cooper
OL:OL35730490W.description: On his eleventh birthday at the winter solstice, Will Stanton learns he is the last of the Old Ones and must gather six Signs of Power to help the Light hold off the rising Dark. A children's fantasy novel steeped in British folklore, second in The Dark Is Rising Sequence.

OL:OL28988W.title: Northern Lights
OL:OL28988W.author: Philip Pullman
OL:OL28988W.description: Lyra Belacqua, a girl raised at Oxford's Jordan College in a world where each person's soul takes animal form as a daemon, journeys to the Arctic to rescue children abducted for sinister experiments. The first book in the His Dark Materials trilogy, published as The Golden Compass in North America.

OL:OL4321141W.title: The Secret History
OL:OL4321141W.author: Donna Tartt
OL:OL4321141W.description: Richard Papen joins a select group of classics students under Professor Julian Morrow at Hampden College in Vermont, and after a Greek ritual leads to a death, the group murders their classmate Bunny Corcoran to protect their secret. An inverted detective story narrated years after the crime.

OL:OL16032925W.title: The Buddha of Suburbia
OL:OL16032925W.author: Hanif Kureishi
OL:OL16032925W.description: Karim Amir, a mixed-race teenager in 1970s suburban South London, follows his father Haroon, who becomes a fashionable guru, into the city's worlds of theatre, sex, and shifting identities. A coming-of-age novel about race, class, and belonging in England.

OL:OL16607777W.title: Nw
OL:OL16607777W.author: Zadie Smith
OL:OL16607777W.description: In a working-class corner of northwest London, four people raised on the same council estate, including Leah Hanwell and the barrister Natalie Blake, navigate adulthood as one of them is killed in a street robbery. A novel told through shifting narrative styles and perspectives.

OL:OL17202418W.title: Station Eleven
OL:OL17202418W.author: Emily St. John Mandel
OL:OL17202418W.description: A flu pandemic kills most of the world's population the night actor Arthur Leander dies onstage, and twenty years later a young actress named Kirsten travels the Great Lakes region with a troupe performing Shakespeare. A novel that moves between the time before and after the collapse.

OL:OL88877W.title: Maurice
OL:OL88877W.author: E. M. Forster
OL:OL88877W.description: Maurice Hall falls in love with the aristocratic Clive Durham at Cambridge, but after Clive marries a woman, Maurice finds a lasting relationship with the gamekeeper Alec Scudder. A novel of same-sex love in early twentieth-century England, written around 1913 and published after the author's death.

OL:OL27052926W.title: Demon Copperhead
OL:OL27052926W.author: Barbara Kingsolver
OL:OL27052926W.description: Born to a teenage mother in a trailer in the Appalachian mountains of Virginia, the red-haired boy nicknamed Demon Copperhead recounts his passage through foster care, child labor, football, and opioid addiction. A novel reworking David Copperfield in present-day Appalachia, a co-winner of the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL1835957W.title: Fun Home
OL:OL1835957W.author: Alison Bechdel
OL:OL1835957W.description: Alison Bechdel recounts her childhood in rural Pennsylvania with her father Bruce, a funeral director and English teacher who hid his homosexuality, and her own coming out as a lesbian shortly before his death. A graphic memoir about family, sexuality, and literature.

OL:OL573193W.title: Hunger
OL:OL573193W.author: Knut Hamsun
OL:OL573193W.description: A starving young writer wanders the streets of Kristiania, unable to pay his rent or sell his articles, his hunger driving him toward erratic behavior and delusion. An early psychological novel that follows its narrator's deteriorating mind.

OL:OL21784995W.title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveller
OL:OL21784995W.author: Italo Calvino
OL:OL21784995W.description: A Reader buys the new novel only to find it defective, and his attempts to obtain the complete text lead through ten opening chapters of different unfinished books and into a conspiracy involving a fraudulent translator. A novel addressed in the second person, alternating frame chapters with the openings of invented works.

OL:OL3942386W.title: Palm-Wine Drinkard
OL:OL3942386W.author: Amos Tutuola
OL:OL3942386W.description: A man devoted to palm-wine follows his dead tapster into the land of the dead, passing through forests, towns, and encounters with spirits and strange creatures before returning home with a magic egg. A novel based on Yoruba folktales, written in a nonstandard English.

OL:OL712025W.author: Roberto Bolaño
OL:OL712025W.description: Across five linked parts, European critics search for a reclusive German author, a professor and his daughter settle in the Mexican border city of Santa Teresa, and hundreds of women are murdered there as the killings go unsolved. A long posthumous novel centered on violence against women on the Mexican border.

OL:OL77746W.title: Anne of Green Gables
OL:OL77746W.author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
OL:OL77746W.description: Orphan Anne Shirley is mistakenly sent to the elderly siblings Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at their farm Green Gables on Prince Edward Island, where her imagination and temper reshape the household and the village of Avonlea. A coming-of-age novel and the first in a series.

OL:OL17616758W.title: The Sellout
OL:OL17616758W.author: Paul Beatty
OL:OL17616758W.description: A Black man known as "Bonbon" farms on the outskirts of Los Angeles in the vanished town of Dickens, and to put it back on the map he reinstates segregation and takes on an aging former child actor as his slave, eventually facing the Supreme Court. A satirical novel about race in America that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL53071W.title: The English Patient
OL:OL53071W.author: Michael Ondaatje
OL:OL53071W.description: In a bombed Italian villa near the end of World War II, the nurse Hana cares for a badly burned, unidentified man whose memories return to a doomed desert love affair, while the thief Caravaggio and the sapper Kip join them. A novel told out of sequence, joint winner of the Booker Prize.

OL:OL115647W.title: Possession
OL:OL115647W.author: A. S. Byatt
OL:OL115647W.description: Scholars Roland Michell and Maud Bailey uncover a hidden love affair between the Victorian poets Randolph Henry Ash and Christabel LaMotte, and their research draws them together in the present. A novel set in two time periods that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL464517W.title: A Place of Greater Safety
OL:OL464517W.author: Hilary Mantel
OL:OL464517W.description: From childhood through the Terror, Georges Danton, Camille Desmoulins, and Maximilien Robespierre rise through the French Revolution until their friendship breaks and Danton and Desmoulins are sent to the guillotine in 1794. A historical novel of the Revolution told from many viewpoints.

OL:OL25451958W.title: Eugene Onegin
OL:OL25451958W.author: Alexander Pushkin
OL:OL25451958W.description: Eugene Onegin, a bored St. Petersburg dandy, retreats to a country estate, rejects the love of Tatyana Larina, kills his friend Lensky in a duel, and later finds Tatyana married and unattainable. A novel in verse written almost entirely in fourteen-line stanzas.

OL:OL81295W.title: Sons and Lovers
OL:OL81295W.author: D. H. Lawrence
OL:OL81295W.description: In a Nottinghamshire mining town, Gertrude Morel turns away from her coarse collier husband and pours her love into her sons, and her son Paul grows up torn between his devotion to her and his relationships with Miriam and Clara. A semi-autobiographical novel about a mother's possessive bond and a young man's struggle to find independence.

OL:OL20893680W.title: Piranesi
OL:OL20893680W.author: Susanna Clarke
OL:OL20893680W.description: Piranesi lives alone in a vast labyrinthine House of endless halls filled with statues and flooded by tides, keeping careful journals and meeting only a man he calls the Other, until clues suggest the House holds another person and a hidden truth about who he is. A novel that gradually reveals the mystery of its narrator's identity and imprisonment.

OL:OL482454W.title: Cloud Atlas
OL:OL482454W.author: David Mitchell
OL:OL482454W.description: Six nested stories span the South Pacific in the 1850s to a post-apocalyptic future, ranging from a notary's journal and a composer's letters to a present-day publisher's mishaps and a clone's testimony, each interrupted midway and later resumed. A novel built from interlocking narratives across centuries that share recurring motifs and a birthmark.

OL:OL16805415W.title: Americanah
OL:OL16805415W.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
OL:OL16805415W.description: Ifemelu leaves Nigeria to study in the United States, where she starts a popular blog about race, while her teenage love Obinze becomes an undocumented immigrant in London, and years later both return to Lagos. A novel about race, identity, and immigration spanning Nigeria, America, and Britain.

OL:OL697431W.title: Wise Children
OL:OL697431W.author: Angela Carter
