OL:OL697431W.description: On their seventy-fifth birthday, retired showgirl twins Dora and Nora Chance look back over a century of their theatrical family, the illegitimate daughters of Shakespearean actor Melchior Hazard who refused to acknowledge them. A comic novel narrated by Dora that traces three generations of a stage family.

OL:OL37832922W.title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
OL:OL37832922W.author: Shirley Jackson
OL:OL37832922W.description: Eighteen-year-old Merricat Blackwood lives in isolation with her sister Constance and ailing Uncle Julian after the rest of the family died of arsenic poisoning years earlier, shunned by the hostile village until a cousin arrives seeking the family money. A novel told by Merricat about agoraphobia, guilt, and a household under siege.

OL:OL1888776W.title: The Millstone
OL:OL1888776W.author: Margaret Drabble
OL:OL1888776W.description: Rosamund Stacey, a self-reliant young academic in 1960s London, becomes pregnant after a single encounter with a man she barely knows and decides to keep and raise the child alone. A novel about unmarried motherhood, independence, and the British welfare system of the period.

OL:OL19663905W.title: Commonwealth
OL:OL19663905W.author: Ann Patchett
OL:OL19663905W.description: When Bert Cousins kisses Beverly Keating at a christening party in 1960s Los Angeles, two marriages break apart and reform into one blended family, whose six children spend uneasy summers together over the following fifty years. A novel that moves back and forth in time to trace how a single act reshapes two families.

OL:OL24314402W.title: Matrix
OL:OL24314402W.author: Lauren Groff
OL:OL24314402W.description: Cast out of the royal court at seventeen, Marie de France is sent to run a poor, disease-ridden English abbey, where over decades she transforms it into a powerful, self-sufficient community of nuns guided by her visions. A historical novel imagining the life of the medieval poet as a prioress.

OL:OL3991459W.title: The Bone People
OL:OL3991459W.author: Keri Hulme
OL:OL3991459W.description: On the coast of New Zealand's South Island, the reclusive artist Kerewin Holmes is drawn into the lives of Joe Gillayley and his mute foster son Simon, a bond that exposes love, violence, and Māori heritage. A novel blending English and Māori that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL2625431W.title: Kafka on the Shore
OL:OL2625431W.author: Haruki Murakami
OL:OL2625431W.description: Fifteen-year-old Kafka Tamura runs away from his Tokyo home to escape his father's prophecy, while in a parallel thread the aging Nakata, who can talk to cats, searches for something he has lost, their stories converging in a library in Shikoku. A surreal novel weaving two narratives full of dreams, metaphysics, and the supernatural.

OL:OL1057179W.title: Swami and Friends
OL:OL1057179W.author: R. K. Narayan
OL:OL1057179W.description: In the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi, schoolboy Swaminathan navigates lessons, cricket, and quarrels with friends like Rajam and Mani against the backdrop of British colonial rule. A novel about boyhood, friendship, and school life, the first book set in Malgudi.

OL:OL37582070W.title: Praiseworthy
OL:OL37582070W.author: Alexis Wright
OL:OL37582070W.description: In the town of Praiseworthy on Australia's northern coast, an Aboriginal man called Cause Man Steel pursues a scheme to herd donkeys into a transport empire against coming climate collapse, while his wife Dance dreams of China and their sons are pulled apart by assimilation and despair. A long, satirical novel about Indigenous sovereignty, colonialism, and ecological crisis.

OL:OL2163649W.title: The Hitch Hiker's Guide to the Galaxy
OL:OL2163649W.author: Douglas Adams
OL:OL2163649W.description: Moments before Earth is demolished to make way for a hyperspace bypass, Arthur Dent is rescued by his friend Ford Prefect, an alien researcher for a galactic guidebook, and the two hitchhike across space alongside the two-headed Zaphod Beeblebrox and a depressed robot. A comic science-fiction novel that began as a radio series.

OL:OL26435W.title: The Girls of Slender Means
OL:OL26435W.author: Muriel Spark
OL:OL26435W.description: In a London hostel for young single women in 1945, the residents of the May of Teck Club share clothes, romances, and ambitions in the months between VE Day and VJ Day, until a fire and a hidden danger upend their lives. A short novel set against the end of the Second World War.

OL:OL74293W.title: Riddley Walker
OL:OL74293W.author: Russell Hoban
OL:OL74293W.description: Generations after a nuclear catastrophe, a young man named Riddley Walker comes of age in a primitive, half-literate England, narrating in a broken future dialect as he uncovers fragments of lost knowledge and a Punch-and-Judy myth. A novel written entirely in an invented degraded English.

OL:OL3958403W.title: Paradise
OL:OL3958403W.author: Abdulrazak Gurnah
OL:OL3958403W.description: Yusuf, a boy in early twentieth-century East Africa, is pawned by his indebted father to a merchant named Aziz and travels with trading caravans into the interior as German colonial power tightens its grip. A novel about servitude and coming of age on the eve of the First World War.

OL:OL931688W.title: Lives of Girls and Women
OL:OL931688W.author: Alice Munro
OL:OL931688W.description: Del Jordan grows up in the small Ontario town of Jubilee in the 1940s, moving through childhood, school, religion, first love, and her ambition to become a writer, observed alongside her encyclopedia-selling mother. A book of linked stories following one girl's coming of age.

OL:OL39379W.title: A Room of One's Own
OL:OL39379W.author: Virginia Woolf
OL:OL39379W.description: Asked to speak on women and fiction, the narrator argues through a series of reflections, including the invented figure of Shakespeare's gifted sister, that a woman needs money and a room of her own to write. An extended essay on women, literature, and the conditions of creativity.

OL:OL107195W.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
OL:OL107195W.author: John Bunyan
OL:OL107195W.description: Christian, burdened by sin, flees the City of Destruction and journeys toward the Celestial City, passing through the Slough of Despond, Vanity Fair, and other allegorical trials with companions like Faithful and Hopeful. A Christian allegory of the believer's spiritual journey, written partly in prison.

OL:OL17764836W.title: Human Acts
OL:OL17764836W.author: Han Kang
OL:OL17764836W.description: After a teenage boy named Dong-ho is killed during the 1980 Gwangju uprising in South Korea, a series of narrators connected to him, including the dead, survivors, and a grieving mother, recount the massacre and its long aftermath. A novel told through linked voices about state violence and its survivors.

OL:OL21678662W.title: Afterlives
OL:OL21678662W.author: Abdulrazak Gurnah
OL:OL21678662W.description: On the East African coast under German colonial rule, Ilyas returns from being conscripted as a colonial soldier while the orphaned Afiya and the young Hamza, who served in the German army, build lives shadowed by war across the first half of the twentieth century. A novel tracing ordinary lives through colonialism and its wars.

OL:OL1875009W.title: Gilead
OL:OL1875009W.author: Marilynne Robinson
OL:OL1875009W.description: In 1956 Iowa, the elderly Congregationalist minister John Ames, dying of heart disease, writes a long letter to his young son recalling his father and abolitionist grandfather and the return of his namesake, a prodigal godson. A novel in the form of one preacher's testament to his child.

OL:OL1449782W.title: All Our Yesterdays
OL:OL1449782W.author: Natalia Ginzburg
OL:OL1449782W.description: In an Italian provincial town before and during the Second World War, Anna and her siblings come of age amid family troubles, fascism, and the war, as Anna's marriage to the older Cenzo Rena draws her into the resistance and its losses. A novel about two families living through Italy's fascist era and the war.

OL:OL1103093W.title: Cranford
OL:OL1103093W.author: Elizabeth Gaskell
OL:OL1103093W.description: In the small English town of Cranford, a community of genteel, mostly unmarried older women led by Miss Matty Jenkyns manage on small incomes, guarding social proprieties through small dramas, a railway, and sudden misfortune. A series of linked sketches of provincial life narrated by a younger visitor.

OL:OL506116W.title: The Adventures of Augie March
OL:OL506116W.author: Saul Bellow
OL:OL506116W.description: Augie March grows up poor in Depression-era Chicago and drifts through a string of jobs, schemes, and lovers, from book theft and union work to eagle-hunting in Mexico, refusing to be pinned to any single fate. A picaresque novel narrated in exuberant first-person voice.

OL:OL11728724W.title: Too Loud a Solitude
OL:OL11728724W.author: Bohumil Hrabal
OL:OL11728724W.description: For thirty-five years Hanťa has compacted wastepaper and discarded books in a Prague cellar, secretly rescuing volumes and absorbing their learning, until a new automated press threatens his trade. A short novel narrated by a self-taught crusher of books under a repressive regime.

OL:OL11690127W.title: The Memory Police
OL:OL11690127W.author: Yoko Ogawa
OL:OL11690127W.description: On an unnamed island, objects and concepts vanish one by one and the inhabitants forget them, enforced by the Memory Police who hunt down those who still remember, while a novelist hides her editor to protect his lingering memories. A dystopian novel about memory, loss, and surveillance.

OL:OL17370186W.title: A Little Life
OL:OL17370186W.author: Hanya Yanagihara
OL:OL17370186W.description: Four college friends, Willem, JB, Malcolm, and the brilliant, damaged lawyer Jude St. Francis, build careers and lives in New York over decades, as Jude's hidden history of abuse continues to mark him. A long novel centered on trauma, friendship, and self-harm.

OL:OL27905681W.title: Siddhartha
OL:OL27905681W.author: Hermann Hesse
OL:OL27905681W.description: In ancient India, the Brahmin's son Siddhartha leaves home to seek enlightenment, passing through asceticism, sensual love with the courtesan Kamala, and wealth before finding wisdom beside a river and its ferryman. A novel about one man's spiritual search set in the time of the Buddha.

OL:OL112769W.title: Lolly Willowes, Or, the Loving Huntsman
OL:OL112769W.author: Sylvia Townsend Warner
OL:OL112769W.description: Laura Willowes, an unmarried Englishwoman expected to spend her life serving her brother's household, breaks away to a remote village called Great Mop, where she discovers it is full of witches and makes a pact with the Devil. A novel about a spinster's escape into independence and witchcraft.

OL:OL32028W.title: Who Will Run the Frog Hospital?
OL:OL32028W.author: Lorrie Moore
OL:OL32028W.description: Middle-aged Berie Carr, unhappily married and traveling in Paris, recalls the summer of 1972 in upstate New York, when at fifteen she worked at an amusement park and idolized her bolder best friend Sils. A short novel about adolescent friendship recalled from adulthood.

OL:OL16810448W.title: Life After Life
OL:OL16810448W.author: Kate Atkinson
OL:OL16810448W.description: Ursula Todd is born in England in 1910 and dies repeatedly, living her life over and over with variations that send her through both World Wars and, in one version, toward a plan to kill Hitler. A novel structured around a woman who relives her life many times.

OL:OL1437339W.title: The Tartar Steppe
OL:OL1437339W.author: Dino Buzzati
OL:OL1437339W.description: Giovanni Drogo, a young officer, is posted to the remote Bastiani Fortress on the edge of a desert, where he spends his life waiting for an enemy invasion across the northern steppe that never comes. A novel about anticipation and the passing of time, often compared to the work of Kafka.

OL:OL26427W.title: Loitering With Intent
OL:OL26427W.author: Muriel Spark
OL:OL26427W.description: In London around 1949, aspiring novelist Fleur Talbot takes a job running the Autobiographical Association for the controlling Sir Quentin Oliver, then discovers that events from her unfinished novel are bleeding into real life as Quentin plagiarizes and exploits her manuscript. A short, autobiographical novel shortlisted for the Booker Prize, about the blurring of fiction and life.

OL:OL15196311W.title: The Piano Teacher
OL:OL15196311W.author: Elfriede Jelinek
OL:OL15196311W.description: Erika Kohut, a repressed piano teacher at the Vienna Conservatory who still shares a bed with her domineering mother, begins a sadomasochistic relationship with her student Walter Klemmer that ends in violence. A novel by the Austrian writer who later won the Nobel Prize, adapted into a 2001 film.

OL:OL23199W.title: Cannery Row
OL:OL23199W.author: John Steinbeck
OL:OL23199W.description: On Cannery Row in Monterey, California, the marine biologist Doc, the Chinese grocer Lee Chong, and Mack and his gang of unemployed drifters live among the sardine canneries, and the men try to throw Doc a party that goes badly wrong. A short, episodic novel about life among the poor of a coastal town.

OL:OL20877028W.title: Restoration
OL:OL20877028W.author: Rose Tremain
OL:OL20877028W.description: Robert Merivel, a medical student in the reign of Charles II, wins royal favor by curing the king's dog and is made a sham husband to one of the king's mistresses, but his fall from grace leads him through the plague and the Great Fire of London. A historical novel shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL37572547W.title: The Safekeep
OL:OL37572547W.author: Yael van der Wouden
OL:OL37572547W.description: In 1961 rural Netherlands, the reclusive Isabel guards her late mother's house until her brother's girlfriend Eva comes to stay for the summer, and their wary relationship turns to desire as Isabel uncovers how the family acquired the home during the war. A debut novel that won the Women's Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL55238W.title: The Book of Daniel
OL:OL55238W.author: E. L. Doctorow
OL:OL55238W.description: Daniel Isaacson, a graduate student in the radical politics of the 1960s, reconstructs the story of his parents Paul and Rochelle, communists executed as atomic spies in a case modeled on the Rosenbergs, while his sister Susan breaks down. A novel told through fragmented narration and shifting perspectives.

OL:OL1244914W.title: La Princesse De Cleves
OL:OL1244914W.author: Madame de La Fayette
OL:OL1244914W.description: At the court of Henri II of France, the young and virtuous Princesse de Clèves falls in love with the Duc de Nemours but stays loyal to her husband, even confessing her passion to him rather than act on it. Published anonymously, it is regarded as one of the first psychological novels.

OL:OL17873642W.title: Outline
OL:OL17873642W.author: Rachel Cusk
OL:OL17873642W.description: A British writer flies to Athens to teach a summer writing course, and across ten encounters she mostly listens as strangers, students, and friends tell her about their marriages, ambitions, and disappointments, revealing herself only by reflection. The first book in a trilogy, built almost entirely from reported conversation.

OL:OL671818W.title: The Dirty Dust
OL:OL671818W.author: Máirtín Ó Cadhain
OL:OL671818W.description: In a Connemara graveyard, the recently buried dead keep talking, and Caitríona Pháidín carries on her lifelong feud with her sister Neil amid the gossip, grudges, and scandal of the corpses around her. Written in Irish and considered a landmark of the language's modern literature.

K:cc83b0188ed4.title: The Confidence-Man: His Masquerade
K:cc83b0188ed4.author: Herman Melville
K:cc83b0188ed4.description: On April Fool's Day, a series of con men board the Mississippi steamboat Fidèle and test the trust of the passengers, taking on disguises as a beggar, an herb doctor, and a genial cosmopolitan in a string of episodes and debates. The last novel its author published in his lifetime, a satire of American optimism and credulity.

K:d47d8cd099f0.title: The Book of Evidence
K:d47d8cd099f0.author: John Banville
K:d47d8cd099f0.description: Freddie Montgomery, a cultured and amoral scientist returned to Ireland in debt, tries to steal a Dutch painting from a family friend and bludgeons to death a maid who catches him, then narrates his crime and trial from prison. A novel shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the first of a trilogy.

K:8a9c82a087df.title: The Lost Father
K:8a9c82a087df.author: Mona Simpson
K:8a9c82a087df.description: Mayan Atassi, a medical student in New York, becomes obsessed with finding the Egyptian father who abandoned her and her mother in childhood, hiring detectives and searching across the United States and the Middle East before tracing him to California. A sequel that continues the story of the narrator of an earlier novel.

K:ffa3f721b881.title: Sergeant Getulio
K:ffa3f721b881.author: João Ubaldo Ribeiro
K:ffa3f721b881.description: Sergeant Getúlio, a brutal policeman in the backlands of Sergipe, Brazil, is ordered to transport a political prisoner across the state and presses on with the journey even after being told to release the man, narrating his violence in a long monologue. A novel told in the sergeant's rough vernacular voice.

K:1a0c06d3d2a9.title: Closely Watched Trains
K:1a0c06d3d2a9.author: Bohumil Hrabal
K:1a0c06d3d2a9.description: At a small railway station in German-occupied Czechoslovakia near the end of the war, the young apprentice dispatcher Miloš Hrma struggles with his sexual inexperience and a suicide attempt while the lecherous Hubička plots to sabotage a German munitions train. A novella adapted into an Oscar-winning Czech film.

K:d5233d03a440.title: Olive Kitteridge
K:d5233d03a440.author: Elizabeth Strout
K:d5233d03a440.description: Across thirteen linked stories set in the coastal town of Crosby, Maine, the blunt retired schoolteacher Olive Kitteridge appears at the center or the edges of her neighbors' lives, enduring her husband's stroke, her son's distance, and her own old age. A book of stories that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

K:3514747cc632.title: Edwin Mullhouse : The Life and Death of an American Writer 1943-1954 by Jeffrey Cartwright
K:3514747cc632.author: Steven Millhauser
K:3514747cc632.description: Jeffrey Cartwright writes a meticulous biography of his childhood neighbor Edwin Mullhouse, a suburban boy who composes a novel called Cartoons and dies mysteriously at age eleven, chronicling Edwin's life from baby talk to his final feverish work. A debut novel framed as the biography of a child genius.

K:4887539c2e6c.title: Anywhere but Here
K:4887539c2e6c.author: Mona Simpson
K:4887539c2e6c.description: Adele August and her twelve-year-old daughter Ann drive west from Bay City, Wisconsin, to Beverly Hills in an unpaid-for Lincoln so Ann can become a child star, while relatives left behind tell their own side of the story. A novel about an unstable, ambitious mother and her daughter, narrated across several voices.

K:8af4cd2c59d0.title: Save Me the Waltz
K:8af4cd2c59d0.author: Zelda Fitzgerald
K:8af4cd2c59d0.description: Alabama Beggs, a Southern judge's daughter, marries the painter David Knight and lives a glamorous Jazz Age life in New York and Europe before throwing herself into ballet, until an infected foot ends her hope of becoming a prima ballerina. A semi-autobiographical novel and its author's only published novel.

K:79ce80bb8360.title: The World According to Garp
K:79ce80bb8360.author: John Irving
K:79ce80bb8360.description: T. S. Garp, conceived when his nurse mother Jenny Fields impregnates herself by a dying soldier, grows up to become a writer and family man whose life is marked by wrestling, fiction, and sudden violence amid his mother's rise as a feminist icon. A bestselling novel later adapted into a film.

K:7caeae871bb0.title: A Sportsman's Notebook
K:7caeae871bb0.author: Ivan Turgenev
K:7caeae871bb0.description: A hunting gentleman wanders the Russian countryside and recounts his encounters with the peasants and landowners he meets, in a cycle of sketches that quietly expose the cruelties of serfdom. A collection credited with helping turn public opinion toward the abolition of serfdom.

K:fc982ab632c4.title: A Personal Matter
K:fc982ab632c4.author: Kenzaburo Oë
K:fc982ab632c4.description: Bird, a frustrated young man in Japan whose wife gives birth to a brain-damaged baby, drifts through drink and an affair while wrestling with whether to let the infant die or accept responsibility for it. A semi-autobiographical novel by a writer who later won the Nobel Prize.

K:0b5a2838b308.title: Henry V
K:0b5a2838b308.author: William Shakespeare
K:0b5a2838b308.description: The young King Henry V presses his claim to the French throne, invades France, and against overwhelming odds wins the Battle of Agincourt before wooing the French princess Katherine to seal peace between the two crowns. A history play known for its patriotic speeches, including the St Crispin's Day oration.

K:f0a6ce516e75.title: Hombre
K:f0a6ce516e75.author: Elmore Leonard
K:f0a6ce516e75.description: John Russell, a white man raised by Apaches, is shunned by the other passengers of a stagecoach until outlaws rob them and strand them in the desert, where his survival skills make him their reluctant leader. A western novel later adapted into a film starring Paul Newman.

K:dc15508e1ca2.title: Oryx and Crake
K:dc15508e1ca2.author: Margaret Atwood
K:dc15508e1ca2.description: Snowman, who may be the last human alive, survives among genetically engineered Crakers after a plague, and recalls his earlier life as Jimmy alongside his brilliant friend Crake and the woman Oryx in a corporate-run world. The first book of a speculative trilogy, shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

K:d27ac1dd1b67.title: Montana 1948
K:d27ac1dd1b67.author: Larry Watson
K:d27ac1dd1b67.description: In the small town of Bentrock, Montana, twelve-year-old David Hayden watches his sheriff father confront his own brother, a respected war-hero doctor accused of sexually assaulting Native American women, forcing the family to choose between loyalty and justice. A short novel narrated by David as an adult.

K:46d79f6e7173.title: A Fan’s Notes
K:46d79f6e7173.author: Frederick Exley
K:46d79f6e7173.description: A man named Fred Exley drifts through upstate New York, bars, and mental hospitals, obsessed with the New York Giants and the football star Frank Gifford, as he reckons with alcoholism, failure, and his distance from the American dream. A semi-autobiographical work subtitled a fictional memoir.

K:d36692a00746.title: True Grit
K:d36692a00746.author: Charles Portis
K:d36692a00746.description: Fourteen-year-old Mattie Ross hires the hard-drinking, one-eyed U.S. marshal Rooster Cogburn to track down Tom Chaney, the hired hand who murdered her father, and insists on riding into Indian Territory with him and a Texas Ranger named LaBoeuf. A western narrated by Mattie as an old woman, twice adapted into film.

K:dd4cd6f4f20e.title: Clockers
K:dd4cd6f4f20e.author: Richard Price
K:dd4cd6f4f20e.description: In the fictional New Jersey city of Dempsy, low-level cocaine dealer Strike works the housing-project trade while homicide detective Rocco Klein investigates a killing that Strike's straight-arrow brother has confessed to, suspecting Strike is really to blame. A crime novel later adapted into a film by Spike Lee.

K:efbff58fd7a8.title: Pricksongs & Descants
K:efbff58fd7a8.author: Robert Coover
K:efbff58fd7a8.description: A collection of experimental short fictions that retell fairy tales, biblical stories, and folk myths in fractured forms, including "The Babysitter," which spins one evening into dozens of overlapping versions. An influential early work of American postmodern fiction.

K:6417f1b08a9e.title: The Railway Children
K:6417f1b08a9e.author: E. Nesbit
K:6417f1b08a9e.description: After their father is imprisoned on a false charge of spying, Roberta, Peter, and Phyllis move with their mother to a cottage called Three Chimneys near a railway line, where they befriend an old gentleman who eventually helps clear their father's name. A children's classic set beside an English railway.

K:4c60eb382dfb.title: JR
K:4c60eb382dfb.author: William Gaddis
K:4c60eb382dfb.description: Eleven-year-old J R Vansant, inspired by a school field trip to Wall Street, uses payphones and mail orders to parlay penny stocks into a sprawling paper empire of companies, with his music teacher's friend Edward Bast pulled in to front it. A novel told almost entirely in unattributed dialogue, winner of the National Book Award.

K:dc6a20c417be.title: Voyage of the 'Dawn Treader'
K:dc6a20c417be.author: C. S. Lewis
K:dc6a20c417be.description: Edmund and Lucy Pevensie and their cousin Eustace are pulled into Narnia aboard King Caspian's ship the Dawn Treader, which sails east past strange islands toward the world's end in search of seven lost lords, accompanied by the valiant mouse Reepicheep. The third published book of the Narnia series.

K:6e30a694fd3c.title: The Lorax
K:6e30a694fd3c.author: Dr
K:6e30a694fd3c.description: The Once-ler recounts how he chopped down the colorful Truffula trees to manufacture Thneeds, ignoring the Lorax who speaks for the trees until the land is polluted and barren. A rhymed children's picture book about environmental destruction and corporate greed.

K:8ef0f612f76c.title: The War with the Newts
K:8ef0f612f76c.author: Karel Capek
K:8ef0f612f76c.description: A sea captain discovers a race of intelligent newts near Sumatra, and humans soon enslave and exploit them for pearl diving and coastal engineering until the newts acquire human knowledge, multiply, and wage war to flood the continents for living space. A satirical science fiction novel mocking nationalism, racial theory, and colonial exploitation.

K:6a5199e9f862.title: Auto-da-Fé
K:6a5199e9f862.author: Elias Canetti
K:6a5199e9f862.description: Peter Kien, a reclusive Viennese philologist devoted to his vast library, marries his greedy housekeeper Therese, who throws him out into the city's underworld, and his unraveling ends when he sets fire to his books. A novel known for its grotesque comedy and its portrait of an isolated intellectual's descent into madness.

K:896212b4cae6.title: Red the Fiend
K:896212b4cae6.author: Gilbert Sorrentino
K:896212b4cae6.description: Red, a brutalized Irish-American boy, lives with his mother in his grandparents' Brooklyn home, where his sadistic grandmother torments him with beatings, spoiled food, and cruel errands until he grows into a violent adolescent. A novel built from short repetitive episodes that traces how abuse shapes a child.

K:2eac8d90cd3c.title: Masquerade and Other Stories
K:2eac8d90cd3c.author: Robert Walser
K:2eac8d90cd3c.description: Sketches, scenes, and short prose pieces wander through landscapes, dreamscapes, and city streets, observing servants, clerks, and ordinary moments with skewed comparisons and sudden shifts of perspective. A selection of the author's short prose written across his career, valued for its playful, digressive style.

K:5de38993394d.title: Goodbye, Columbus
K:5de38993394d.author: Philip Roth
K:5de38993394d.description: Neil Klugman, a Newark library clerk, spends a summer romancing Brenda Patimkin, a wealthy Radcliffe student from suburban Short Hills, and their class differences strain the affair. The title novella appears with five short stories on Jewish-American life; the book won the National Book Award.

K:c38bae3f9782.title: The Way of All Flesh
K:c38bae3f9782.author: Samuel Butler
K:c38bae3f9782.description: Ernest Pontifex grows up under his domineering clergyman father Theobald, drifts into a disastrous marriage and prison, and finally breaks free of his family's expectations, all narrated by his godfather Overton. A semi-autobiographical novel, published posthumously, that attacks Victorian family life and religious hypocrisy.

K:90e7c6ad9946.title: Cane
K:90e7c6ad9946.author: Jean Toomer
K:90e7c6ad9946.description: Interlinked stories, poems, and a dramatic sketch move from rural Georgia through the urban North and back south, depicting Black women, men, and communities. An experimental work mixing prose, verse, and drama, associated with the Harlem Renaissance.

K:ddb8f05c3627.title: A Clockwork Orange
K:ddb8f05c3627.author: Anthony Burgess
K:ddb8f05c3627.description: Alex, the teenage leader of a gang who speaks the invented slang Nadsat and delights in violence, is jailed and subjected to aversion therapy that strips him of free will. A dystopian novel exploring conditioning, criminality, and moral choice.

K:ec96ab3c1683.title: Angle of Repose
K:ec96ab3c1683.author: Wallace Stegner
K:ec96ab3c1683.description: Lyman Ward, a wheelchair-bound retired historian, pieces together the marriage of his grandparents, the genteel artist Susan Burling and the engineer Oliver Ward, as they move through frontier mining towns in the nineteenth-century American West. A novel about marriage, ambition, and the settling of the West that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:5e80ea6b9d08.title: Bluebeard
K:5e80ea6b9d08.author: Kurt Vonnegut
K:5e80ea6b9d08.description: Rabo Karabekian, an aging one-eyed Armenian-American painter once part of the Abstract Expressionist movement, writes his autobiography at his East Hampton estate while refusing to reveal what he keeps locked in his potato barn. A novel about art, war, and the Armenian genocide framed as a fictional memoir.

K:f4b1dfef3b9c.title: Tell Me a Riddle
K:f4b1dfef3b9c.author: Tillie Olsen
K:f4b1dfef3b9c.description: The title novella follows an elderly married couple, Russian-Jewish immigrants, who quarrel over how to spend their final years as the wife is dying of cancer and revisits the ideals of her youth. A collection of a novella and three stories about working-class women and family life.

K:4c91ce3a8a63.title: Works of William Shakespeare
K:4c91ce3a8a63.author: William Shakespeare
K:4c91ce3a8a63.description: The plays, sonnets, and narrative poems gather tragedies such as Hamlet and King Lear, comedies, English histories, and the sonnet sequence. The collected works of the English playwright, central to the literary canon and continuously performed worldwide.

K:ee0cb4357f1c.title: The Thin Man
K:ee0cb4357f1c.author: Dashiell Hammett
K:ee0cb4357f1c.description: Retired detective Nick Charles and his wealthy wife Nora are drawn into the disappearance of an eccentric inventor and a related murder while drinking their way through New York society. A hardboiled detective novel known for its witty banter between the married sleuths.

K:1e17977a66bd.title: Parables and Paradoxes
K:1e17977a66bd.author: Franz Kafka
K:1e17977a66bd.description: Short parables and aphorisms rework myths and biblical and classical figures, including Prometheus, the Sirens, the Tower of Babel, and Sancho Panza, alongside fragments drawn from notebooks and letters. A posthumous compilation of brief enigmatic pieces by the author.

K:01d151000e8d.title: Fiskadoro
K:01d151000e8d.author: Denis Johnson
K:01d151000e8d.description: Decades after a nuclear holocaust, in the Florida Keys town of Twicetown, the teenage Fiskadoro and his clarinet teacher Mr. Cheung live among survivors who have lost most memory of the past, including a hundred-year-old grandmother who recalls the fall of Saigon. A post-apocalyptic novel about memory, culture, and survival.

K:1553218ce7b2.title: The Messiah of Stockholm
K:1553218ce7b2.author: Cynthia Ozick
K:1553218ce7b2.description: Lars Andemening, a lonely book reviewer in Stockholm, believes he is the son of the Polish writer Bruno Schulz, and his world is upended when a woman appears claiming to hold the manuscript of Schulz's lost novel The Messiah. A short novel about Holocaust memory, literary obsession, and forgery.

K:db767ae52941.title: Lucy
K:db767ae52941.author: Jamaica Kincaid
K:db767ae52941.description: Lucy, a nineteen-year-old from the Caribbean, takes a job as an au pair for a wealthy white couple in a North American city, observing their unraveling marriage while reckoning with her anger toward her mother and her colonial upbringing. A novel about migration, identity, and a young woman's break from her past.

K:dc60bff5362f.title: V.
K:dc60bff5362f.author: Thomas Pynchon
K:dc60bff5362f.description: Benny Profane drifts among a crew of New York bohemians while Herbert Stencil pursues clues to a mysterious woman or entity known only as V. across decades and continents. A debut novel weaving two storylines into an intricate puzzle of history and conspiracy.

K:bd7c5b4ada3f.title: The White Album
K:bd7c5b4ada3f.author: Joan Didion
K:bd7c5b4ada3f.description: Essays examine California and American life in the late 1960s and 1970s, covering the Manson murders, the Black Panthers, Hollywood, water politics, and the author's own experiences. A collection of journalism that surveys the unraveling of the era's culture.

K:62b0567b695e.title: Last Exit to Brooklyn
K:62b0567b695e.author: Hubert Selby
K:62b0567b695e.description: Linked stories set among the bars, factories, and tenements of 1950s Brooklyn depict prostitutes, dockworkers, a striking labor union, a transvestite, and a brutal gang rape. A novel told in stark vernacular that drew an obscenity trial in Britain.

K:252d8e6a371c.title: Stories of Carson McCullers
K:252d8e6a371c.author: Carson McCullers
K:252d8e6a371c.description: Stories follow lonely and yearning characters across small Southern towns, among them a deaf-mute, a boy who hires himself out, and a wife discovering her husband's affair. A gathering of the author's short fiction, including "The Ballad of the Sad Café."

K:8ea95c8da16e.title: Long Day’s Journey into Night
K:8ea95c8da16e.author: Eugene O’Neill
K:8ea95c8da16e.description: Over one long day at their Connecticut summer home, the Tyrone family confronts the mother's morphine addiction, the father's miserliness, and the sons' drinking and illness, as old grievances resurface. A largely autobiographical play, published and staged after the author's death, that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:efb5a50a426d.title: The Prelude
K:efb5a50a426d.author: William Wordsworth
K:efb5a50a426d.description: In blank verse, the poet traces his own life from childhood through his schooling, his time in revolutionary France, a spiritual crisis, and his recovery, examining how nature shaped his imagination. A long autobiographical poem published after the poet's death.

K:f9197dea01cf.title: Casa Guidi Windows
K:f9197dea01cf.author: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
K:f9197dea01cf.description: From the windows of her Florence home, the speaker watches the Italian struggle against Austrian rule, voicing early hope for the Risorgimento in the first part and sober disappointment in the second. A long political poem in two parts on Italian unification.

K:338726f56a1d.title: The Giving Tree
K:338726f56a1d.author: Shel Silverstein
K:338726f56a1d.description: A tree gives a boy her apples, branches, and finally her trunk over the course of his life, asking nothing in return as he grows old. A children's picture book about generosity and the relationship between giving and taking.

K:5ffdad6601d4.title: Bertha
K:5ffdad6601d4.description: Bertha, a Norwegian queen, repeatedly leads her people into war against barbarian invaders whenever she grows bored with peacetime rule, demanding fresh conquests and ceremonies. A short comic verse play.

K:b874087092e5.title: Blithe Spirit
K:b874087092e5.author: Noël Coward
K:b874087092e5.description: The novelist Charles Condomine holds a séance with the eccentric medium Madame Arcati that accidentally summons the ghost of his first wife Elvira, visible only to him, to the dismay of his second wife Ruth. A comedy about a haunted second marriage.

K:424e6fcde8db.title: When I Grow Too Old to Dream
K:424e6fcde8db.author: Oscar Hammerstein
K:424e6fcde8db.description: A romantic ballad whose lyrics promise that even when youth and dreams fade, the singer will remember a beloved, introduced in the film The Night Is Young. A popular song standard of the 1930s.

K:155118d6152f.title: Seven Pillars of Wisdom
K:155118d6152f.author: T. E. Lawrence
K:155118d6152f.description: The author recounts his role advising the Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire during the First World War, describing desert guerrilla campaigns, the capture of Aqaba and Damascus, and his own divided loyalties. An autobiographical account of the Arabian campaign.

K:7aacbb2da237.title: Man’s Fate
K:7aacbb2da237.author: André Malraux
K:7aacbb2da237.description: During the failed 1927 Communist uprising in Shanghai, revolutionaries including the half-French Kyo and the terrorist Chen fight Chiang Kai-shek's forces and face capture and execution. A novel about revolution, terror, and the meaning of action, which won the Prix Goncourt.

K:c5bdc240b49e.title: Black Lamb and Grey Falcon: A Journey Through Yugoslavia
K:c5bdc240b49e.author: Rebecca West
K:c5bdc240b49e.description: An account of the author's travels through Yugoslavia in the late 1930s interweaves Balkan landscapes and people with long digressions on the region's history, religion, and politics. A travel book over a thousand pages long, widely regarded as a major work of the genre.

K:8454daa94c7a.title: Darkness at Noon
K:8454daa94c7a.author: Arthur Koestler
K:8454daa94c7a.description: Rubashov, an old Bolshevik imprisoned during the Stalinist purges, is interrogated by the regime he helped build and pressured to confess to crimes he did not commit. A novel about totalitarianism and the show trials.

K:4572192529ff.title: Homage to Catalonia
K:4572192529ff.author: George Orwell
K:4572192529ff.description: A memoir of fighting in the Spanish Civil War, recounting the author's training in Barcelona, service on the Aragon front with the POUM militia, a throat wound, and the May 1937 street fighting that turned him against Soviet-backed suppression of his own side. A firsthand account of the war that shaped his political outlook.

K:214345a72a1d.title: Kaputt
K:214345a72a1d.author: Curzio Malaparte
K:214345a72a1d.description: A war correspondent travels the Eastern Front of World War II, moving through the siege of Leningrad, dinners with Nazi officials, and corpse-laden trains in devastated Romania, in six sections each named for an animal. A largely fictionalized witness account written by a former fascist sympathizer.

K:a84147873529.title: Kidnapped
K:a84147873529.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
K:a84147873529.description: Orphaned David Balfour goes to claim his inheritance from his miserly uncle Ebenezer in mid-eighteenth-century Scotland, is kidnapped onto a ship bound for the Carolina plantations, and after a shipwreck flees across the Highlands with the Jacobite Alan Breck Stewart. An adventure novel of David's journey to recover his rights.

K:ce25ec2e8db5.title: The Europeans
K:ce25ec2e8db5.author: Henry James
K:ce25ec2e8db5.description: Eugenia Münster and her brother Felix Young, two Europeanized siblings, arrive in mid-nineteenth-century New England to visit their plain-living Wentworth relatives, and the contrast in manners reshapes everyone's plans for marriage. A short comedy about the meeting of Old World and New World attitudes.

K:c446848d2470.title: The English Teacher
K:c446848d2470.author: R. K. Narayan
K:c446848d2470.description: Krishna, an English lecturer at a college in Malgudi, settles into family life when his wife Susila and daughter Leela join him, then loses Susila to typhoid and turns to communicating with her through a medium. An autobiographical novel about grief and the search for inner peace.

K:ba0db5877d24.title: Gaudy Night
K:ba0db5877d24.author: Dorothy L. Sayers
K:ba0db5877d24.description: Harriet Vane returns to her Oxford women's college, Shrewsbury, for a reunion and is drawn into investigating a campaign of poison-pen letters and vandalism, eventually with help from Lord Peter Wimsey. A detective novel that centers on women's right to academic life.

K:234979824b21.title: Daybook: The Journey of an Artist
K:234979824b21.author: Anne Truitt
K:234979824b21.description: Over seven years of journal entries, a sculptor reflects on her shift from psychology to art, her Maryland childhood, and the daily work of making color-driven sculpture while raising a family. A journal that examines the demands of an artist's life.

K:ae686b9f3f5e.title: The Birthday Party
K:ae686b9f3f5e.author: Harold Pinter
K:ae686b9f3f5e.description: Stanley Webber, a former pianist hiding out in a seaside boarding house run by Meg and Petey, is visited by two strangers, Goldberg and McCann, who interrogate him and take him away after a birthday party held in his honor. A play whose details are left deliberately uncertain.

K:47e0fe1f5575.title: The Homecoming
K:47e0fe1f5575.author: Harold Pinter
K:47e0fe1f5575.description: Teddy, a philosophy professor in America, brings his wife Ruth to meet his all-male working-class family in North London, where his father Max and brothers propose Ruth stay behind to live among them. A play that ends with Teddy leaving without her.

K:2f9cd8e7abef.title: The Zoo Story
K:2f9cd8e7abef.description: Jerry, a lonely drifter, approaches Peter, a comfortable publishing executive, on a Central Park bench and forces a conversation about his rooming house and a landlady's dog before provoking a struggle over the bench that ends in his own death. A one-act play about isolation in the city.

K:4fa2340b7789.title: Bullet Park
K:4fa2340b7789.author: John Cheever
K:4fa2340b7789.description: In a New York commuter suburb, advertising executive Eliot Nailles tries to reach his withdrawn son Tony while a disturbed newcomer named Paul Hammer settles nearby and fixes on murdering Tony at a church altar. A novel about suburban anxiety that builds to a near-sacrifice.

K:ad9ddab46bc3.title: Disturbing the Peace
K:ad9ddab46bc3.author: Richard Yates
K:ad9ddab46bc3.description: John Wilder, a New York advertising-space salesman, sinks into drinking and adultery, breaks down at a convention, threatens his family, and is committed to the psychiatric ward at Bellevue. A semi-autobiographical novel tracing an alcoholic's mental collapse.

K:dd6318e3c408.title: Manchild in the Promised Land
K:dd6318e3c408.author: Claude Brown
K:dd6318e3c408.description: Sonny narrates his coming of age in Harlem during the 1940s and 1950s, moving through theft, drugs, reform school, and the street life around him before finding a way out. An autobiographical work that drew wide attention to ghetto life during the civil rights era.

K:eec2f45b4e0a.title: The Loved One
K:eec2f45b4e0a.author: Evelyn Waugh
K:eec2f45b4e0a.description: Dennis Barlow, an out-of-work English poet in Hollywood, takes a job at a pet mortuary and courts Aimée Thanatogenos, a cosmetician at the lavish Whispering Glades funeral park, while competing with the mortician Mr. Joyboy. A satire of the Los Angeles funeral business and British expatriates.

K:23ded9392b69.title: Flat Stanley
K:23ded9392b69.author: Jeff Brown
K:23ded9392b69.description: Stanley Lambchop wakes up flattened by a fallen bulletin board and turns his new shape to advantage, sliding under doors, flying as a kite, traveling by mail, and posing as a painting to catch art thieves before his brother pumps him back to normal. A children's book of an ordinary boy's flat adventures.

K:0b1ced26bddf.title: The Blazing World
K:0b1ced26bddf.author: Siri Hustvedt
K:0b1ced26bddf.description: Harriet Burden, an installation artist ignored by the New York art world, exhibits her work under three male front men to test whether it will be better received, then struggles to be believed when she claims authorship. Presented as documents compiled by a scholar after her death.

K:b6a27884a317.title: Survival in Auschwitz
K:b6a27884a317.author: Primo Levi
K:b6a27884a317.description: A chemist deported from Italy describes daily survival in Auschwitz, recording the labor, hunger, selections, and routines of the camp and the ways prisoners held onto their humanity. A memoir of his year in the Nazi camp.

K:0a09f6895a0f.title: The Lottery and Other Stories
K:0a09f6895a0f.author: Shirley Jackson
K:0a09f6895a0f.description: Twenty-five stories, closing with "The Lottery," in which a small town gathers for an annual drawing that ends in a stoning, alongside other pieces tracing everyday menace and unease in ordinary American life. The only collection of her stories published in her lifetime.

K:7fdb16d0611a.title: The Stone Diaries
K:7fdb16d0611a.author: Carol Shields
K:7fdb16d0611a.description: Daisy Goodwill, whose mother dies giving birth to her in 1905 Manitoba, narrates her own life as it moves through marriage, widowhood, gardening, and old age across Canada and the United States. A fictional autobiography that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:84f983ef2571.title: The Beggar Maid
K:84f983ef2571.author: Alice Munro
K:84f983ef2571.description: Ten linked stories follow Rose, a girl raised by her practical stepmother Flo in small-town Ontario, as she wins a scholarship, marries, divorces, and builds a career away from home over nearly forty years. Published in Canada as "Who Do You Think You Are?" and a Governor General's Award winner.

K:311923238ca3.title: The Plot Against America
K:311923238ca3.author: Philip Roth
K:311923238ca3.description: In an alternate 1940, aviator Charles Lindbergh defeats Franklin Roosevelt for the presidency, signs accords with Germany and Japan, and stokes antisemitism, all witnessed by the Roth family in Newark and narrated by a boy named after the author. An alternate-history novel of creeping fascism in America.

K:d9591b1f5d49.title: Fancies and Goodnights
K:d9591b1f5d49.author: John Collier
K:d9591b1f5d49.description: Fifty stories of dark comedy, murder, and the supernatural, including "The Chaser," "Evening Primrose," and "Wet Saturday," marked by ironic twists and macabre wit. A collection that won the International Fantasy Award and an Edgar Award.

K:2e6a85d46d4c.title: Larry's Party
K:2e6a85d46d4c.author: Carol Shields
K:2e6a85d46d4c.description: Larry Weller, a Winnipeg florist who discovers a gift for designing garden mazes, moves through two marriages and twenty years of work and self-doubt, the chapters mirroring the turns of his labyrinths. A novel about an ordinary man's life that won the Orange Prize.

K:8af39279a369.title: Don't Let's Go to the Dogs Tonight
K:8af39279a369.author: Alexandra Fuller
K:8af39279a369.description: The author recalls her childhood on farms in war-torn Rhodesia and later Malawi and Zambia, amid family hardship, her mother's drinking, the deaths of siblings, and the violence of the Rhodesian Bush War. A memoir of growing up white in southern Africa.

K:adfba3021149.title: Lies of Silence
K:adfba3021149.author: Brian Moore
K:adfba3021149.description: Belfast hotel manager Michael Dillon, about to leave his wife for a younger woman, is taken hostage with her by the Provisional IRA and ordered to drive a car bomb into his own hotel, then faces a choice about whether to inform on the gunmen. A novel about the Troubles and personal conscience.

K:d9e576e5e9b8.title: Cal
K:d9e576e5e9b8.author: Bernard MacLaverty
K:d9e576e5e9b8.description: Cal, a young Catholic in 1980s Northern Ireland who served as getaway driver in the IRA killing of a policeman, falls in love with the dead man's widow Marcella while wracked by guilt. A novel of the Troubles and a doomed relationship.

K:a3fdf9ab88d1.title: That Night
K:a3fdf9ab88d1.author: Alice McDermott
K:a3fdf9ab88d1.description: A grown woman recalls a night in her 1960s Long Island suburb when Rick and his friends drove up looking for his girlfriend Sheryl, whose mother had sent her away after a pregnancy, sparking a brawl on the lawn. A novel narrated by a child who watched it happen.

K:42fc701268b1.title: The Human Stain
K:42fc701268b1.author: Philip Roth
K:42fc701268b1.description: Coleman Silk, a classics professor at a small Massachusetts college, is forced out after a remark deemed racist, concealing that he is a light-skinned Black man who has passed as white for decades, then takes up with a younger cleaning woman. Narrated by Nathan Zuckerman against the backdrop of the 1998 Clinton scandal.

K:5e6a219f1f98.title: Wheat That Springeth Green
K:5e6a219f1f98.author: J. F. Powers
K:5e6a219f1f98.description: Joe Hackett, a Midwestern boy who dreams of sainthood, becomes a Catholic priest, drifts into worldly comforts of baseball and beer as a suburban pastor, then moves toward a plainer faith. A novel tracing one priest's spiritual life across decades.

K:0b6de2d1f716.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
K:0b6de2d1f716.author: Mark Twain
K:0b6de2d1f716.description: Tom Sawyer, a mischievous boy in the Mississippi River village of St. Petersburg, tricks friends into whitewashing a fence, witnesses a graveyard murder by Injun Joe, runs off to play pirate, and hunts for buried treasure with Huckleberry Finn. A novel of boyhood along the river.

K:d99a5155c78c.title: The Black Book
K:d99a5155c78c.author: Orhan Pamuk
K:d99a5155c78c.description: Galip, an Istanbul lawyer whose wife Rüya has vanished, searches the city for her and for her half-brother Celal, a famous newspaper columnist who is also missing, eventually moving into Celal's flat and taking over his column. A novel that weaves stories of Istanbul into a search for identity.

K:7218170b4f39.title: The haiku of Matsuo Basho
K:7218170b4f39.description: A collection of haiku by the Japanese master of the form, short seventeen-syllable poems on seasons, travel, and nature drawn from his life as a wandering poet. Verses by the figure regarded as the greatest writer of haiku.

K:980abe074752.title: I, Claudius
K:980abe074752.author: Robert Graves
K:980abe074752.description: Written as the secret memoir of the stammering, limping Claudius, dismissed as a fool by his family, the book recounts the murders, intrigues, and poisonings of the Julio-Claudian dynasty from Augustus through Caligula. A historical novel that won the James Tait Black Prize.

K:57af164fa280.title: Eleven Kinds of Loneliness
K:57af164fa280.author: Richard Yates
K:57af164fa280.description: Office clerks, soldiers, jazz musicians, and cab drivers move through New York and its suburbs in eleven stories, each centered on a person cut off from the people around them. The debut collection is known for its plain prose and its bleak portraits of mid-century American disappointment.

K:22d8a45acf9c.title: The Three Musketeers
K:22d8a45acf9c.author: Alexandre Dumas
K:22d8a45acf9c.description: In 1620s France, the young Gascon d'Artagnan travels to Paris to join the King's Musketeers and befriends Athos, Porthos, and Aramis, who together oppose Cardinal Richelieu and his agent Milady de Winter over a scandal involving the queen's diamonds. A historical adventure novel famous for the rallying cry "all for one and one for all."

K:44a6e161192f.title: Mother's Milk
K:44a6e161192f.author: Edward St
K:44a6e161192f.description: Across four successive Augusts from 2000 to 2003, Patrick Melrose watches his marriage strain as his wife devotes herself to their two young sons and his mother signs the family's French estate over to a New Age guru. The fourth Patrick Melrose novel, it was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

K:e544d536217c.title: Patrimony
K:e544d536217c.author: Philip Roth
K:e544d536217c.description: A son cares for his eighty-six-year-old father as the retired insurance man declines from a brain tumor, recording his stubbornness, his memories, and the physical indignities of his final illness. A memoir about a father and son that won the National Book Critics Circle Award.

K:02b36d7b19db.title: The Road to Wellville
K:02b36d7b19db.author: T.C. Boyle
K:02b36d7b19db.description: At his Battle Creek sanitarium in 1907, the cereal magnate and health crusader John Harvey Kellogg subjects guests like the ailing Will Lightbody to enemas, electrotherapy, and a strict vegetarian regimen, while con men and rival cereal makers scheme nearby. A comic historical novel about the early American health-food industry.

K:39ac4c40de96.title: The Confessions of Nat Turner
K:39ac4c40de96.author: William Styron
K:39ac4c40de96.description: Awaiting execution in a Virginia jail in 1831, the enslaved preacher Nat Turner narrates the visions, grievances, and bloody slave rebellion that left dozens of white people dead in Southampton County. A first-person novel that won the Pulitzer Prize and drew sharp criticism from some Black writers for its portrayal of Turner.

K:f5c99485bebc.title: Rites of Passage
K:f5c99485bebc.author: William Golding
K:f5c99485bebc.description: Aboard a warship bound for Australia in the early nineteenth century, the young aristocrat Edmund Talbot keeps a journal recording the voyage and the humiliation and death of the clergyman Robert Colley at the hands of crew and passengers. The first book of the To the Ends of the Earth trilogy, it won the Booker Prize.

K:965aa95cc729.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
K:965aa95cc729.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
K:965aa95cc729.description: An old sailor stops a wedding guest and tells how he shot an albatross at sea, dooming his ship to drift through becalmed and supernatural waters as his crewmates die and he alone survives to do penance. A long narrative poem that opened Lyrical Ballads and became a landmark of English Romanticism.

K:b71de4b4c34d.title: Impressions of Africa
K:b71de4b4c34d.author: Raymond Roussel
K:b71de4b4c34d.description: Shipwrecked European travelers stage an elaborate gala of bizarre performances and machines for the coronation of Talou VII in the imaginary African kingdom of Ponukele, after which the narrative doubles back to explain each spectacle. A novel built from a secret method of puns that influenced the Surrealists and Oulipo.

K:1b84fbb9cd5b.title: Correction
K:1b84fbb9cd5b.author: Thomas Bernhard
K:1b84fbb9cd5b.description: In a garret in an Austrian forest, an unnamed narrator sorts through the papers of his dead friend Roithamer, a scientist who built a perfect cone-shaped house for his sister and then, after her death, endlessly revised his manuscript before killing himself. A novel written in dense, looping prose obsessed with revision and self-correction.

K:a18626111ae6.title: Stories and Texts for Nothing
K:a18626111ae6.author: Samuel Beckett
K:a18626111ae6.description: Three stories follow expelled, wandering narrators through cities and rooms, paired with thirteen short prose pieces in which a disembodied voice circles the impossibility of speaking or existing. Originally written in French, the collection extends the bare, monologic style of the author's postwar fiction.

K:13778f54d567.title: Woman Hollering Creek
K:13778f54d567.author: Sandra Cisneros
K:13778f54d567.description: Mexican American girls and women across Texas and the border move through childhood, marriage, and disappointment in twenty-two stories, including one in which a young wife named Cleófilas flees an abusive husband. A story collection drawing on Chicana life and the folklore of La Llorona.

K:afe7479aaf9f.title: Dhalgren
K:afe7479aaf9f.author: Samuel R. Delany
K:afe7479aaf9f.description: A young amnesiac known only as the Kid arrives in Bellona, a midwestern city cut off from the rest of America by an unexplained catastrophe, where time and geography warp and he joins a roaming gang and writes poetry. A long, experimental science fiction novel known for its dense structure and circular ending.

K:5e444245aa75.title: Dawn
K:5e444245aa75.author: Octavia Butler
K:5e444245aa75.description: Centuries after a nuclear war, Lilith Iyapo wakes aboard the ship of the alien Oankali, who have saved humanity but intend to interbreed with the survivors before returning them to a healed Earth. The first novel of the Xenogenesis trilogy, it examines consent, race, and biological difference.

K:2c5e83e0ac55.title: Texaco
K:2c5e83e0ac55.author: Patrick Chamoiseau
K:2c5e83e0ac55.description: Marie-Sophie Laborieux recounts the founding and defense of Texaco, a shantytown on the edge of Fort-de-France, tracing her family from slavery through generations of struggle to build a community against demolition. A novel mixing French and Creole that won the Prix Goncourt.

K:e50b74904533.title: The Woman Warrior
K:e50b74904533.author: Maxine Hong Kingston
K:e50b74904533.description: A Chinese American girl growing up in California weaves her mother's "talk-stories," family history, and Chinese legend into five linked accounts, including the tale of a woman warrior and a suicidal "no-name" aunt. A memoir that blends autobiography and myth and helped define Asian American literature.

K:7787f9851a27.title: Distant Star
K:7787f9851a27.author: Roberto Bolaño
K:7787f9851a27.description: The narrator Arturo B. traces the career of Carlos Wieder, a pilot and poet who exploits the 1973 Chilean coup to write verse in the sky while murdering women, until a detective sets out to track him down years later. A short novel about art, fascism, and violence under the Pinochet dictatorship.

K:c4f21abbbc5f.title: The Children's Bach
K:c4f21abbbc5f.author: Helen Garner
K:c4f21abbbc5f.description: In suburban Melbourne, the settled marriage of Athena and Dexter is unsettled when Dexter's old friend Elizabeth arrives with her sister, her lover Philip, and his young daughter, drawing the couple into new desires and values. A short novel about music, family, and ordinary domestic life.

K:d0df8db93983.title: Train Dreams
K:d0df8db93983.author: Denis Johnson
K:d0df8db93983.description: Robert Grainier, a day laborer in the early twentieth-century American West, loses his wife and daughter to a wildfire and lives out his days alone in the woods of Idaho among loggers, railroads, and his own grief. A novella that was a Pulitzer Prize finalist.

K:6271ee36187d.title: Binocular Vision: New and Selected Short Stories
K:6271ee36187d.author: Edith Pearlman
K:6271ee36187d.description: Thirty-four stories span Jewish family life, wartime Europe, and the fictional Boston suburb of Godolphin, following ordinary people through love affairs, displacement, and small reckonings. A career-spanning collection of new and selected stories that won the National Book Critics Circle Award.

K:231bca317353.title: Lucy Gayheart
K:231bca317353.author: Willa Cather
K:231bca317353.description: Lucy Gayheart, a young woman from a small Nebraska town, goes to Chicago to study music and falls in love with an aging singer, a passion that pulls her away from her hometown and a steady local suitor. A late novel about ambition, longing, and small-town life.

K:0dc8a61b0116.title: McKay's Bees
K:0dc8a61b0116.author: Thomas McMahon
K:0dc8a61b0116.description: In 1855, Gordon McKay leads his wife, her twin brother, and a band of German craftsmen from Massachusetts to Kansas to found a town and make a fortune from beekeeping, only to face border violence, disease among the hives, and his own unraveling. A historical novel that mingles fictional settlers with figures like Thoreau and John Brown.

K:baf4e47c178b.title: The Little Disturbances of Man
K:baf4e47c178b.author: Grace Paley
K:baf4e47c178b.description: Men and women in and around New York talk their way through love affairs, marriages, and family troubles in ten stories, several narrated by sharp-tongued Bronx and Greenwich Village women. A debut collection known for its comic, vernacular voices.

K:8e2c404ad22c.title: Starting Out in the Evening
K:8e2c404ad22c.author: Brian Morton
K:8e2c404ad22c.description: Heather Wolfe, an ambitious graduate student, talks the forgotten elderly novelist Leonard Schiller into helping with her thesis, and their sessions reshape his life and that of his daughter Ariel before a stroke intervenes. A novel about literary ambition, aging, and reputation.

K:ecda3b6d23cc.title: My Life and Other Stories
K:ecda3b6d23cc.author: Anton Chekhov
K:ecda3b6d23cc.description: A provincial governor's son rejects his class to work as a common house-painter in "My Life," joined by other stories of Russian peasants, doctors, and disappointed lovers from the author's mature period. The title novella and its companions depict everyday Russian provincial life around the turn of the century.

K:ca1e830c3408.title: Collected Poems of Elizabeth Bishop
K:ca1e830c3408.author: Elizabeth Bishop
K:ca1e830c3408.description: Poems set in Nova Scotia, Florida, and Brazil observe fish, maps, filling stations, and lost things with exact, restrained attention, gathering work written across the poet's life including "The Fish," "The Moose," and "One Art." A posthumous collected edition of a major American poet's verse.

OL:OL5721472W.title: Scoop
OL:OL5721472W.author: Evelyn Waugh
OL:OL5721472W.description: John Boot, a mild nature columnist, is mistaken for a famous novelist and dispatched by a London newspaper to cover a civil war in the fictional African country of Ishmaelia, where bungling reporters invent the news they file. A satire of Fleet Street and foreign correspondence.

K:3b88c3e85b6a.title: The Life of Henri Brulard
K:3b88c3e85b6a.author: Stendhal
K:3b88c3e85b6a.description: Looking back from middle age, the narrator recounts his unhappy childhood in Grenoble, his hatred of his father, and his joy at joining Napoleon's army on its march into Italy. An unfinished autobiography written in the 1830s and published decades after the author's death.

K:9104123dca5b.title: The Bottle Factory Outing
K:9104123dca5b.author: Beryl Bainbridge
K:9104123dca5b.description: Two London bottle-factory workers, Freda and Brenda, join a staff outing into the English countryside that goes wrong, ending in death and a clumsy attempt to dispose of a body. A short comic novel that won the Guardian Fiction Prize.

K:66969004ba8b.title: The Death of A Beekeeper
K:66969004ba8b.author: Lars Gustafsson
K:66969004ba8b.description: Told through the recovered notebooks of Lars Lennart Westin, a divorced former schoolteacher who keeps bees by a Swedish lake, the book follows his thoughts after he learns he has terminal cancer and chooses not to seek treatment. A novel about solitude, pain, and mortality.

K:0698a31697cc.title: Wolf Whistle
K:0698a31697cc.author: Lewis Nordan
K:0698a31697cc.description: In Arrow Catcher, Mississippi, in 1955, a Black boy called Bobo is murdered for whistling at a white woman and his killers are tried and acquitted, witnessed by townspeople including the teacher Alice Conroy. A novel that fictionalizes the murder of Emmett Till using elements of magic realism.

K:307944949e96.title: With
K:307944949e96.author: Donald Harrington
K:307944949e96.description: After a state trooper named Sog Alan abducts eight-year-old Robin Kerr to a remote Ozark mountaintop and then dies, she grows to adulthood alone in the wild, kept company by animals and the ghost of a boy who once lived there. A novel set in the author's invented Arkansas town of Stay More.

K:7e4cb1cf59ac.title: Taking Care
K:7e4cb1cf59ac.author: Joy Williams
K:7e4cb1cf59ac.description: Ordinary people face illness, marriage, and loss in sixteen stories, including a lay preacher caring for his infant granddaughter while his wife is hospitalized. A collection known for its oblique, unsettling treatment of domestic life.

K:1dc5ba74ec0c.title: The Comedians
K:1dc5ba74ec0c.author: Graham Greene
K:1dc5ba74ec0c.description: Brown, an English hotel owner, returns to Port-au-Prince under François Duvalier and the Tontons Macoutes, finding a government minister dead in his pool and his lover Martha married to a South American ambassador, while a con man named Jones drifts toward the rebels. A novel set in Haiti to attack the Duvalier regime, which condemned the book in response.

K:3a143b2c0545.title: Ninety-two in the Shade
K:3a143b2c0545.author: Thomas McGuane
K:3a143b2c0545.description: Thomas Skelton, a college dropout in Key West, decides to set up as a skiff fishing guide despite a death threat from the established guide Nichol Dance, who has already killed a man and burns Skelton's boat. The standoff between the two builds toward a violent end.

K:1f288c612b3c.title: Phineas Finn: The Irish Member
K:1f288c612b3c.author: Anthony Trollope
K:1f288c612b3c.description: Phineas Finn, a young Irishman newly admitted to the bar, wins a seat in the British Parliament and rises through London political society while entangled with Lady Laura Standish, Violet Effingham, and Madame Max Goesler before resigning over the question of Irish tenant rights. The second of the Palliser political novels.

K:2269bb9ee4d7.title: Pictures from an Institution
K:2269bb9ee4d7.author: Randall Jarrell
K:2269bb9ee4d7.description: At Benton, an exclusive women's college, an unnamed narrator records the academic year and the arrival of novelist Gertrude Johnson, who mines the place for her next book, among a cast of professors and their families. A campus satire built from character sketches rather than plot.

K:e7524b57d0d3.title: Adolphe
K:e7524b57d0d3.author: Benjamin Constant
K:e7524b57d0d3.description: Adolphe, a restless young man, seduces Ellénore, the older mistress of a count, then finds himself trapped in a relationship he no longer wants, unable to leave her even as his pursuit of a career pulls them apart. A short French novel known for its analysis of a failing love affair.

K:d2e22cdb10e6.title: Anton Reiser
K:d2e22cdb10e6.author: Karl Philipp Moritz
K:d2e22cdb10e6.description: Anton Reiser endures a harsh Pietist childhood in Hanover and a miserable apprenticeship as a hatter in Brunswick, escaping into books and an obsession with the theatre as he wanders in pursuit of an acting career. One of the earliest psychological novels, drawn closely from its author's own life.

K:d1f9c293a49b.title: The Golovlyev Family
K:d1f9c293a49b.author: Mikhail Saltykov
K:d1f9c293a49b.description: On the Golovlyovo estate, the matriarch Arina Petrovna rules her serfs and family until power passes to her hypocritical, pious son Porfiry, nicknamed Little Judas, whose scheming accompanies the family's drinking, ruin, and successive deaths. A Russian novel about the decay of a landowning family.

K:cd83dfc92563.title: The Tale of the Genji
K:cd83dfc92563.author: Shikibu Murasaki
K:cd83dfc92563.description: Hikaru Genji, the handsome son of an emperor and a low-ranking concubine, is made a commoner and moves through the Heian court in a long series of love affairs, including his marriage to the young Murasaki, while the later chapters follow his descendants. Often called the world's first novel.

K:20113bd8060f.title: The Dukays
K:20113bd8060f.author: Lajos Zilahy
K:20113bd8060f.description: Count István Dukay and Countess Menti ignore the collapse of their world as their four children scatter across interwar and wartime Europe, from a daughter in love with a dying monarch to a son drawn into Nazism. A novel tracing the decline of a Hungarian aristocratic family after the First World War.

K:2118bf5ef223.title: Effi Briest
K:2118bf5ef223.author: Theodor Fontane
K:2118bf5ef223.description: Seventeen-year-old Effi Briest is married off to the much older Baron von Innstetten and moves to a remote Pomeranian town, where loneliness leads to a brief affair with Major Crampas; years later her husband finds the letters, kills Crampas in a duel, and casts Effi out. A German realist novel of marriage and adultery.

K:fec9ed81ecd9.title: The Maias
K:fec9ed81ecd9.author: Eca de Queiroz
K:fec9ed81ecd9.description: In nineteenth-century Lisbon, the aristocrat Carlos da Maia idles away his days with his friend João da Ega and falls in love with Maria Eduarda, not knowing she is his sister, bringing tragedy to the last generation of the declining Maia family. A Portuguese realist novel satirizing Lisbon society.

K:db109b1e87a7.title: Bhagavadgita
K:db109b1e87a7.description: On the field of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna falters before battle against his own kinsmen, and his charioteer Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu, counsels him on duty, action, and devotion across eighteen chapters of verse. A Hindu scripture embedded in the Mahabharata that sets out core ideas of dharma and yoga.

K:128cdaa33246.title: Mahabharata
K:128cdaa33246.description: Two branches of a royal family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, quarrel over the throne of Hastinapura until their dispute erupts into the great war at Kurukshetra, told across roughly 100,000 verses interwoven with myth, genealogy, and moral discourse. One of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India.

K:b691062fe51f.title: Galpo Guccho
K:b691062fe51f.author: Rabindranath Tagore
K:b691062fe51f.description: Across eighty-four stories set largely in rural Bengal, ordinary people face poverty, marriage, caste, and the pull of modern ideas, observed against the riverside landscape of their villages. A three-volume collection that remains among the most widely read works of Bengali short fiction.

K:4c98833a4f69.title: The Selected Poems of Pablo Neruda
K:4c98833a4f69.author: Pablo Neruda
K:4c98833a4f69.description: A bilingual selection drawing on the full range of the Chilean poet's career, from early love poems and the surrealist Residence on Earth to the political Canto General and the everyday Elemental Odes, with Spanish and English on facing pages. A comprehensive single-volume anthology of his poetry.

K:2a36d724bd0a.title: The Power of Now: A Guide to Spiritual Enlightenment
K:2a36d724bd0a.author: Eckhart Tolle
K:2a36d724bd0a.description: A spiritual teacher lays out, partly in question-and-answer form, the idea that emotional suffering comes from identifying with the mind and that liberation lies in living fully in the present moment, with exercises and concepts such as the "pain-body." A self-help book drawing on Buddhist and other spiritual traditions.

K:08cd5694dbf4.title: The Executioner's Song
K:08cd5694dbf4.author: Norman Mailer
K:08cd5694dbf4.description: Across Utah and the Western states, the paroled convict Gary Gilmore commits two murders, is sentenced to death, and demands his own execution by firing squad rather than appeal, in the first U.S. execution after the death penalty's reinstatement. A documentary novel assembled from interviews and records that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:99a3f7848da8.title: The Quiet American
K:99a3f7848da8.author: Graham Greene
K:99a3f7848da8.description: Thomas Fowler, a jaded British journalist in 1950s Saigon, watches the idealistic young American Alden Pyle, a covert CIA agent, draw close to his Vietnamese companion Phuong and meddle in the war as French colonial rule collapses. A novel that anticipated American involvement in Vietnam.

K:ab419a1d43cc.title: Jazz
K:ab419a1d43cc.author: Toni Morrison
K:ab419a1d43cc.description: In 1920s Harlem, the salesman Joe Trace shoots his teenage lover Dorcas, and his wife Violet slashes the dead girl's face at the funeral, after which the narrative reaches back through their pasts into the nineteenth-century South. The second novel in a trilogy that began with Beloved.

K:0906563c5cec.title: Stop-Time
K:0906563c5cec.author: Frank Conroy
K:0906563c5cec.description: A man recalls his poor, unsettled childhood and adolescence shuttling between New York City and rural Florida, including a difficult stepfather and an institutionalized father, in episodes told with the detail of fiction. A memoir that influenced many later American writers.

K:560a5a213fc5.title: Saturday
K:560a5a213fc5.author: Ian McEwan
K:560a5a213fc5.description: Henry Perowne, a London neurosurgeon, moves through a single Saturday in February 2003 as an anti-war march fills the streets, his day disrupted by a car accident and a violent confrontation with a man named Baxter that follows him home. A novel set on one day against the run-up to the Iraq War.

K:a90d7fbfdbe6.title: Sleepless Nights
K:a90d7fbfdbe6.author: Elizabeth Hardwick
K:a90d7fbfdbe6.description: A woman named Elizabeth looks back over her life in fragments, recalling her Kentucky childhood, years in New York, Amsterdam, and Boston, and the men and women she has known, in a book that abandons plot for memory. An early example of what is now called autofiction.

K:7ebf1ebfbc39.title: Speedboat
K:7ebf1ebfbc39.author: Renata Adler
K:7ebf1ebfbc39.description: Jen Fain, a young New York journalist, narrates her life in disconnected fragments, observations, and vignettes spanning boarding school, teaching, political speechwriting, and city life, with no continuous storyline. A novel built from episodic fragments that won the Hemingway Award for a first novel.

K:89f0af62ddc6.title: The Furies
K:89f0af62ddc6.author: Janet Hobhouse
K:89f0af62ddc6.description: Helen, the last of several generations of New York women who flee mothers they cannot live with, recalls a chaotic childhood, an English education at Oxford, a marriage to the wealthy Edward, her mother's suicide, and her own brush with cancer. An autobiographical novel published after its author's death.

K:431d0058d78e.title: Beautiful Ruins
K:431d0058d78e.author: Jess Walter
K:431d0058d78e.description: In 1962, an Italian innkeeper named Pasquale watches a dying American starlet arrive by boat at his tiny coastal village, a chance encounter that the novel traces across fifty years and into present-day Hollywood, with the filming of Cleopatra in the background. A satire of fame that moves between Italy and Hollywood.

K:4d5d604ff4ca.title: Runaway
K:4d5d604ff4ca.author: Alice Munro
K:4d5d604ff4ca.description: Across eight stories, including a linked trio about a woman named Juliet, characters confront marriage, escape, and betrayal, among them a young wife who cannot bring herself to leave her husband. A collection that won the Giller Prize.

K:7b9f9939d12b.title: The Book of Laughter and Forgetting
K:7b9f9939d12b.author: Milan Kundera
K:7b9f9939d12b.description: In seven loosely linked parts, Czech characters under Communist rule try to recover or erase love letters, memories, and a vanished past, among them the dissident Mirek and the widow Tamina, in a book the author compared to a musical composition. A novel about memory, laughter, and political forgetting.

K:084e65163770.title: The Green House
K:084e65163770.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
K:084e65163770.description: Over some forty years in Peru, intertwined stories link the desert town of Piura, where a man builds a brothel called the Green House, with the Amazon jungle near the Marañón, following nuns, smugglers, soldiers, and an Indian girl. A novel told through fragmented, shifting timelines.

K:e755c669d849.title: Dune
K:e755c669d849.author: Frank Herbert
K:e755c669d849.description: On the desert planet Arrakis, the only source of the spice melange, young Paul Atreides survives the betrayal and murder of his father, flees into the dunes with his mother, and joins the Fremen as he rises to lead them and seize control of the empire. One of the best-selling science fiction novels.

K:3b1ea60fa0c9.title: Red Dragon
K:3b1ea60fa0c9.author: Thomas Harris
K:3b1ea60fa0c9.description: Retired FBI profiler Will Graham is drawn back to hunt a serial killer who slaughters whole families at the full moon, consulting the imprisoned cannibal Hannibal Lecter for insight while the killer, Francis Dolarhyde, acts out a delusion drawn from a William Blake painting. The first novel to feature Lecter.

K:b16667acb539.title: The Thin Red Line
K:b16667acb539.author: James Jones
K:b16667acb539.description: C-for-Charlie Company lands on Guadalcanal and fights its way across the island against entrenched Japanese forces, with men such as Captain Stein and First Sergeant Welsh facing fear, exhaustion, and death. A World War II novel drawn from its author's combat experience.

K:37f1230ecf68.title: Fear of Flying
K:37f1230ecf68.author: Erica Jong
K:37f1230ecf68.description: Isadora Wing, a twenty-nine-year-old poet, flies to a psychoanalysts' conference in Vienna with her husband and embarks on an affair, narrating her sexual fantasies and her search for freedom from conventional marriage. A novel known for its frank treatment of female sexuality and its place in second-wave feminism.

K:1a1889c95894.title: The Silence of the Lambs
K:1a1889c95894.author: Thomas Harris
K:1a1889c95894.description: FBI trainee Clarice Starling is sent to interview the imprisoned cannibal Hannibal Lecter for help catching a serial killer called Buffalo Bill, who skins his female victims, trading personal disclosures for Lecter's clues. The sequel to Red Dragon and the best-known book in the Lecter series.

K:21a1935dbe9f.title: Stranger in a Strange Land
K:21a1935dbe9f.author: Robert A. Heinlein
K:21a1935dbe9f.description: Valentine Michael Smith, born on Mars and raised by Martians, comes to Earth as a young man and, baffled by human customs, gathers followers and founds a Martian-influenced Church of All Worlds. A science fiction novel that uses Smith's outsider view to question religion, money, monogamy, and death, and that coined the word "grok."

K:90279cddc790.title: Fuzz
K:90279cddc790.author: Ed McBain
K:90279cddc790.description: In the 87th Precinct, detectives receive extortion notes demanding money or city officials will be killed, and the assassinations begin, pointing to their recurring nemesis the Deaf Man, while Carella goes undercover to catch someone setting sleeping vagrants on fire. One of the 87th Precinct police procedurals, the fourth to feature the Deaf Man.

K:e46b6ba3a6a4.title: Alligator
K:e46b6ba3a6a4.author: Shelley Katz
K:e46b6ba3a6a4.description: When a huge alligator begins killing in the Florida swamplands, wealthy Rye Whitman hires the local guide Lee Ferris to hunt it, and the two men are driven together by mutual need and hatred through storms, fire, and bloodshed. A killer-creature thriller released in the wake of Jaws that questions whether the hunters or the beast are the real monsters.

K:7cf4197a34ab.title: The Sum of All Fears
K:7cf4197a34ab.author: Tom Clancy
K:7cf4197a34ab.description: Jack Ryan, now Deputy Director of the CIA, works to defuse a Middle East crisis as Palestinian and former East German terrorists detonate a nuclear bomb at the Super Bowl in Denver and stage a false-flag attack to push the United States and Soviet Union toward nuclear war. A political thriller and the sixth Jack Ryan novel.

K:32360bf742ca.title: The Emigrants
K:32360bf742ca.author: W. G. Sebald
K:32360bf742ca.description: A narrator recounts the lives of four Jewish émigrés who left Germany for England and the United States, piecing together their histories of exile, memory, and loss alongside unlabeled black-and-white photographs. A prose work that blends biography, fiction, and documentary and deals with the long aftermath of the Holocaust.

K:15dff4e8c1b2.title: A Legacy
K:15dff4e8c1b2.author: Sybille Bedford
K:15dff4e8c1b2.description: Two very different German families joined by marriage, the wealthy Jewish Merzes of Berlin and the Catholic aristocratic von Feldens of Baden, move through tumults and tragedies in the decades before the First World War, narrated by Francesca, daughter of Baron Julius von Felden. A semi-autobiographical novel based on the author's own family.

K:17da81fb1052.title: The Duel
K:17da81fb1052.author: Anton Chekhov .
K:17da81fb1052.description: In a seaside town in the Caucasus, the disillusioned civil servant Laevsky tires of his married mistress Nadezhda and runs up debts, while the Social Darwinist zoologist Von Koren goads him into a duel.
