A novella that contrasts their opposed worldviews and ends with Laevsky's chastened change of heart.

K:ac3c75abbf8c.title: W, or The Memory of Childhood
K:ac3c75abbf8c.author: Georges Perec
K:ac3c75abbf8c.description: Alternating chapters pair the author's uncertain memories of his French wartime childhood with a fictional account of W, an island off Tierra del Fuego founded by Olympic enthusiasts where life is organized entirely around brutal athletic competition. A work that uses the island as an allegory for totalitarian regimes and the Nazi camps.

K:76f8b9527010.title: The Sheltering Sky
K:76f8b9527010.author: Paul Bowles
K:76f8b9527010.description: Port and Kit Moresby, a married American couple from New York, travel into the North African desert with their friend Tunner, their marriage fraying as they move deeper into the Sahara until Port's stolen passport and a bout of meningitis turn the journey deadly. A first novel about alienation and disintegration among Western travelers in postwar Algeria and Morocco.

K:224747d4604b.title: Going to Meet the Man
K:224747d4604b.author: James Baldwin
K:224747d4604b.description: Eight stories range from Black boys growing up in Harlem to a jazz pianist's struggle with addiction in "Sonny's Blues" and a white Southern deputy's memories of a lynching in the title story. The author's only collection of short fiction, gathering work published between 1948 and 1965.

K:76d530224b46.title: Tennessee Williams: Plays 1937–1955
K:76d530224b46.description: Collects the early and major plays, among them The Glass Menagerie, A Streetcar Named Desire, Summer and Smoke, The Rose Tattoo, Camino Real, and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, along with earlier works such as Spring Storm and Battle of Angels. A Library of America volume covering the dramatist's rise and most celebrated period.

K:e64e736a51a8.title: The Book of Love: Poems of Ecstasy and Longing
K:e64e736a51a8.author: Rumi
K:e64e736a51a8.description: A themed selection of love poems by the thirteenth-century Persian Sufi mystic, arranged around states of love from sudden infatuation and union to grief and friendship, in English versions by Coleman Barks. A popular modern compilation of the poet's verse on human and divine love.

K:990969c891b1.title: Sophie’s Choice
K:990969c891b1.author: William Styron
K:990969c891b1.description: In a Brooklyn boardinghouse in 1947, the young Southern writer Stingo befriends the Polish Catholic Auschwitz survivor Sophie Zawistowska and her brilliant, unstable Jewish lover Nathan Landau, and learns of the impossible choice Sophie was forced to make at the camp. A novel about the Holocaust and its aftermath that won the National Book Award.

K:fa54fed8dbb3.title: A Confederacy of Dunces
K:fa54fed8dbb3.author: John Kennedy Toole
K:fa54fed8dbb3.description: Ignatius J. Reilly, an overweight, misanthropic medieval scholar who lives with his mother in early-1960s New Orleans, is pushed to find work and stumbles through misadventures with French Quarter characters. A picaresque comic novel published after the author's death that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:7080743d9f68.title: The Sot-Weed Factor
K:7080743d9f68.author: John Barth
K:7080743d9f68.description: A fictionalized Ebenezer Cooke is named Poet Laureate of Maryland and sails from London to the colony to write its praises, undergoing a sprawling series of adventures while striving to keep his virginity. A long satirical novel written in mock eighteenth-century style that marked the author's turn to postmodernism.

K:d5042792cf40.title: Some Other Place. The Right Place
K:d5042792cf40.author: Donald Harington
K:d5042792cf40.description: Just out of Sarah Lawrence, Diana discovers that eighteen-year-old Day can, under hypnosis, become her dead grandfather Daniel Lyam Montross, and the two travel to the places he lived as Day reveals Montross's full life story. A novel of reincarnation, suppressed memory, and family secrets told across musical movements.

K:aa06efa6ffb9.title: Answered Prayers
K:aa06efa6ffb9.author: Truman Capote
K:aa06efa6ffb9.description: P.B. Jones, a bisexual hustler and would-be writer, moves through the literary and high-society world of mid-century New York, recounting scandalous confidences drawn from the rich and famous. An unfinished novel published after the author's death, including the chapter that exposed his socialite friends.

K:6071bcc4c2a5.title: The Ice Age
K:6071bcc4c2a5.author: Margaret Drabble
K:6071bcc4c2a5.description: Anthony Keating, a former BBC producer turned property developer, takes stock of his life from a Yorkshire cottage after a heart attack while his friends face IRA bombings, collapsing property deals, and a daughter imprisoned behind the Iron Curtain. A state-of-England novel set during the economic crises of 1970s Britain.

K:a3a5d5c3c211.title: The Radiant Way
K:a3a5d5c3c211.author: Margaret Drabble
K:a3a5d5c3c211.description: Three Cambridge-educated friends, the psychiatrist Liz Headleand, the prison teacher Alix Bowen, and the art scholar Esther Breuer, are followed through seven years of 1980s Britain that begin at Liz's New Year's Eve party and unfold against a London serial killer. A social novel critiquing Thatcher-era England.

K:5edf5b07c259.title: Play It as It Lays
K:5edf5b07c259.author: Joan Didion
K:5edf5b07c259.description: Maria Wyeth, a minor actress whose marriage and career are falling apart, drifts through Los Angeles and the Nevada desert, recovering in a psychiatric hospital as she recalls the breakdown that brought her there. A novel of 1960s emptiness told in short, fragmented chapters.

K:0c9bc31275dd.title: Fight Club
K:0c9bc31275dd.author: Chuck Palahniuk
K:0c9bc31275dd.description: An insomniac office worker finds relief in support groups, then meets the charismatic Tyler Durden and starts an underground bare-knuckle fighting club that grows into the anti-consumerist cult Project Mayhem, until he realizes he and Tyler are the same person. A debut novel about masculinity and consumer culture.

K:844116884044.title: Decline and Fall
K:844116884044.author: Evelyn Waugh
K:844116884044.description: Theology student Paul Pennyfeather is wrongly expelled from Oxford, takes a teaching post at a shabby Welsh school, becomes entangled with the wealthy Margot Beste-Chetwynde and her white-slavery dealings, and ends up imprisoned before returning to his studies. A first novel that satirizes 1920s British society with black comedy.

K:8b14ad140aeb.title: Breaking and Entering
K:8b14ad140aeb.author: Joy Williams
K:8b14ad140aeb.description: Willie and Liberty, lovers since their teens, drift through the Florida Keys breaking into vacant vacation homes to live in them while the owners are away, as Liberty senses Willie pulling away and their aimless life turning dangerous. A novel about two rootless drifters on the edges of affluent Florida.

K:051a111d303b.title: Collected Stories of Elizabeth Bowen
K:051a111d303b.author: Elizabeth Bowen
K:051a111d303b.description: Seventy-nine stories span the author's career from the 1920s through the postwar years, many centered on women and on Anglo-Irish life, often turning on transience, unease, and wartime London. A comprehensive gathering of the Irish writer's short fiction.

K:fd173963c7a7.title: We Were the Mulvaneys
K:fd173963c7a7.author: Joyce Carol Oates
K:fd173963c7a7.description: The seemingly perfect Mulvaney family of rural Mt. Ephraim, New York, unravels over fifteen years after daughter Marianne is raped following a school dance, as the father's drinking, lost reputation, and bankruptcy scatter the family. A family novel narrated by the youngest son, Judd.

K:e4d6b7a4689e.title: Night
K:e4d6b7a4689e.author: Elie Wiesel
K:e4d6b7a4689e.description: A teenage boy and his father are deported from their Transylvanian town to Auschwitz and then Buchenwald, where he witnesses and endures the horrors of the camps and the collapse of his faith. A memoir of the Holocaust, first written in Yiddish, that became a cornerstone of Holocaust literature.

K:cea4e1a79452.title: Masters of the Dew
K:cea4e1a79452.author: Jacques Roumain
K:cea4e1a79452.description: Manuel returns to the drought-stricken Haitian village of Fonds Rouge after years cutting cane in Cuba and, drawing on the political solidarity he learned abroad, searches for water and tries to unite the feuding villagers through collective labor. A peasant novel of human suffering and social awakening in rural Haiti.

K:b2ed6357b917.title: A Tale of Two Cities
K:b2ed6357b917.author: Charles Dickens
K:b2ed6357b917.description: Dr. Manette, freed after eighteen years in the Bastille, is reunited in London with his daughter Lucie, whose suitors include the exiled French aristocrat Charles Darnay and the dissolute barrister Sydney Carton, all drawn into the Reign of Terror in Paris. A historical novel set in London and Paris during the French Revolution, ending in Carton's sacrifice.

K:4ed9d5c4ad28.title: The Folded Leaf
K:4ed9d5c4ad28.author: William Maxwell
K:4ed9d5c4ad28.description: In 1920s suburban Chicago, the bookish, motherless Lymie Peters and the athletic Spud Latham form an intense adolescent friendship that carries into college, where their rivalry over Sally Forbes builds toward a crisis and Lymie's attempt on his own life. A novel about male friendship with an undercurrent of unspoken attraction.

K:10f18a0254cc.title: The Gate of Angels
K:10f18a0254cc.author: Penelope Fitzgerald
K:10f18a0254cc.description: In 1912 Cambridge, the young physicist Fred Fairly, a fellow of the fictional college St Angelicus, collides on his bicycle with Daisy Saunders in the dark, and the two are mistakenly put to bed together to recover, after which Fred falls in love but loses track of her. A historical novel, the author's only one with a happy ending.

K:fee34cabb897.title: The Member of the Wedding
K:fee34cabb897.author: Carson McCullers
K:fee34cabb897.description: During a hot Georgia summer, twelve-year-old tomboy Frankie Addams becomes obsessed with her brother's wedding and convinces herself she will leave town with the couple, passing her days in the kitchen with the cook Berenice and her young cousin John Henry. A coming-of-age novel about loneliness and belonging.

K:5a6ed0245636.title: Break It Down
K:5a6ed0245636.author: Lydia Davis
K:5a6ed0245636.description: Thirty-four very short stories, including the title piece in which a man at a desk tallies the dollar cost of a love affair, work through brevity, understatement, and sudden shifts of voice. An early collection that helped establish the author's compressed, precise form of short fiction.

K:9f3328e101b2.title: Joseph Andrews
K:9f3328e101b2.author: Henry Fielding
K:9f3328e101b2.description: Joseph Andrews, a virtuous young footman dismissed by Lady Booby for refusing her advances, travels from London toward Somersetshire to reunite with his beloved Fanny, falling in with the absent-minded Parson Abraham Adams and meeting robbers and mishaps along the road. A comic novel its author called a "comic epic poem in prose."

K:ecccc5395ea7.title: On the Eve
K:ecccc5395ea7.author: Ivan Turgenev
K:ecccc5395ea7.description: Elena Stakhova, a Russian gentlewoman courted by a sculptor and a scholar, instead falls for Dmitri Insarov, a Bulgarian revolutionary, and secretly marries him to follow him toward the coming war for his homeland. A third novel set on the eve of the Crimean War, built around a heroine who chooses purpose over comfort.

K:6d4d03ec89c9.title: Where Angels Fear to Tread
K:6d4d03ec89c9.author: E. M. Forster
K:6d4d03ec89c9.description: The widowed Lilia Herriton travels to Tuscany and marries Gino, a younger Italian dentist's son, prompting her late husband's English family to send her brother-in-law Philip to Monteriano, where a struggle over her infant son ends in the baby's death. A first novel contrasting English propriety with Italian life.

K:bf599939f01f.title: Cold Mountain
K:bf599939f01f.author: Charles Frazier
K:bf599939f01f.description: W. P. Inman, a wounded Confederate deserter, walks home across the Carolinas toward Ada Monroe, while Ada and a drifter named Ruby struggle to keep her late father's farm near Cold Mountain alive. A first novel set in the last months of the American Civil War that alternates between the two characters' journeys.

K:45d423f10268.title: Red Shift
K:45d423f10268.author: Alan Garner
K:45d423f10268.description: Three pairs of lovers in the same Cheshire landscape are linked across time: teenagers Tom and Jan in the present, the epileptic Macey among Roman deserters, and Thomas Rowley during a Civil War massacre. A novel told largely in clipped dialogue, with events in different eras echoing one another.

K:9bc0b5729601.title: Les Liaisons Dangereuses
K:9bc0b5729601.author: Pierre Choderlos de Laclos
K:9bc0b5729601.description: The Marquise de Merteuil and the Vicomte de Valmont, former lovers and amoral rivals, scheme through letters to corrupt the young Cécile de Volanges and seduce the virtuous Madame de Tourvel, until their plots destroy them both. An epistolary novel exposing the cruelty and vanity of French aristocratic society.

K:ced3e731d0b5.title: Oldest Living Confederate Widow Tells All
K:ced3e731d0b5.author: Allan Gurganus
K:ced3e731d0b5.description: Ninety-nine-year-old Lucy Marsden, speaking from a North Carolina rest home, recounts her marriage at fifteen to Confederate veteran "Captain Willie" Marsden and the lives entangled with his, including his former slave Castalia. A long monologue that retells the American South across a century through one woman's voice.

K:ec3fd432acea.title: The Passion
K:ec3fd432acea.author: Jeanette Winterson
K:ec3fd432acea.description: Henri, a young soldier cooking chickens for Napoleon, and Villanelle, a web-footed Venetian boatman's daughter who works in a casino, cross paths amid the wreckage of the Russian campaign and make their way to Venice. A novel mixing the Napoleonic Wars with fantasy and questions of passion.

K:0fb96ea874bc.title: Ulverton
K:0fb96ea874bc.author: Adam Thorpe
K:0fb96ea874bc.description: Across twelve stories in differing voices and forms, the fictional English village of Ulverton passes through three hundred years of births, deaths, farming, and change from Cromwell's era to the 1980s. A first novel that pieces together a place's history through diaries, letters, sermons, and a television script.

K:1dc9509e5ec7.title: Othello, The Moor of Venice
K:1dc9509e5ec7.author: William Shakespeare
K:1dc9509e5ec7.description: In Venice and Cyprus, the Moorish general Othello, manipulated by his resentful ensign Iago, comes to believe his wife Desdemona has betrayed him with his lieutenant Cassio, and smothers her before learning of her innocence and killing himself. A major tragedy centered on jealousy, manipulation, and deception.

K:e62e1fa9cb0f.title: The Old Forest and Other Stories
K:e62e1fa9cb0f.author: Peter Taylor
K:e62e1fa9cb0f.description: Fourteen stories set in the American South between the 1930s and 1950s, including the title piece in which a Memphis man recalls how a young woman vanished into a city forest after a car accident a week before his wedding. A collection drawn from fifty years of work, several pieces first appearing in The New Yorker.

K:657587407b2f.title: Henderson the Rain King
K:657587407b2f.author: Saul Bellow
K:657587407b2f.description: Eugene Henderson, a restless, wealthy American haunted by an inner voice crying "I want, I want," flees to the African interior and is improbably crowned rain king by the Wariri. A comic novel about midlife restlessness and the search for meaning, reportedly its author's favorite.

K:63a6f8d4a3cf.title: At Play in the Fields of the Lord
K:63a6f8d4a3cf.author: Peter Matthiessen
K:63a6f8d4a3cf.description: In a malarial outpost on the upper Amazon, the missionary Martin Quarrier tries to convert the Niaruna people while Lewis Moon, a part-Indian mercenary hired to drive them out, instead parachutes in and joins them. A novel of clashing outsiders that examines missionary faith and the destruction of native cultures.

K:f3d3d81a13a1.title: Sacred Hunger
K:f3d3d81a13a1.author: Barry Unsworth
K:f3d3d81a13a1.description: Aboard the slave ship Liverpool Merchant in the 1750s, the physician Matthew Paris joins a triangular-trade voyage that ends in mutiny, while his cousin Erasmus Kemp, the owner's son, later hunts down the survivors who founded a settlement in Florida. A novel about greed and the Atlantic slave trade.

K:4915c4a456eb.title: Gargantua and Pantagruel
K:4915c4a456eb.author: François Rabelais
K:4915c4a456eb.description: The giant Gargantua and his son Pantagruel move through a series of bawdy, fantastical adventures alongside the rogue Panurge, mixing crude comedy with learned satire of medieval scholarship, religion, and law. A collective title for five comic novels that became landmarks of French Renaissance literature.

K:0b33bb451da1.title: Finnegans Wake
K:0b33bb451da1.author: James Joyce
K:0b33bb451da1.description: Through the dreaming night of Dublin innkeeper Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker, his wife Anna Livia Plurabelle, and their children Shem and Shaun, the book cycles through guilt, gossip, and the river Liffey in an invented multilingual language. A work known for being among the most difficult in English literature.

K:aaeea62a115f.title: Seven Gothic Tales
K:aaeea62a115f.author: Isak Dinesen
K:aaeea62a115f.description: Seven long tales set mostly in the nineteenth century, among them "The Deluge at Norderney" and "The Monkey," involving aristocrats, storms, and questions of identity and fate, told with embedded stories and narrative irony. The debut collection that established its Danish author's reputation in the English-speaking world.

K:16e06883edc4.title: Silence
K:16e06883edc4.author: Shusaku Endo
K:16e06883edc4.description: Sebastião Rodrigues, a Portuguese Jesuit, slips into seventeenth-century Japan to find his apostatized mentor and minister to hidden Christians, but is captured and pressed to trample on an image of Christ to end the torture of others. A novel about persecution, apostasy, and the silence of God.

K:40880fd45ba7.title: Heat and Dust
K:40880fd45ba7.author: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala
K:40880fd45ba7.description: In two interwoven stories, the Englishwoman Olivia leaves her civil-servant husband during the 1920s Raj for an Indian prince, while decades later her step-granddaughter retraces Olivia's path through the same Indian town. A novel that won the Booker Prize, set across colonial and post-independence India.

K:b38daef16aea.title: The Book of Mark.
K:b38daef16aea.description: The shortest of the four canonical gospels narrates the ministry of Jesus from his baptism by John the Baptist through his teaching, healings, and exorcisms to his crucifixion, burial, and empty tomb. The earliest of the gospels, written in plain Greek and a source for Matthew and Luke.

K:aafaa386e9f2.title: The Dead
K:aafaa386e9f2.author: James Joyce
K:aafaa386e9f2.description: Gabriel Conroy attends his aunts' Christmas party in Dublin, then learns at the hotel afterward that his wife Gretta has long carried the memory of Michael Furey, a boy who died young for love of her. The closing, longest story of the Dubliners collection, ending with snow falling over Ireland.

K:3dc75f99b576.title: Stories of Nathaniel Hawthorne
K:3dc75f99b576.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
K:3dc75f99b576.description: A gathering of tales by the New England author, including "Young Goodman Brown," "The Birthmark," and "Rappaccini's Daughter," dealing with sin, guilt, science, and Puritan hypocrisy, often through allegory and the supernatural. Stories drawn from collections such as Twice-Told Tales and Mosses from an Old Manse.

K:9df5ca05129f.title: Little, Big
K:9df5ca05129f.author: John Crowley
K:9df5ca05129f.description: Smoky Barnable walks from the City to marry Daily Alice Drinkwater at Edgewood, a strange house outside New York, and is drawn into a family saga spanning generations whose members commune with fairies and live inside a "Tale." A fantasy novel about a family and the unseen realm at the edge of their world.

K:625b79762741.title: The Pillow-Book of Sei Shonagon
K:625b79762741.description: A court lady to Empress Teishi in Heian-era Japan sets down lists, anecdotes, poems, and sharp observations of palace life, recording what she finds elegant, vexing, or absurd. A foundational work of Japanese prose and one of the best sources on tenth-century court society.

K:f8c105f058d5.title: Doting
K:f8c105f058d5.author: Henry Green
K:f8c105f058d5.description: At two dinner parties bracketing the story, Arthur and Diana Middleton, their teenage son Peter, and a pair of younger women drift through flirtations and half-affairs in postwar London. The author's last novel, written almost entirely in dialogue, drawing a line between doting and loving.

K:534ca77bf091.title: Blindness
K:534ca77bf091.author: Henry Green
K:534ca77bf091.description: John Haye, a schoolboy with literary ambitions, is blinded when a boy throws a stone through his train window, and must remake his life in the country with his stepmother and a local girl named Joan. The author's first novel, written while he was still at Eton.

K:1fbb54b59724.title: How German Is It
K:1fbb54b59724.author: Walter Abish
K:1fbb54b59724.description: Ulrich Hargenau, son of a man executed for the 1944 plot against Hitler, returns to the German town of Würtenburg, where the new community of Brumholdstein stands on the site of a former concentration camp. A postmodern novel probing how postwar Germany lives with its recent past.

K:bd00376b9180.title: The Assistant
K:bd00376b9180.author: Bernard Malamud
K:bd00376b9180.description: Morris Bober, an aging Jewish grocer barely scraping by in Brooklyn, takes on Frank Alpine, a drifter who had helped rob him, as an unpaid assistant, and Frank falls for Morris's daughter Helen while wrestling with his own guilt. A novel about poverty, conscience, and moral struggle.

K:225e0e2f049d.title: The Fall
K:225e0e2f049d.author: Albert Camus
K:225e0e2f049d.description: In an Amsterdam bar, the former Paris lawyer Jean-Baptiste Clamence delivers a long confession to a stranger, recounting his fall from self-satisfied respectability after he failed to save a woman who drowned. A monologue novel that examines guilt, judgment, and bad faith.

K:50d0889fba0e.title: Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy
K:50d0889fba0e.author: John Le Carré
K:50d0889fba0e.description: The aging spymaster George Smiley is brought out of retirement to hunt a Soviet mole burrowed at the top of British intelligence, narrowing the suspects among his own former colleagues at the "Circus." The first book of the Karla trilogy, drawing on Cold War betrayal and the Philby case.

K:276c1877072e.title: Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes (A Harlot High and Low)
K:276c1877072e.author: Honoré de Balzac
K:276c1877072e.description: Lucien de Rubempré rises in Paris under the secret control of the criminal Vautrin, who poses as a Spanish priest, until Lucien's love for the courtesan Esther van Gobseck and a banker's obsession with her bring them to ruin and arrest. A continuation of Lost Illusions within the author's Human Comedy cycle.

K:524993036073.title: The Maigret series of detective novels
K:524993036073.author: Georges Simenon
K:524993036073.description: Commissaire Jules Maigret, a pipe-smoking inspector of the Paris crime brigade, solves murders less by deduction than by absorbing the atmosphere and psychology of the people and places involved. A series of seventy-five novels and many stories that reshaped detective fiction.

K:0230eeaf324c.title: Nice Work
K:0230eeaf324c.author: David Lodge
K:0230eeaf324c.description: Robyn Penrose, a young academic at Rummidge University, is paired with Vic Wilcox, the managing director of a struggling engineering firm, in a shadowing scheme that forces the worlds of literary theory and industry together. A campus novel set in 1980s Thatcher-era England.

K:80f80a40eeab.title: Changing Places
K:80f80a40eeab.description: Two professors, the cautious Englishman Philip Swallow and the brash American Morris Zapp, swap jobs and lives for six months between Rummidge in England and the campus of Euphoria State in California. A campus novel told in shifting forms, from letters to news clippings to a screenplay.

K:2d245b5f48f1.title: Small World
K:2d245b5f48f1.description: Young Irish literary critic Persse McGarrigle chases the beautiful Angelica Pabst from one academic conference to another, while veteran scholars like Morris Zapp and Philip Swallow compete across a globe-trotting circuit of literary theory and intrigue. The second book in the Campus Trilogy, a satire of academic conferences and rival schools of criticism shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

K:f78f2190768a.title: Cities of the Red Night
K:f78f2190768a.author: William S. Burroughs
K:f78f2190768a.description: A band of radical pirates tries to live by the freedom articles of Captain Mission while, in a near-present strand, a detective hunts a boy abducted for a sex ritual and a virus tied to the cities of the red night spreads. The first volume of the Red Night Trilogy, told in a nonlinear, fragmented structure across different times and places.

K:a7dff9c2e44e.title: A Disaffection
K:a7dff9c2e44e.author: James Kelman
K:a7dff9c2e44e.description: Over one week, 29-year-old Glasgow schoolteacher Patrick Doyle grows bitter about his work and his life, drinks heavily, and pines for a married fellow teacher, Alison Houston, who rejects him. Written in Glasgow dialect and stream of consciousness, it won the James Tait Black Memorial Prize and was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

K:61c9c451d3cd.title: Men at Arms
K:61c9c451d3cd.author: Evelyn Waugh
K:61c9c451d3cd.description: Guy Crouchback, heir to a declining English Roman Catholic family, returns from Italy at the start of the Second World War and joins the Royal Corps of Halberdiers, training under Brigadier Ritchie-Hook alongside the eccentric Apthorpe. The first novel of the Sword of Honour trilogy, it won the James Tait Black Memorial Prize.

K:87dd2eb9156a.title: Officers and Gentlemen
K:87dd2eb9156a.description: Guy Crouchback joins a commando brigade training on a Scottish island, then is caught up in the chaotic British evacuation of Crete, where he meets the slippery Corporal-Major Ludovic and barely escapes by boat to Egypt. The second novel of the Sword of Honour trilogy, covering the early war and the Crete debacle.

K:1735e32fc58c.title: Unconditional Surrender
K:1735e32fc58c.description: Now forty and judged too old for active service, Guy Crouchback knocks about wartime London, remarries his ex-wife Virginia to take responsibility for her child by another man, and finally undertakes a liaison mission to Yugoslav partisans. The closing novel of the Sword of Honour trilogy, published in North America as The End of the Battle.

K:c49562153000.title: The Man Who Cried I Am
K:c49562153000.author: John A.Williams
K:c49562153000.description: Max Reddick, a Black American novelist and journalist dying of cancer, travels through Europe to attend a friend's funeral and recover papers exposing the King Alfred Plan, a secret government scheme to intern Black Americans. Several characters are modeled on figures such as Richard Wright, Chester Himes, and James Baldwin.

K:a03d515550d1.title: And Then We Heard the Thunder
K:a03d515550d1.author: John Oliver Killens
K:a03d515550d1.description: Solly Saunders, a Harvard-trained Black GI, serves in a segregated U.S. Army unit during the Second World War, moving through Indochina, Australia, and a racial riot in South Brisbane that pushes him toward Black activism. A novel about racism in the armed forces during the war.

K:b13d439ea66c.title: Days Without Weather
K:b13d439ea66c.author: Cecil Brown
K:b13d439ea66c.description: Jonah Drinkwater, a young Black migrant from the rural South, tries to break into the Los Angeles entertainment world as a comedian and screenwriter, attempting to film a slave-revolt story amid Hollywood's stereotyping and betrayals. The narrative weaves stand-up comedy material through its portrait of Black performers and writers in the film industry.

K:501f494331a3.title: The Wig
K:501f494331a3.author: Charles Wright
K:501f494331a3.description: Lester Jefferson, a young Black man in 1960s New York, uses hair straightener to grow silken curls he calls "The Wig," believing it will let him join the Great Society, and stumbles through a series of absurd misadventures and rejections. A satirical novel using absurd humor to expose the era's racial dynamics.

K:b5d527740304.title: Black Magic
K:b5d527740304.author: Amiri Baraka
K:b5d527740304.description: Three sequences of poems, Sabotage, Target Study, and Black Art, collect work written between 1961 and 1967 that moves from recognizing American racial injustice toward a militant Black nationalist manifesto. A collection marking the poet's break from white culture and turn to Black nationalism.

K:9cc5b917e8b7.title: Snake-back Solos
K:9cc5b917e8b7.author: Quincy Troupe
K:9cc5b917e8b7.description: Selected poems written between 1969 and 1977 mix jazz rhythms, street speech, and personal and political subjects from an African American poet's voice. The collection won an American Book Award.

K:a17eec71ce8a.title: Solitudes Crowded with Loneliness: Selected Poems 1969-1977
K:a17eec71ce8a.author: Bob Kaufman
K:a17eec71ce8a.description: A decade of poems gathers odes to Charles Mingus, Hart Crane, Ray Charles, and Albert Camus alongside love lyrics, political rants, prison poems, and the prose meditation "Second April." The first collection by a San Francisco Beat poet known for spontaneous, jazz-inflected oral verse.

K:61ba8d737730.title: Sitting Pretty
K:61ba8d737730.author: Al Young
K:61ba8d737730.description: Over one year, Sidney J. Prettymon, a divorced and unemployed San Francisco man known as Sit, philosophizes about life on a radio call-in show, fights drinking and jail time, reconnects with his cancer-stricken ex-wife, and lands work pitching shows. A comic novel carried by Prettymon's first-person voice.

K:bf8d0f88d122.title: The Big Sky
K:bf8d0f88d122.author: A. B. Guthrie
K:bf8d0f88d122.description: Hot-tempered young Boone Caudill flees an abusive Kentucky home in the 1830s, heads up the Missouri River, and becomes a fur trapper and mountain man, marrying the Blackfoot woman Teal Eye before jealousy drives him to kill his closest friend. The first of six novels in a sequence tracing the American West, noted for depicting frontier life without romanticism.

K:95d47d6a83b3.title: The Moon and Sixpence
K:95d47d6a83b3.author: W. Somerset Maugham
K:95d47d6a83b3.description: Charles Strickland, a middle-aged London stockbroker, abruptly abandons his wife and children to become a painter, lives in poverty in Paris, ruins a friend's marriage, and finally settles in Tahiti with a young woman. The story is loosely based on the life of the painter Paul Gauguin.

K:96f5809e4069.title: Aesop's Fables
K:96f5809e4069.description: Short tales, most featuring talking animals, each end in a moral lesson about virtues and vices such as cunning, vanity, and the consequences of one's actions. A collection credited to a Greek storyteller and passed down and expanded over centuries as the best-known body of fables.

K:511f77d53adb.title: The legends of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table
K:511f77d53adb.description: Retold tales of King Arthur, his wizard Merlin, Queen Guinevere, and the knights of Camelot, who gather at the Round Table, swear a code of chivalry, and undertake quests including the search for the Holy Grail. A retelling of the Arthurian legends drawn from the medieval tradition behind works such as Le Morte d'Arthur.

K:d20e64b8c042.title: Henry IV, Parts I
K:d20e64b8c042.author: William Shakespeare
K:d20e64b8c042.description: King Henry IV faces rebellion from the fiery Hotspur and his allies while his son Prince Hal idles in taverns with the boastful Sir John Falstaff, then redeems himself by killing Hotspur at the Battle of Shrewsbury. A history play balancing court politics, comic tavern scenes, and Hal's coming of age.

K:e75a67015493.title: The Ballad of the Sad Café
K:e75a67015493.author: Carson McCullers
K:e75a67015493.description: In an isolated Southern town, the strong, solitary Miss Amelia Evans takes in a hunchbacked stranger, Cousin Lymon, and opens a café, until her ex-husband Marvin Macy returns and Lymon's infatuation with him brings on a brawl that ruins her. A novella about a love triangle, first published in a magazine and later collected with short stories.

K:fa57ad62d5c6.title: La Bête Humaine
K:fa57ad62d5c6.author: Émile Zola
K:fa57ad62d5c6.description: Engine driver Jacques Lantier, afflicted by an urge to kill women, works the Paris–Le Havre railway line in the late 1860s and becomes entangled with stationmaster Roubaud and his wife Séverine after Roubaud murders a man aboard a train. The seventeenth novel in the Rougon-Macquart series, set among railway workers.

K:c22e8571b3fc.title: Geek Love
K:c22e8571b3fc.author: Katherine Dunn
K:c22e8571b3fc.description: Carnival owners Al and Lil Binewski deliberately breed deformed children using drugs and radioactive material, and their albino dwarf daughter Olympia narrates how her brother Arturo, born with flippers, builds a cult whose followers have their limbs amputated. A novel about a traveling family freak show that was a National Book Award finalist.

K:f495c2bbe6aa.title: Almost Paradise
K:f495c2bbe6aa.author: Susan Isaacs
K:f495c2bbe6aa.description: Nicholas and Jane Cobleigh meet as students at Brown, marry despite different backgrounds, and rise to fame as he becomes a Hollywood star and she overcomes agoraphobia, before career strain and infidelity pull them apart and an accident leaves Jane near death. A novel tracing the rise and unraveling of a celebrity marriage.

K:8cc7ecd87308.title: Shining Through
K:8cc7ecd87308.author: Susan Isaacs
K:8cc7ecd87308.description: Linda Voss, a secretary from Queens secretly in love with her Wall Street lawyer boss, marries him and is drawn into wartime intelligence work for the OSS, eventually going undercover in Nazi Berlin. A Second World War novel later adapted into a 1992 film.

K:1fd1f5c65114.title: A Tree Grows in Brooklyn
K:1fd1f5c65114.author: Betty Smith
K:1fd1f5c65114.description: Beginning in 1912, eleven-year-old Francie Nolan grows up poor in the Williamsburg tenements of Brooklyn with her brother Neely, hardworking mother, and charming but alcoholic father, navigating poverty and the hopes of an Irish-German immigrant family. A semi-autobiographical coming-of-age novel.

K:99a15e609eba.title: Sheila Levine Is Dead and Living in New York
K:99a15e609eba.author: Gail Parent
K:99a15e609eba.description: Past thirty, unmarried, and exhausted from searching for a nice Jewish husband, Sheila Levine decides to kill herself and writes a long suicide note recounting her misadventures in New York. A dark comic novel framed entirely as that suicide note.

K:9dba8bbf7481.title: Pearl
K:9dba8bbf7481.author: Tabitha King
K:9dba8bbf7481.description: Pearl Dickinson arrives in the small town of Nodd's Ridge, Maine, takes over the local diner, and wins the affection of garage owner Reuben Styles and the unstable poet David Christopher, drawing her into the town's tangled web of love, jealousy, and old secrets. A novel set in a close-knit Maine community.

K:f3bd7d9cd95b.title: Everybody Pays
K:f3bd7d9cd95b.author: Andrew Vachss
K:f3bd7d9cd95b.description: Crime stories take readers into the workings of evil through figures such as a fugitive blues musician, urban mercenaries, and the crook Cross, whose crew breaks a young woman out of a Peruvian jail in the title novella. A collection of thirty-eight stories, the author's second.

K:657b2b4a5716.title: Rule of the Bone
K:657b2b4a5716.author: Russell Banks
K:657b2b4a5716.description: Chappie, a 14-year-old who drops out of school and gets a tattoo that earns him the name Bone, drifts through trouble in upstate New York before traveling to Jamaica under the guidance of a Rastafarian migrant worker called I-Man. A coming-of-age novel told in the narrator's voice.

K:6e39cb76d442.title: Gone with the Wind
K:6e39cb76d442.author: Margaret Mitchell
K:6e39cb76d442.description: Willful Southern belle Scarlett O'Hara struggles to hold onto her family's Georgia plantation, Tara, through the Civil War and Reconstruction, pining for the married Ashley Wilkes while clashing with the roguish Rhett Butler. A best-selling novel that won the 1937 Pulitzer Prize and inspired the 1939 film.

K:5b01431b2a0f.title: The Paper Bag Princess
K:5b01431b2a0f.author: Robert Munsch
K:5b01431b2a0f.description: When a dragon burns down her castle and carries off Prince Ronald, Princess Elizabeth, left with only a paper bag to wear, tracks the dragon to its cave, tricks it into exhausting itself, and frees Ronald, who then complains about her appearance. A children's picture book that reverses the princess-and-dragon fairy tale.

K:85c796e3a0f0.title: Turtle Moon
K:85c796e3a0f0.author: Alice Hoffman
K:85c796e3a0f0.description: In Verity, Florida, recently divorced Lucy Rosen's troubled son Keith finds an abandoned baby and flees after the infant's mother is found murdered, leading cop Julian Cash to search for the boy and uncover the killing. A novel set during the May turtle-nesting season.

K:39d2beb10b6e.title: The Time Traveler's Wife
K:39d2beb10b6e.author: Audrey Niffennegger
K:39d2beb10b6e.description: Henry DeTamble, a Chicago librarian with a genetic disorder that pulls him uncontrollably through time, repeatedly meets the artist Clare Abshire at different ages, and the two build a marriage strained by his unpredictable disappearances. A debut novel told in alternating first-person perspectives and later adapted for film and television.

K:429ebb6de68d.title: The Patron Saint of Liars
K:429ebb6de68d.author: Ann Patchett
K:429ebb6de68d.description: Rose, unhappily married and newly pregnant in California, abandons her husband and drives to St. Elizabeth's, a Kentucky home for unwed mothers, where she stays on, marries the caretaker, and conceals her first marriage for the rest of her life. A debut novel told in turn by Rose, her husband, and her daughter Sissy.

K:186d7e7da316.title: Ill Seen, Ill Said
K:186d7e7da316.author: Samuel Beckett
K:186d7e7da316.description: An aging, solitary woman moves through a bleak landscape between her cabin and a gravestone, watched by an unnamed observing eye that struggles to see and describe her clearly. A short late prose work that pushes language toward minimalism and silence.

K:9529cd67cb83.title: Dirty Snow
K:9529cd67cb83.author: Georges Simenon
K:9529cd67cb83.description: Frank, the nineteen-year-old son of a brothel keeper in a German-occupied town, drifts into theft and murders an officer while deliberately letting a neighbor witness the killing, then sinks further into crime during a relentless winter. A bleak study of a young criminal's mind, written outside the author's detective fiction.

K:f3bef513288a.title: New Grub Street
K:f3bef513288a.author: George Gissing
K:f3bef513288a.description: In the literary and journalistic world of 1880s London, the talented but uncommercial novelist Edwin Reardon watches his health and marriage collapse, while the cynical, self-promoting journalist Jasper Milvain rises to wealth and influence. A novel about poverty and ambition in the Victorian publishing trade.

K:adc0c3e969c5.title: Go Down, Moses
K:adc0c3e969c5.author: William Faulkner
K:adc0c3e969c5.description: Across seven linked stories, the McCaslin-Beauchamp family of Mississippi moves from slavery to the eve of World War II, centered on Isaac McCaslin, who in "The Bear" learns the woods and later renounces his tainted inheritance. The book traces race, kinship, and the history of the American South.

K:86c79232ad7b.title: Letters to Yesenin
K:86c79232ad7b.author: Jim Harrison
K:86c79232ad7b.description: In thirty prose-poem letters addressed to the Russian poet Sergei Yesenin, who hanged himself in 1925, the writer confides his own depression, suicidal thoughts, poverty, and daily life on a Michigan farm. A book of poems written during a period of personal crisis.

K:f15eab275905.title: Big Bad Love
K:f15eab275905.author: Larry Brown
K:f15eab275905.description: Ten stories follow rural Mississippi men who drink too much, chase women, and drive pickup trucks, including a writer on trial for plagiarism and another chronicling his struggle to get published. A collection about working-class Southern lives, sex, and obsession.

K:43a7a41f5606.title: The Complete Poems of Anna Ahkmatova
K:43a7a41f5606.author: Anna Ahkmatova
K:43a7a41f5606.description: More than eight hundred poems gather the lifetime work of a Russian poet, drawn from her early books through her later sequences on love, loss, and life under Soviet repression. The definitive English-language edition of her collected verse.

K:b8f63c3e8554.title: Self-Portrait with Woman
K:b8f63c3e8554.author: Andrzej Szczypiorski
K:b8f63c3e8554.description: Kamil, a Warsaw sociologist summoned to Geneva for an oral-history project on the fall of Eastern European communism, recounts his life through portraits of the women he has loved against six decades of Polish history. A novel of memory, love, and political survival, originally published in Polish.

K:5c6f63dda7c1.title: Hugging the Shore: Essays and Criticism
K:5c6f63dda7c1.author: John Updike
K:5c6f63dda7c1.description: A large gathering of book reviews and essays surveys writers including Nabokov, Melville, Hawthorne, Whitman, Edmund Wilson, and Muriel Spark, along with pieces on figures such as Doris Day and Louise Brooks. A critical collection that won the National Book Critics Circle Award.

K:0a427d1f8faf.title: The Painted Bird
K:0a427d1f8faf.author: Jerzy Kosinski
K:0a427d1f8faf.description: A dark-eyed boy taken for a Jew or Gypsy wanders alone through villages in wartime Eastern Europe after his foster mother dies, enduring beatings, abuse, and cruelty from superstitious peasants. A novel about a child's survival amid the violence of World War II.

K:7b6996b5e5d9.title: The Last Chronicle of Barset
K:7b6996b5e5d9.author: Anthony Trollope
K:7b6996b5e5d9.description: In the cathedral county of Barsetshire, the poor, proud curate Josiah Crawley is accused of stealing a cheque, an accusation that strains his family and friends, while subplots follow Grace Crawley's courtship and the death of Mrs. Proudie. The final novel in the Barsetshire series.

K:1d2a45e65297.title: Summer Lightning
K:1d2a45e65297.author: P. G. Wodehouse
K:1d2a45e65297.description: At Blandings Castle, Lord Emsworth's prize pig the Empress is stolen and his brother Galahad's scandalous memoirs threaten the family's reputation, as several thwarted couples scheme amid mistaken identities. A comic novel in the Blandings Castle series.

K:10150da613f8.title: Edisto
K:10150da613f8.author: Padget Powell
K:10150da613f8.description: Simons Manigault, a precocious twelve-year-old raised on a remote stretch of the South Carolina coast by his eccentric mother, befriends a mysterious drifter named Taurus who introduces him to the wider adult world. A coming-of-age novel narrated by the boy.

K:2753623cf2c8.title: Nausea
K:2753623cf2c8.author: Jean
K:2753623cf2c8.description: Antoine Roquentin, a solitary historian living in the seaside town of Bouville while researching an eighteenth-century figure, is overtaken by waves of revulsion he calls "the Nausea" as ordinary objects lose their familiar meaning. A philosophical novel in diary form, central to existentialism.

K:1142c6098f6d.title: The Histories
K:1142c6098f6d.author: Herodotus
K:1142c6098f6d.description: A long prose account in nine books traces the rise of the Persian Empire and the causes and course of the Greco-Persian Wars, weaving in geography, customs, and stories of the peoples of the known world. An early work of history by the writer called the "Father of History."

K:fc55a5b4798e.title: The Good Soldier Svejk
K:fc55a5b4798e.author: Jaroslav Hasek
K:fc55a5b4798e.description: Josef Svejk, a Prague dog dealer of dubious wits, is drafted into the Austro-Hungarian army during World War I and bumbles through arrests, asylums, and the front, his cheerful obedience exposing the absurdity of the war machine. An unfinished satirical novel in multiple volumes.

K:97c74aaee58b.title: Novellas
K:97c74aaee58b.author: Leo Tolstoy
K:97c74aaee58b.description: A collection of shorter fiction gathers works such as "The Death of Ivan Ilyich," "Master and Man," "The Kreutzer Sonata," and "Hadji Murad," ranging over death, faith, marriage, and war. Short novels and tales from the author's later career.

K:3dff16151b37.title: Burning Your Boats: The Collected Short Stories
K:3dff16151b37.author: Angela Carter
K:3dff16151b37.description: Forty-two stories, gathering the author's four published collections along with early and uncollected work, retell fairy tales and folklore and range from Japan and jazz to Gothic and surreal modern settings. A posthumous volume of her complete short fiction.

K:18a93d157004.title: The House of Breath
K:18a93d157004.author: William Goyen
K:18a93d157004.description: The narrator addresses the people and places he recalls from his childhood in the small Texas town of Charity, including the relative Folner who left and returns home in a cheap coffin. A first novel built from plotless, image-driven meditations on memory, family, and place.

K:19d0058befb1.title: Sixty Stories
K:19d0058befb1.author: Donald Barthelme
K:19d0058befb1.description: Sixty stories drawn from the author's first six collections mix collage, parody, and absurd invention, treating modern anxieties with fragmented and unconventional forms. A gathering of his short fiction, much of it first published in The New Yorker.

K:1eb8c32d422e.title: The Street of Crocodiles
K:1eb8c32d422e.author: Bruno Schulz
K:1eb8c32d422e.description: In a Galician town, the boy Jozef narrates the decline of his father Jacob, a merchant slipping into psychosis, amid transformations of objects, seasons, and the disreputable district of the title. A collection of interlinked stories, originally published in Polish.

K:20121da40aef.title: Amours de Voyage
K:20121da40aef.author: Arthur Hugh Clough
K:20121da40aef.description: Among English tourists in Rome during the Roman Republic of 1848, the hesitant young Claude falls for Mary Trevellyn but cannot bring himself to act, and the two repeatedly fail to connect as the French army besieges the city. A verse novel told through letters.

K:4c52ca01da6f.title: The Woman in the Dunes
K:4c52ca01da6f.author: Kobo Abe
K:4c52ca01da6f.description: Jumpei Niki, a Tokyo teacher collecting insects, misses his bus and is lodged by villagers in a house at the bottom of a sand pit, where he is trapped and made to shovel back the encroaching sand alongside the woman who lives there. A novel about confinement and the meaning of existence.

K:bf7805dad43e.title: Life & Times of Michael K
K:bf7805dad43e.author: J. M. Coetzee
K:bf7805dad43e.description: Michael K, a simple Cape Town gardener with a cleft lip, sets out during a civil war to carry his dying mother to her rural birthplace, then lives alone tending a garden as authorities repeatedly detain him in camps. A novel set in a war-torn South Africa that won the Booker Prize.

K:711ea85aabb6.title: A Man of the People
K:711ea85aabb6.author: Chinua Achebe
K:711ea85aabb6.description: Odili, a young teacher in a newly independent African country, grows disillusioned with his former schoolmaster Chief Nanga, a corrupt government minister, and after a personal betrayal joins a rival party to oppose him until a military coup intervenes. A satirical novel of postcolonial politics.

K:0ebceaccfbc5.title: For Bread Alone
K:0ebceaccfbc5.author: Mohamed Choukri
K:0ebceaccfbc5.description: Beginning in the famine-struck Rif in 1942, the narrator recounts a childhood of hunger and a brutal father, then his life as a homeless adolescent in Tangier amid theft, drugs, and prostitution before he learns to read at twenty. The first volume of the author's autobiography, originally written in Arabic.

K:a643b2fb24c7.title: A Wrinkle in Time
K:a643b2fb24c7.author: Madeline L'Engle
K:a643b2fb24c7.description: Meg Murry, her brother Charles Wallace, and their friend Calvin travel through space and time, guided by three otherworldly beings, to rescue Meg's scientist father and confront the dark force IT on the planet Camazotz. A children's science-fantasy novel that won the Newbery Medal.

K:67787770c51b.title: The Ponder Heart
K:67787770c51b.author: Eudora Welty
K:67787770c51b.description: In rural Clay County, Mississippi, the wealthy, childlike Uncle Daniel gives away the family fortune and drifts through marriages until he lands in a murder trial, all retold by his garrulous niece Edna Earle. A short comic novel driven by Edna Earle's talkative narration.

K:1a7a36a0d16e.title: Kristin Lavransdatter
K:1a7a36a0d16e.author: Sigrid Undset
K:1a7a36a0d16e.description: In fourteenth-century Norway, Kristin Lavransdatter defies her father to marry the man she desires, then lives through a turbulent marriage, motherhood, sin, and faith before dying of plague in a convent. A trilogy of historical novels set in the Middle Ages.

K:341323661942.title: The Sheltered Life
K:341323661942.author: Ellen Glasgow
K:341323661942.description: In a declining Richmond neighborhood before World War I, young Jenny Blair Archbald idolizes her beautiful neighbor Eva Birdsong and grows attracted to Eva's unfaithful husband George, until Eva discovers them and shoots him dead. A novel about the evasions of genteel Southern society.

K:a16808037043.title: River of Earth
K:a16808037043.author: James Still
K:a16808037043.description: A young boy watches his Appalachian family in eastern Kentucky waver between scratching out a living as independent farmers and taking uncertain work in the coal mines. A novel of mountain life narrated by the child.

K:375a9e07d437.title: Arcadia
K:375a9e07d437.author: Tom Stoppard
K:375a9e07d437.description: At an English country house, two timelines unfold side by side: in the early 1800s the young mathematician Thomasina works with her tutor Septimus, while in the present academics Hannah and Bernard piece together what happened there. A play that interweaves science, Romanticism, and the limits of knowledge.

K:10471e0b18f2.title: The Chronicles of Narnia
K:10471e0b18f2.author: C.S. Lewis
K:10471e0b18f2.description: Four English children pass through a wardrobe into Narnia, a land of talking animals and mythical creatures ruled by the lion Aslan, and across seven books they help free it from the White Witch and other tyrants. A fantasy series with Christian allegory, illustrated by Pauline Baynes.

K:0fca861b17e1.title: Paris Trout
K:0fca861b17e1.author: Pete Dexter
K:0fca861b17e1.description: In a small Georgia town in the 1950s, the bigoted store owner and loan shark Paris Trout shoots and kills a young Black girl and wounds her mother over a car-deal dispute, then bribes and blackmails his way clear of real punishment as his grip on reality unravels. It won the National Book Award for Fiction.

K:78a38f583c34.title: The Book of Leviathan
K:78a38f583c34.author: Peter Blegvad
K:78a38f583c34.description: Levi, a faceless baby clutching a stuffed rabbit, drifts through surreal episodes alongside a talking cat in a comic strip that ran in The Independent on Sunday, collected here in one volume. Known for blending dream logic with childhood whimsy.

K:1e0a4d7bcb95.title: 1982, Janine
K:1e0a4d7bcb95.author: Alasdair Gray
K:1e0a4d7bcb95.description: Jock McLeish, a divorced and alcoholic alarm-system supervisor nearing fifty, spends a sleepless night in a Scottish hotel room assembling an elaborate pornographic fantasy while memories of his real life break in and drive him toward a suicide attempt. Known for its typographic experimentation and its use of pornography as a narrative device.

K:f3f337c3afb6.title: The Beans of Egypt, Maine
K:f3f337c3afb6.author: Carolyn Chute
K:f3f337c3afb6.description: In the poor rural town of Egypt, Maine, the large and hard-living Bean family struggles with drink, the law, and grinding poverty, all watched across the road by young Earlene, who lives with her widowed father. It established the author's fictional Egypt and its working-class characters.

K:51e6b95a9cd3.title: Letourneau's Used Auto Parts
K:51e6b95a9cd3.author: Carolyn Chute
K:51e6b95a9cd3.description: In Egypt, Maine, and the neighboring shantytown of Miracle City, the junkyard owner Big Lucien Letourneau shelters the destitute, elderly, and homeless along with his many children and ex-wives while struggling to pay the men who work his auto-salvage yard. A second novel set in the author's impoverished fictional Maine.

K:1add81b78f3d.title: Merry Men
K:1add81b78f3d.author: Carolyn Chute
K:1add81b78f3d.description: Across two generations in Egypt, Maine, the Barrington and Johnson families live out poverty and eccentricity, from tree-planting Lloyd Barrington to road-keeper Forest Johnson, while a hunting death and a widow's return stir the town's tensions of class and privilege. A novel continuing the author's portrait of rural Maine.

K:46a4b1d05491.title: The Horse's Mouth
K:46a4b1d05491.author: Joyce Cary
K:46a4b1d05491.description: Just out of jail, the aging and irrepressible painter Gulley Jimson scrounges money from patrons, chases an old painting held by his former wife Sara, and pursues grand mural visions across London until a stroke ends his work. Told in the artist's voice, the third book of the author's First Trilogy.

K:55139e036082.title: Death of the Fox
K:55139e036082.author: George Garrett
K:55139e036082.description: Sir Walter Raleigh, fallen from favor and condemned under James I, awaits and faces execution while his memories reconstruct Elizabethan England and his service to Queen Elizabeth I. A long historical novel, the first volume of the author's Elizabethan Trilogy.

K:2472ca9a8402.title: The Succession
K:2472ca9a8402.author: George Garrett
K:2472ca9a8402.description: As Elizabeth I's reign nears its end, the aging queen and James VI of Scotland maneuver through letters, rivalries, and intrigue over who will inherit the English throne. A historical novel built from period documents, the second volume of the author's Elizabethan Trilogy.

K:9f73cdf60017.title: Entered from the Sun
K:9f73cdf60017.author: George Garrett
K:9f73cdf60017.description: In 1597, four years after Christopher Marlowe's killing, the out-of-work actor Joseph Hunnyman and the scarred former soldier William Barfoot are hired by rival factions to investigate the playwright's death in Elizabethan London. A historical novel, the third volume of the author's Elizabethan Trilogy.

K:c984175795c3.title: Continental Drift
K:c984175795c3.author: Russell Banks
K:c984175795c3.description: Bob Dubois, a discontented New Hampshire oil-burner repairman, moves his family to Florida chasing a better life and slides into crime, while Vanise Dorsinville flees Haiti by boat toward the same coast, their paths converging fatally in Miami's Little Haiti. A novel about American greed, immigration, and economic desperation.

K:87301aefcad9.title: Street of Lost Footsteps
K:87301aefcad9.author: Lyonel Trouillot
K:87301aefcad9.description: Over one violent night in Port-au-Prince, a brothel madam, a taxi driver, and a postal worker narrate the chaos of an uprising pitting the Prophet's followers against the dictator Deceased Forever-Immortal. Translated from French, it sets present-day bloodshed against centuries of Haitian history.

K:326fa432a334.title: The Conference of the Birds
K:326fa432a334.author: Farid ud
K:326fa432a334.description: The birds of the world gather to seek a king and set out under the hoopoe's guidance to find the legendary Simorgh, crossing seven valleys until only thirty survive and discover the divine they sought within themselves. A Persian Sufi allegorical poem of more than four thousand lines.

K:f8d2878ae6e1.title: The Complete Aubrey/Maturin Novels
K:f8d2878ae6e1.author: Patrick O'Brian
K:f8d2878ae6e1.description: Captain Jack Aubrey of the Royal Navy and his ship's surgeon and intelligence agent Stephen Maturin form a lasting friendship across twenty completed naval novels set during the Napoleonic Wars. A historical sequence collected here, noted for its period detail and its central male friendship.

K:abe0b2fd942d.title: Antony and Cleopatra
K:abe0b2fd942d.author: William Shakespeare
K:abe0b2fd942d.description: Torn between his passion for Cleopatra in Egypt and his duties as a Roman triumvir, Mark Antony marries Octavius Caesar's sister but returns to the queen, leading to war at Actium and, after defeat, the suicides of both lovers. A tragedy drawn from Plutarch's account of the Roman world.

K:f4a7c850e2d0.title: The Three Sisters
K:f4a7c850e2d0.author: Anton Chekhov
K:f4a7c850e2d0.description: Stuck in a provincial Russian town, the cultured Prozorov sisters Olga, Masha, and Irina long to return to Moscow while their brother Andrei's marriage and debts erode the family's hopes and the army garrison that enlivens their lives departs. A play about thwarted longing and provincial stagnation.

K:318a64542de6.title: The Old Wives' Tale
K:318a64542de6.author: Arnold Bennett
K:318a64542de6.description: Constance and Sophia Baines, daughters of a draper in the Staffordshire town of Bursley, follow very different paths over sixty years, the steady Constance staying home while the bold Sophia elopes to Paris, until the sisters are reunited in old age. A realist novel tracing two ordinary lives.

K:2640473d9825.title: Sunset Song
K:2640473d9825.author: Lewis Grassic Gibbon
K:2640473d9825.description: Chris Guthrie comes of age on a farm in the fictional parish of Kinraddie in northeast Scotland, enduring her mother's suicide, her harsh father, marriage, childbirth, and widowhood as the First World War shatters her rural community. Written in Scots-inflected prose, the first part of the trilogy A Scots Quair.

K:82d873c938c3.title: A Simple Heart
K:82d873c938c3.author: Gustave Flaubert
K:82d873c938c3.description: Félicité, a devoted servant in provincial Normandy, gives her affection over a lifetime to her mistress's children, her nephew, and finally a parrot, losing each in turn until she dies imagining the bird as the Holy Ghost. A short story published in the collection Three Tales.

K:c44bc6707def.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
K:c44bc6707def.author: Thomas Hardy
K:c44bc6707def.description: Bathsheba Everdene, a headstrong young woman who inherits a farm in rural Wessex, is courted by the steadfast shepherd Gabriel Oak, the obsessive landowner William Boldwood, and the reckless soldier Sergeant Troy, whom she marries to her cost. The author's first major success, serialized anonymously in Cornhill Magazine.

K:4c8daf6025b8.title: Charming Billy
K:4c8daf6025b8.author: Alice McDermott
K:4c8daf6025b8.description: At Billy Lynch's funeral in an Irish Catholic community in Queens, family and friends recall his lifelong drinking and the lost love of Eva, an Irish girl whose desertion was hidden from him by a cousin's lie that she had died. It won the National Book Award for Fiction.

K:93826f95527b.title: The Age of Grief
K:93826f95527b.author: Jane Smiley
K:93826f95527b.description: A thirty-five-year-old dentist gradually realizes his wife, his professional partner, is in love with another man, and he struggles over whether to confront her or feign ignorance while caring for their three young daughters. The title novella, paired with five short stories.

K:551d456e5736.title: The Feast of Love
K:551d456e5736.author: Charles Baxter
K:551d456e5736.description: Walking the predawn streets of Ann Arbor, an insomniac writer meets his neighbor Bradley, who recounts overlapping stories of love among friends and lovers, including Bradley's two failed marriages and the longings of Chloé, Oscar, and others. A novel told through interwoven first-person accounts.

K:8536b3d2e012.title: Harriet the Spy
K:8536b3d2e012.author: Louise Fitzhugh
K:8536b3d2e012.description: Eleven-year-old Harriet M. Welsch roams her Upper East Side neighborhood recording blunt observations of everyone in a secret notebook, until classmates find it, read her harsh judgments, and turn on her. A children's novel often cited as a landmark in the genre.

K:7d841d955f13.title: Gusev
K:7d841d955f13.author: Anton Chekhov
K:7d841d955f13.description: Aboard a ship carrying discharged soldiers home from the Far East, the dying peasant Gusev lies in the sick-bay arguing with the consumptive intellectual Pavel Ivanitch, drifting into homesick delirium before his death and burial at sea. A short story drawn from the author's own voyage from Sakhalin.

K:181ab9076020.title: Peter Pan
K:181ab9076020.author: J. M. Barrie
K:181ab9076020.description: Peter Pan, the boy who refuses to grow up, flies into the Darlings' London nursery and carries Wendy and her brothers to Neverland, where they join the Lost Boys and face the pirate Captain Hook. A stage play later expanded into the novel Peter and Wendy.

K:e815f844e746.title: The Diary of a Country Priest
K:e815f844e746.author: Georges Bernanos
K:e815f844e746.description: A young, sickly priest newly assigned to the parish of Ambricourt in northern France records in his journal his struggles with a hostile flock, his own doubts, and the stomach cancer that is killing him. A novel framed as the priest's diary, awarded the Grand Prix du roman de l'Académie française.

K:5fe6c7acdf20.title: Pale Horse, Pale Rider
K:5fe6c7acdf20.author: Katherine Anne Porter
K:5fe6c7acdf20.description: Three short novels include the title story, in which the newspaperwoman Miranda and the soldier Adam fall in love in Denver during the 1918 influenza epidemic that nearly kills her and does kill him, alongside "Old Mortality" and "Noon Wine." A volume of short fiction.

K:6c0d609d9d64.title: Armies of the Night
K:6c0d609d9d64.author: Norman Mailer
K:6c0d609d9d64.description: Recounting the October 1967 March on the Pentagon against the Vietnam War, the author casts himself in the third person as a participant among hippies, pacifists, and intellectuals, then shifts to a wider historical account of the protest. A nonfiction novel that won the Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award.

K:2f4c8d677be7.title: Begin Again: Collected Poems
K:2f4c8d677be7.author: Grace Paley
K:2f4c8d677be7.description: Poems gathered from a lifetime range over New York City life, rural Vermont, friendship, and political protest, combining the author's two earlier collections with previously unpublished work. A collected volume by a writer better known for short fiction.

K:f7a78d944a1a.title: Duty of Delight: The Diaries of Dorothy Day
K:f7a78d944a1a.description: Spanning 1934 to 1980, these diaries record the daily life, faith, and activism of the Catholic Worker movement's co-founder, from its founding through the days before her death, drawn from journals sealed for twenty-five years. Edited by Robert Ellsberg and published by Marquette University Press.

K:dc3157e14d3a.title: Every War Has Two Losers
K:dc3157e14d3a.author: William Stafford
K:dc3157e14d3a.description: Excerpts from the poet's daily journals between 1951 and 1991, along with questions and reflections, lay out a lifelong case against war drawn from his experience as a World War II conscientious objector. A posthumously published selection from a lifetime of journals.

K:757e916ddfbf.title: Nothing Ever Dies: Vietnam and the Memory of War
K:757e916ddfbf.author: Viet Nguyen
K:757e916ddfbf.description: Drawing on history, film, literature, and museum studies, the book examines how the Vietnam War is remembered and forgotten in the United States, Vietnam, and beyond, arguing that all wars are fought twice, first on the battlefield and then in memory. A work of cultural criticism that calls for an ethics of "just memory" recognizing the humanity of all sides. A finalist for the National Book Award in nonfiction.

K:3a782691b2f8.title: Peace is Every Step
K:3a782691b2f8.author: Thich Nhat Hanh
K:3a782691b2f8.description: Across three sections, a Zen monk offers meditations, exercises, and personal anecdotes for practicing mindfulness in daily life, beginning with conscious breathing and moving through transforming difficult emotions toward peace and engaged action. A widely read introduction to Buddhist mindfulness practice for Western readers.

K:ed1f9faeb251.title: A Primer for Forgetting
K:ed1f9faeb251.author: Lewis Hyde
K:ed1f9faeb251.description: Drawing on figures from Hesiod to Borges and on personal experience including his mother's dementia, the book gathers collage-like entries arguing that forgetting is not only loss but a path to peace, renewal, and the ability to move past trauma. A blend of scholarship, memoir, and social criticism organized around an imaginary Museum of Forgetting.

K:b76811e41ab1.title: Veterans of War, Veterans of Peace
K:b76811e41ab1.author: Maxine Hong Kingston
K:b76811e41ab1.description: Compiled from writing-and-meditation workshops led for hundreds of war veterans, the anthology gathers poems and prose by combatants, war widows, children, conscientious objectors, and survivors of abuse, spanning five wars. A collection focused on trauma, healing, and the aftermath of violence.

K:4d294337a579.title: War Is a Force That Gives Us Meaning
K:4d294337a579.author: Chris Hedges
K:4d294337a579.description: Drawing on classical literature and his years as a war correspondent in Central America and the Balkans, the author argues that war seduces whole societies with myths and a sense of purpose, and can become exhilarating and addictive even as it destroys. A finalist for the National Book Critics Circle Award and a bestseller.

K:ccbd99f8db96.title: Scaramouche
K:ccbd99f8db96.author: Rafael Sabatini
K:ccbd99f8db96.description: Andre-Louis Moreau, a young lawyer in Revolution-era France, vows vengeance after a nobleman provokes and kills his idealistic friend in a duel, then hides among traveling commedia dell'arte players as the clown Scaramouche before becoming a fencing master and revolutionary. A historical adventure set during the French Revolution.

K:0bbe1409ea00.title: Tales of Mystery and Imagination
K:0bbe1409ea00.author: Edgar Allan Poe
K:0bbe1409ea00.description: Suspenseful Gothic and detective tales collected under this title, including "The Fall of the House of Usher," "The Tell-Tale Heart," "The Pit and the Pendulum," "The Cask of Amontillado," and the Dupin stories "The Murders in the Rue Morgue" and "The Purloined Letter." The first collection to gather these Gothic and mystery stories under this enduring title.

K:08a7cf1a0712.title: The Day of the Locust
K:08a7cf1a0712.author: Nathanael West
K:08a7cf1a0712.description: Tod Hackett, a young set designer at a Hollywood studio, becomes entangled with a crowd of failed actors, hangers-on, and disappointed people who came to California to die, while planning a painting called "The Burning of Los Angeles." It ends in a frenzied mob at a film premiere. A novel about Hollywood and the disillusionment behind the American dream.

K:d0a40c7217af.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
K:d0a40c7217af.author: Ken Kesey
K:d0a40c7217af.description: On a psychiatric ward ruled by the controlling Nurse Ratched, the brash con man Randle McMurphy feigns insanity to avoid prison labor and incites the patients to rebel, narrated by the silent, supposedly deaf Chief Bromden. A novel about institutional authority and individuality that ends in lobotomy and a mercy killing.

K:4f66351958b2.title: The Public Burning
K:4f66351958b2.author: Robert Coover
K:4f66351958b2.description: Vice President Richard Nixon narrates the days before the 1953 execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, which becomes a public spectacle staged in Times Square, presided over by a folksy, foul-mouthed Uncle Sam battling the communist Phantom. A satirical novel mixing real and fictional figures from Cold War America.

K:87c8463799ea.title: Dom Casmurro
K:87c8463799ea.author: Joaquim Maria Machado de Assis
K:87c8463799ea.description: Bento Santiago, an elderly Brazilian man nicknamed Dom Casmurro, looks back on his youth in Rio de Janeiro, his love for his childhood sweetheart Capitu whom he abandons the seminary to marry, and his growing suspicion that she betrayed him with his best friend Escobar. A novel known for its unreliable narrator and deliberate ambiguity about Capitu's guilt.

K:9d1689f04b64.title: Outer Dark
K:9d1689f04b64.author: Cormac McCarthy
K:9d1689f04b64.description: In a remote, turn-of-the-century Appalachian landscape, Rinthy Holme sets out to find the infant her brother Culla fathered with her and abandoned in the woods, while Culla wanders the country pursued by a mysterious, murderous trio. A bleak novel of incest, guilt, and violence told in alternating chapters.

K:1d6d9be6aabe.title: Varieties of Religious Experience
K:1d6d9be6aabe.author: William James
K:1d6d9be6aabe.description: Drawn from the author's Gifford Lectures at Edinburgh in 1901-1902, the book studies individual religious experience and mysticism across traditions, focusing on personal conversion, saintliness, and "religious geniuses" rather than institutions. A foundational work in the psychology of religion.

K:102159e87fc4.title: Spring in Fialta
K:102159e87fc4.description: Victor, a Russian emigre, recounts his chance meetings over the years with Nina, a married fellow exile he has flirted with since a first kiss in Russia, culminating in a final encounter in the fictional Mediterranean town of Fialta. A story about memory and lost love that gives its name to a collection by the same author.

K:93e28f48bab5.title: Lord Jim
K:93e28f48bab5.author: Joseph Conrad
K:93e28f48bab5.description: The seaman Marlow pieces together the story of Jim, a young officer who abandons the pilgrim-crowded steamship Patna in a moment of panic, is publicly disgraced, and seeks redemption as a trader in the remote settlement of Patusan. A novel about guilt, honor, and a single failure that defines a life.

K:8c4c6c09644e.title: Death in Midsummer and Other Stories
K:8c4c6c09644e.author: Yukio Mishima
K:8c4c6c09644e.description: Nine stories selected by the author for translation, ranging from a family destroyed by a drowning at a seaside resort to a young officer and his wife committing ritual suicide in "Patriotism," alongside tales set among temples, actors, and modern Japanese life. A collection that spans realism, Noh drama, and traditional Japanese themes.

K:1853076a8c85.title: A Streetcar Named Desire
K:1853076a8c85.author: Tennessee Williams
K:1853076a8c85.description: The fading Southern belle Blanche DuBois arrives at the cramped New Orleans apartment of her sister Stella and Stella's brutish husband Stanley Kowalski, who exposes Blanche's hidden past, ruins her chance at marriage, and drives her toward a breakdown. A Pulitzer Prize-winning play that ends with Blanche taken away to an institution.

K:477c9d08e620.title: A Raisin in the Sun
K:477c9d08e620.author: Lorraine Hansberry
K:477c9d08e620.description: On Chicago's South Side, the Younger family awaits a ten-thousand-dollar insurance check after the father's death, with Walter Lee wanting to invest in a liquor store, Mama hoping to buy a house, and Beneatha needing tuition, until a move into a white neighborhood tests them. A play about a Black family confronting racism and deferred dreams.

K:2646e0cbd1fb.title: Gorilla, My Love
K:2646e0cbd1fb.author: Toni Cade Bambara
K:2646e0cbd1fb.description: Fifteen stories portray African Americans in urban settings from the late 1950s to the early 1970s, many narrated by sharp, streetwise young Black girls, including the title story and "The Lesson," in which children confront wealth disparity on Fifth Avenue. A collection noted for its vernacular voice and everyday community life.

K:1bf59004ee1f.title: China Men
K:1bf59004ee1f.author: Maxine Hong Kingston
K:1bf59004ee1f.description: Four generations of Chinese American men are recounted through blended history and myth, from a great-grandfather on Hawaiian sugar plantations and a grandfather building the transcontinental railroad to the author's laundryman father and a brother serving in Vietnam. A work of memoir and legend that won the National Book Award for nonfiction.

K:fcd0044b6f11.title: Call It Sleep
K:fcd0044b6f11.author: Henry Roth
K:fcd0044b6f11.description: Six-year-old David Schearl grows up in the Jewish immigrant tenements of New York's Lower East Side, caught between his loving mother Genya and his aloof, violent father Albert, while absorbing fragments of family secrets and Hebrew scripture. A modernist novel of immigrant childhood told largely through a child's perceptions.

K:7c9dee7eea81.title: A Rage in Harlem
K:7c9dee7eea81.author: Chester Himes
K:7c9dee7eea81.description: In Harlem, the gullible, devout Jackson is swindled out of his savings by his lover Imabelle and a con man's fake money-multiplying scheme, then turns to his cross-dressing twin brother Goldy as detectives Coffin Ed Johnson and Grave Digger Jones move through the chaos. The first novel in the author's Harlem crime cycle.

K:f3ee75551dbf.title: What I Loved
K:f3ee75551dbf.author: Siri Hustvedt
K:f3ee75551dbf.description: The art historian Leo Hertzberg narrates twenty-five years of friendship with the painter Bill Wechsler in New York, following the intertwined lives of their wives and sons until tragedy and a son's monstrous deceptions tear at the families. A novel about love, art, loss, and psychology.

K:f1f161897fa8.title: The Mambo Kings Play Songs of Love
K:f1f161897fa8.author: Oscar Hijuelos
K:f1f161897fa8.description: Cuban brothers Cesar and Nestor Castillo come to 1950s New York, form a mambo band, and reach a peak appearance on I Love Lucy, after which Nestor's death and fading fame leave the aging Cesar looking back on lovers, music, and a vanished way of life. A novel that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

K:de786bfe883b.title: Falling Angel
K:de786bfe883b.author: William Hjortsberg
K:de786bfe883b.description: In 1959 New York, down-and-out private investigator Harry Angel is hired by the mysterious Louis Cyphre to find a missing crooner named Johnny Favorite, and his search leads through black magic, voodoo, and a string of murders toward a damning revelation. A hardboiled detective story with supernatural horror, later filmed as Angel Heart.

K:587bd9af598e.title: The Outward Room
K:587bd9af598e.author: Millen Brand
K:587bd9af598e.description: After a breakdown following her brother's death, Harriet Demuth escapes a mental hospital, rides the rails into Depression-era New York, and pawns her belongings to survive until she meets a machine-shop worker named John and slowly rebuilds a sense of self. A novel about recovery from mental illness and an emerging love.

K:c7e7d2f655c6.title: Uncle Vanya
K:c7e7d2f655c6.author: Anton Chekhov
K:c7e7d2f655c6.description: On a decaying Russian country estate, the retired professor Serebryakov and his young second wife Yelena disrupt the lives of Vanya and his niece Sonya, who have worked the land for years, as Vanya and the doctor Astrov fall for Yelena and Vanya's resentment boils over into a botched shooting. A play about wasted lives and missed chances.

K:91b0a9fa0abe.title: The Evening of the Holiday
K:91b0a9fa0abe.author: Shirley Hazzard
K:91b0a9fa0abe.description: Sophie, a young woman of English and Italian parentage, falls into a summer love affair with Tancredi, an Italian separated from his wife, in the Italian countryside during a festival, knowing from the start that he cannot fully commit. A short first novel about a brief romance and its subtle emotional shifts.

K:44c5d47ee599.title: The Towers of Trebizond
K:44c5d47ee599.author: Rose Macaulay
K:44c5d47ee599.description: The narrator Laurie travels from Istanbul toward legendary Trebizond with her eccentric Aunt Dot, a high Anglican priest, and a temperamental camel on a mission to convert Turkish women, encountering spies and absurd misadventures before the journey turns to a serious crisis of faith. A comic travel novel that becomes a meditation on belief and doubt.

K:f1ab318088af.title: The Chateau
K:f1ab318088af.author: William Maxwell
K:f1ab318088af.description: In 1948, the young American couple Harold and Barbara Rhodes travel through war-battered France on holiday, staying as paying guests at a chateau in the Loire Valley run by the genteel but impoverished Madame Vienot, puzzling over the reserve of the people they meet. A novel about postwar France and the bafflement of traveling abroad.

K:f01b5be61f50.title: What's for Dinner?
K:f01b5be61f50.author: James Schuyler
K:f01b5be61f50.description: In three small-town American households, the childless Norris and Lottie Taylor drift through a comfortable but troubled marriage as Lottie drinks herself toward collapse and goes off to dry out, while a Catholic family struggles with unruly twin sons and a widow looks for love. A novel told largely in dialogue across overlapping domestic lives.

K:2b24f3659ce7.title: A Voice Through a Cloud
K:2b24f3659ce7.author: Denton Welch
K:2b24f3659ce7.description: An art student is struck by a car while cycling to visit his uncle on a holiday, and the narrative follows his long ordeal in hospital wards and a nursing home, recording the staff, fellow patients, visitors, and memories with close attention. An unfinished autobiographical novel left incomplete at the author's death.

K:d6a7af191ac4.title: Medea
K:d6a7af191ac4.author: Euripides
K:d6a7af191ac4.description: In Corinth, the sorceress Medea, abandoned by Jason for the daughter of King Creon, takes revenge by sending the bride a poisoned dress and crown that kill her and her father, then murders her own two sons before escaping to Athens. A Greek tragedy first performed in 431 BCE.

K:aa2ae157f2a5.title: Life on the Mississippi
K:aa2ae157f2a5.author: Mark Twain
K:aa2ae157f2a5.description: A young man trains as a steamboat pilot on the Mississippi River before the Civil War, then returns decades later to travel the river by steamboat and record how it and the towns along it have changed. A memoir blending pilot reminiscences with travel reporting and history of the river.

K:9c46bcbe4006.title: The White Tiger
K:9c46bcbe4006.author: Aravind Adiga
K:9c46bcbe4006.description: Balram Halwai, the son of a rickshaw puller from a poor Indian village, narrates his rise from servant and chauffeur to a Bangalore entrepreneur in a series of letters addressed to the Chinese premier, recounting how he murdered his employer to escape servitude. A picaresque novel about class and corruption in modern India that won the Booker Prize.

K:93056a9c86fa.title: The Book of Ebenezer Le Page
K:93056a9c86fa.author: G. B. Edwards
K:93056a9c86fa.description: Ebenezer Le Page, a Guernsey islander who never marries, looks back over his long life from the late nineteenth century to the 1960s, recalling family quarrels, two world wars, and his search for an heir before he befriends the young artist Neville Falla. Written in Guernsey English and published posthumously, it is known for capturing the island's character and dialect.
