K:b57874a47c85.title: Harold and the Purple Crayon
K:b57874a47c85.author: Crockett Johnson
K:b57874a47c85.description: Harold, a small boy with a purple crayon, draws a moon, a path, and a whole world around himself as he goes for a walk, conjuring and erasing landscapes until he finds his way back to bed. A picture book in which the child's drawings become the events of the story.

K:26a310599722.title: Essays
K:26a310599722.author: Michel de Montaigne
K:26a310599722.description: In hundreds of short prose pieces, the writer examines himself and topics ranging from friendship, education, and cannibals to fear, idleness, and death, drawing on classical authors and his own experience. The founding work of the personal essay form, expanded across three books over fifteen years.

K:11db7aaa5eac.title: Little Women
K:11db7aaa5eac.author: Louisa May Alcott
K:11db7aaa5eac.description: The four March sisters—Jo, Meg, Beth, and Amy—grow up with their mother in Massachusetts while their father serves as a chaplain in the Civil War, facing poverty, illness, romance, and the deaths and marriages of early adulthood. A domestic novel originally issued in two volumes and partly based on the author's own family.

K:a7c3b274f87c.title: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock
K:a7c3b274f87c.author: T. S. Eliot
K:a7c3b274f87c.description: J. Alfred Prufrock, a hesitant, aging man, addresses an unnamed companion as he wanders through a city evening, agonizing over whether to ask an "overwhelming question" and measuring out a life of social anxiety and missed chances. A dramatic monologue regarded as a founding poem of literary modernism.

K:e0e175903a2c.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
K:e0e175903a2c.description: Gilgamesh, the tyrannical king of Uruk, is matched and then befriended by the wild man Enkidu, and together they kill the forest guardian Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven; after Enkidu dies, Gilgamesh wanders in search of immortality and meets the flood survivor Utnapishtim. An ancient Mesopotamian poem preserved on cuneiform tablets and among the earliest known works of literature.

K:ddf7db56b887.title: The Celestina
K:ddf7db56b887.description: Calisto, a young nobleman, becomes infatuated with Melibea and hires the old bawd and procuress Celestina to win her, an intrigue that ends with Celestina murdered by Calisto's servants over their reward and the deaths of both lovers. A work written entirely in dialogue and a foundational text of Spanish literature.

K:6a405b4c5ae0.title: Whoroscope
K:6a405b4c5ae0.description: The seventeenth-century philosopher René Descartes mutters a rambling monologue while waiting for his breakfast egg, weaving together memories, his ideas, and details of his life as he meditates on time. A dense, allusion-packed poem that was the first separately published work by its author.

K:0f8ff0529f09.title: El Señor Presidente
K:0f8ff0529f09.description: In an unnamed Latin American country, a dictator known only as the President tightens his grip on power after a colonel's killing, ordering his aide Miguel Cara de Ángel to ruin General Canales, though the aide instead falls in love with the general's daughter Camila. A dictator novel that makes early use of techniques later called magic realism.

K:0e16b3a111b7.title: This Side of Paradise
K:0e16b3a111b7.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
K:0e16b3a111b7.description: Amory Blaine, a handsome and self-absorbed young Midwesterner, attends Princeton, drifts through romances and friendships, serves in World War I, and gropes toward a sense of himself amid the disillusionment of his generation. A loosely autobiographical first novel that made its author famous.

K:41363635176b.title: Franny and Zooey
K:41363635176b.author: J. D. Salinger
K:41363635176b.description: Franny Glass suffers a spiritual and emotional breakdown over a college weekend, obsessing over a Russian prayer book, while her brother Zooey, an actor, tries to talk her back to herself in their family's New York apartment. Two linked stories about the precocious, religiously searching Glass siblings.

K:c99f3f06678b.title: Look Homeward, Angel
K:c99f3f06678b.author: Thomas Wolfe
K:c99f3f06678b.description: Eugene Gant grows up in the mountain town of Altamont in the fictional state of Old Catawba, the youngest child of a stonecutter father and a boardinghouse-keeping mother, and yearns to escape his family and small-town life. A largely autobiographical first novel tracing the protagonist from birth to young manhood.

K:13977efd1a72.title: Doctor Zhivago
K:13977efd1a72.author: Boris Pasternak
K:13977efd1a72.description: Yuri Zhivago, a physician and poet, is swept up in the Russian Revolution and civil war, torn between his wife Tonya and his love for Lara as the upheaval scatters and breaks his family. A novel banned in the Soviet Union and first published in Italy whose author was awarded the Nobel Prize.

K:b88ea723aa90.title: The Wings of the Dove
K:b88ea723aa90.author: Henry James
K:b88ea723aa90.description: Milly Theale, a dying young American heiress, arrives in London and Venice, where the penniless Kate Croy steers her own secret fiancé Merton Densher to court Milly and inherit her fortune. A late novel known for its psychological depth and moral ambiguity.

K:c254788e9d13.title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur’s Court
K:c254788e9d13.author: Mark Twain
K:c254788e9d13.description: Hank Morgan, a nineteenth-century Connecticut factory engineer, is knocked unconscious and wakes in sixth-century Britain at King Arthur's court, where he uses modern know-how to pass as a magician and tries to modernize the medieval kingdom. A satirical novel mixing comedy with criticism of monarchy, chivalry, and superstition.

K:e196441b3ce0.title: Embers
K:e196441b3ce0.author: Sándor Márai
K:e196441b3ce0.description: An elderly Hungarian general receives a visit from Konrad, the friend who vanished forty-one years earlier, and over a single night's dinner reopens the betrayal involving the general's late wife Krisztina through a long confrontation of speeches and silences. A novel built almost entirely around one night's conversation.

K:070d3b8bcaf9.title: The Old Man and the Sea
K:070d3b8bcaf9.author: Ernest Hemingway
K:070d3b8bcaf9.description: Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman who has gone eighty-four days without a catch, hooks a giant marlin far out in the Gulf Stream and battles it for days, only to have sharks devour the fish as he tows it home. A short novel cited when its author won the Nobel Prize.

K:ac5b6d062e10.title: A Room with a View
K:ac5b6d062e10.author: E. M. Forster
K:ac5b6d062e10.description: Lucy Honeychurch, a young Englishwoman traveling in Florence, is unsettled by the free-spirited George Emerson, then returns home to Surrey and her conventional fiancé Cecil Vyse while struggling to admit her real feelings. A comedy of manners contrasting English propriety with passion and honesty.

K:cb2fc13975c7.title: The Ten Thousand Things
K:cb2fc13975c7.author: Maria Dermout
K:cb2fc13975c7.description: Felicia returns to her grandmother's spice estate on a Moluccan island in the Dutch East Indies with her young son Himpies, settling into island life among its objects and legends until violent deaths, including her son's, force her to reckon with loss. A novel set in colonial Indonesia and structured around the island and its bays.

K:03915260da83.title: The Burning Plain and Other Stories
K:03915260da83.author: Juan Rulfo
K:03915260da83.description: Across seventeen short stories, peasants, drifters, and killers move through the drought-stricken plains of rural Mexico in the wake of the Revolution and the Cristero War, enduring poverty, vengeance, and isolation. A story collection that helped establish its author's reputation.

K:51b945ee82cf.title: La Flor de Lis
K:51b945ee82cf.author: Elena Poniatowska
K:51b945ee82cf.description: Mariana, born into a French aristocratic family, emigrates with her mother and sister to Mexico during World War II while her father fights in Europe, and gradually learns the country and herself, falling under the influence of the troubling priest Father Teufel. A semi-autobiographical coming-of-age novel.

K:308cbc3a6913.title: Borderlands/La Frontera
K:308cbc3a6913.author: Gloria Anzaldúa
K:308cbc3a6913.description: Mixing essays, poetry, history, and personal memoir, the book examines life on the Texas–Mexico border and the figure of the new mestiza, drawing on the author's upbringing and moving among English, Spanish, and Spanglish. A foundational work of Chicana and borderlands theory.

K:695a2abbc378.title: The Book of Embraces
K:695a2abbc378.author: Eduardo Galeano
K:695a2abbc378.description: Dozens of very short prose pieces blend autobiography, dreams, anecdotes, political reflection, and parable, accompanied by the author's own line drawings and grouped into thematic sections. A fragmentary book responding in part to the author's exile from Uruguay.

K:e17f60d00c46.title: Dreamtigers
K:e17f60d00c46.author: Jorge Luis Borges
K:e17f60d00c46.description: A collection of short prose pieces and poems gathers parables, sketches, and reflections on mirrors, tigers, dreams, blindness, and the act of writing. Considered by its author his most personal book, originally published in Spanish as El hacedor.

K:045279d14d64.title: Maud Martha
K:045279d14d64.author: Gwendolyn Brooks
K:045279d14d64.description: In thirty-four brief vignettes, Maud Martha Brown grows up, marries, and raises a daughter on Chicago's South Side, meeting everyday slights of race, class, and colorism. Noted for its compact, poetic prose and its focus on an ordinary Black woman's everyday life.

K:dc73aeed2ba3.title: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
K:dc73aeed2ba3.author: Junot Diaz
K:dc73aeed2ba3.description: Oscar de León, an overweight Dominican American science-fiction fan growing up in New Jersey and desperate for love, is shadowed by a family curse called fukú, with the narration reaching back to his mother's and grandfather's suffering under the Trujillo dictatorship. A novel mixing slang, footnotes, and genre references that won the Pulitzer Prize.

K:fd3d08694663.title: On Writing
K:fd3d08694663.author: Stephen King
K:fd3d08694663.description: Part memoir of the author's life and reading habits and part practical guide, the book recounts his early years and recovery from a near-fatal accident while setting out his advice on grammar, story, and the writer's daily work. A nonfiction book on the craft of writing.

K:194791ccb5ba.title: Sonnets
K:194791ccb5ba.author: William Shakespeare
K:194791ccb5ba.description: Across 154 poems, the speaker urges a beautiful young man to marry and reproduce, then addresses time, mortality, and the immortalizing power of verse, before turning to a sensual and faithless "Dark Lady." A sequence of sonnets first collected in a 1609 quarto.

K:c683eff1be4e.title: Enemies, A Love Story
K:c683eff1be4e.author: Isaac Bashevis Singer
K:c683eff1be4e.description: Herman Broder, a Holocaust survivor living in postwar New York, juggles three women—his peasant wife Yadwiga who hid him, his volatile mistress Masha, and his first wife Tamara, who reappears after he believed her dead. A novel about a survivor's guilt and entanglements among Jewish refugees.

K:c363338a638c.title: The Story of a New Name
K:c363338a638c.author: Elena Ferrante
K:c363338a638c.description: Lila, newly and unhappily married to Stefano, and her friend Lenù, who is winning her way through school, come of age in 1960s Naples as Lila begins an affair with Nino on the island of Ischia and Lenù leaves for university in Pisa. The second of the Neapolitan Novels, continuing the two women's lifelong friendship.

K:169fd6846378.title: The Story of a Lost Child
K:169fd6846378.author: Elena Ferrante
K:169fd6846378.description: Lenù returns to Naples to live with Nino while Lila builds a business in the old neighborhood, and the two friends raise their daughters side by side until Lila's child Tina vanishes and is never found, decades before Lila herself disappears. The fourth and final Neapolitan Novel.

K:275b5f71a8ce.title: Faust
K:275b5f71a8ce.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
K:275b5f71a8ce.description: Heinrich Faust, an aging scholar dissatisfied with knowledge, strikes a wager with the devil Mephistopheles, who serves him on earth in exchange for his soul, and embarks on a journey that includes seducing and ruining the young Gretchen. A two-part dramatic poem widely regarded as a central work of German literature.

K:77395a1b3d2c.title: The Hour of the Star
K:77395a1b3d2c.author: Clarice Lispector
K:77395a1b3d2c.description: Macabéa, a poor, sickly typist from the northeastern backlands living in the slums of Rio de Janeiro, loves movies and Coca-Cola and drifts through a bleak life narrated by the self-conscious writer Rodrigo S.M. The final novel published before its author's death, known for its experimental narration and its portrait of poverty.

K:045ff572e567.title: The I Ching (Book of Changes)
K:045ff572e567.description: A book of divination built around sixty-four hexagrams formed from broken and unbroken lines, each paired with cryptic judgments and commentaries used to interpret change and guide decisions. One of the oldest Chinese classics, later layered with philosophical appendices known as the Ten Wings.

K:dd91428bf960.title: Howl
K:dd91428bf960.author: Allen Ginsberg
K:dd91428bf960.description: The opening line announces that the best minds of a generation have been destroyed by madness, and the long-lined poem catalogs hipsters, addicts, poets, and outcasts before invoking the industrial monster Moloch and addressing the institutionalized Carl Solomon. A defining work of the Beat Generation that became the subject of an obscenity trial.

K:9ee9a85c69af.title: She Had Some Horses
K:9ee9a85c69af.author: Joy Harjo
K:9ee9a85c69af.description: Across these poems women confront fear, despair, abuse, and survival, with recurring horses serving as a binding image for the speaker's past, present, and future selves and for Native experience in the American landscape. A poetry collection drawing on Muscogee heritage, chant, and prayer.

K:b76210de9d29.title: The Branch Will Not Break
K:b76210de9d29.author: James Wright
K:b76210de9d29.description: These poems move through the rural American Midwest, observing horses in a field, a drunk in a ditch, and small towns at nightfall in spare free verse marked by sudden interior leaps. A collection that broke from the author's earlier formal style and influenced the Deep Image movement.

K:30ead11b9ea3.title: Plays of Molière
K:30ead11b9ea3.author: Molière
K:30ead11b9ea3.description: These comedies stage doctors, misers, hypocrites, and social climbers, from the religious fraud Tartuffe to the jealous Arnolphe and the miserly Harpagon, exposing human vanity and pretension through farce and verse. A body of French stage comedy that became a foundation of the classical repertoire.

K:5f36c5d443e5.title: The Golden Argosy
K:5f36c5d443e5.author: Van H. Cartmell & Charles Grayson, editors
K:5f36c5d443e5.description: This anthology gathers widely reprinted short stories in the English language, bringing together classic tales by many well-known authors in a single volume. A popular general-reader collection often cited as a favorite by Stephen King.

OL:OL1794911W.title: McTeague
OL:OL1794911W.author: Frank Norris
OL:OL1794911W.description: McTeague, a brutish, unlicensed dentist in San Francisco, marries Trina, who wins a lottery and grows miserly, and their union collapses into poverty, violence, and a fatal pursuit into Death Valley. A naturalist novel tracing how greed and heredity drive its characters to ruin.

K:6e28afa38b7a.title: Lord of the Flies
K:6e28afa38b7a.author: William Golding
K:6e28afa38b7a.description: British schoolboys stranded on a deserted island after a plane crash try to govern themselves under Ralph and the intellectual Piggy, but Jack's hunters descend into savagery, fear of a "beast," and killing. An allegorical novel about the fragility of civilization and the human capacity for cruelty.

K:0b4e8412f576.title: The Awakening
K:0b4e8412f576.author: Kate Chopin
K:0b4e8412f576.description: Edna Pontellier, a wife and mother summering in Grand Isle and New Orleans, awakens to her own desires and independence, takes up painting, leaves her husband's home, and pursues an attraction to Robert Lebrun. A novel about a woman's sexual and personal awakening that was widely condemned at publication.

K:ac0e26c055a2.title: A Doll's House
K:ac0e26c055a2.author: Henrik Ibsen
K:ac0e26c055a2.description: Nora Helmer, who secretly borrowed money to save her husband Torvald's health, is blackmailed by the clerk Krogstad, and when the truth surfaces she confronts the hollowness of her marriage and walks out. A play known for its closing scene and its critique of nineteenth-century marriage and gender roles.

K:a138dd8423fd.title: Ahab's Wife
K:a138dd8423fd.author: Sena Jeter Naslund
K:a138dd8423fd.description: Una, who declares that Ahab was neither her first husband nor her last, recounts her life from a Kentucky childhood to a lighthouse near New Bedford, a whaling voyage disguised as a boy, and marriage to the captain of the Pequod. A novel that imagines a full life for a woman mentioned only briefly in Moby-Dick.

K:e3054b98467a.title: Treasure Island
K:e3054b98467a.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
K:e3054b98467a.description: Young Jim Hawkins discovers a treasure map at his family's inn and sails aboard the Hispaniola, where the ship's cook Long John Silver leads a mutiny in a hunt for buried pirate gold. An adventure novel that shaped popular ideas of pirates, treasure maps, and the sea quest.

K:a80f75f0262c.title: Voss
K:a80f75f0262c.author: Patrick White
K:a80f75f0262c.description: The German explorer Johann Ulrich Voss leads an expedition to cross the Australian continent in 1845 while maintaining an intense, partly telepathic bond with Laura Trevelyan, a young woman in Sydney, as his party perishes in the outback. A novel by a Nobel laureate based loosely on the explorer Ludwig Leichhardt.

K:c04a7bb2098d.title: Eugénie Grandet
K:c04a7bb2098d.author: Honoré de Balzac
K:c04a7bb2098d.description: In provincial Saumur, the miser Félix Grandet hoards a fortune while his sheltered daughter Eugénie falls in love with her ruined cousin Charles, gives him her savings, and waits years for a return that betrays her. A novel of provincial avarice that forms part of the author's Comédie humaine.

K:e0f9a8053cb0.title: Stoner
K:e0f9a8053cb0.author: John Williams
K:e0f9a8053cb0.description: William Stoner, the son of Missouri farmers, becomes an English professor at the University of Missouri and endures an unhappy marriage, academic feuds, and a brief love affair while quietly devoting himself to teaching. A novel about an ordinary academic life that found a wide readership decades after publication.

K:7b543bc3522c.title: Of a Fire on the Moon
K:7b543bc3522c.author: Norman Mailer
K:7b543bc3522c.description: Reporting from inside NASA at Houston and Cape Kennedy, the narrator recounts the Apollo 11 mission, the Saturn V launch, and the first Moon landing while reflecting on technology, the astronauts, and the meaning of the achievement. A work of literary nonfiction first serialized in Life magazine.

K:ae7bc4876491.title: The Widow's Children
K:ae7bc4876491.author: Paula Fox
K:ae7bc4876491.description: On the eve of a trip to Africa, Laura Maldonada Clapper gathers her brother Carlos, her timid daughter Clara, and an editor friend in a New York hotel and restaurant while concealing that her mother has died that morning, and the evening curdles into family cruelty. A novel built around a single night of escalating family conflict.

K:a6471b33c355.title: Shah of Shahs
K:a6471b33c355.author: Ryszard Kapuscinski
K:a6471b33c355.description: Locked in a Tehran hotel room, the narrator studies photographs and notes to reconstruct the fall of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, the last Shah of Iran, his secret police, and the 1979 revolution that brought Ayatollah Khomeini to power. A work of literary reportage on the Iranian Revolution.

K:4a1582700162.title: Dog Soldiers
K:4a1582700162.author: Robert Stone
K:4a1582700162.description: John Converse, a journalist in Vietnam, arranges to smuggle heroin to the United States through the merchant sailor Ray Hicks, but when the deal goes wrong Hicks goes on the run with the drugs and Converse's wife Marge. A novel about the drug trade and the collapse of 1960s idealism that shared the National Book Award.

K:f529982965ab.title: Snowblind: A Brief Career in the Cocaine Trade by Robert Sabbag
K:f529982965ab.description: Working from interviews, the narrator traces the career of Zachary Swan, a pseudonymous American smuggler who ran cocaine from Colombia into New York in the early 1970s using elaborate scams to evade customs and protect his accomplices. A work of literary nonfiction credited as an early account of the cocaine trade.

K:2953c272b0db.title: Endgame
K:2953c272b0db.author: Samuel Beckett
K:2953c272b0db.description: In a bare room, the blind, chair-bound Hamm and his servant Clov bicker and depend on each other while Hamm's legless parents, Nagg and Nell, live in two ashbins, all amid a dead world outside. A one-act play associated with the Theatre of the Absurd.

K:ff6d975a1944.title: Paradise
K:ff6d975a1944.author: Toni Morrison
K:ff6d975a1944.description: In the all-Black Oklahoma town of Ruby, the leading men attack a nearby former mansion called the Convent where a group of women with troubled pasts have taken refuge, and the novel circles back to trace both the town's founding and the women's stories. A novel completing a trilogy that began with Beloved.

K:c60a0eea87b7.title: End Zone
K:c60a0eea87b7.author: Don DeLillo
K:c60a0eea87b7.description: Gary Harkness, a blocking back at tiny Logos College in west Texas, narrates a season of football alongside a growing obsession with nuclear war fed by his modern-warfare class and Major Staley. A novel that treats the language and violence of football as a meditation on warfare.

K:a1f43a005993.title: Père Goriot
K:a1f43a005993.author: Honoré de Balzac
K:a1f43a005993.description: In a shabby Paris boarding house, the retired merchant Goriot beggars himself for his two ungrateful married daughters while the ambitious young Eugène de Rastignac learns the ruthless ways of society from the criminal Vautrin. A novel central to the author's Comédie humaine.

K:492220bfdfb3.title: L'Assommoir (The Dram Shop)
K:492220bfdfb3.description: Gervaise, a laundress in working-class Paris, builds a modest life and her own shop, but her husband Coupeau's drinking after an accident drags the household into alcoholism, debt, and ruin. A naturalist novel about poverty and drink in the slums, part of the Rougon-Macquart cycle.

K:f2fd0db8a049.title: Bel-Ami
K:f2fd0db8a049.author: Guy de Maupassant
K:f2fd0db8a049.description: Georges Duroy, a poor former soldier in Paris, uses his looks and a series of affairs with influential women to climb through the world of newspapers, finance, and society. A novel of social ambition and seduction in the Belle Époque press world.

K:06f29fad4727.title: BUtterfield 8
K:06f29fad4727.author: John O'Hara
K:06f29fad4727.description: Gloria Wandrous wakes in a married executive's apartment, takes his wife's mink coat, and moves through the speakeasies and café society of early-1930s New York toward a destructive end. A novel loosely based on the death of socialite Starr Faithfull.

K:8c937ec47a21.title: The Studs Lonigan trilogy
K:8c937ec47a21.description: William "Studs" Lonigan grows up among lower-middle-class Irish Catholics on Chicago's South Side, drifting from a tough adolescence into street gangs, drink, failed ambitions, and decline through the boom years and the onset of the Depression. A trilogy of social-realist novels tracing one man's wasted life.

K:dc87d80d15af.title: Our Town
K:dc87d80d15af.author: Thornton Wilder
K:dc87d80d15af.description: A Stage Manager directly addresses the audience and guides scenes of daily life, love, marriage, and death in the small New Hampshire town of Grover's Corners, centered on George Gibbs and Emily Webb. A play performed on a nearly bare stage that became a staple of American theater.

K:a3b2c0f514f1.title: Strangers in Paradise: Stories
K:a3b2c0f514f1.author: Lee K. Abbott
K:a3b2c0f514f1.description: These stories follow ordinary men in the American Southwest, from a golf club in the Mimbres Valley to soldiers in Vietnam, dwelling on fathers and sons, marriage, loss, and obsession in an ornate, talkative voice. A collection that includes O. Henry and Pushcart prize-winning stories.

K:dd748adf6a89.title: The Infinities
K:dd748adf6a89.author: John Banville
K:dd748adf6a89.description: As the mathematician Adam Godley lies comatose and dying, his family gathers at the country house while the Greek gods Hermes, Zeus, and Pan move among them, with Zeus seducing the younger Adam's wife Helen. A novel narrated by Hermes and adapted from Kleist's play Amphitryon.

K:46174f5902ed.title: No Country for Old Men
K:46174f5902ed.author: Joel and Ethan Coen
K:46174f5902ed.description: Hunting near the Texas-Mexico border, Vietnam veteran Llewelyn Moss stumbles on a drug deal gone wrong and takes a satchel holding $2.4 million, drawing the hitman Anton Chigurh and aging sheriff Ed Tom Bell into his pursuit. A crime novel that became the basis for the Coen brothers' Academy Award-winning film.

K:2bd4e83e8ced.title: Winter's Tale
K:2bd4e83e8ced.author: Mark Helprin
K:2bd4e83e8ced.description: Peter Lake, a turn-of-the-century burglar in a mythical New York, breaks into the Penn mansion and falls in love with the dying heiress Beverly, while a magical white horse and the spans of a century carry the story across time. A magic realism novel set in a reimagined New York City.

K:46995cafc66f.title: Island: The Collected Stories
K:46995cafc66f.author: Alistair MacLoed
K:46995cafc66f.description: Sixteen stories, most set among the miners, fishermen, and farmers of Cape Breton, follow families bound to a hard landscape and their Scottish Highland past across generations. A collection gathering the author's two earlier story volumes plus two previously unpublished pieces.

K:8d2e8c06fc69.title: The Love of a Good Woman: Stories
K:8d2e8c06fc69.author: Alice Munro
K:8d2e8c06fc69.description: Across eight stories set largely in small-town Ontario, women and men face secrets, betrayals, and turning points in ordinary lives, including the title story in which boys find a drowned optometrist and a nurse weighs what she suspects about a death. A collection that won the Giller Prize and the National Book Critics Circle Award.

K:9305502d9df8.title: Running in the Family
K:9305502d9df8.author: Michael Ondaatje
K:9305502d9df8.description: Returning to Sri Lanka, the island once called Ceylon, the narrator pieces together the lives of his Dutch-Burgher family, centered on his hard-drinking father Mervyn and his grandmother Lalla, mixing memory, poems, and travel writing. A fictionalized memoir told in fragments rather than chronological order.

K:a7499dcf0afb.title: Mason & Dixon
K:a7499dcf0afb.author: Thomas Pynchon
K:a7499dcf0afb.description: Surveyors Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon meet in London, travel to South Africa and St. Helena, then map the boundary line between Pennsylvania and Maryland through colonial America, their adventures narrated years later by Reverend Wicks Cherrycoke. A historical novel written in a style imitating eighteenth-century English prose.

K:e1f9510c3e82.title: The Fever
K:e1f9510c3e82.author: Wallace Shawn
K:e1f9510c3e82.description: Alone in a hotel room in an unnamed, war-torn country, a feverish, unnamed traveler delivers a long monologue examining personal comfort, poverty, and complicity in the suffering of the world's poor. A one-person play first performed by its author in private apartments.

K:1805d8e86b3f.title: Resurrection
K:1805d8e86b3f.author: Leo Tolstoy
K:1805d8e86b3f.description: Nobleman Dmitri Nekhlyudov recognizes a prostitute on trial for murder as Katyusha Maslova, the servant he once seduced and abandoned, and follows her toward Siberian exile as he tries to atone and gives away his land. The author's last major novel, sharply critical of the legal system, church, and aristocracy.

K:ab3d90b147f7.title: Norwood
K:ab3d90b147f7.author: Charles Portis
K:ab3d90b147f7.description: Naive ex-Marine Norwood Pratt leaves Ralph, Texas, to collect a seventy-dollar debt in New York City, agreeing to drive cars north for a con man and meeting a circus performer, a college-educated chicken, and a young woman he marries on the bus home. A deadpan comic road novel.

K:2b69cf0b1a11.title: The Postman Always Rings Twice
K:2b69cf0b1a11.author: James M. Cain
K:2b69cf0b1a11.description: Drifter Frank Chambers stops at a roadside California diner, begins an affair with the owner's young wife Cora, and conspires with her to murder her older husband Nick for the insurance money. A crime novel notorious on publication and frequently banned, later adapted to film several times.

OL:OL26504281W.title: Old Filth Trilogy
OL:OL26504281W.author: Jane Gardam
OL:OL26504281W.description: Across three novels, the elderly retired barrister Edward Feathers, nicknamed Old Filth for "Failed in London Try Hong Kong," his wife Betty, and his rival Terry Veneering recall their lives from colonial Hong Kong to retirement in England, each book retelling events from a different perspective. A trilogy centered on a child of British colonials sent back to England for schooling.

OL:OL34028309W.title: North Woods
OL:OL34028309W.author: Daniel Mason
OL:OL34028309W.description: A yellow house in the woods of western Massachusetts passes through four centuries of occupants, among them Puritan lovers, an apple-growing soldier, twin spinster sisters, a crime reporter, and a panther, told through prose, letters, poems, and case notes. A work of historical fiction tracing one place across generations.

OL:OL19956847W.title: Foster
OL:OL19956847W.author: Claire Keegan
OL:OL19956847W.description: In 1981 rural Ireland, a young girl is sent to stay with the Kinsellas, distant relatives on a Wexford farm, while her mother prepares to give birth, and there she finds a warmth and attention absent from her own crowded home. A novella later adapted into the Irish-language film An Cailín Ciúin.

OL:OL16142488W.title: The Patrick Melrose Novels
OL:OL16142488W.author: Edward St Aubyn
OL:OL16142488W.description: Five novels follow Patrick Melrose from a childhood in the south of France marked by his father's abuse and his mother's neglect, through heroin addiction in New York, into marriage, parenthood, and a reckoning at his mother's death. A semi-autobiographical sequence about surviving an upper-class English family.

OL:OL2772007W.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
OL:OL2772007W.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
OL:OL2772007W.description: Confined for a rest cure in an upstairs room by her physician husband John, a new mother forbidden to write keeps a secret journal and becomes fixated on the room's yellow wallpaper, behind which she comes to believe a woman is trapped. An early work of American feminist literature about a woman's mental breakdown.

OL:OL1400708W.title: Little Boy Lost
OL:OL1400708W.author: Marghanita Laski
OL:OL1400708W.description: After his French wife is killed by the Gestapo and their infant son vanishes in wartime France, Englishman Hilary Wainwright travels to a small-town orphanage to determine whether a boy living there is the child he lost. A novel later adapted into a Bing Crosby film.

OL:OL2435539W.title: Mrs. Palfrey at the Claremont
OL:OL2435539W.author: Elizabeth Taylor
OL:OL2435539W.description: Recently widowed Mrs. Palfrey moves into the genteel Claremont Hotel in South Kensington among other lonely elderly residents and, after a fall, befriends a young aspiring writer named Ludo, whom she passes off to the others as her grandson. A novel shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL11103938W.title: Dr Gully
OL:OL11103938W.author: Elizabeth Jenkins
OL:OL11103938W.description: Florence Ricardo, trapped in marriage to the alcoholic Captain Ricardo, begins a passionate affair with the older physician James Manby Gully, and after she remarries the barrister Charles Bravo and he is fatally poisoned, suspicion falls on Gully. A novel based on the unsolved 1876 Charles Bravo poisoning case.

OL:OL890896W.title: The Vicar of Wakefield
OL:OL890896W.author: Oliver Goldsmith
OL:OL890896W.description: The clergyman Dr. Charles Primrose, his wife, and children lose their fortune, suffer a daughter's seduction, a house fire, and the vicar's imprisonment before a series of revelations restores their happiness. A first-person novel read as both a sentimental tale and a satire of one.

OL:OL17838472W.title: Golden Hill
OL:OL17838472W.author: Francis Spufford
OL:OL17838472W.description: A young stranger named Mr. Smith steps off a ship in colonial New York carrying a bill for one thousand pounds, refuses to explain his business, and unsettles the city's merchants and politicians as suspicion grows about who he really is. A historical novel that won the Costa First Novel Award and the Ondaatje Prize.

OL:OL2824324W.title: The Long View
OL:OL2824324W.author: Elizabeth Jane Howard
OL:OL2824324W.description: Antonia Fleming faces solitude in 1950s London as her marriage to Conrad has emptied out, and the narrative moves backward in time, tracing their relationship from war years and motherhood to their first meeting in the 1920s. A novel built on reverse chronology.

OL:OL3128704W.title: The Plains
OL:OL3128704W.author: Gerald Murnane
OL:OL3128704W.description: A young filmmaker from "Outer Australia" travels inland to the plains to make a film about the region and its landowners, attaches himself to a wealthy patron, and spends twenty years in his library taking notes for a film he never makes. A short novel read as a parable about appearance, meaning, and the Australian interior.

OL:OL35382740W.title: Latecomers
OL:OL35382740W.author: Anita Brookner
OL:OL35382740W.description: Thomas Hartmann and Thomas Fibich, two Jewish men who came to England as boys via the Kindertransport, sustain a lifelong friendship and a greeting-card business across decades, the expansive Hartmann set against the anxious, grief-haunted Fibich. A novel about two refugees, their wives, and their children.

OL:OL166434W.title: Family and Friends
OL:OL166434W.author: Anita Brookner
OL:OL166434W.description: The widowed matriarch Sofka presides over a wealthy Jewish family in interwar London as her four children take divergent paths, the dutiful Alfred running the business, the pleasure-seeking Frederick and Betty leaving for the Riviera and Hollywood, and the passive Mimi remaining at home. A novel bookended by two wedding photographs decades apart.

OL:OL1863387W.title: Reading Turgenev
OL:OL1863387W.author: William Trevor
OL:OL1863387W.description: Mary Louise Dallon, a farm girl in southeastern Ireland trapped in an unconsummated marriage to the older draper Elmer Quarry, falls in love with her invalid cousin Robert, who reads her Turgenev, and after his death retreats into the attic to preserve his memory. One of two novellas published together as Two Lives, shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL221348W.title: The Last Samurai
OL:OL221348W.author: Helen Dewitt
OL:OL221348W.description: Single mother Sibylla raises her precociously gifted son Ludo in a London flat, showing him Kurosawa's Seven Samurai as a substitute father figure, while the boy, fluent in many languages by childhood, sets out to identify and test a series of candidates for his real father. A debut novel later named to a New York Times list of the century's best books.

OL:OL1993499W.title: The Swimming-Pool Library
OL:OL1993499W.author: Alan Hollinghurst
OL:OL1993499W.description: In early 1980s London, the privileged young gay aristocrat William Beckwith saves an elderly man, Lord Nantwich, from collapse in a public toilet and is drawn into writing his biography, uncovering a history of homosexual life and the persecution that shaped it. A debut novel set on the eve of the AIDS crisis.

OL:OL31098954W.title: Tom Lake
OL:OL31098954W.author: Ann Patchett
OL:OL31098954W.description: During the spring of 2020, Lara tells her three grown daughters, gathered at the family's cherry orchard in northern Michigan, the story of her youthful romance with the actor Peter Duke at a summer theater company called Tom Lake, where she once played Emily in Our Town. A novel threaded with Thornton Wilder and Chekhov.

OL:OL10987860W.title: The Improvement of Human Reason
OL:OL10987860W.author: Ibn Tufayl
OL:OL10987860W.description: Raised alone on a desert island by a gazelle, the feral child Hayy ibn Yaqdhan reasons his way from observation of nature toward knowledge of the soul, the cosmos, and the divine, and later encounters human society and its religion. A twelfth-century Arabic philosophical tale that influenced later European thinkers.

OL:OL14867079W.title: Joseph and His Brothers
OL:OL14867079W.author: Thomas Mann
OL:OL14867079W.description: Retelling the Book of Genesis, the four-part novel follows Jacob and then his favored son Joseph, who is sold into slavery by his brothers, rises in Egypt through Potiphar's house and prison, and finally feeds his family during famine. A tetralogy the author considered his greatest work.

OL:OL74650W.title: Operation Shylock
OL:OL74650W.author: Philip Roth
OL:OL74650W.description: A narrator named Philip Roth travels to Israel, attends the war-crimes trial of John Demjanjuk, and discovers an impostor using his name and promoting "Diasporism," a plan to resettle Israeli Jews in Europe, before being drawn into an intelligence operation. A novel that blurs fact and fiction and is subtitled A Confession.

OL:OL14860424W.title: Hopscotch
OL:OL14860424W.author: Julio Cortázar
OL:OL14860424W.description: Horacio Oliveira drifts through 1950s Paris with the woman called La Maga and a circle of bohemian intellectuals, then returns to Buenos Aires, in a book whose chapters can be read straight through or by jumping among them in a prescribed order. An experimental novel offering multiple reading sequences.

OL:OL515754W.title: Flowers for Algernon
OL:OL515754W.author: Daniel Keyes
OL:OL515754W.description: Charlie Gordon, a man with an IQ of 68, undergoes an experimental surgery that triples his intelligence, recording his transformation in progress reports as he outpaces his doctors and watches the lab mouse Algernon, who had the same operation, decline and die. A novel expanded from an award-winning short story, told entirely through Charlie's journal entries.

OL:OL17434786W.title: The Thing About December
OL:OL17434786W.author: Donal Ryan
OL:OL17434786W.description: Over one year in a rural Irish village, Johnsey Cunliffe, a gentle, slow young man, loses both parents, inherits the family farm, and becomes the target of bullies and land-grabbers who want his property as developers move in. A debut novel narrated through Johnsey's bewildered, lonely voice.

OL:OL15723140W.title: The Spy Who Came in From the Cold
OL:OL15723140W.author: John le Carré
OL:OL15723140W.description: British agent Alec Leamas is sent on a final Cold War mission to East Germany, posing as a defector in a scheme to discredit a senior East German intelligence officer, only to discover he is a pawn in a deeper plot. An espionage novel that rejected the glamour of the spy genre for moral murkiness.

OL:OL67238W.title: The Country of the Pointed Firs
OL:OL67238W.author: Sarah Orne Jewett
OL:OL67238W.description: A Boston writer spends a summer in the small coastal town of Dunnet Landing, Maine, boarding with the herbalist and widow Almira Todd and coming to know the fishermen, retired sea captains, and aging residents of the community. A collection of linked sketches associated with American regionalism.

OL:OL12827W.title: Shadows on the Rock
OL:OL12827W.author: Willa Cather
OL:OL12827W.description: In late seventeenth-century Quebec, the apothecary Euclide Auclair and his daughter Cécile build a settled life on the rock of the colonial town, keeping French customs through harsh winters as governors, bishops, and missionaries pass through. A novel built from small episodes of frontier colonial life.

OL:OL1518582W.title: I Capture the Castle
OL:OL1518582W.author: Dodie Smith
OL:OL1518582W.description: Seventeen-year-old Cassandra Mortmain records in her journal the impoverished life of her eccentric family in a crumbling English castle, where her father's writer's block has left them destitute until two American brothers inherit the nearby estate. A coming-of-age novel told through Cassandra's diary entries.

OL:OL12996734W.title: The Ice Palace
OL:OL12996734W.author: Tarjei Vesaas
OL:OL12996734W.description: In a Norwegian village, eleven-year-old Siss forms an intense bond with the newcomer Unn, who the next day wanders alone into a frozen waterfall of ice caves and disappears, leaving Siss bound by grief and a private vow. A short novel about friendship and loss, translated from Norwegian.

OL:OL60148W.title: Fire and Hemlock
OL:OL60148W.author: Diana Wynne Jones
OL:OL60148W.description: Clearing her room, Polly Whittacker uncovers a hidden second set of memories of her friendship with cellist Thomas Lynn, whose life is bound to the otherworldly Laurel in a reworking of the ballads "Tam Lin" and "Thomas the Rhymer." A young-adult fantasy weaving folklore into modern English life.

OL:OL20026655W.title: The Lie Tree
OL:OL20026655W.author: Frances Hardinge
OL:OL20026655W.description: On the remote Victorian island of Vane, fourteen-year-old Faith Sunderly investigates her naturalist father's mysterious death and discovers a strange tree that yields visions of truth only when fed lies that must then be spread among people. A historical fantasy that won the Costa Book of the Year.

OL:OL1930756W.title: The Hounds of the Morrigan
OL:OL1930756W.author: Pat O'Shea
OL:OL1930756W.description: In a Galway bookshop, ten-year-old Pidge frees an ancient serpent from a book and is drawn with his five-year-old sister Brigit into a quest to recover a blood-stained pebble before the goddess the Morrigan can destroy all that is good. A long children's fantasy steeped in Irish mythology.

OL:OL457172W.title: Haroun and the Sea of Stories
OL:OL457172W.author: Salman Rushdie
OL:OL457172W.description: Young Haroun sets out to restore his storyteller father Rashid's lost gift, traveling to the moon Kahani where the Sea of Stories is being poisoned by the silence-loving ruler Khattam-Shud. A children's fantasy that doubles as an allegory about storytelling and free speech.

OL:OL2539795W.title: The Slap
OL:OL2539795W.author: Christos Tsiolkas
OL:OL2539795W.description: At a suburban Melbourne barbecue, a man slaps a misbehaving child who is not his own, and the fallout from this single act is told across eight chapters from the viewpoints of eight people who witnessed it. A novel examining family, class, and ethnicity in contemporary Australia.

OL:OL8026340W.title: The Cider House Rules
OL:OL8026340W.author: John Irving
OL:OL8026340W.description: Homer Wells grows up in the St. Cloud's orphanage in rural Maine under Dr. Wilbur Larch, an ether-addicted obstetrician who secretly performs abortions and trains Homer as his successor before the young man leaves to make his own way. A novel that examines abortion, fate, and belonging.

OL:OL27442749W.title: Cloudstreet
OL:OL27442749W.author: Tim Winton
OL:OL27442749W.description: Two working-class families, the Pickles and the Lambs, share a sprawling house on Cloud Street in Perth over twenty years, weathering accidents, drownings, business ventures, and reconciliations. An Australian novel tracing the entwined lives of two families after the Second World War.

OL:OL505944W.title: The Razor's Edge
OL:OL505944W.author: William Somerset Maugham
OL:OL505944W.description: Returning from the First World War, American pilot Larry Darrell rejects a conventional career and his engagement to Isabel Bradley, traveling through Paris and India in search of spiritual meaning while a narrator tracks his circle over twenty-four years. A novel drawing on Indian mysticism and self-realization.

OL:OL471932W.title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
OL:OL471932W.author: Agatha Christie
OL:OL471932W.description: In the village of King's Abbot, the wealthy Roger Ackroyd is found stabbed soon after learning a secret about a recent suicide, and the retired detective Hercule Poirot investigates with the help of the local doctor who narrates the case. A detective novel famous for its controversial twist ending.

OL:OL1326310W.title: The Sea, the Sea
OL:OL1326310W.author: Iris Murdoch
OL:OL1326310W.description: Retired theatre director Charles Arrowby withdraws to a remote seaside house to write his memoirs, but his solitude collapses when he discovers his lost first love Hartley living nearby and becomes obsessed with winning her back. A novel narrated by Charles that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL1921191W.title: Falling Man
OL:OL1921191W.author: Don DeLillo
OL:OL1921191W.description: After escaping the collapsing World Trade Center on September 11, lawyer Keith Neudecker returns dazed to his estranged wife Lianne and their son, while a performance artist restages the image of a man falling from the towers. A novel about the aftermath of the September 11 attacks.

OL:OL166482W.title: The Affirmation
OL:OL166482W.author: Christopher Priest
OL:OL166482W.description: Unemployed and grieving a breakup, Peter Sinclair retreats to a country cottage and writes a fantasy version of himself who has won an immortality treatment in the Dream Archipelago, until his two identities begin to merge and the real one becomes impossible to tell. A novel of unreliable, shifting reality.

OL:OL13632840W.title: Darkmans
OL:OL13632840W.author: Nicola Barker
OL:OL13632840W.description: In the Kent town of Ashford, reshaped by the Channel Tunnel, the laundry-supervising Beede, his drug-dealing son Kane, a chiropractor, and others find their lives disrupted by the lingering spirit of a medieval court jester named John Scogin. A long novel mixing comedy, history, and the supernatural.

OL:OL17921667W.title: Family Life
OL:OL17921667W.author: Akhil Sharma
OL:OL17921667W.description: In late-1970s Queens, eight-year-old Ajay Mishra and his immigrant family build a new American life until his older brother Birju is left brain-damaged by a swimming-pool accident, reshaping the household around his care. An autobiographical novel that won the Folio Prize.

OL:OL1822527W.title: Sag Harbor
OL:OL1822527W.author: Colson Whitehead
OL:OL1822527W.description: Fifteen-year-old Benji Cooper spends the summer of 1985 in the Black middle-class beach community of Sag Harbor, working a job scooping ice cream and navigating friendships, BB-gun fights, and music with his brother and friends. A coming-of-age novel told in loosely linked episodes.

OL:OL2897798W.title: Watchmen
OL:OL2897798W.author: Alan Moore
OL:OL2897798W.description: In an alternate 1985 where costumed vigilantes are outlawed and nuclear war looms, the murder of a former hero named the Comedian draws masked figures including Rorschach, Nite Owl, and the godlike Doctor Manhattan into uncovering a wider conspiracy. A graphic novel that reshaped the superhero form.

OL:OL20032812W.title: Problems
OL:OL20032812W.author: Jade Sharma
OL:OL20032812W.description: Maya, a married graduate-school dropout in New York with a stalled thesis, an affair with a former professor, and a heroin habit, watches her marriage and life unravel as her addiction deepens. A debut novel about addiction told in short, blunt sections.

OL:OL501810W.title: Breath
OL:OL501810W.author: Tim Winton
OL:OL501810W.description: On the coast of Western Australia, middle-aged paramedic Bruce Pike recalls his teenage years surfing with his friend Loonie under the reckless former champion Sando, who pushes them toward ever more dangerous waves. A novel about risk, fear, and coming of age.

OL:OL17635446W.title: Exit West
OL:OL17635446W.author: Mohsin Hamid
OL:OL17635446W.description: As civil war engulfs their unnamed city, young lovers Nadia and Saeed flee through mysterious doors that open onto other countries, joining a global wave of migrants in Greece, London, and California. A novel about migration that uses magical doorways between places.

OL:OL2056818W.title: Maus
OL:OL2056818W.author: Art Spiegelman
OL:OL2056818W.description: Cartoonist Art interviews his father Vladek, a Polish Jewish Holocaust survivor, about his ordeal in Nazi-occupied Poland and Auschwitz, with Jews drawn as mice and Germans as cats. A graphic memoir, serialized over a decade, that won a special Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL28856510W.title: Bee Sting
OL:OL28856510W.author: Paul Murray
OL:OL28856510W.description: In a small Irish town after the 2008 financial crash, the Barnes family unravels as car-dealer Dickie's business fails, his wife Imelda sells off jewelry, their daughter Cass drifts, and young PJ retreats online, each carrying buried secrets. A novel told in long sections from each family member's view.

OL:OL42396177W.title: Stag Dance
OL:OL42396177W.author: Torrey Peters
OL:OL42396177W.description: In an illegal winter logging camp, a group of lumberjacks plan a dance in which some will attend as women, and the largest, plainest axman volunteers, igniting jealousy and obsession over a younger jack. The title novella in a collection of three stories and one novel about gender and transition.

OL:OL11295370W.title: Trout Fishing in America
OL:OL11295370W.author: Richard Brautigan
OL:OL11295370W.description: Loosely linked chapters use the phrase "Trout Fishing in America" as a title, a character, a hotel, and an act, ranging across the narrator's Pacific Northwest childhood, his life in San Francisco, and an Idaho camping trip. A book that blends anecdote and comic critique of American culture.

OL:OL11221642W.title: Union Street
OL:OL11221642W.author: Pat Barker
OL:OL11221642W.description: On a single street in a declining northeastern English town, seven working-class women, from the eleven-year-old Kelly to the dying Old Alice and the aging prostitute Dinah, face poverty, violence, and the collapse of local industry. A debut novel built from seven linked stories.

OL:OL1812933W.title: American Psycho
OL:OL1812933W.author: Bret Easton Ellis
OL:OL1812933W.description: Wealthy young Manhattan investment banker Patrick Bateman narrates his life of designer clothes, restaurant reservations, and status obsession alongside escalating accounts of torture and murder that may or may not be real. A satirical novel about 1980s consumerism that drew controversy for its violence.

OL:OL15706660W.title: Something Happened
OL:OL15706660W.author: Joseph Heller
OL:OL15706660W.description: Middle-aged corporate executive Bob Slocum delivers a long interior monologue about his fears, his unhappy marriage, his troubled children, and his anxieties at the office, circling toward a dread he cannot name. A novel told entirely through one man's anxious inner voice.

OL:OL14934891W.title: Summertime
OL:OL14934891W.author: J. M. Coetzee
OL:OL14934891W.description: A fictional biographer interviews five people who knew the late writer John Coetzee about his life in 1970s Cape Town, compiling their unflattering recollections alongside fragments from his notebooks. A metafictional memoir, the third of three autobiographical volumes, that presents its author as already dead.

OL:OL98454W.title: Cat's Cradle
OL:OL98454W.author: Kurt Vonnegut
OL:OL98454W.description: The narrator sets out to write about the day the atomic bomb fell and instead tracks the children of its co-inventor and the substance ice-nine to the impoverished Caribbean island of San Lorenzo, where the outlawed religion of Bokononism holds sway. A satirical science-fiction novel about science, religion, and the end of the world.

OL:OL857552W.title: Conversation in the Cathedral
OL:OL857552W.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
OL:OL857552W.description: Santiago Zavala, the disaffected son of a Peruvian government insider, meets his father's former chauffeur Ambrosio by chance and the two talk for hours in a Lima bar called The Cathedral, unraveling lives shaped by the 1950s dictatorship of Manuel Odría. A long novel that interweaves many voices and timelines to portray corruption across Peruvian society.

OL:OL1682158W.title: Leviathan
OL:OL1682158W.author: Paul Auster
OL:OL1682158W.description: Peter Aaron recounts the life of his friend Benjamin Sachs, a writer who, after a near-fatal fall, abandons his old life and becomes a bomber who blows up replicas of the Statue of Liberty before dying when one of his devices detonates by a Wisconsin roadside. A novel about American radicalism, identity, and chance.

OL:OL36506504W.title: James
OL:OL36506504W.author: Percival L. Everett
OL:OL36506504W.description: Jim, an enslaved man on the Mississippi who learns he is about to be sold, flees and travels with the runaway boy Huck, retelling the events of Huckleberry Finn from his own perspective as a literate, calculating narrator. A reimagining of Mark Twain's novel that won the Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award.

OL:OL11927W.title: The Golden Gate
OL:OL11927W.author: Vikram Seth
OL:OL11927W.description: In 1980s San Francisco, lonely tech worker John Brown is set up through a personal ad placed by his friend Janet, beginning a romance with lawyer Liz that founders amid jealousy and the city's anti-nuclear politics. A novel written entirely in rhymed sonnets modeled on Pushkin's Eugene Onegin.

OL:OL754948W.title: Wittgenstein's Mistress
OL:OL754948W.author: David Markson
OL:OL754948W.description: Kate, a woman who believes she is the last person alive on earth, types fragmentary first-person statements from a house on a beach, drifting among memories, errors, and references to Western art and philosophy. An experimental novel built from short, often self-correcting sentences about memory, language, and isolation.

OL:OL1139069W.title: Oblomov
OL:OL1139069W.author: Ivan Aleksandrovich Goncharov
OL:OL1139069W.description: Ilya Ilyich Oblomov, a young Russian nobleman, can barely leave his bed or room, and even a love affair with the lively Olga and the prodding of his energetic friend Stolz fail to rouse him from his indolence. A novel whose hero gave the Russian language the term "Oblomovism" for dreamy inertia.

OL:OL14857300W.title: Boredom
OL:OL14857300W.author: Alberto Moravia
OL:OL14857300W.description: Dino, a wealthy Roman painter who has stopped working and feels cut off from reality, takes up with Cecilia, the young model of a neighbor who has just died, and slides into a jealous obsession with possessing her. A novel about alienation and erotic fixation that won the Viareggio Prize.

OL:OL35997793W.title: Aunt Julia and the Script-Writer
OL:OL35997793W.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
OL:OL35997793W.description: Eighteen-year-old Mario, who writes news bulletins at a Lima radio station, falls in love with his older divorced relative Julia while the station's manic scriptwriter Pedro Camacho churns out radio serials that grow increasingly deranged. A partly autobiographical novel that alternates the love story with Camacho's wild soap-opera episodes.

OL:OL19926957W.title: Strange Tales From a Chinese Studio
OL:OL19926957W.author: Pu Songling
OL:OL19926957W.description: Close to five hundred classical Chinese tales of fox spirits, ghosts, scholars, demons, and transcendents, blurring the line between the supernatural and ordinary life and often turning on the theme of passionate attachment. A collection written over decades during the Qing dynasty and published after its author's death.

OL:OL5846570W.title: The Translator
OL:OL5846570W.author: Leila Aboulela
OL:OL5846570W.description: Sammar, a Sudanese widow working as an Arabic translator at a university in Aberdeen, grows close to Rae, a secular Scottish Middle East scholar, but their relationship runs into barriers of faith and culture. A novel set between Scotland and Khartoum about love, religion, and exile.

OL:OL816266W.title: Marabou Stork Nightmares
OL:OL816266W.author: Irvine Welsh
OL:OL816266W.description: Roy Strang lies in a coma in an Edinburgh hospital, narrating from a fantasy African expedition to hunt a marabou stork while memories surface of his brutal Scottish upbringing and his part in a gang rape. A novel that moves between coma fantasy, past, and present to confront violence and guilt.

OL:OL3958400W.title: By the Sea
OL:OL3958400W.author: Abdulrazak Gurnah
OL:OL3958400W.description: Saleh Omar, an elderly Zanzibari man, arrives in England seeking asylum on a passport bearing another man's name, and his story becomes entangled with that of Latif Mahmud, the son of the man whose identity he took. A novel told in two voices about exile, betrayal, and memory between Zanzibar and England.

OL:OL37871715W.title: Home to Harlem
OL:OL37871715W.author: Claude McKay
OL:OL37871715W.description: Jake Brown deserts the U.S. Army in World War I, returns to Harlem, and searches the neighborhood's nightlife for a woman named Felice while befriending Ray, an educated Haitian dining-car worker. A novel of Harlem working-class life that became a best seller during the Harlem Renaissance.

OL:OL20914620W.title: Telephone
OL:OL20914620W.author: Percival L. Everett
OL:OL20914620W.description: Zach Wells, a geology professor whose young daughter is dying of a terminal neurological disease, finds a note reading "help me" sewn into a shirt he ordered and travels to New Mexico in search of its source. A novel released in three slightly different versions, each with a different ending.

OL:OL14861047W.title: The Wings of a Dove
OL:OL14861047W.author: Henry James
OL:OL14861047W.description: Milly Theale, a dying young American heiress, travels to London and Venice, where the penniless Kate Croy encourages her own secret fiancé to court Milly so they can inherit her money. A late novel known for its psychological depth and moral ambiguity.

OL:OL11376124W.title: Tarka the Otter
OL:OL11376124W.author: Henry Williamson
OL:OL11376124W.description: Tarka, an otter born in an Devon holt, learns to swim and hunt, loses his mother and a mate, fathers cubs, and is pursued through the rivers Taw and Torridge by a pack of otterhounds led by the hound Deadlock. A closely observed account of an otter's life that won the Hawthornden Prize.

OL:OL16846W.title: The Information
OL:OL16846W.author: Martin Amis
OL:OL16846W.description: Richard Tull, a failing forty-year-old London novelist, is consumed by envy of his old friend Gwyn Barry, whose mediocre book has made him rich and famous, and sets out to ruin him by enlisting violent men he cannot control. A novel about literary rivalry and male resentment.

OL:OL258416W.title: The Bridge on the Drina
OL:OL258416W.author: Ivo Andrić
OL:OL258416W.description: Across roughly four centuries, the Ottoman-built bridge over the Drina at Višegrad stands witness to the townspeople and the upheavals of empire, from its sixteenth-century construction to its damage in World War I. A historical novel by a Nobel laureate spanning generations of Bosnian, Serbian, and Muslim life.

OL:OL48286W.title: The Alexandria Quartet
OL:OL48286W.author: Lawrence Durrell
OL:OL48286W.description: In Alexandria before and during World War II, the narrator Darley reconstructs the tangled love affairs and political intrigues binding Justine, her husband Nessim, the writer Pursewarden, and others, with three books retelling the same events from shifting perspectives and a fourth carrying the story forward. A tetralogy that experiments with viewpoint and time.

OL:OL1980233W.title: Pig Earth
OL:OL1980233W.author: John Berger
OL:OL1980233W.description: Peasants in a French Alpine village work the land, slaughter pigs, make hay, and endure long winters, their lives rendered in linked stories, poems, and essays, including the tale of the exiled Lucie Cabrol. The first book of a trilogy about peasant life and its displacement.

OL:OL35358393W.title: By Grand Central Station I Sat Down and Wept
OL:OL35358393W.author: Elizabeth Smart
OL:OL35358393W.description: A woman recounts in heightened, biblical prose her consuming love affair with a married man, moving from California through arrest at the U.S. border to grief and longing. A short novel in prose poetry based on the author's affair with the poet George Barker.

OL:OL26743128W.title: Zone
OL:OL26743128W.author: Mathias Enard
OL:OL26743128W.description: Francis Mirković, a Croatian war veteran turned French intelligence agent, rides a train from Milan to Rome carrying a briefcase of secrets and turning over memories of Mediterranean wars, atrocities, and his own past. A novel written almost entirely as a single sentence over its narrator's journey.

OL:OL100040W.title: Omeros
OL:OL100040W.author: Derek Walcott
OL:OL100040W.description: On the island of Saint Lucia, the fishermen Achille and Hector both love the beautiful housemaid Helen, while a retired English officer and his wife and the blind seer Seven Seas move through a narrative loosely echoing Homer. An epic poem written in terza rima by a Nobel laureate.

OL:OL545415W.title: Tree of Smoke
OL:OL545415W.author: Denis Johnson
OL:OL545415W.description: William "Skip" Sands, a young CIA officer running psychological operations in Vietnam under his larger-than-life uncle Colonel Francis Sands, becomes caught in a murky intelligence scheme as the Houston brothers drift through the same war. A novel of the Vietnam War that won the National Book Award.

OL:OL26004554W.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
OL:OL26004554W.author: Gabrielle Zevin
OL:OL26004554W.description: Childhood friends Sam Masur and Sadie Green reunite as students in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and build a hit video game together, then found a company and weather creative clashes, love, and tragedy over three decades. A novel about friendship, collaboration, and game design.

OL:OL260101W.title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
OL:OL260101W.author: Anne Brontë
OL:OL260101W.description: Gilbert Markham becomes fascinated by Helen Graham, a mysterious widow who has taken refuge at Wildfell Hall with her young son, and her journal reveals that she has fled her dissolute, abusive husband Arthur Huntingdon. A novel framed by letters and a diary, often called an early feminist work.

OL:OL466987W.title: The Tale of the 1002nd Night
OL:OL466987W.author: Joseph Roth
OL:OL466987W.description: When the Shah of Persia visits late nineteenth-century Vienna and desires a noblewoman, the cavalry officer Baron Taittinger arranges a substitute from a brothel, setting off a chain of misfortunes that ruins Taittinger and his former mistress Mizzi Schinagl. The author's final novel, completed in exile and published posthumously.

OL:OL3032583W.title: Journey by Moonlight
OL:OL3032583W.author: Antal Szerb
OL:OL3032583W.description: Mihály, a Budapest man on his honeymoon in Italy, becomes separated from his bride and wanders from city to city toward Rome, pursued by figures from a bohemian youth haunted by sex and death. A Hungarian novel about a man unable to leave his past behind.

OL:OL20844W.title: Red Badge of Courage
OL:OL20844W.author: Stephen Crane
OL:OL20844W.description: Henry Fleming, a young Union recruit in the American Civil War, flees in panic during his first battle, then returns to his regiment wrestling with shame and a longing to prove his courage. A short novel known for its psychological study of fear and its impressionistic battle scenes.

OL:OL3412512W.title: The Recognitions
OL:OL3412512W.author: William Gaddis
OL:OL3412512W.description: Wyatt Gwyon, a New England minister's son who abandons religion for painting, falls in despair and begins forging Old Master canvases for a dealer who sells them as genuine, while a sprawling cast pursues authenticity in postwar New York and Europe. A long novel about forgery, art, and faith.

OL:OL17635834W.title: Lincoln in the Bardo
OL:OL17635834W.author: George Saunders
OL:OL17635834W.description: Over a single night in 1862, the spirits in a Georgetown cemetery observe President Lincoln cradling the body of his dead son Willie, while the boy lingers among the dead in a Buddhist-inflected limbo. A novel built from fragmentary voices and quotations that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL471565W.title: And Then There Were None
OL:OL471565W.author: Agatha Christie
OL:OL471565W.description: Ten strangers are lured to an isolated island off the Devon coast by an absent host, accused by a recording of past killings they were never punished for, and murdered one by one in the pattern of a nursery rhyme. A mystery in which the guests must reckon with a killer among them.

OL:OL17762217W.title: Pachinko
OL:OL17762217W.author: Min Jin Lee
OL:OL17762217W.description: Sunja, the daughter of a poor family in early twentieth-century Korea, becomes pregnant by a married man and instead marries a kind minister who takes her to Japan, where four generations of the family endure poverty and discrimination across the colonial era and into the late 1980s. A multigenerational saga about Koreans living as a marginalized minority in Japan.

OL:OL1815834W.title: Possessing the Secret of Joy
OL:OL1815834W.author: Alice Walker
OL:OL1815834W.description: Tashi, an African woman from the Olinka people who appeared in The Color Purple, undergoes ritual genital cutting as a young woman, suffers lasting physical and psychological damage, and eventually returns to confront and kill the woman who performed it, standing trial for the murder. A novel that examines female genital mutilation and its effects.

OL:OL19721019W.title: In the Distance
OL:OL19721019W.author: Hernán Díaz
OL:OL19721019W.description: Håkan Söderström, a young Swedish emigrant separated from his brother in the chaos of a New York-bound voyage, lands in California and walks eastward across the nineteenth-century American West, encountering prospectors, settlers, and scientists while struggling with a language he does not speak. A reverse-frontier Western about a solitary immigrant.

OL:OL1636262W.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
OL:OL1636262W.author: Norton Juster
OL:OL1636262W.description: Milo, a bored boy who receives a mysterious tollbooth, drives his toy car into the Kingdom of Wisdom and, with the watchdog Tock and the Humbug, sets out to rescue the banished princesses Rhyme and Reason. A children's fantasy built on wordplay and puns about the value of learning.

OL:OL836970W.title: The Third Lie
OL:OL836970W.author: Ágota Kristóf
OL:OL836970W.description: Lucas, who fled his unnamed Central European country decades earlier, returns after the fall of the Iron Curtain and tries to reconcile with the past, while his twin brother Klaus, who stayed behind, offers a contradictory account of their shared history. The final book of a trilogy about identical twins, war, and unreliable memory.

OL:OL28192620W.title: Promise at Dawn
OL:OL28192620W.author: Romain Gary
OL:OL28192620W.description: Recollections of a boyhood spent in Vilnius, Poland, and the French Riviera, dominated by an adoring Russian former actress mother who is certain her son is destined for greatness, followed by his years as a wartime aviator for France. An autobiographical work about a mother's fierce ambition for her son.

OL:OL23105227W.title: In Diamond Square
OL:OL23105227W.author: Mercè Rodoreda
OL:OL23105227W.description: Natàlia, a young shop-girl in the working-class Gràcia district of Barcelona, is courted at a dance in Diamond Square by the forceful Quimet, marries him, and raises children through poverty and the upheaval of the Spanish Civil War as her husband goes off to fight. A first-person account of an ordinary woman's life amid war.

OL:OL25437676W.title: June Rain
OL:OL25437676W.author: Jabbour Douaihy
OL:OL25437676W.description: Eliyya returns to his Lebanese village forty years after a 1957 church massacre that killed his father and divided the town into two feuding clans, gathering conflicting accounts from those who witnessed or survived the killings. A novel based on a real sectarian massacre, told from many viewpoints.

OL:OL1603637W.title: Men in the Sun and Other Palestinian Stories
OL:OL1603637W.author: Ghassan Kanafani
OL:OL1603637W.description: Three Palestinian refugees of different generations, Abu Qais, Assad, and the teenaged Marwan, pay a driver to smuggle them in the empty water tank of a lorry from Iraq across the desert to find work in Kuwait. The title novella heads a collection of stories about Palestinian displacement after 1948.

OL:OL13648915W.title: The Book of Night Women
OL:OL13648915W.author: Marlon James
OL:OL13648915W.description: Lilith, born into slavery on a Jamaican sugar plantation at the end of the eighteenth century, is drawn by a group of enslaved women who sense a dark power in her and are plotting a violent revolt. A novel about slavery, brutality, and rebellion narrated in Jamaican patois.

OL:OL20384700W.title: Ghost Wall
OL:OL20384700W.author: Sarah Moss
OL:OL20384700W.description: Seventeen-year-old Silvie spends two weeks in northern England on an Iron Age reenactment with her abusive, nationalist father, an archaeology professor, and his students, foraging and living as ancient Britons until the experiment turns dangerous. A short novel about controlling fathers, class, and the appeal of an imagined past.

OL:OL2504658W.title: The Joys of Motherhood
OL:OL2504658W.author: Buchi Emecheta
OL:OL2504658W.description: Nnu Ego, born in the Igbo village of Ibuza, moves to colonial Lagos through an arranged marriage and sacrifices everything to raise many children, only to find that the rewards she expected from motherhood never arrive. A novel about womanhood and motherhood in colonial Nigeria.

OL:OL2645473W.title: Quicksand
OL:OL2645473W.author: Nella Larsen
OL:OL2645473W.description: Helga Crane, the daughter of a white Danish mother and an absent West Indian father, drifts restlessly from a Southern Black school to Chicago, Harlem, and Copenhagen, never finding acceptance, before marrying a preacher and sinking into rural poverty and constant childbearing. A Harlem Renaissance novel about a mixed-race woman's search for belonging.

OL:OL20799434W.title: The Vanishing Half
OL:OL20799434W.author: Brit Bennett
OL:OL20799434W.description: Identical twins Desiree and Stella flee their small Louisiana town of light-skinned Black residents in 1954, after which Stella disappears to live as a white woman in California while Desiree returns home with a dark-skinned daughter, the two lives later intersecting through their children. A novel about racial passing and its consequences across generations.

OL:OL19753331W.title: Ordinary People
OL:OL19753331W.author: Diana Evans
OL:OL19753331W.description: Two Black British couples in South London, Melissa and Michael and Stephanie and Damian, navigate the strains of long-term relationships, parenthood, and middle age over the years between Obama's election and Michael Jackson's death. A novel about modern marriage and family life.

OL:OL20642211W.title: To Be Taught, If Fortunate
OL:OL20642211W.author: Becky Chambers
OL:OL20642211W.description: Ariadne and three fellow astronauts aboard the ship Merian travel beyond the Solar System to study life on four distant worlds, adapting their bodies to each planet, until messages from a crippled Earth suggest no one may be left to receive their findings. An epistolary science fiction novella about space exploration and human curiosity.

OL:OL2917008W.title: Gormenghast
OL:OL2917008W.author: Mervyn Peake
OL:OL2917008W.description: Titus Groan, seventy-seventh Earl of the crumbling castle Gormenghast, grows from boyhood chafing against its endless rituals while the ruthless kitchen boy Steerpike murders and schemes his way toward power, leading to a final confrontation amid a great flood. The second novel in a fantasy sequence set in a vast, decaying castle.

OL:OL27420W.title: Blindness
OL:OL27420W.author: José Saramago
OL:OL27420W.description: An unexplained epidemic of white blindness sweeps an unnamed city, and the afflicted are herded into a filthy quarantined asylum where order collapses, while a doctor's wife who secretly retains her sight guides a small group through the breakdown of society. A novel about social collapse following a mass loss of sight.

OL:OL26398W.title: Memento Mori
OL:OL26398W.author: Muriel Spark
OL:OL26398W.description: A circle of elderly upper-class Londoners, centered on Dame Lettie Colston, begin receiving anonymous phone calls from a voice that tells each of them, "Remember you must die," prompting suspicion, investigation, and reflection on their own mortality. A novel about old age and death told with dark comedy.

OL:OL43775W.title: Samskara
OL:OL43775W.author: U. R. Anantha Murthy
OL:OL43775W.description: When Naranappa, a Brahmin who flouted caste rules by drinking, eating meat, and living with a low-caste woman, dies in a South Indian agrahara, the respected scholar Praneshacharya cannot determine who may perform the funeral rites, and his crisis deepens after he sleeps with the dead man's mistress. A novel about caste, ritual, and a Brahmin's loss of certainty.

OL:OL2009183W.title: Sport and a Pastime
OL:OL2009183W.author: James Salter
OL:OL2009183W.description: In provincial France in the early 1960s, an American college dropout, Phillip Dean, conducts an affair with a young French woman, Anne-Marie, as the couple drives between towns and hotels, all of it imagined and reconstructed by an unnamed narrator who is largely absent from the events. A novel known for its erotic frankness and unreliable narration.

OL:OL2465642W.title: The Sportswriter
OL:OL2465642W.author: Richard Ford
OL:OL2465642W.description: Frank Bascombe, a failed novelist turned New Jersey sportswriter divorced and grieving the death of his young son, moves through the events of one Easter weekend marked by a botched date, a friend's suicide, and his own detached search for contentment. The first novel in a series following an ordinary suburban American man.

OL:OL15210983W.title: Molloy
OL:OL15210983W.author: Samuel Beckett
OL:OL15210983W.description: In the first half, the vagrant Molloy sets out on a crippled, meandering journey to find his mother and ends up in a ditch; in the second, the agent Jacques Moran is sent to track Molloy down and gradually disintegrates into a similar wandering decline. An experimental novel in two monologues about decay and futility.

OL:OL10429255W.title: Caught
OL:OL10429255W.author: Henry Green
OL:OL10429255W.description: Richard Roe, an upper-class widower, serves in London's Auxiliary Fire Service in the months of waiting before the Blitz under the working-class officer Pye, whose deranged sister once abducted Roe's young son, complicating the two men's strained relationship. A novel about the home front and the early air raids on London.

OL:OL2085293W.title: The Spiral Ascent
OL:OL2085293W.author: Edward Upward
OL:OL2085293W.description: Alan Sebrill, a would-be poet from modest origins who teaches to earn a living, joins the Communist Party, marries, and spends decades trying to reconcile his commitment to political struggle with his desire to write. An autobiographical trilogy about a poet's lifelong tension between art and politics.

OL:OL1206495W.title: Elders and Betters
OL:OL1206495W.author: Ivy Compton-Burnett
OL:OL1206495W.description: The Donne family moves to the country to be near their relatives, and when the dying Aunt Sukey leaves two conflicting wills, her niece Anna destroys the wrong one, setting off a contest of self-interest that strains the two families' good manners. A novel told almost entirely in dialogue about family power and inheritance.

OL:OL35623W.title: Parable of the Sower
OL:OL35623W.author: Octavia E. Butler
OL:OL35623W.description: In a near-future California wrecked by climate disaster and social collapse, teenage Lauren Olamina, who feels others' pain as her own, flees her destroyed walled community and leads survivors north while developing a new belief system she calls Earthseed. A dystopian novel about survival and the founding of a religion.

OL:OL1970213W.title: The Birthday Boys
OL:OL1970213W.author: Beryl Bainbridge
OL:OL1970213W.description: Five members of Robert Falcon Scott's 1910–1913 expedition to Antarctica, including Scott himself, Edward Wilson, and Lawrence Oates, each narrate a stretch of the doomed race to the South Pole, where the Norwegian Amundsen beats them and the returning party perishes. A novel reconstructing the Scott expedition through its members' voices.

OL:OL3171069W.title: The Haunting of Hill House
OL:OL3171069W.author: Shirley Jackson
OL:OL3171069W.description: Dr. John Montague invites several people with reported paranormal experiences to spend a summer in the sinister Hill House, where the fragile, lonely Eleanor Vance grows increasingly attached to the place as the group experiences mounting supernatural disturbances. A gothic horror novel that leaves its hauntings ambiguous.

OL:OL136820W.title: The Garden of the Finzi-Continis
OL:OL136820W.author: Giorgio Bassani
OL:OL136820W.description: In 1930s Ferrara, the narrator falls in love with Micòl, daughter of the wealthy and aristocratic Jewish Finzi-Contini family, whose walled garden and tennis court become a refuge for young Jews barred from society as Mussolini's racial laws tighten toward deportation. A novel about Jewish life in Italy under fascism.

OL:OL16672348W.title: All That Is
OL:OL16672348W.author: James Salter
OL:OL16672348W.description: Philip Bowman, who survives a kamikaze attack as a young naval officer in the Pacific, returns to become a New York book editor in the decades after the war, moving through a failed marriage and a string of love affairs and betrayals. A novel tracing one man's loves and career across postwar America.

OL:OL551015W.title: Fingersmith
OL:OL551015W.author: Sarah Waters
OL:OL551015W.description: In 1860s England, Sue Trinder, a young thief raised among London criminals, is sent to pose as a maid to the sheltered heiress Maud Lilly as part of a swindler's plot to seize her fortune, but the two women fall in love and the scheme reveals deeper deceptions. A Victorian-set novel of crime, deception, and reversals.

OL:OL1863359W.title: Felicia's Journey
OL:OL1863359W.author: William Trevor
OL:OL1863359W.description: Felicia, a pregnant eighteen-year-old Irish girl, crosses to the English Midlands to search for the boyfriend who abandoned her, where she falls into the orbit of Joseph Hilditch, a mild-mannered catering manager who has preyed on vulnerable young women before. A novel about a naive girl and a predatory man.

OL:OL14919676W.title: Strangers
OL:OL14919676W.author: Anita Brookner
OL:OL14919676W.description: Paul Sturgis, a retired London bank manager resigned to bachelorhood, dutifully visits his cousin's widow Helena and, to dodge her Christmas invitation, takes a holiday in Venice where he meets the younger, divorcing Vicky Gardner. A late novel built almost entirely from one solitary man's memories and reflections on loneliness.

OL:OL553752W.title: American Tabloid
OL:OL553752W.author: James Ellroy
