OL:OL553752W.description: Pete Bondurant, Kemper Boyd, and Ward Littell, three rogue operatives moving between the FBI, the CIA, the Mafia, and the Kennedy circle, become entangled in election rigging, the Bay of Pigs, and ultimately the plot to assassinate John F. Kennedy. The first book of the Underworld USA Trilogy, mixing fiction with documented history of American corruption.

OL:OL7920206W.title: Titus Groan
OL:OL7920206W.author: Mervyn Peake
OL:OL7920206W.description: In the vast crumbling castle of Gormenghast, the birth of Titus, heir to Lord Sepulchrave, disrupts centuries of rigid ritual while the ruthless kitchen boy Steerpike climbs from the kitchens toward power. The first novel in the Gormenghast sequence, known for its elaborate Gothic world and grotesque characters.

OL:OL15723133W.title: Smiley's People
OL:OL15723133W.author: John le Carré
OL:OL15723133W.description: Called out of retirement, George Smiley investigates the murder of an old agent, an exiled Soviet general in London, and follows the trail through émigré circles toward a final reckoning with the Soviet spymaster Karla. The third and last novel of the Karla Trilogy, ending Smiley's long duel with his adversary.

OL:OL262505W.title: The Valley of Fear
OL:OL262505W.author: Arthur Conan Doyle
OL:OL262505W.description: Sherlock Holmes deciphers a coded warning from a Moriarty agent and travels to Birlstone manor, where the master of the house has been found dead from a shotgun blast; the second half recounts the American secret-society events behind the killing. The fourth and final Holmes novel, split between an English mystery and a backstory drawn from the Molly Maguires.

OL:OL15008W.title: The Collector
OL:OL15008W.author: John Fowles
OL:OL15008W.description: Frederick Clegg, a withdrawn clerk and butterfly collector who comes into money, abducts the art student Miranda Grey and imprisons her in the cellar of his isolated cottage, the story told first from his viewpoint and then from her diary. A debut thriller alternating between captor and captive and threaded with British class conflict.

OL:OL29907510W.title: Sorrows of Young Werther
OL:OL29907510W.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
OL:OL29907510W.description: Werther, a young man staying at Wahlheim, falls in love with Lotte, who is engaged and then married to Albert, and his hopeless passion deepens into despair until he takes his own life, all recounted in his letters. An epistolary novel of the Sturm und Drang movement that made its author famous across Europe.

OL:OL52449W.title: Elective Affinities
OL:OL52449W.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
OL:OL52449W.description: The nobleman Eduard and his wife Charlotte settle into married life on their country estate until the arrival of the Captain and Charlotte's niece Ottilie draws the four into crossed attractions that end in tragedy. A novel that frames human passion through an extended metaphor of chemical affinities.

OL:OL16938494W.title: Simplicissimus
OL:OL16938494W.author: Hans Jakob Christoffel von Grimmelshausen
OL:OL16938494W.description: A nameless peasant boy whose farm is destroyed by marauding soldiers grows up amid the Thirty Years' War, serving as fool, soldier, and rogue across a ravaged Holy Roman Empire. Often called the first major German novel, a picaresque account of war, cruelty, and survival.

OL:OL8193478W.title: The Adventures of Oliver Twist
OL:OL8193478W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL8193478W.description: Oliver Twist, an orphan raised in a brutal workhouse, runs away to London and falls in with Fagin's gang of young pickpockets, the menacing Bill Sikes, and the kindly Nancy as his true parentage is gradually uncovered. A novel that exposed the workhouse system and London's criminal underworld.

OL:OL1940374W.title: Trilby
OL:OL1940374W.author: George du Maurier
OL:OL1940374W.description: In bohemian 1850s Paris, the tone-deaf artist's model Trilby O'Ferrall is hypnotized by the sinister musician Svengali, who transforms her into a celebrated singer wholly under his control until his death breaks the spell. A sensation novel that gave the English language the figure of Svengali.

OL:OL30274067W.title: Roxana
OL:OL30274067W.author: Daniel Defoe
OL:OL30274067W.description: Roxana, abandoned penniless with five children after her husband squanders their money, becomes the mistress of a landlord, a French prince, and other wealthy men, amassing a fortune while concealing her past until a grown daughter threatens to expose her. A first-person narrative of a woman trading virtue for financial independence.

OL:OL13116995W.title: The Monk
OL:OL13116995W.author: Matthew Gregory Lewis
OL:OL13116995W.description: Ambrosio, a revered monk in Madrid, is seduced by Matilda, a woman who has entered the monastery disguised as a man, and descends through lust, rape, and murder to a pact with the devil and his own destruction. A Gothic novel notorious in its day for its sexual and blasphemous content.

OL:OL109871W.title: The Way We Live Now
OL:OL109871W.author: Anthony Trollope
OL:OL109871W.description: The financier Augustus Melmotte arrives in London with a mysterious past and a fraudulent railway scheme, drawing aristocrats, speculators, and fortune-hunters into his orbit before his credit collapses and he poisons himself. A long satirical novel attacking the greed and dishonesty of Victorian society.

OL:OL64465W.title: Point Counter Point
OL:OL64465W.author: Aldous Huxley
OL:OL64465W.description: A large cast of London intellectuals and socialites, including the novelist Philip Quarles, the writer Walter Bidlake, and figures modeled on real contemporaries, pursue tangled love affairs and clashing ideas. A novel structured like musical counterpoint, with parallel plots set against each other.

OL:OL106079W.title: Stamboul Train
OL:OL106079W.author: Graham Greene
OL:OL106079W.description: Passengers on the express train from Ostend to Istanbul, among them the currant trader Myatt, the chorus girl Coral Musker, and the exiled revolutionary Dr. Czinner, see their lives intersect over the three-day journey. The novel that brought its author his first commercial success.

OL:OL1921184W.title: The Names
OL:OL1921184W.author: Don DeLillo
OL:OL1921184W.description: James Axton, an American risk analyst living in Greece, is drawn into the mystery of a cult that murders its victims to match their initials with place names, even as his marriage to an archaeologist falls apart. A novel preoccupied with language, naming, and American power abroad.

OL:OL1858636W.title: Voyage in the Dark
OL:OL1858636W.author: Jean Rhys
OL:OL1858636W.description: Anna Morgan, brought from her Caribbean home to a cold England by her stepmother, drifts through life as a chorus girl, becomes the kept mistress of an older man, and spirals downward after he leaves her. A novel told in fragmented, memory-laced narration about displacement and decline.

OL:OL59794W.title: Earthsea
OL:OL59794W.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
OL:OL59794W.description: In the island archipelago of Earthsea, the gifted young mage Ged unleashes a deadly shadow through pride, then pursues it across the seas to confront and reckon with it, with later volumes following the priestess Tenar and the dying of magic. A fantasy sequence beginning with A Wizard of Earthsea and built around true names and balance.

OL:OL863735W.title: The Heart of Midlothian
OL:OL863735W.author: Walter Scott
OL:OL863735W.description: After the 1736 Porteous Riot in Edinburgh, Jeanie Deans refuses to lie to save her sister Effie, condemned for child murder, and walks to London to plead with the queen for a pardon. A historical novel set in eighteenth-century Scotland, often considered its author's finest.

OL:OL52114W.title: The War of the Worlds
OL:OL52114W.author: H. G. Wells
OL:OL52114W.description: Cylinders fall from Mars near Woking, and the Martians emerge with heat-rays and towering tripods to devastate southern England, while the narrator struggles to survive and reach his wife. A pioneering alien-invasion story in which the invaders are finally killed by Earth's bacteria.

OL:OL166496W.title: The Inverted World
OL:OL166496W.author: Christopher Priest
OL:OL166496W.description: Helward Mann comes of age in Earth City, a settlement winched endlessly along railway tracks across a planet to stay near a shifting "optimum," and his work beyond the city reveals the warped truth about their world. A science fiction novel that measures time in distance and turns on a final shift in perspective.

OL:OL17062866W.title: Citizen
OL:OL17062866W.author: Claudia Rankine
OL:OL17062866W.description: Across prose, poetry, and images, an unnamed second-person "you" accumulates the everyday racial slights and larger traumas of Black life in America, from microaggressions to the deaths of Trayvon Martin and others and incidents involving Serena Williams. A book-length lyric on race that mixes essay, verse, and visual art.

OL:OL547745W.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
OL:OL547745W.author: Helen Fielding
OL:OL547745W.description: Bridget Jones, a single thirtysomething Londoner, records a year of resolutions, weight counts, and cigarettes in her diary while juggling her caddish boss Daniel Cleaver and the reserved barrister Mark Darcy. A diary novel loosely based on Pride and Prejudice and credited with launching modern chick lit.

OL:OL25516127W.title: Nightcrawling
OL:OL25516127W.author: Leila Mottley
OL:OL25516127W.description: Kiara Johnson, a teenager scraping by in an East Oakland apartment complex, turns to sex work to cover the rent and care for the neglected boy next door, then becomes a key witness in a police sexual-abuse scandal. A debut novel based on a real Oakland Police Department case.

OL:OL36045730W.title: Where We Come From
OL:OL36045730W.author: Oscar Casares
OL:OL36045730W.description: In Brownsville, Texas, the retired schoolteacher Nina secretly shelters an undocumented teenager named Daniel in a rental house, a situation that grows dangerous when her visiting twelve-year-old godson Orly discovers him. A novel about family, the border, and the risks of harboring migrants.

OL:OL21671152W.title: Poor
OL:OL21671152W.author: Caleb Femi
OL:OL21671152W.description: Poems paired with original photography trace the lives of young Black boys growing up on the North Peckham estate in south London, set against its concrete walls, violence, and gentrifying streets. A debut collection written in south-London dialect that won the Forward Prize for Best First Collection.

OL:OL4126109W.title: Noughts & Crosses
OL:OL4126109W.author: Malorie Blackman
OL:OL4126109W.description: In an alternate Britain where dark-skinned Crosses rule over light-skinned Noughts under harsh segregation, Sephy, a Cross politician's daughter, and Callum, a Nought, sustain a forbidden love as violence and terrorism tear their world apart. A young-adult novel that inverts racial hierarchy to examine prejudice, the first of a series.

OL:OL2191789W.title: Sister Outsider
OL:OL2191789W.author: Audre Lorde
OL:OL2191789W.description: Fifteen essays and speeches written between 1976 and 1984 examine race, sexism, homophobia, class, and the uses of anger from the standpoint of a Black lesbian poet and activist. A foundational work of Black feminist and intersectional thought.

OL:OL36270985W.title: House on the Borderland
OL:OL36270985W.author: William Hope Hodgson
OL:OL36270985W.description: Two men fishing in remote western Ireland find a ruined house above an abyss and a recluse's journal recounting his besiegement by monstrous swine-creatures and his visions of the sun's death and the end of the universe. An early cosmic-horror novel that influenced later weird-fiction writers.

OL:OL11294796W.title: The Journal of Albion Moonlight
OL:OL11294796W.author: Kenneth Patchen
OL:OL11294796W.description: The shape-shifting Albion Moonlight and his companions wander across America and the battlefields of Europe in a fragmented, surreal journal that rages against war and fascism as Europe falls in 1940. An experimental antiwar work that the author had to self-publish by subscription.

OL:OL2066160W.title: The Spider's House
OL:OL2066160W.author: Paul Bowles
OL:OL2066160W.description: In Fez during Morocco's 1954 uprising against French colonial rule, the lives of the American expatriate writer Stenham and a poor Arab boy, Amar, who backs the rebellion, become entwined amid the turmoil. A novel about the gulf between cultures set during a real political crisis.

OL:OL26414465W.title: Who Was Changed and Who Was Dead
OL:OL26414465W.author: Barbara Comyns
OL:OL26414465W.description: The Willoweed family endures a summer flood and then a wave of madness and grisly deaths in their English village, watched by the sisters Emma and Hattie under the tyranny of their grandmother. A tragicomic novel banned in Ireland on its release.

OL:OL1326349W.title: The Unicorn
OL:OL1326349W.author: Iris Murdoch
OL:OL1326349W.description: Marian Taylor arrives as governess at Gaze Castle on a remote Irish coast and finds no children to teach, only Hannah Crean-Smith, a beautiful woman confined to the house for seven years as punishment for betraying her husband. A Gothic novel in which the surrounding characters debate whether Hannah is a captive innocent or a willing prisoner of guilt.

OL:OL7171684W.title: Europe After the Rain
OL:OL7171684W.author: Alan Burns
OL:OL7171684W.description: An unnamed narrator moves through a ruined, unnamed country where a war some say has ended but whose violence continues, searching for a girl whose father and brother are tied to rebel activity. An experimental novel, named after a Max Ernst painting, that uses collage and cut-up techniques to blur the line between wartime and peace.

OL:OL27820956W.title: After Sappho
OL:OL27820956W.author: Selby Wynn Schwartz
OL:OL27820956W.description: In cascading first-person-plural vignettes, a chorus of women writers, painters, and performers across late-nineteenth and early-twentieth-century Europe, among them Colette, Sarah Bernhardt, Eleonora Duse, Natalie Barney, and Virginia Woolf, take Sappho as their model. A novel that reimagines feminist and lesbian artists fighting for liberation and control over their own lives.

OL:OL55221W.title: A Flag for Sunrise
OL:OL55221W.author: Robert Stone
OL:OL55221W.description: An American anthropologist, a nun losing her faith, and a violent ex-Coast Guard drifter are drawn into a revolution in the fictional Central American republic of Tecan, where the anthropologist agrees to gather information for the CIA. A novel about American intervention abroad and the collision of political and religious idealism with moral ambiguity.

OL:OL1855887W.title: The Child in Time
OL:OL1855887W.author: Ian McEwan
OL:OL1855887W.description: Two years after his three-year-old daughter Kate is snatched from a supermarket, Stephen Lewis, a writer of children's books, drifts through grief while his marriage to Julie comes apart and he sits on a government committee on childcare. A novel that won the Whitbread Award and weaves domestic loss together with ideas about time and memory.

OL:OL25687457W.title: Aubrey-Maturin Series
OL:OL25687457W.author: Patrick O'Brian
OL:OL25687457W.description: Captain Jack Aubrey of the Royal Navy and his ship's surgeon and friend Stephen Maturin, a physician, naturalist, and intelligence agent, sail through the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars from 1800 toward Waterloo. A sequence of twenty completed nautical historical novels known for their detailed period accuracy and the central friendship.

OL:OL20494708W.title: A Girl Is a Half-Formed Thing
OL:OL20494708W.author: Eimear McBride
OL:OL20494708W.description: An unnamed Irish girl grows up alongside her older brother, whose childhood brain tumour shadows the family, while she contends with a religious mother and abuse, narrating her life from inside her fractured thoughts. A debut novel told in a fragmented stream-of-consciousness style that breaks ordinary grammar and syntax.

OL:OL19344016W.title: Milkman
OL:OL19344016W.author: Anna Burns
OL:OL19344016W.description: An eighteen-year-old known only as middle sister, living in an unnamed city during the Troubles, is pursued by an older married paramilitary called Milkman, and rumours of an affair turn her community and her mother against her. A novel that won the Booker Prize, narrated in long, digressive sentences without proper names.

OL:OL2527681W.title: A Question of Power
OL:OL2527681W.author: Bessie Head
OL:OL2527681W.description: Elizabeth, a mixed-race South African who has fled to the Botswanan village of Motabeng to teach and garden, slides into a mental breakdown haunted by two men, Sello and Dan, who may not be real. A semi-autobiographical novel that moves between everyday village work and hallucinatory nighttime visions of power and madness.

OL:OL1863366W.title: The Story of Lucy Gault
OL:OL1863366W.author: William Trevor
OL:OL1863366W.description: On the Cork coast in the early 1920s, nine-year-old Lucy Gault runs away rather than leave her family's threatened house, and a series of mistakes convinces her parents she has drowned, so they flee abroad while she is found alive and raised by servants. A novel about the lifelong consequences of that misunderstanding.

OL:OL20032791W.title: Grief Is the Thing With Feathers
OL:OL20032791W.author: Max Porter
OL:OL20032791W.description: In a London flat, a Ted Hughes scholar and his two young sons reel from the sudden death of their wife and mother, and a talking crow arrives as trickster, babysitter, and healer who vows to stay until the family no longer needs him. A short book that mixes prose, poetry, and fable.

OL:OL27482W.title: The Hobbit
OL:OL27482W.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
OL:OL27482W.description: Bilbo Baggins, a comfort-loving hobbit, is swept up by the wizard Gandalf and thirteen dwarves on a journey across Middle-earth to reclaim their treasure from the dragon Smaug, finding a magic ring along the way. A children's fantasy novel that became a classic and led to its sequel, The Lord of the Rings.

OL:OL41078W.title: The Fall of the House of Usher
OL:OL41078W.author: Edgar Allan Poe
OL:OL41078W.description: An unnamed narrator visits his boyhood friend Roderick Usher at the family's decaying mansion, where Roderick's twin sister Madeline is entombed while still alive and returns to bring about the siblings' deaths as the house itself collapses into the tarn. A Gothic short story built on a haunted house, illness, and doubling.

OL:OL27411628W.title: Emily Wilde's Encyclopaedia of Faeries
OL:OL27411628W.author: Heather Fawcett
OL:OL27411628W.description: In 1909, Emily Wilde, a brilliant and prickly Cambridge dryadologist, travels to the remote Scandinavian village of Hrafnsvik to study its faeries for her encyclopaedia, aided and irritated by her charming rival Wendell Bambleby. A fantasy novel told through Emily's journal as she investigates the hidden fae of the surrounding forest.

OL:OL5280446W.title: Bear
OL:OL5280446W.author: Marian Engel
OL:OL5280446W.description: Lou, a lonely Toronto archivist, is sent to a remote northern Ontario island to catalogue the library of the late Colonel Cary's estate, where she forms an increasingly intimate, sexual bond with the property's resident bear. A short Canadian novel about isolation and renewal, often called the country's most controversial book.

OL:OL20783698W.title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
OL:OL20783698W.author: Ocean Vuong
OL:OL20783698W.description: Little Dog, a young Vietnamese American man, writes a letter to his illiterate mother that reconstructs the family's history from wartime Vietnam through their life in Hartford, recalling his grandmother Lan and his first love, Trevor. A novel in the form of an unsent letter exploring race, class, and masculinity.

OL:OL1259171W.title: Proxopera
OL:OL1259171W.author: Benedict Kiely
OL:OL1259171W.description: Granda Binchey, an elderly retired teacher, is held hostage with his family by masked IRA men who force him to drive a bomb into his Irish town while the others are kept under guard. A short novel about the Troubles, written in response to the proxy bombings that used ordinary people to deliver explosives.

OL:OL12104489W.title: Coming Through Slaughter
OL:OL12104489W.author: Michael Ondaatje
OL:OL12104489W.description: In 1907 New Orleans, cornet player Buddy Bolden juggles barbering, family, and music through his last sane months as an early jazz pioneer, until his behaviour grows erratic and his friend, the detective Webb, searches for him. A fragmented, jazz-influenced fictionalization of a real musician's collapse.

OL:OL24364471W.title: Rig Veda
OL:OL24364471W.author: Anonymous
OL:OL24364471W.description: The collection gathers 1,028 hymns in Vedic Sanskrit, arranged in ten books, addressed to deities such as Indra, Agni, and Soma and used in ritual, with sections on cosmology and creation. One of the oldest religious texts in any Indo-European language and the foundational scripture of the Vedas.

OL:OL63250W.title: All About H. Hatterr
OL:OL63250W.author: G. V. Desani
OL:OL63250W.description: H. Hatterr, the son of a European merchant officer and a woman from Penang and raised in Calcutta missionary schools, travels to seven Oriental cities to consult seven sages, escaping each encounter more battered than enlightened. A comic novel known for its exuberant, mongrel English mixing slang, archaisms, and Indian idiom.

OL:OL1884862W.title: Silent Spring
OL:OL1884862W.author: Rachel Carson
OL:OL1884862W.description: Marshalling evidence on DDT and other synthetic pesticides, this environmental science book documents how chemical spraying poisons ecosystems, kills birds and other wildlife, and endangers human health, and accuses the chemical industry of spreading disinformation. It is widely credited with launching the modern environmental movement and helping bring about a U.S. ban on agricultural DDT.

OL:OL627069W.title: The Real Life of Sebastian Knight
OL:OL627069W.author: Vladimir Nabokov
OL:OL627069W.description: The narrator V. sets out to write a biography of his late half-brother, the Russian-born English novelist Sebastian Knight, tracking down Sebastian's Cambridge contemporaries, former lovers, and his secretary to refute a misleading earlier account. The first English-language novel by its author, often cited as a forerunner of the postmodernist novel.

OL:OL31256W.title: The Grass Is Singing
OL:OL31256W.author: Doris Lessing
OL:OL31256W.description: On a failing farm in 1940s Southern Rhodesia, Mary Turner enters a loveless marriage to the unsuccessful farmer Dick and is found murdered by their black servant Moses, the rest of the book retracing the events that led there. A first novel that examines the racial politics of white-ruled colonial Africa.

OL:OL33658345W.title: The Coming Bad Days
OL:OL33658345W.author: Sarah Bernstein
OL:OL33658345W.description: An unnamed woman leaves the man she lives with and moves to a stone cottage in a university town to research the poet Paul Celan, then befriends the decisive, assured Clara as an unexplained curfew, missing girls, and deteriorating weather grip the city. A debut novel concerned with femininity, isolation, and dread.

OL:OL863837W.title: A Kestrel for a Knave
OL:OL863837W.author: Barry Hines
OL:OL863837W.description: Over a single day in a South Yorkshire mining village, fifteen-year-old Billy Casper endures a neglectful home, a brutal school, and a paper round, finding purpose only in training a kestrel named Kes, until his brother Jud takes revenge on the bird. A novel about a working-class boy failed by the education system, filmed as Kes.

OL:OL816259W.title: Trainspotting
OL:OL816259W.author: Irvine Welsh
OL:OL816259W.description: Mark Renton and a circle of heroin users, con men, and brawlers including Sick Boy, Spud, and the violent Begbie drift through the housing schemes of Leith, Edinburgh, cycling through addiction, withdrawal, and attempts at escape. Written in Scots dialect across loosely linked stories, it became a cult novel and the basis for the 1996 film.

OL:OL60988W.title: How Late It Was, How Late
OL:OL60988W.author: James Kelman
OL:OL60988W.description: Sammy, a Glasgow ex-convict, wakes in a lane after a drinking binge, fights with plainclothes police, and comes to realize he has gone blind, then struggles through interrogations and the benefits bureaucracy as he adjusts. Written in working-class Glaswegian dialect and stream of consciousness, it won the 1994 Booker Prize.

OL:OL1707638W.title: True History of the Kelly Gang
OL:OL1707638W.author: Peter Carey
OL:OL1707638W.description: In his own ungrammatical voice, the Australian bushranger Ned Kelly recounts his hardscrabble Irish-immigrant childhood, his slide into outlawry, the shootout at Stringybark Creek, and the gang's final armoured stand against police. A fictional memoir modelled on Kelly's Jerilderie Letter that won the 2001 Booker Prize.

OL:OL2916988W.title: The Gormenghast Novels
OL:OL2916988W.author: Mervyn Peake
OL:OL2916988W.description: Within the vast, decaying castle of Gormenghast, bound by endless ritual, the heir Titus Groan is born and grows up while the ambitious kitchen boy Steerpike schemes his way upward through murder and manipulation, until Titus finally leaves to wander the outside world. A trilogy comprising Titus Groan, Gormenghast, and Titus Alone.

OL:OL472250W.title: Sleeping Murder
OL:OL472250W.author: Agatha Christie
OL:OL472250W.description: Newlywed Gwenda Reed buys an old English house she feels she somehow knows, and a sudden memory of witnessing a strangling leads her and Miss Marple to investigate the long-ago disappearance of her stepmother Helen. Written during the Second World War but published posthumously as the last Miss Marple novel.

OL:OL48197W.title: The Street
OL:OL48197W.author: Ann Petry
OL:OL48197W.description: Lutie Johnson, a young single Black mother, leaves her unfaithful husband and moves with her son Bub into a tenement on 116th Street in 1944 Harlem, where poverty and male predation steadily close in until she kills a man and flees. A novel about race, gender, and class, the first by a Black woman to sell over a million copies.

OL:OL465059W.title: The Amazing Mr Blunden
OL:OL465059W.author: Antonia Barber
OL:OL465059W.description: Caretaking an abandoned London house, Lucy and Jamie meet the ghosts of Sara and Georgie Latimer, children from a century earlier, and use a book of instructions to travel back in time and save them from the murderous Wickenses, aided by the lawyer Mr. Blunden. A children's time-travel fantasy first published as The Ghosts.

OL:OL1647068W.title: Soldiers of Salamis
OL:OL1647068W.author: Javier Cercas
OL:OL1647068W.description: A writer named Javier Cercas investigates how the Falangist poet Rafael Sánchez Mazas escaped execution at the end of the Spanish Civil War when a Republican soldier found him hiding yet chose not to give him away, and tracks down an old veteran, Miralles, who may have been that soldier. A novel blending fact and fiction about war and memory.

OL:OL712021W.title: By Night in Chile
OL:OL712021W.author: Roberto Bolaño
OL:OL712021W.description: Father Sebastián Urrutia Lacroix, an aging Jesuit priest and literary critic, delivers a feverish deathbed monologue recalling his career under the Pinochet dictatorship, including lessons on Marxism he gave to the general and his officers. A short novel that satirizes the Chilean literary establishment's complicity with the regime.

OL:OL14861980W.title: The Man Who Planted Trees
OL:OL14861980W.author: Jean Giono
OL:OL14861980W.description: Hiking through a desolate valley in Provence in 1913, the narrator meets Elzéard Bouffier, a solitary shepherd who spends decades planting acorns and saplings until the barren land becomes a living forest dotted with streams and settlers. A short allegorical tale about one person's patient, anonymous restoration of the land.

OL:OL2196005W.title: Moominland Midwinter
OL:OL2196005W.author: Tove Jansson
OL:OL2196005W.description: Moomintroll wakes early from winter hibernation while his family sleeps and must survive a strange snow-covered world, befriending Too-ticky and Little My and encountering the deadly Lady of the Cold. The sixth Moomin book, marking a darker and more introspective turn in the series.

OL:OL1984734W.title: Flaubert's Parrot
OL:OL1984734W.author: Julian Barnes
OL:OL1984734W.description: Geoffrey Braithwaite, a widowed retired English doctor, travels through France chasing details of Gustave Flaubert's life, fixating on which of two museums holds the stuffed parrot that sat on the writer's desk. A postmodern work mixing biography, criticism, and fiction, with Braithwaite's own grief surfacing throughout.

OL:OL1793164W.title: Three Men in a Boat
OL:OL1793164W.author: Jerome K. Jerome
OL:OL1793164W.description: George, Harris, and the narrator J., along with the dog Montmorency, take a two-week boating holiday up the Thames from Kingston to Oxford, their trip filled with mishaps and digressions. A comic novel that began as a serious travel guide before the humor took over.

OL:OL7922785W.title: The Fish Can Sing
OL:OL7922785W.author: Halldór Laxness
OL:OL7922785W.description: The orphaned boy Álfgrímur grows up among eccentrics at Brekkukot, a turf cottage in early twentieth-century Reykjavík, and becomes fascinated by Garðar Hólm, a celebrated Icelandic singer whose returns prompt him to question his own future. A coming-of-age novel built from character sketches and episodes.

OL:OL15125374W.title: Seasons of Anomy
OL:OL15125374W.author: Wole Soyinka
OL:OL15125374W.description: Ofeyi, an advertising executive in an unnamed African nation, spreads revolutionary ideas from the commune of Aiyéró and then crosses a country torn by massacres to search for his abducted lover, Iriyise. The author's second novel, retelling the Orpheus myth against Nigeria's 1966 violence.

OL:OL661946W.title: Allah Is Not Obliged
OL:OL661946W.author: Ahmadou Kourouma
OL:OL661946W.description: Birahima, a ten-year-old orphan, leaves Ivory Coast for Liberia to find his aunt, falls in with the marabout Yacouba, and becomes a child soldier carrying a Kalashnikov through the civil wars of Liberia and Sierra Leone. The narrator recounts the brutality in crude, profane language.

OL:OL954635W.title: A River Called Time
OL:OL954635W.author: Mia Couto
OL:OL954635W.description: Mariano, raised in the city, returns to his village for his grandfather's funeral only to find the old man caught between life and death, and begins receiving letters apparently written by him that reveal the secret of his own birth. A novel blending Mozambican tradition with the boundary between the living and the dead.

OL:OL24141556W.title: Crooked Plow
OL:OL24141556W.author: Itamar Vieira Junior
OL:OL24141556W.description: Sisters Bibiana and Belonísia find a knife hidden in their grandmother's room and one is left mute after it cuts her tongue, binding the two together as they grow up among tenant farmers in the Chapada Diamantina of Bahia. A family saga about Afro-Brazilian laborers living under the long aftermath of slavery.

OL:OL50557W.title: Tar Baby
OL:OL50557W.author: Toni Morrison
OL:OL50557W.description: Jadine, a Black Sorbonne graduate and model sponsored by a wealthy white family, falls for Son, a drifter who washes up at their Caribbean estate, and their affair exposes the tensions binding the household. The author's fourth novel, examining race, class, and identity among Black Americans.

OL:OL9907660W.title: Record of a Night Too Brief
OL:OL9907660W.author: Kawakami Hiromi
OL:OL9907660W.description: Three stories run from a woman's surreal journey through an endless night with a shifting companion, to a family preparing for the wedding of a brother who has vanished, to a worker whose accidental step on a snake brings it into her apartment claiming to be her mother. Three novellas mixing folklore and the fantastic, awarded the Akutagawa Prize.

OL:OL3923952W.title: No Longer Human
OL:OL3923952W.author: Osamu Dazai
OL:OL3923952W.description: Through notebooks he leaves behind, Ōba Yōzō recounts a life of alienation, hiding his fear of people behind clowning before sliding into alcohol, drugs, and a failed double suicide. A novel of postwar Japanese literature, published shortly after its author's own suicide.

OL:OL11334034W.title: Ice
OL:OL11334034W.author: Anna Kavan
OL:OL11334034W.description: An unnamed narrator pursues a fragile, nameless young woman across a world being engulfed by advancing ice after a nuclear catastrophe, repeatedly losing and finding her amid hallucinations and collapsing societies. A surreal, dreamlike novel that blurs reality and the narrator's delusions.

OL:OL1845165W.title: Confessions of a Mask
OL:OL1845165W.author: Yukio Mishima
OL:OL1845165W.description: Kochan, a frail boy growing up in militarist and wartime Japan, traces his developing attraction to other men, hides it behind a performed "normal" self, and courts a woman named Sonoko to maintain the disguise. A largely autobiographical novel that brought its author early fame.

OL:OL25803691W.title: Scattered All Over the Earth
OL:OL25803691W.author: Yoko Tawada
OL:OL25803691W.description: Hiruko, a climate refugee from a Japan that has vanished from the map, teaches immigrant children in Denmark using her invented Pan-Scandinavian language and sets off across Europe with the linguist Knut to find anyone who still speaks her mother tongue. The first book of a trilogy about language, migration, and identity.

OL:OL37277W.title: The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas
OL:OL37277W.author: Gertrude Stein
OL:OL37277W.description: Written in the voice of the author's companion Alice B. Toklas, the book recounts their life together at the rue de Fleurus apartment in Paris and their circle of artists and writers including Picasso, Matisse, and Hemingway. A memoir cast as someone else's autobiography.

OL:OL1184871W.title: Chéri
OL:OL1184871W.author: Colette
OL:OL1184871W.description: Léa, a forty-nine-year-old retired courtesan, ends her six-year affair with Chéri, a beautiful and selfish young man half her age, when his arranged marriage to the young Edmée pulls him away, though he keeps returning to her. A novel about the parting of an aging woman and her much younger lover.

OL:OL267174W.title: Ivan Ilyitch
OL:OL267174W.author: Leo Tolstoy
OL:OL267174W.description: A high-court judge in nineteenth-century Russia, having lived a conventional and self-satisfied life, suffers a fall and a fatal illness, and as his family and colleagues recoil he confronts the emptiness of his existence and the simple compassion of his servant Gerasim. A novella about mortality and the meaning of a life.

OL:OL1002138W.title: The Passion According to G.h.
OL:OL1002138W.author: Clarice Lispector
OL:OL1002138W.description: G.H., a well-off Rio sculptor, enters her departed maid's room, panics at a cockroach, crushes it in a wardrobe door, and the sight triggers a mystical breakdown that ends with her eating the dead insect. A philosophical monologue regarded as a landmark of Latin American literature.

OL:OL37505411W.title: Martyr!
OL:OL37505411W.author: Kaveh Akbar
OL:OL37505411W.description: Cyrus Shams, a queer Iranian-American poet in Indiana recovering from addiction, becomes obsessed with martyrdom and travels to a Brooklyn museum to meet Orkideh, a dying artist whose performance leads him toward the truth about his mother, killed when her plane was shot down. A novel about grief, addiction, and the search for a meaningful death.

OL:OL53069W.title: In the Skin of a Lion
OL:OL53069W.author: Michael Ondaatje
OL:OL53069W.description: Patrick Lewis leaves rural Ontario for Toronto in the 1920s, working as a searcher for a missing millionaire and among the immigrant laborers who build the city's bridge and waterworks, before his radicalization leads him toward a bombing. A novel recovering the hidden lives of the immigrants who built early Toronto.

OL:OL12163507W.title: Maps
OL:OL12163507W.author: Nuruddin Farah
OL:OL12163507W.description: Askar, orphaned in the Ogaden, is raised by Misra, a woman from the contested borderlands, and as he grows up and moves to Mogadishu he struggles with his identity even as Somalia fights over its own. The first book of a trilogy, partly told in the second person.

OL:OL8911551W.title: A Mind at Peace
OL:OL8911551W.author: Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar
OL:OL8911551W.description: In Istanbul on the eve of World War II, the young scholar Mümtaz loves Nuran, a recently divorced woman, while his mentor İhsan lies ill and the tormented Suat works to break the couple apart. A novel about Turkish identity caught between Ottoman past and republican present.

OL:OL2957601W.title: On the Edge of Reason
OL:OL2957601W.author: Miroslav Krleža
OL:OL2957601W.description: A respectable fifty-two-year-old lawyer ruins his comfortable life when he speaks an unwelcome truth at a dinner party, calling out an industrialist's boast of murder, and is then dragged through slander, a trial, imprisonment, and ruin. A first-person novel of bureaucratic satire and the cost of honesty.

OL:OL1806976W.title: The Dew Breaker
OL:OL1806976W.author: Edwidge Danticat
OL:OL1806976W.description: A Haitian immigrant in Brooklyn, long taken by his daughter Ka for a former prisoner of the Duvalier regime, confesses that he was in fact a torturer, and surrounding stories follow the lives his victims and their families lead in exile. Linked stories that can be read as a novel, set among Haitians marked by the dictatorship.

OL:OL20681799W.title: Eighth Life
OL:OL20681799W.author: Nino Haratischvili
OL:OL20681799W.description: Niza, a Georgian living in Germany, recounts a century of her family's history to her runaway niece Brilka, tracing six generations from the Russian Revolution through Soviet rule and civil war, all tied to a cursed family recipe for hot chocolate. A multigenerational saga of Georgia across the twentieth century.

OL:OL2718328W.title: The Outsiders
OL:OL2718328W.author: S. E. Hinton
OL:OL2718328W.description: Ponyboy Curtis, a teenage greaser in 1960s Tulsa, narrates the escalating violence with the wealthier Socs after his friend Johnny kills a boy who attacks them, sending the two into hiding and toward tragedy. A coming-of-age novel written when its author was a teenager.

OL:OL34173139W.title: Things We Lost in the Fire
OL:OL34173139W.author: Mariana Enriquez
OL:OL34173139W.description: Across twelve stories, women and girls in contemporary Argentina face haunted houses, disappearances, addiction, and an epidemic of women setting themselves on fire, with the country's troubled history simmering beneath. A horror story collection that joins the supernatural to social violence.

OL:OL3198244W.title: The Lonely Londoners
OL:OL3198244W.author: Samuel Selvon
OL:OL3198244W.description: Moses Aloetta, a Trinidadian who has lived in London for years, meets newcomers like the young Galahad at Waterloo Station and gathers with other West Indian immigrants whose Sunday talks reveal the work, racism, and loneliness of postwar London. A novel narrated in Caribbean creolized English.

OL:OL26582938W.title: Golden Age
OL:OL26582938W.author: Wang Xiaobo
OL:OL26582938W.description: Wang Er, a young man sent to a commune in Yunnan during the Cultural Revolution, drifts into an affair with the doctor Chen Qingyang, and when they are exposed he turns the public struggle sessions into something close to absurd performance. A novella using sex and absurdity to portray the Maoist era.

OL:OL59863W.title: The Dispossessed
OL:OL59863W.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
OL:OL59863W.description: Shevek, a physicist from the anarchist moon Anarres, travels to the capitalist sister planet Urras to share his work on a unifying theory of time, finding rejection and frustration on both worlds, told in alternating chapters of his two lives. A science fiction novel exploring anarchism, capitalism, and the limits of utopia.

OL:OL3846785W.title: Amongst Women
OL:OL3846785W.author: John McGahern
OL:OL3846785W.description: Michael Moran, an aging IRA veteran of Ireland's War of Independence, rules his County Leitrim household with a controlling and often cruel hand, while his second wife Rose and his children both love and fear him and his sons leave for London. A novel told largely through the family's memories of the past.

OL:OL166437W.title: Hotel Du Lac
OL:OL166437W.author: Anita Brookner
OL:OL166437W.description: Edith Hope, a romance novelist sent into exile by her friends after a scandalous affair, settles at a calm lakeside hotel on Lake Geneva and observes the other English guests, including the brittle Mrs Pusey and the self-possessed Mr Neville, who proposes a marriage of convenience. It won the 1984 Booker Prize.

OL:OL41597565W.title: A Sentimental Journey
OL:OL41597565W.author: Laurence Sterne
OL:OL41597565W.description: The Reverend Mr. Yorick travels through France with his servant La Fleur, recording his encounters and emotional responses to the people he meets along the way. Left unfinished at the author's death, it gave new currency to the word "sentimental" and helped shape the literature of sensibility.

OL:OL16821748W.title: Sudden Death
OL:OL16821748W.author: Álvaro Enrigue
OL:OL16821748W.description: Caravaggio and the poet Francisco de Quevedo face each other in a tennis match in Rome, while interlocking episodes range across the Counter-Reformation, the conquest of Mexico under Hernán Cortés, and a ball made from the hair of the beheaded Anne Boleyn. A genre-crossing historical novel that mixes fiction, essay, and documentary fragments.

OL:OL10426441W.title: Towards the End of the Morning
OL:OL10426441W.author: Michael Frayn
OL:OL10426441W.description: John Dyson, a journalist stuck in the crossword and nature-notes department of an obscure national newspaper in the declining years of Fleet Street, dreams of fame and a chance on television, while his younger colleague Bob drifts through work and an unwanted engagement. A comic novel about newspaper life and ambition.

OL:OL16809803W.title: The Goldfinch
OL:OL16809803W.author: Donna Tartt
OL:OL16809803W.description: Thirteen-year-old Theo Decker survives a bombing at the Metropolitan Museum of Art that kills his mother, and in the chaos he takes a small Dutch painting of a goldfinch, which he keeps hidden as his life carries him through New York, Las Vegas, and the antiques trade. It won the 2014 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL37487420W.title: Cartucho
OL:OL37487420W.author: Nellie Campobello
OL:OL37487420W.description: In short vignettes drawn from a young girl's memories of Parral and Villa Ocampo, soldiers, executions, and gun battles of the Mexican Revolution unfold around the figure of Pancho Villa's forces. Often described as the only account of the Revolution written from a woman's perspective.

OL:OL4100647W.title: The Empty Book
OL:OL4100647W.author: Josefina Vicens
OL:OL4100647W.description: José García, a gray accountant in Mexico City, buys two notebooks meaning to draft random notes in one and compose a real book in the other, but finds he has nothing to say and writes only about that emptiness. An early Mexican metafictional novel that won the Xavier Villaurrutia Award.

OL:OL20942111W.title: Murphy
OL:OL20942111W.author: Samuel Beckett
OL:OL20942111W.description: Murphy, an idle Irishman in London who would rather sit naked in his rocking chair than work, evades the woman who wants to marry him and takes a job as an attendant at a mental asylum, where he feels he has found his kindred spirits. An early comic novel by a writer better known for his later plays.

OL:OL698192W.title: Memory of Fire
OL:OL698192W.author: Eduardo Galeano
OL:OL698192W.description: Across three volumes, hundreds of short numbered episodes retell the history of the Americas from creation myths and pre-Columbian times through conquest, colonialism, and the twentieth century. A genre-blurring work of history, myth, and literature that gives voice to the conquered and the poor.

OL:OL19670981W.title: The Moor's Account
OL:OL19670981W.author: Laila Lalami
OL:OL19670981W.description: Mustafa, a Moroccan slave renamed Estebanico, accompanies the disastrous Narváez expedition to Florida in 1527, and as the party dwindles to four survivors who cross the continent living among Indigenous peoples, he sets down his own account of the journey. A finalist for the 2015 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL21364937W.title: Slave Old Man
OL:OL21364937W.author: Patrick Chamoiseau
OL:OL21364937W.description: An old slave on a Martinique sugar plantation suddenly flees into the dense forest, pursued by his master and a fearsome mastiff, and loses all sense of self as he runs through the night toward freedom. A short novel of the Créolité movement, translated into English in 2018.

OL:OL20801026W.title: Minor Detail
OL:OL20801026W.author: Adania Shibli
OL:OL20801026W.description: In the summer of 1949 in the Negev desert, Israeli soldiers kill a group of Bedouin and capture a young woman whom they rape, murder, and bury in the sand; decades later a woman in Ramallah becomes obsessed with uncovering the full story after noticing it happened on her birthday. Based on a documented wartime crime.

OL:OL3440705W.title: Savushun
OL:OL3440705W.author: Simin Daneshvar
OL:OL3440705W.description: In Shiraz during the Allied occupation of Iran in the final years of the Second World War, Zari struggles to hold her family together as her husband Yusuf refuses to sell his crops to feed the foreign troops. Widely regarded as the first novel published in Persian by a woman.

OL:OL1168007W.title: Animal Farm
OL:OL1168007W.author: George Orwell
OL:OL1168007W.description: The animals of Manor Farm drive out their drunken owner and run the farm themselves, but the pigs Napoleon and Snowball vie for control until Napoleon seizes power and the ideals of equality give way to a new tyranny. An allegory of the Russian Revolution and the rise of Stalin.

OL:OL796465W.title: The Alchemist
OL:OL796465W.author: Paulo Coelho
OL:OL796465W.description: Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd, follows a recurring dream to the Egyptian pyramids in search of treasure, crossing North Africa and meeting a crystal merchant, an Englishman, and an alchemist who teaches him to read the world's signs. One of the best-selling books ever published, translated into dozens of languages.

OL:OL8398736W.title: The Blind Owl
OL:OL8398736W.author: Sadegh Hedayat
OL:OL8398736W.description: An unnamed narrator who paints designs on pen cases withdraws into isolation and recounts his obsession with a mysterious woman and his descent into madness, in a narrative where memory, dream, and murder blur together and the second half distorts the first. A foundational work of modern Iranian fiction.

OL:OL16273321W.title: Invitation to a Beheading
OL:OL16273321W.author: Vladimir Nabokov
OL:OL16273321W.description: Cincinnatus C., a prisoner in a fictitious country, is condemned to death for "gnostical turpitude" and spends his final days in a cell among absurd jailers and a fellow inmate who turns out to be his executioner. A novel about an individual marked for death by a conformist world.

OL:OL3827330W.title: After Midnight
OL:OL3827330W.author: Irmgard Keun
OL:OL3827330W.description: Nineteen-year-old Sanna, who has fled to Frankfurt after being arrested in Cologne for a remark about Hitler, tries to live and love among friends and family as Nazi rule tightens and informers surround her. Written in exile by an author whose books were burned by the regime.

OL:OL1451547W.title: Michael Kohlhaas
OL:OL1451547W.author: Heinrich von Kleist
OL:OL1451547W.description: The horse dealer Michael Kohlhaas, cheated and humiliated by a Saxon nobleman who seizes two of his horses, is denied justice in the courts and raises an armed band that burns towns in pursuit of redress until he is captured and executed. A novella based on the real sixteenth-century case of Hans Kohlhase.

OL:OL751418W.title: A Model Childhood
OL:OL751418W.author: Christa Wolf
OL:OL751418W.description: A narrator returns with her family to the Polish town where she grew up as Nelly Jordan, a girl shaped by Nazi schooling and propaganda, and addresses her own past self in the second person as she tries to write about that childhood. A novel about memory and complicity under the Third Reich.

OL:OL891814W.title: Arrow of God
OL:OL891814W.author: Chinua Achebe
OL:OL891814W.description: Ezeulu, chief priest of the god Ulu in the Igbo villages of Umuaro, clashes with rivals, British colonial officials, and Christian missionaries in 1920s Nigeria, and his refusal to call the New Yam Feast brings famine and turns his people away from the old gods. The third of the author's African novels.

OL:OL2970107W.title: Season of Migration to the North
OL:OL2970107W.author: Tayeb Salih
OL:OL2970107W.description: A young Sudanese man returns to his village on the Nile after years studying in England and befriends Mustafa Sa'eed, an enigmatic newcomer who reveals a violent past among the women of London. Often named the most important Arabic novel of the twentieth century.

OL:OL1845327W.title: Thirst for Love
OL:OL1845327W.author: Yukio Mishima
OL:OL1845327W.description: Etsuko, a widow living in her father-in-law's household near Osaka, becomes the old man's mistress while nursing a consuming desire for the young gardener Saburo, an obsession that builds toward violence. An early novel exploring unrequited longing and the wish to cause pain.

OL:OL697437W.title: The Magic Toyshop
OL:OL697437W.author: Angela Carter
OL:OL697437W.description: After her parents die in a plane crash, fifteen-year-old Melanie and her younger siblings are sent to live in South London with their tyrannical uncle Philip, a maker of life-sized puppets, alongside his mute wife Margaret and her two Irish brothers. An early novel by an author later known for reworking fairy tales.

OL:OL86034W.title: Morvern Callar
OL:OL86034W.author: Alan Warner
OL:OL86034W.description: Morvern Callar, a young supermarket worker in a remote Scottish port, wakes to find her boyfriend dead by suicide on the kitchen floor; she conceals the body, takes his money, passes off his unpublished novel as her own, and heads to the Spanish rave scene. Narrated largely in Scots.

OL:OL17792692W.title: Hurricane Season
OL:OL17792692W.author: Fernanda Melchor
OL:OL17792692W.description: Children find the body of the Witch in an irrigation canal outside the poor Mexican village of La Matosa, and successive chapters circle through the lives of the townspeople to reveal how and why she was killed. Told in long, unbroken blocks of colloquial, paragraph-free prose.

OL:OL5869550W.title: Senseless
OL:OL5869550W.author: Paul Golding
OL:OL5869550W.description: George, the jaded narrator, looks back on his life in 1980s London, moving through nightclubs, drugs, and desire, his story centered on his strained bond with his brother Kelly and his deep love for his friend Matthew. A novel about gay life and the excesses of the decade.

OL:OL118276W.title: A Guest of Honour
OL:OL118276W.author: Nadine Gordimer
OL:OL118276W.description: Colonel James Bray, a former British colonial administrator expelled for his sympathies with independence, is invited back to a newly free African state by its new president, only to be caught between the president and his estranged radical rival as the country splits. The author's longest novel, set entirely outside South Africa.

OL:OL1937850W.title: A New Life
OL:OL1937850W.author: Bernard Malamud
OL:OL1937850W.description: Seymour Levin, an eastern Jew and recovering alcoholic fleeing a failed past, arrives to teach English at a science-minded college in the Pacific Northwest state of Cascadia and is drawn into department politics and an affair with a colleague's wife. The author's first fully realistic novel, drawn from his years teaching in Oregon.

OL:OL20509686W.title: Ducks, Newburyport
OL:OL20509686W.author: Lucy Ellmann
OL:OL20509686W.description: An unnamed Ohio housewife and former history teacher bakes pies and tends her family while her mind runs in one nearly unbroken sentence over memory, anxiety, and American violence, intercut with the story of a mountain lion searching for her stolen cubs. It won the 2019 Goldsmiths Prize.

OL:OL69271W.title: The Country Girls
OL:OL69271W.author: Edna O'Brien
OL:OL69271W.description: Caithleen Brady and her bold friend Baba grow up together in rural 1950s Ireland, move from a strict convent school to life in Dublin, and pursue romance, with Caithleen drawn to the married Mr Gentleman. Banned in Ireland on publication, it opened a trilogy about the two women's lives.

OL:OL33658335W.title: The Fortnight in September,
OL:OL33658335W.author: R. C. Sherriff
OL:OL33658335W.description: The Stevens family of Dulwich set out on their annual two-week holiday to the seaside resort of Bognor, staying at the same guest house and following their familiar routines while each member quietly reckons with private hopes and disappointments. A first novel about the ordinary life of a lower-middle-class English family.

OL:OL1337126W.title: The Code of the Woosters
OL:OL1337126W.author: P. G. Wodehouse
OL:OL1337126W.description: Bertie Wooster is dispatched by his Aunt Dahlia to disparage an antique cow creamer, which lands him at Totleigh Towers entangled with Sir Watkyn Bassett, the would-be dictator Roderick Spode, and two broken engagements, leaving Jeeves to extricate him. One of the best-known Jeeves and Wooster novels.

OL:OL2694535W.title: The Siege of Krishnapur
OL:OL2694535W.author: J. G. Farrell
OL:OL2694535W.description: During the Indian Rebellion of 1857, British residents and soldiers of the fictional town of Krishnapur, led by the Collector Mr Hopkins, barricade themselves in the Residency and endure a long siege that strips away their Victorian certainties. The second book in the Empire Trilogy, it won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL25098381W.title: Silas Marner
OL:OL25098381W.author: George Eliot
OL:OL25098381W.description: Silas Marner, a weaver wrongly cast out of his religious community, hoards gold in isolation in the village of Raveloe until his money is stolen and a golden-haired orphan named Eppie wanders into his cottage, whom he raises as his own. A short novel about loss, money, and redemption through love.

OL:OL43226430W.title: Home
OL:OL43226430W.author: Marilynne Robinson
OL:OL43226430W.description: Glory Boughton returns to Gilead, Iowa, to care for her dying father, the Reverend Robert Boughton, and is soon joined by her wayward, alcoholic brother Jack, who seeks refuge and tries to reconcile with the family he abandoned. A companion novel to Gilead, retelling the same events from the Boughton household.

OL:OL17658187W.title: All the Names
OL:OL17658187W.author: José Saramago
OL:OL17658187W.description: Senhor José, a low-level clerk at the Central Registry of Births, Marriages and Deaths, accidentally picks up an unknown woman's record card and becomes obsessed with tracing her life, breaking into a school and the cemetery to learn who she was. A novel about bureaucracy, identity, and the link between the living and the dead.

OL:OL76524W.title: The 39 Steps
OL:OL76524W.author: John Buchan
OL:OL76524W.description: Richard Hannay, a bored mining engineer newly returned to London, finds a murdered spy in his flat and flees to the Scottish moors, pursued by both police and a German spy ring as he tries to stop the theft of British defense secrets before war breaks out. An early chase thriller that helped define the genre.

OL:OL43336312W.title: Samuel Beckett Trilogy Molloy; Malone Dies; the Unnamable
OL:OL43336312W.author: Samuel Beckett
OL:OL43336312W.description: Three monologues by aging, decrepit narrators unfold in succession: Molloy and the detective Moran who hunts him, the bedridden Malone telling himself stories as he dies, and a disembodied voice that cannot stop speaking. Three novels regarded as a landmark of postwar fiction and a foundation of its author's reputation as a novelist.

OL:OL25796415W.title: Still Life
OL:OL25796415W.author: A. S. Byatt
OL:OL25796415W.description: In 1950s Yorkshire and Cambridge, Frederica Potter pursues knowledge and love at university while her sister Stephanie, married to a curate, contends with motherhood and their brother Marcus recovers from a breakdown. The second book in the Frederica Quartet.

OL:OL20883297W.title: Klara and the Sun
OL:OL20883297W.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
OL:OL20883297W.description: Klara, an artificial Friend powered by the sun, observes the world from a store window and is chosen to live with the sickly teenager Josie, whose mother harbors a hidden plan should her daughter die. A science fiction novel told from the perspective of an android narrator who worships the sun.

OL:OL38700W.title: Nostromo
OL:OL38700W.author: Joseph Conrad
OL:OL38700W.description: In the fictional South American country of Costaguana, the incorruptible Italian dockworker Nostromo is entrusted with smuggling a fortune in silver from the San Tomé mine during a revolution, a charge that gradually corrupts him. A novel about politics, greed, and the destructive pull of material wealth.

OL:OL506111W.title: Humboldt's Gift
OL:OL506111W.author: Saul Bellow
OL:OL506111W.description: Charlie Citrine, a successful but floundering Chicago writer, looks back on his dead friend and mentor, the brilliant poet Von Humboldt Fleisher, while his own life unravels amid divorce, lawsuits, and a comic entanglement with a small-time gangster. A novel about art, success, and failure in America that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL42393484W.title: Tongues I
OL:OL42393484W.author: Anders Nilsen
OL:OL42393484W.description: A modern retelling of the Prometheus myth weaves together a god chained to a mountain and tormented daily by an eagle he befriends, an aimless American hitchhiker crossing a desert with a teddy bear, and an orphaned East African girl sent to kill, accompanied by a talking chicken. The first volume of a graphic novel about humanity and technology.

OL:OL25803688W.title: The Employees
OL:OL25803688W.author: Olga Ravn
OL:OL25803688W.description: Aboard the interstellar Six-Thousand Ship, human and humanoid crew members give numbered statements to a committee after taking aboard strange objects from a planet, as the humanoids grow attached to them and reject the idea that they were made only for work. A novel built from workplace reports that questions what makes someone human.

OL:OL17321997W.title: Here
OL:OL17321997W.author: Richard McGuire
OL:OL17321997W.description: A single corner of one room is shown across hundreds of thousands of years, its overlapping panels jumping between prehistoric wilderness, the lives of the families who occupy the house, and a distant future. A wordless graphic novel known for using a fixed viewpoint to layer many eras at once.

OL:OL34388805W.title: The Maniac
OL:OL34388805W.author: Benjamín Labatut
OL:OL34388805W.description: The physicist Paul Ehrenfest despairs as science turns destructive, the polymath John von Neumann helps build the atomic bomb and the early computer, and decades later the Go master Lee Sedol faces the AI program AlphaGo. A fictionalized account centered on von Neumann and the rise of modern computing and artificial intelligence.

OL:OL21016756W.title: A Void
OL:OL21016756W.author: Georges Perec
OL:OL21016756W.description: Anton Vowl, an insomniac eccentric, goes missing in a Paris convulsed by unrest, and the friends who ransack his flat and search his diary for clues vanish one by one as they near the truth. A novel written entirely without the letter e.

OL:OL3820668W.title: Textermination
OL:OL3820668W.author: Christine Brooke-Rose
OL:OL3820668W.description: Emma Bovary, Emma Woodhouse, Captain Ahab, Odysseus, Huck Finn, and other figures from literature gather at the San Francisco Hilton for a convention where they pray to remain alive in readers' minds, until terrorists attack and television characters flood in. A satire of the academy, the literary canon, and cultural memory.

OL:OL19341943W.title: The City & the City
OL:OL19341943W.author: China Miéville
OL:OL19341943W.description: Inspector Tyador Borlú investigates a murder in the city of Besźel, a case that forces him across an invisible border into Ul Qoma, a second city occupying the same physical space whose residents are trained to "unsee" one another. A detective novel set in two overlapping cities that won the Hugo, World Fantasy, and Arthur C. Clarke awards.

OL:OL860032W.title: If This Is a Man / the Truce
OL:OL860032W.author: Primo Levi
OL:OL860032W.description: A young Italian Jewish chemist is deported to Auschwitz and records the daily struggle to survive the camp, then in the companion volume traces his long, wandering journey home across Eastern Europe after liberation. Two memoirs widely regarded as central works of Holocaust testimony.

OL:OL10247572W.title: Sultana's Dream
OL:OL10247572W.author: Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain
OL:OL10247572W.description: Sultana falls asleep and is led through Ladyland, a country where women run science and government while men are kept secluded indoors, powered by inventions that harness solar energy and control the weather. An early feminist science fiction story that inverts the practice of purdah.

OL:OL19908W.title: Kim
OL:OL19908W.author: Rudyard Kipling
OL:OL19908W.description: Kimball O'Hara, an orphaned white boy raised in the streets of Lahore, befriends a Tibetan lama on a spiritual quest and is recruited as a courier into the British spy network of the Great Game across colonial India. A novel about a boy moving between Indian and imperial worlds.

OL:OL35700703W.title: Mussel Feast
OL:OL35700703W.author: Birgit Vanderbeke
OL:OL35700703W.description: A mother and her two teenage children sit down to a celebratory meal of mussels, waiting for the father whose promotion they expect, and as the evening drags on the daughter's monologue lays bare the fear and tyranny that has ruled their household. A novella that mirrors the collapse of an authoritarian regime within one family.

OL:OL19074847W.title: Overstory
OL:OL19074847W.author: Richard Powers
OL:OL19074847W.description: Nine Americans, each marked in some way by trees, are drawn together around efforts to protect the last of the continent's old-growth forests, their separate stories converging into acts of activism and resistance. A novel about trees and human time that won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL16810597W.title: The Luminaries
OL:OL16810597W.author: Eleanor Catton
OL:OL16810597W.description: In 1866 gold-rush Hokitika, New Zealand, a stranger named Walter Moody stumbles into a secret meeting of twelve men investigating a vanished prospector, a dead hermit, and an attempted suicide, each connected to a fortune in gold. A novel structured around astrology that won the Booker Prize.

OL:OL17625869W.title: The Green Road
OL:OL17625869W.author: Anne Enright
OL:OL17625869W.description: Rosaleen Madigan's four grown children have scattered from County Clare to Dublin, New York, and Mali, and when she announces she will sell the family home they return for one last Christmas together. A novel told in two parts that follows each family member separately before bringing them back home.

OL:OL17764501W.title: The Noise of Time
OL:OL17764501W.author: Julian Barnes
OL:OL17764501W.description: The composer Dmitri Shostakovich waits by the elevator with a packed suitcase, expecting arrest after Stalin condemns his opera, and across three episodes endures the compromises and humiliations of making art under Soviet dictatorship. A historical novel about conscience and the cost of survival under tyranny.

OL:OL17267887W.title: Tale for the Time Being
OL:OL17267887W.author: Ruth Ozeki
OL:OL17267887W.description: In British Columbia, the writer Ruth finds a Hello Kitty lunchbox washed ashore containing the diary of Nao, a bullied Tokyo schoolgirl who plans to kill herself but first sets out to record the life of her Buddhist nun great-grandmother. A novel that alternates between the two women across the Pacific.

OL:OL1905255W.title: The House of the Spirits
OL:OL1905255W.author: Isabel Allende
OL:OL1905255W.description: Across four generations of the Trueba family, the clairvoyant Clara, her landowner husband Esteban, and their descendants live through love, feuds, and the political upheaval of an unnamed South American country leading to a military coup. A multigenerational family saga blending domestic life with magical realism.

OL:OL3951520W.title: Middlesex
OL:OL3951520W.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
OL:OL3951520W.description: Cal Stephanides, born intersex and raised as the girl Calliope in Detroit, traces a rare genetic mutation back through three generations of a Greek-American family, from a village in Asia Minor to the discovery of his true biology in adolescence. A family epic and coming-of-age story that won the Pulitzer Prize.

OL:OL17363016W.title: The Emperor's Babe
OL:OL17363016W.author: Bernardine Evaristo
OL:OL17363016W.description: Zuleika, a black Nubian girl married off to a wealthy older Roman in third-century Londinium, grows bored with her marriage and begins an affair with the visiting emperor Septimius Severus. A novel told in verse that mixes contemporary slang with Roman London.

OL:OL971643W.title: Visitation
OL:OL971643W.author: Jenny Erpenbeck
OL:OL971643W.description: A house on a lake outside Berlin passes through the hands of a dozen owners and occupants across a century of German history, from a Jewish family forced to flee to wartime requisition, the East German state, and reunification. A novel that tells the country's upheavals through one piece of land and its inhabitants.

OL:OL894246W.title: Grey King
OL:OL894246W.author: Susan Cooper
OL:OL894246W.description: Will Stanton, recovering from illness in the Welsh mountains, sets out with the white dog Cafall and the local boy Bran to wake the sleeping Sleepers and find a golden harp, fulfilling an ancient prophecy against the forces of the Dark. The fourth book in the Dark Is Rising sequence, winner of the Newbery Medal.

OL:OL27494639W.title: Under Milk Wood
OL:OL27494639W.author: Dylan Thomas
OL:OL27494639W.description: Over the course of one spring day and night, the inhabitants of the small Welsh seaside town of Llareggub reveal their dreams, secrets, and daily routines as two narrators guide the listener through their lives. A radio drama for voices known for its musical language and large cast of townsfolk.

OL:OL45865W.title: Danny the Champion of the World
OL:OL45865W.author: Roald Dahl
OL:OL45865W.description: Danny lives with his widowed father in a gypsy caravan beside their filling station, idolizing him until he discovers his father's secret hobby of poaching pheasants from the woods of the rich, cruel landowner Victor Hazell, and helps hatch an audacious plan. A children's novel about a boy and his father.

OL:OL2233736W.title: The Pursuit of Love
OL:OL2233736W.author: Nancy Mitford
OL:OL2233736W.description: Linda Radlett, the most beautiful and wayward daughter of the eccentric aristocratic Radlett family at Alconleigh, pursues love across the 1920s and 1930s, falling first for a Tory politician, then a Communist, and finally a French duke named Fabrice, all narrated by her cousin Fanny. A comic novel satirizing the British upper class, drawn closely from the author's own family.

OL:OL1921198W.title: Libra
OL:OL1921198W.author: Don DeLillo
OL:OL1921198W.description: Lee Harvey Oswald moves through his childhood, defection to the Soviet Union, and return to America, where he is drawn into a fictional CIA conspiracy to shoot at President Kennedy, while archivist Nicholas Branch tries decades later to assemble the assassination's fragments. A novel blending documented history with invented conspiracy.

OL:OL228720W.title: If Beale Street Could Talk
OL:OL228720W.author: James Baldwin
OL:OL228720W.description: In early 1970s Harlem, nineteen-year-old Tish discovers she is pregnant just as her fiancé Fonny, a young sculptor, is jailed on a false rape charge, and the two families work to free him before the baby arrives. The author's only novel narrated by a woman, centered on a Black couple's love and the legal system stacked against them.

OL:OL1184856W.title: The Vagabond
OL:OL1184856W.author: Colette
OL:OL1184856W.description: Renée Néré, a divorced woman in Paris, supports herself as a music-hall dancer and weighs a new suitor, Maxime, against the independence she has built, finally choosing her wandering life and a tour abroad over remarriage. Drawn from the author's own years performing after her divorce.

OL:OL60979W.title: The Busconductor Hines
OL:OL60979W.author: James Kelman
OL:OL60979W.description: Rab Hines hates his job as a Glasgow bus conductor and dreams of emigrating to Australia or training as a driver, while living with his wife Sandra and young son Paul in a cramped tenement flat. Written entirely in Glaswegian vernacular, it was the author's debut and drew attention for its working-class voice.

OL:OL1326304W.title: The Bell
OL:OL1326304W.author: Iris Murdoch
OL:OL1326304W.description: At Imber Court, an Anglican lay community beside a Benedictine convent in Gloucestershire, the arrival of a new bell coincides with the tangled lives of the unhappy Dora, the troubled leader Michael, and young Toby, leading to scandal and the community's collapse. A novel concerned with religion, guilt, and desire.

OL:OL4212427W.title: A Compass Error
OL:OL4212427W.author: Sybille Bedford
OL:OL4212427W.description: Flavia Herbert spends a summer in the south of France in the 1930s studying for Oxford while protecting her mother's affair, until a worldly older woman seduces her and exploits her trust, leaving lasting damage. A coming-of-age novel and sequel to A Favourite of the Gods.

OL:OL3260491W.title: Waterland
OL:OL3260491W.author: Graham Swift
OL:OL3260491W.description: Tom Crick, a history teacher in Greenwich facing forced retirement after his wife snatches a baby, abandons his lessons to tell his students about his childhood in the Fenland of eastern England, including a 1943 drowning, an abortion, and his family's dark secrets. A novel built from fragmented, non-chronological storytelling about history and the past.

OL:OL2433540W.title: Tales of the City
OL:OL2433540W.author: Armistead Maupin
OL:OL2433540W.description: Mary Ann Singleton leaves Cleveland for 1970s San Francisco and rents an apartment at 28 Barbary Lane, where the marijuana-growing landlady Anna Madrigal and tenants including Mona, Brian, and the gay Michael Tolliver become her new family. The first book in a series that began as a newspaper serial.

OL:OL166971W.title: Demons
OL:OL166971W.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
OL:OL166971W.description: A provincial Russian town descends into chaos as the conspirator Pyotr Verkhovensky assembles a revolutionary cell and the magnetic, amoral aristocrat Nikolai Stavrogin exerts a destructive influence over those around him, leading to murder and suicide. A political novel attacking the radical and nihilist movements of the era, also translated as The Possessed and The Devils.

OL:OL42397165W.title: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny
OL:OL42397165W.author: Kiran Desai
OL:OL42397165W.description: Between 1996 and 2002, two young Indians whose families are long acquainted, the aspiring novelist Sonia and the struggling journalist Sunny, meet by chance on a train in India and carry on a romance that moves between India and the United States. Shortlisted for the 2025 Booker Prize.

OL:OL20044855W.title: Transit
OL:OL20044855W.author: Rachel Cusk
OL:OL20044855W.description: Faye, a writer newly divorced, moves back to London with her two sons and renovates a derelict flat, and the book unfolds through the conversations she has with builders, students, former lovers, and others she meets. The second book in the Outline trilogy, built almost entirely from other people's talk.

OL:OL6831429W.title: The Bloater
OL:OL6831429W.author: Rosemary Tonks
OL:OL6831429W.description: Min, a BBC sound engineer in London married to the barely-noticed George, is pursued by a pompous, physically overblown opera singer she nicknames the Bloater while weighing whether to take the musicologist Billy as a lover. A short comic novel written in a few weeks and long out of print before its rediscovery.

OL:OL2645476W.title: Passing
OL:OL2645476W.author: Nella Larsen
OL:OL2645476W.description: Irene Redfield, a light-skinned Black woman in 1920s Harlem, reunites with her childhood friend Clare Kendry, who has been passing as white and is married to a racist man unaware of her background, and grows increasingly anxious as Clare reenters her life. A novella that ends with Clare's fatal fall from a window.

OL:OL43115667W.title: The Palliser Novels
OL:OL43115667W.author: Anthony Trollope
OL:OL43115667W.description: Across six linked novels, the wealthy aristocrat and politician Plantagenet Palliser and his wife Lady Glencora move through English political and social life, with recurring characters facing elections, scandals, marriages, and money troubles. A series concerned with Victorian parliamentary politics, running from Can You Forgive Her? to The Duke's Children.

OL:OL28556190W.title: Miss Marjoribanks
OL:OL28556190W.author: Margaret Oliphant
OL:OL28556190W.description: Lucilla Marjoribanks returns to the provincial town of Carlingford after her education and sets out to organize its social life around her weekly Thursday evenings, managing courtships and a parliamentary candidate until her father's sudden death exposes his ruined finances. The fifth book in the Chronicles of Carlingford.

OL:OL41016555W.title: Pickwick Papers
OL:OL41016555W.author: Charles Dickens
OL:OL41016555W.description: Samuel Pickwick and three fellow members of the Pickwick Club travel the English countryside by coach to report on what they see, falling into comic mishaps, a breach-of-promise lawsuit, and a debtors' prison, accompanied by Pickwick's sharp-tongued servant Sam Weller. The author's first novel, originally issued in monthly installments.

OL:OL1449843W.title: The Road to the City
OL:OL1449843W.author: Natalia Ginzburg
OL:OL1449843W.description: Delia, a seventeen-year-old girl from a poor rural family in Italy, longs to escape to the city and is seduced by Giulio, an affluent medical student she hopes to marry, overlooking her real feeling for the gentle Nini and ending up pregnant and resigned to her fate. The author's first published work, issued under a pseudonym during the war.

OL:OL116089W.title: In the Time of the Butterflies
OL:OL116089W.author: Julia Alvarez
OL:OL116089W.description: The Mirabal sisters—Patria, Minerva, María Teresa, and the surviving Dedé—live and resist under Rafael Trujillo's dictatorship in the Dominican Republic, joining the underground until three are murdered on a mountain road in 1960. Historical fiction based on the real sisters known as the Butterflies.

OL:OL42974304W.title: Moderato Cantabile
OL:OL42974304W.author: Marguerite Duras
OL:OL42974304W.description: Anne Desbaresdes, a wealthy woman taking her son to piano lessons in a small French town, becomes fixated on a murder she half-witnesses in a café and returns repeatedly to drink and talk with an unemployed man named Chauvin, imagining the dead lovers' relationship. A spare novel of repressed desire that brought the author wide fame.

OL:OL19740451W.title: The Discomfort of Evening
OL:OL19740451W.author: Lucas Rijneveld
OL:OL19740451W.description: Ten-year-old Jas lives with her strict Reformed family on a Dutch dairy farm and, after her older brother Matthies drowns in a skating accident, sinks into grief and disturbed behavior as the family falls apart. The author's debut novel, which won the International Booker Prize in 2020.

OL:OL20150260W.title: Normal People
OL:OL20150260W.author: Sally Rooney
OL:OL20150260W.description: In County Sligo, Ireland, popular schoolboy Connell and the wealthy outcast Marianne begin a secret relationship that continues, breaks, and resumes through their years at Trinity College in Dublin, shaped by class difference and miscommunication. Winner of the Costa Best Novel award and adapted for television.

OL:OL37949460W.title: Intermezzo
OL:OL37949460W.author: Sally Rooney
OL:OL37949460W.description: In Dublin and rural Ireland after their father's death, two brothers grieve and stumble through relationships: Ivan, a twenty-two-year-old former chess prodigy who falls for the older Margaret, and Peter, a thirty-two-year-old lawyer torn between his young girlfriend Naomi and his ex Sylvia. The author's fourth novel, focused on brothers and grief.

OL:OL1925470W.title: The Bonfire of the Vanities
OL:OL1925470W.author: Tom Wolfe
OL:OL1925470W.description: Sherman McCoy, a wealthy Wall Street bond trader, takes a wrong turn into the Bronx with his mistress and is involved in a hit-and-run that injures a young Black man, setting off a chain of events driven by ambitious lawyers, a tabloid journalist, and racial politics in 1980s New York. A satirical novel of greed and class first serialized in Rolling Stone.

OL:OL16239762W.title: Gone Girl
OL:OL16239762W.author: Gillian Flynn
OL:OL16239762W.description: On their fifth wedding anniversary in North Carthage, Missouri, Amy Dunne disappears and her husband Nick becomes the prime suspect, until alternating narratives and Amy's diary reveal that she has staged the whole disappearance to frame him. A psychological thriller alternating between the husband's and wife's accounts.

OL:OL2824299W.title: The Light Years
OL:OL2824299W.author: Elizabeth Jane Howard
OL:OL2824299W.description: Over the summers of 1937 and 1938, the wealthy Cazalet family—brothers Hugh, Edward, and Rupert, their wives, children, parents, and unmarried sister Rachel—gather at their Sussex country house as the threat of another world war approaches. The first book in the Cazalet Chronicles.

OL:OL2435538W.title: Angel
OL:OL2435538W.author: Elizabeth Taylor
OL:OL2435538W.description: Angelica Deverell, a shopkeeper's imaginative daughter, escapes her drab origins by writing wildly popular and absurd romance novels, gaining wealth and fame before sliding into critical ridicule, isolation, and decline. A novel charting the rise and fall of a deluded, self-important author.

OL:OL1999221W.title: The Tunnel
OL:OL1999221W.author: William H. Gass
OL:OL1999221W.description: William Frederick Kohler, a history professor who has just finished a major study of Nazi Germany, finds himself unable to write its introduction and instead pours out a bitter, digressive account of his own life while secretly digging a tunnel beneath his basement. A long, experimental novel that took its author twenty-six years to write.

OL:OL119209W.title: A Boy's Own Story
OL:OL119209W.author: Edmund White
OL:OL119209W.description: An unnamed narrator looks back on his adolescence in 1950s America as a self-conscious gay boy navigating early sexual encounters, family, and shame, culminating in his betraying a teacher he has slept with to the school authorities. A semi-autobiographical novel and the first of a trilogy.

OL:OL2535336W.title: The Trick Is to Keep Breathing
OL:OL2535336W.author: Janice Galloway
