OL:OL2535336W.description: Joy Stone, a twenty-seven-year-old drama teacher living outside Glasgow, unravels into depression, anorexia, and self-blame after her married lover drowns on holiday and her mother dies. The author's debut, told in an experimental style that plays with typography and stream of consciousness.

OL:OL16509148W.title: The Song of Achilles
OL:OL16509148W.author: Madeline Miller
OL:OL16509148W.description: Patroclus, exiled as a boy to Phthia, befriends and falls in love with the half-divine Achilles, training with the centaur Chiron and following him to the Trojan War, where Achilles' rage after Patroclus' death seals both their fates. A retelling of the Iliad from Patroclus' viewpoint that won the Orange Prize.

OL:OL20878208W.title: Detransition, Baby
OL:OL20878208W.author: Torrey Peters
OL:OL20878208W.description: Reese, a trans woman who longs to be a mother, and her ex Ames, who has detransitioned to live as a man, are drawn back together when Ames's lover and boss Katrina becomes pregnant and the three consider raising the child together. A novel about gender, parenthood, and trans life, nominated for the Women's Prize for Fiction.

OL:OL24511712W.title: The Trees
OL:OL24511712W.author: Percival L. Everett
OL:OL24511712W.description: In Money, Mississippi, a series of murders of white men related to Emmett Till's killers each leave behind a second body resembling the lynched Till, and Black detectives Ed Morgan and Jim Davis investigate as similar killings spread across the country. A satirical novel about lynching and racial violence, shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

OL:OL17343073W.title: Vernon Subutex 1
OL:OL17343073W.author: Virginie Despentes
OL:OL17343073W.description: Vernon Subutex, once the owner of a famed Paris record shop, slides into homelessness after his benefactor rock star dies, then becomes the object of a frantic search because he holds the musician's last filmed confessions. The first book of a Paris-set trilogy that moves through a wide cast of contemporary French characters.

OL:OL27811097W.title: Love Me Tender
OL:OL27811097W.author: Constance Debré
OL:OL27811097W.description: After leaving her husband and lawyer career to write and date women, the narrator shares custody of her young son Paul until her ex turns against her, stripping her custody down to brief supervised visits as she lives between borrowed rooms. A work of autofiction about a mother's loss of her child and her pursuit of an austere, independent life.

OL:OL27853003W.title: Big Swiss
OL:OL27853003W.author: Jen Beagin
OL:OL27853003W.description: Greta, a forty-five-year-old who has moved to Hudson, New York, transcribes a sex therapist's sessions and becomes fixated on a client she nicknames Big Swiss, a married gynecologist, then engineers a chance meeting and an affair while hiding that she knows the woman's secrets. A comic novel about trauma, attraction, and deception.

OL:OL27344918W.title: Mammoth
OL:OL27344918W.author: Eva Baltasar
OL:OL27344918W.description: A disillusioned young lesbian academic in her late twenties sets out to get pregnant with no partner, then abandons the city for an isolated farmhouse where she tends lambs, takes up with a shepherd, and strips her life down to the raw. A short, harsh novel about wage labor, motherhood, and the urge to feel alive.

OL:OL1916914W.title: A Long Way Down
OL:OL1916914W.author: Nick Hornby
OL:OL1916914W.description: Four strangers meet on the roof of a London tower block on New Year's Eve, each intending to jump, and abandon their plans once they find one another: disgraced TV host Martin, devoted mother Maureen, teenage Jess, and American musician JJ. A dark comedy narrated in turn by the four would-be suicides.

OL:OL27847855W.title: We All Want Impossible Things
OL:OL27847855W.author: Catherine Newman
OL:OL27847855W.description: Ash moves her dying best friend Edi from New York into a hospice in her small Massachusetts town and spends Edi's last weeks at her side, reminiscing, while her own marriage falls apart and her daughter refuses school. A novel about friendship, caregiving, and grief that mixes humor with the slow approach of death.

OL:OL5782000W.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
OL:OL5782000W.author: Khaled Hosseini
OL:OL5782000W.description: Mariam, an illegitimate girl from Herat, is married off to the Kabul shoemaker Rasheed, who years later also takes the much younger Laila as a second wife, and the two women endure his abuse through decades of Afghan war and Taliban rule. A novel about the bond between two women set against thirty years of Afghanistan's history.

OL:OL1103203W.title: North and South
OL:OL1103203W.author: Elizabeth Gaskell
OL:OL1103203W.description: Margaret Hale leaves the rural south of England for the grim industrial town of Milton, where she clashes with the mill owner John Thornton over a workers' strike and the hardships of factory life even as their antagonism turns to attraction. An industrial novel about the conflict between employers and workers and between tradition and modernity.

OL:OL20743965W.title: Hamnet
OL:OL20743965W.author: Maggie O'Farrell
OL:OL20743965W.description: In 1590s Stratford, the herbalist Agnes and her glove-maker husband raise their children while he works in London, and their eleven-year-old son Hamnet dies of plague, plunging the family into grief that later shapes the play Hamlet. A historical novel imagining the life and loss behind Shakespeare's family.

OL:OL16142094W.title: Wonder
OL:OL16142094W.author: R. J. Palacio
OL:OL16142094W.description: August Pullman, a ten-year-old born with a facial difference caused by Treacher Collins syndrome, leaves homeschooling to enter fifth grade at Beecher Prep, where he faces stares, bullying, and betrayal but also gains loyal friends. A children's novel told through several narrators about acceptance and kindness.

OL:OL724072W.title: Heat of the Day
OL:OL724072W.author: Elizabeth Bowen
OL:OL724072W.description: In wartime London after the Blitz, Stella Rodney is told by the intelligence agent Harrison that her lover Robert Kelway is a German spy, and that he will stay silent only if she leaves Robert for him. A novel of espionage, suspicion, and divided loyalties set in the early 1940s.

OL:OL2883788W.title: Arturo's Island
OL:OL2883788W.author: Elsa Morante
OL:OL2883788W.description: Arturo Gerace grows up nearly alone on the island of Procida in the Bay of Naples, idolizing his often-absent father, until the arrival of his young stepmother Nunziata and the discovery of his father's secrets strip away his illusions. A coming-of-age novel about a boy's passage from childhood fantasy to disenchantment.

OL:OL12126363W.title: The Waiting Years
OL:OL12126363W.author: Fumiko Enchi
OL:OL12126363W.description: In late nineteenth-century Japan, Tomo, the dutiful wife of the official Yukitomo, is sent to choose a concubine for her husband and then must absorb his serial affairs across decades while holding the household together. A novel about a woman's endurance within a patriarchal upper-class family.

OL:OL672263W.title: Lead Us Into Temptation
OL:OL672263W.author: Breandán Ó hEithir
OL:OL672263W.description: In a thinly disguised Galway during Easter 1949, around the declaration of the Irish Republic, the boozy university student Martin Melody drinks, chases women, and dodges study with his disreputable friends while his father lies dying. A comic novel of Irish student life and small-town characters, the only Irish-language book to top Ireland's bestseller list.

OL:OL468850W.title: Of Love and Other Demons
OL:OL468850W.author: Gabriel García Márquez
OL:OL468850W.description: In eighteenth-century colonial Cartagena, twelve-year-old Sierva María, the neglected daughter of a marquis, is bitten by a rabid dog and shut in a convent to be exorcised, where the priest Cayetano Delaura is sent to examine her and falls in love. A short novel about superstition, faith, and forbidden love.

OL:OL5869525W.title: The Gathering
OL:OL5869525W.author: Anne Enright
OL:OL5869525W.description: Veronica Hegarty gathers with her large Irish family in Dublin for the wake of her brother Liam, who drowned himself, and circles back over their shared childhood and a buried act of abuse she once witnessed. A novel narrated by a grieving sister piecing together her family's history.

OL:OL15146628W.title: Miss Smilla's Feeling for Snow
OL:OL15146628W.author: Peter Høeg
OL:OL15146628W.description: Smilla Jaspersen, a half-Inuit scientist living in Copenhagen, refuses to accept that a Greenlandic boy from her building died by accidentally falling from a snowy roof, and her reading of his tracks pulls her into a conspiracy reaching to a glacier off Greenland. A thriller built on its narrator's knowledge of snow and ice.

OL:OL456089W.title: The Shipping News
OL:OL456089W.author: Annie Proulx
OL:OL456089W.description: Quoyle, a hapless newspaperman from upstate New York, moves with his aunt and two daughters to his ancestral Newfoundland after his unfaithful wife dies, and rebuilds his life covering car wrecks and shipping news for a local paper. A novel about a broken man remaking himself in a harsh coastal community.

OL:OL20937995W.title: Women Talking
OL:OL20937995W.author: Miriam Toews
OL:OL20937995W.description: In an isolated Mennonite colony, eight women gather secretly in a hayloft to decide whether to stay, leave, or fight after learning that men in their community have been drugging and raping them, with August Epp recording their debate. A novel imagined from real assaults in a Bolivian Mennonite settlement.

OL:OL11382843W.title: Territory of Light
OL:OL11382843W.author: Yuko Tsushima
OL:OL11382843W.description: After her husband leaves her, an unnamed woman moves with her two-year-old daughter into a sunlit fourth-floor Tokyo apartment and spends a year struggling with single motherhood, her job, her child's tantrums, and pressure to reconcile. A novel following a young divorced mother across twelve months.

OL:OL19343569W.title: Freshwater
OL:OL19343569W.author: Akwaeke Emezi
OL:OL19343569W.description: Ada, a Nigerian girl born with one foot in the spirit world, carries ogbanje spirits who take fuller form after she moves to America for college and is assaulted, splitting into voices like the fierce Asughara who seize control of her life. A novel about a fractured self told largely by the spirits inhabiting her.
